docs.title: Presenton internals, Parts I to VI
docs.text:
Reads: README.md, start.js, nginx.conf, servers/fastapi/api/main.py, servers/nextjs/proxy.ts · Builds on: Home · Time: ~8 min

This is the entry point for the Presenton half of the book. It shows the whole running system on one diagram, then lists every chapter in Parts I to VI with a one-line description so you can jump straight to the subsystem you need. If you read nothing else before opening the code, read the diagram and the four chapters of Part I.

docs.title: The whole system on one page
docs.text:
Presenton ships as one container (or one desktop app) that runs several cooperating processes. In the Docker image, node start.js supervises everything (start.js:720), nginx is the only listener reachable from outside, and every other server binds to the loopback interface.

flowchart LR
    Browser["Browser"] --> Nginx["nginx, port 80 in the container"]
    ApiClient["REST client with sk-presenton key"] --> Nginx
    McpClient["MCP client"] --> Nginx
    Nginx -->|"/ and Next.js /api routes"| Next["Next.js 16 on 127.0.0.1 port 3000"]
    Nginx -->|"/api/v1, /api/v2, /docs, /openapi.json"| Api["FastAPI on 127.0.0.1 port 8000"]
    Nginx -->|"/mcp"| Mcp["FastMCP server on 127.0.0.1 port 8001"]
    Nginx -->|"/app_data/..., most paths after auth_request"| Files["app_data volume"]
    Next -->|"auth status and server-side fetches"| Api
    Mcp -->|"tools call the REST API"| Api
    Api --> Db[("SQLite fastapi.db or DATABASE_URL")]
    Api --> Llm["Text LLM providers"]
    Api --> Img["Image providers"]
    Api --> Icons["Icon vector index, FastEmbed"]
    Api -->|"spawn node runner.mjs"| Export["Export runtime: Chromium plus @presenton/export-core"]
    Next -->|"spawn node runner.mjs"| Export
    Export -->|"loads /pdf-maker through nginx"| Nginx
    Export --> Files
    Api --> Files

How to read it:

  • nginx (nginx.conf:25) routes by path prefix. Pages and the Next.js-owned /api/* routes go to Next.js, the REST API goes to FastAPI, /mcp goes to the MCP server, and /app_data/... files are served straight from disk. Images, exports, uploads and the two PPTX conversion folders first pass an auth_request subrequest to FastAPI; fonts and template assets are served without one (nginx.conf:159-211).
  • Next.js renders the UI. Its request middleware (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:97) and server layouts ask FastAPI whether the caller is signed in, over the loopback URL in FAST_API_INTERNAL_URL (start.js:485).
  • FastAPI (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:65) owns the data model, the LLM calls, image and icon resolution, authentication, and API keys.
  • The MCP server (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:346) is generated from a static OpenAPI document and forwards tool calls to FastAPI at http://127.0.0.1:8000.
  • The export runtime is a Node script (presentation-export/runner.mjs, copied from scripts/run-presentation-export.mjs) that drives headless Chromium through @presenton/export-core. It opens the /pdf-maker page and writes PPTX or PDF files into app_data/exports.
  • app_data is the only persistent state: the SQLite database (unless DATABASE_URL is set), userConfig.json, generated images, uploads, fonts, template assets, exports and Mem0 memory.

The Electron desktop app runs the same FastAPI and Next.js code without nginx and without the MCP server. Runtime topology contrasts the two in detail.

docs.title: Part I: Orientation
docs.text:
Start here. These chapters give you the mental map that every later chapter assumes.

  • What Presenton is: the product surface (inputs, Standard and Smart modes, templates, editing, export, providers, deployment shapes, workspaces), a 30,000-foot walk from prompt to PPTX, and the core vocabulary.
  • Repository tour: every top-level directory and FastAPI/Next.js subpackage with its key files, verified size statistics, the technology stack with exact versions, and a "where do I look for X" index.
  • Runtime topology: the process tree under start.js, readiness and shutdown, the app_data layout and permissions, every nginx location block, and four request sequence diagrams.
  • Running it locally: docker run, the four Compose services, a minimal .env, first-run admin setup, running from source without Docker, Electron dev, Swagger, API keys with curl, tests and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Part II: Backend
docs.text:
The FastAPI server, from process start to every generation path.

  • FastAPI app and startup: the app object, router mounting, the middleware stack and the lifespan hook (migrations, admin bootstrap, template import).
  • Configuration and LLM providers: how environment variables, userConfig.json and the provider-settings row combine, and how each LLM provider client is built.
  • Data model: every SQLModel table, ownership columns, and the Alembic migration chain.
  • Standard generation pipeline: create, outline stream, prepare, slide stream and the one-shot /generate handler, step by step.
  • Prompts and schemas: the outline, structure and slide-content prompts and the JSON schemas the LLM must satisfy.
  • Streaming (SSE): the server-sent event formats and the helpers that produce them.
  • Document ingestion: uploads, LiteParse and OCR, and how extracted text reaches the prompts.
  • Images, icons, web search: image providers, the FastEmbed icon index, and web grounding.
  • Smart mode: adaptive HTML slides, their prompts, sanitization and streaming.
  • Editing and chat assistant: AI slide edits and the chat assistant with its tools and memory.
  • REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP: the public generation API, async task polling, webhook delivery and the MCP tool surface.

docs.title: Part III: Templates
docs.text:
How a design becomes something an LLM can fill.

  • Template v2 format: the template.json structure, components, elements and the decorative flag on a 1280 by 720 canvas.
  • From template to schema to slide: how layouts become JSON schemas and how generated content is written back into slide UI.
  • Custom templates from PPTX: the PPTX conversion and the vision-model certification passes.
  • Themes and fonts: theme roles, font catalogs and font uploads.

docs.title: Part IV: Frontend
docs.text:
The Next.js application the user actually sees.

  • Next.js architecture: route groups, the request proxy, server-side auth checks and the Redux store.
  • User journey: upload, outline review, streaming generation and the dashboard, page by page.
  • Slide editor: the Konva canvas, Tiptap text editing, selection, undo and autosave.
  • Settings, onboarding, auth UI: account setup and sign-in, provider onboarding, Settings and the admin pages.

docs.title: Part V: Export
docs.text: • PPTX and PDF export: the /pdf-maker page, the export task file, @presenton/export-core, and how the output lands in the owner's export directory.

docs.title: Part VI: Auth, infra, ops
docs.text:
• Auth and multi-user: users, JWT cookies, API keys, owner scoping of rows and files, and the asset authorization rules.
  • Docker build and deployment: the multi-stage Dockerfile, pinned Chromium, image contents and release flow.
  • Electron desktop app: the desktop process model, per-launch desktop credential, packaging and updates.
  • CI, tests, security: the GitHub Actions workflows, the test suites and the security checks.

docs.title: Conventions used in every chapter
docs.text:
• Source citations look like servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:29. Paths are relative to the repository root and line numbers refer to snapshot 571461f.
  • Code excerpts are verbatim apart from elisions marked # ... or // ....
  • Blocks titled Gotcha flag behavior that is easy to break or misread.
  • Endpoints are collected in the Endpoint index and files in the File index.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• Presenton is nginx in front of three loopback servers (Next.js on 3000, FastAPI on 8000, MCP on 8001), all supervised by start.js in Docker.
  • FastAPI owns data, generation, auth and API keys. Next.js renders the UI and checks sessions by calling FastAPI.
  • Exports are produced by a separate Node runtime that drives Chromium against the /pdf-maker page.
  • Everything persistent lives under app_data.
  • Parts I to VI follow the request path: orientation, backend, templates, frontend, export, then operations.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Begin with What Presenton is for the product surface and the end-to-end walk-through.

docs.title: What Presenton is
docs.text:
Reads: README.md, VISION.md, docs/presentation-generation-modes.md, docs/template-v2.md, servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py, servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, servers/fastapi/constants/llm.py · Builds on: Part I landing · Time: ~25 min

This chapter describes Presenton as a product, but every claim is pinned to the code that implements it. You will learn what goes in (prompts, documents, PPTX designs), the two generation modes and how PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE gates them, what ships as templates, how editing and export work, which model providers are supported, and which deployment shapes exist. The chapter ends with a 30,000-foot walk through one Standard generation, naming the function at each step, and a vocabulary table used by the rest of the book.

docs.title: Step 1: The one-paragraph summary
docs.text:
Presenton is an open-source (Apache 2.0) AI presentation generator. A user gives it a prompt, optionally with reference documents, chooses a design, and gets back a deck that is fully editable in the browser and exportable as an editable PPTX or a PDF. It runs self-hosted as a Docker web app or as an Electron desktop app, it exposes the same generation as a REST API and as an MCP server, and it lets you bring your own text and image model providers, including local ones such as Ollama and LM Studio (README.md:40-46).

VISION.md frames the project as "an open source document engine, not a closed design platform", and the code reflects that: almost every behavior is configurable through environment variables or a Settings page, and nothing requires a hosted service except the optional Community gallery and the optional Presenton Cloud provider (README.md:356-369, README.md:563-582).

The rest of this chapter goes through the product surface one feature at a time.

docs.title: Step 2: What goes in
docs.text:
Presenton accepts three kinds of input. Each maps to concrete endpoints.

Input How the user supplies it Where it enters the backend A prompt Text box on the upload page, or content in the API body POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/create (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1681) or POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate (presentation.py:3169) Pre-written slides slides_markdown, one Markdown string per slide (API only) GeneratePresentationRequest.slides_markdown (servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py:10); skips outline generation (presentation.py:2710-2711, presentation.py:2836-2844, see Standard generation pipeline) Reference documents File picker on the upload page, or files in the API body POST /api/v1/ppt/files/upload (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/files.py:79) stores files in a temp directory and returns their paths; DocumentsLoader (servers/fastapi/services/documents_loader.py:163) extracts text Your own PowerPoint design Custom template wizard The template endpoints under /api/v1/ppt/template (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:96), which convert a PPTX into a Template v2 design (see Custom templates from PPTX)

The one-shot API accepts any combination of content, slides_markdown and files, but at least one must be non-empty. The check lives in check_if_api_request_is_valid (presentation.py:2620):

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt)
    # Making sure either content, slides markdown or files is provided
    if not (request.content or request.slides_markdown or request.files):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="Either content or slides markdown or files is required to generate presentation",
        )

    if request.n_slides is not None and request.n_slides <= 0:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="Number of slides must be greater than 0",
        )

    if request.n_slides is not None and request.n_slides > MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail=f"Number of slides cannot be greater than {MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES}",
        )

MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES is 50 (servers/fastapi/constants/presentation.py:4). Each outline is capped at MAX_OUTLINE_CONTENT_WORDS words, read from the MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS environment variable and 100 by default (constants/presentation.py:5-23).

Gotcha

content is declared as a required field (content: str = Field(...), servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py:9). A body that omits content entirely fails Pydantic validation with HTTP 422 before the check above runs, even if slides_markdown is present. Send "content": "" when you only want to supply slides_markdown or files.

Generation can be tuned with tone (default, casual, professional, funny, educational, sales_pitch, from servers/fastapi/enums/tone.py), verbosity (concise, standard, text-heavy, from servers/fastapi/enums/verbosity.py), language, instructions, include_title_slide, include_table_of_contents and web_search.

Gotcha

The README says language defaults to "English" (README.md:814). The code says otherwise: language is Optional[str] with default None and the description "If omitted, model auto-detects language" (servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py:25-28). Pass the language explicitly if you need a deterministic result.

docs.title: Step 3: The two generation modes
docs.text:
Presenton has two different generation engines that share the same database, editor and export path.

Standard Smart Layouts Fixed layouts from a Template v2 design; the LLM only fills schema fields Adaptive HTML slides written by the LLM for the content Outline review Yes: outlines stream to an outline page where the user edits them and picks a template No: generation streams straight into the editor Templates Built-in and custom templates Not used (no template workflow) Stored slide SlideModel.content (JSON) plus SlideModel.ui (layout tree) SlideModel.html_content, with layout_group and layout set to "smart-html" (presentation.py:2062-2066) One-shot API POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate and /generate/async POST /api/v2/ppt/presentation/generate/smart and /generate/smart/async (servers/fastapi/api/v2/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:229, servers/fastapi/api/v2/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:264) Covered in Standard generation pipeline Smart mode

In the browser both modes start from the same upload page. UploadPage.tsx creates the presentation row with generation_mode set, then routes to /outline for Standard or straight to /presentation for Smart (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/upload/components/UploadPage.tsx:517-525). On the server, stream_presentation checks the stored mode and hands Smart presentations to a separate streamer:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt)
@PRESENTATION_ROUTER.get("/stream/{id}", response_model=PresentationWithSlides)
async def stream_presentation(
    id: uuid.UUID, sql_session: AsyncSession = Depends(get_async_session)
):
    presentation = await sql_session.get(PresentationModel, id)
    if not presentation:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Presentation not found")
    if presentation.generation_mode == "smart":
        return await stream_smart_presentation(presentation, sql_session)
    if not presentation.structure:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="Presentation not prepared for stream",
        )

docs.title: 3.1 PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE
docs.text:
An operator chooses which modes users see with one environment variable. FastAPI parses it like this:

servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py (excerpt)
def get_presentation_generation_mode() -> PresentationGenerationMode:
    """Return the enabled generation mode, matching the web UI's fallback."""
    value = (os.getenv("PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE") or "").strip().lower()
    if value in {"standard", "smart", "both"}:
        return value
    return "both"

Next.js has a twin, normalizePresentationGenerationMode (servers/nextjs/utils/presentationGenerationMode.ts:7-21), with the same fallback to "both". The effect of each value:

Value Web UI MCP tools exposed both (default, and any unknown value) Mode selector shown; Standard is selected first (getInitialGenerationMode, presentationGenerationMode.ts:30-34) Standard, template-generation, Smart and shared tools standard Selector hidden, always Standard; template pages available Standard, template-generation and shared tools smart Selector hidden, always Smart; /templates, /custom-template and /template-preview redirect to /dashboard (for example servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/templates/page.tsx:7-14) Smart tools plus the shared tools

The "shared" tools are file upload (/api/v1/ppt/files/mcp-upload) and async task status (/api/v1/async-tasks/status/{id}), which every mode needs (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:88-99). The MCP side is implemented by choosing which OpenAPI routes become tools:

servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py (excerpt)
def get_mcp_route_maps(
    generation_mode: PresentationGenerationMode,
) -> list[RouteMap]:
    """Expose only workflows enabled by PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE."""
    route_maps: list[RouteMap] = []
    if generation_mode in {"both", "standard"}:
        route_maps.extend(MCP_STANDARD_ROUTE_MAPS)
        route_maps.extend(MCP_TEMPLATE_ROUTE_MAPS)
    if generation_mode in {"both", "smart"}:
        route_maps.extend(MCP_SMART_ROUTE_MAPS)
    route_maps.extend(MCP_SHARED_ROUTE_MAPS)
    route_maps.append(RouteMap(mcp_type=MCPType.EXCLUDE))
    return route_maps

Gotcha

PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE is a UI and MCP filter, not an access control. The REST endpoints for both modes stay mounted regardless of the value (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:68-74), and docs/presentation-generation-modes.md says so explicitly. If you need to forbid a mode, you must add a check in the endpoints.

Gotcha

The variable is read from the process environment of both servers at request time. In Docker both inherit it from the container, but if you run Next.js and FastAPI separately you must set the same value in both, and restart both after changing it.

docs.title: Step 4: Templates
docs.text:
A template is a Template v2 design: a JSON document of slide layouts on a 1280 by 720 canvas, each layout made of components, each component made of typed elements. Elements marked decorative: true are fixed artwork; the rest become fields in a JSON schema the LLM fills (docs/template-v2.md:116-117). Template v2 format covers the format.

Sixteen built-in designs live in the top-level templates/ directory, one folder each with a template.json and a static/ folder of fonts and images. At startup, import_default_templates_on_startup (servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py:22) upserts each one into the TemplateV2 table with is_default=True and copies its static assets into app_data/templates/<id>/static (default_templates.py:295-301). Layout counts at this snapshot, counted from each template.json:

Template Layouts Template Layouts civic 29 modern 10 dynamic 32 momentum 28 editorial 24 mosaic 34 executive 32 nova 28 general 12 pulse 28 horizon 28 signal 24 landmark 27 standard 11 verdant 27 swift 9

That is 383 layouts in total. The API default is general (generate_presentation_request.py:29-31).

Custom templates are created from an uploaded PPTX: the export runtime converts the deck to raw element JSON, a vision-capable model certifies each slide into components and editable fields, and the result is stored as a private TemplateV2 row (docs/template-v2.md:7-14). See Custom templates from PPTX.

docs.title: Step 5: Editing
docs.text:
After generation the user lands in the editor at /presentation?id=.... Three editing paths exist:

  1. Direct manipulation. Template v2 slides render on a Konva canvas (servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/surface/TemplateV2KonvaSlide.tsx) with drag, resize, alignment guides, and inline rich-text editing through Tiptap (servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/text/TiptapInlineTextEditor.tsx). Changes flow into Redux and are saved with PATCH /api/v1/ppt/presentation/update or PATCH /api/v1/ppt/presentation/slide_update (presentation.py:2527, presentation.py:2585). See Slide editor.
  2. AI slide edit. The user types an instruction for one slide. Standard slides go to POST /api/v1/ppt/slide/edit (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py:38), Smart slides to POST /api/v1/ppt/slide/edit-html (slide.py:135).
  3. Chat assistant. A conversational panel backed by POST /api/v1/ppt/chat/message and POST /api/v1/ppt/chat/message/stream (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/chat.py:105, chat.py:124), with tools and memory implemented under servers/fastapi/services/chat/. See Editing and chat assistant.

docs.title: Step 6: Export
docs.text: The deck exports as an editable PPTX or as a PDF. Both formats are produced the same way: a Node process runs presentation-export/runner.mjs, which calls runTask from the @presenton/export-core package (scripts/run-presentation-export.mjs:3, scripts/run-presentation-export.mjs:116-119). That package drives headless Chromium against the /pdf-maker?id=... page of the Next.js app and writes the file into app_data/exports. The package version is pinned by "presentationExportVersion": "v1.0.51" in the root package.json and installed by scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs. PPTX and PDF export covers the details.

docs.title: 7.1 Text LLM providers
docs.text:
LLM selects the text provider. The accepted values are the members of LLMProvider (servers/fastapi/enums/llm_provider.py:4-20). Defaults come from servers/fastapi/constants/llm.py and are applied in get_model (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_provider.py:126-175):

LLM Default model when the *_MODEL variable is unset openai gpt-4.1 deepseek deepseek-chat google models/gemini-2.5-flash vertex gemini-2.5-flash azure AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL, then AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT, then gpt-4.1 bedrock us.anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022-v1:0 openrouter openai/gpt-4o fireworks accounts/fireworks/models/llama-v3p1-8b-instruct together openai/gpt-oss-20b cerebras llama-3.3-70b anthropic claude-sonnet-4-20250514 litellm gpt-4.1 lmstudio openai/gpt-oss-20b ollama none (OLLAMA_MODEL must be set) custom none (CUSTOM_MODEL must be set; any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) codex gpt-5.6-luna unless CODEX_MODEL is one of the supported Codex models (constants/llm.py:18-27)

Two more provider paths exist outside that enum. LLM=presenton selects the optional Presenton Cloud provider, in which case maybe_proxy_presenton_cloud_request forwards generation requests to the hosted API instead of calling a model locally (servers/fastapi/services/presenton_cloud_proxy.py:407-460). And codex uses an OAuth sign-in with a ChatGPT account, which is why the Compose services publish host port 1455 for its callback (docker-compose.yml:11-12).

Gotcha

The README's provider table lists models/gemini-2.0-flash as the Google default and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022 as the Anthropic default (README.md:392, README.md:426). The code defaults are models/gemini-2.5-flash and claude-sonnet-4-20250514 (constants/llm.py:6, constants/llm.py:14). When in doubt, trust constants/llm.py.

An unset or unknown LLM fails at the first LLM call, not at startup, with HTTP 500 and the detail "Invalid LLM provider. Please select one of: ..." (utils/llm_provider.py:47-58). This is deliberate: the lifespan docstring says provider availability is checked when used, so account setup still works on an unconfigured instance (servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py:46-53).

Provider configuration chapters: Configuration and LLM providers for text, Images, icons, web search for images and search.

docs.title: 7.2 Image providers
docs.text:
IMAGE_PROVIDER selects how __image_prompt__ fields become pictures. Values come from ImageProvider (servers/fastapi/enums/image_provider.py:4-13):

IMAGE_PROVIDER Kind Credentials pexels Stock search PEXELS_API_KEY pixabay Stock search PIXABAY_API_KEY gemini_flash Generation (Google) GOOGLE_API_KEY nanobanana_pro Generation (Google) GOOGLE_API_KEY gpt-image-2 Generation (OpenAI) OPENAI_API_KEY, quality from GPT_IMAGE_2_QUALITY gpt-image-1.5 Generation (OpenAI) OPENAI_API_KEY, quality from GPT_IMAGE_1_5_QUALITY comfyui Self-hosted generation COMFYUI_URL, COMFYUI_WORKFLOW open_webui Self-hosted generation OPEN_WEBUI_IMAGE_URL, OPEN_WEBUI_IMAGE_API_KEY openai_compatible Any /v1/images/* gateway OPENAI_COMPAT_IMAGE_BASE_URL, _API_KEY, _MODEL

The dispatcher is ImageGenerationService.generate_image (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:187). Image generation can be turned off with DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION. Icons are not generated: __icon_query__ fields are matched against a bundled FastEmbed vector index of Phosphor icons (servers/fastapi/services/icon_finder_service.py:26-28, data in servers/fastapi/assets/icons-vectorstore.json).

docs.title: 7.3 Web search
docs.text: Optional web grounding uses either the provider's native search (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic) or an external provider. WebSearchProvider lists auto, native, searxng, tavily, exa, brave and serper (servers/fastapi/enums/web_search_provider.py), although the README notes that Brave and Serper are hidden until tested (README.md:451).

docs.title: Step 8: Deployment shapes
docs.text:
Shape What runs Entry point Chapter Docker web app nginx, FastAPI, MCP, Next.js, optional Ollama in one container CMD ["node", "/app/start.js"] (Dockerfile:153), image ghcr.io/presenton/presenton Runtime topology, Docker build and deployment Electron desktop app FastAPI and Next.js on loopback ports chosen at launch, inside a desktop window; no nginx, no MCP electron/app/main.ts Electron desktop app REST API The same FastAPI routes, called with an sk-presenton-... API key POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate and friends REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP MCP server A FastMCP Streamable HTTP server at /mcp whose tools are generated from the OpenAPI document servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP

The MCP tool names are fixed by a mapping from OpenAPI operation IDs (mcp_server.py:101-111): start_standard_presentation, start_smart_presentation, list_templates, upload_template_assets, start_template_generation, upload_files and get_job_status. Generation tools all return an async task ID that the client polls with get_job_status.

Gotcha

External REST and MCP access are server features. In Electron, PRESENTON_ELECTRON=true makes mcp_server.py exit immediately (mcp_server.py:319-321, mcp_server.py:419-424), and both HTTP servers reject any request that does not carry the per-launch desktop credential (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/desktop.py:25-48).

docs.title: Step 9: Multi-user workspaces
docs.text:
Presenton keeps a user table and scopes every owned row to a user. The first account created through /api/v1/auth/setup becomes the primary administrator (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:110-152); administrators create, reset and delete other accounts and issue API keys under /api/v1/admin (servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:41).

Isolation is enforced in three places:

  1. Request context. SessionAuthMiddleware resolves the caller from the presenton_session cookie or a bearer API key and stores the user ID in a context variable (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:94-128).
  2. Database. SQLAlchemy event hooks add owner_id == <current user> to every ORM SELECT on owned models and stamp owner_id on new rows (servers/fastapi/services/database.py:66-108). Built-in templates stay visible to everyone because the template filter also admits rows with owner_id IS NULL AND is_default (database.py:86-94).
  3. Files. Generated files go to per-user folders such as app_data/images/users/<user-id>/ (servers/fastapi/utils/asset_directory_utils.py:23-30), and /app_data/... URLs are authorized per path segment (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:106-123).

The Electron app runs auth-disabled and single-user. Auth and multi-user covers all of this in depth.

docs.title: Step 10: One generation, prompt to PPTX, at 30,000 feet
docs.text:
Here is one Standard generation from the browser, with the module and function that does the work at each step. Each later chapter zooms into one or more of these steps.

sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Browser
    participant N as Next.js
    participant A as FastAPI
    participant L as LLM provider
    participant X as Export runtime
    U->>A: POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/create
    A-->>U: presentation row with id
    U->>A: GET /api/v1/ppt/outlines/stream/ID
    A->>L: outline prompt, streamed
    A-->>U: SSE outline chunks
    U->>A: POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/prepare with outlines and template
    A->>L: structure prompt picks a layout per slide
    A-->>U: prepared
    U->>A: GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/stream/ID
    A->>L: one slide-content call per slide
    A-->>U: SSE slides, then asset updates
    U->>N: POST /api/export-presentation
    N->>X: node runner.mjs export task
    X->>N: Chromium loads /pdf-maker
    X-->>N: PPTX written to app_data/exports
    N-->>U: download URL
  1. Collect the request. The upload page (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/upload/components/UploadPage.tsx) gathers prompt, slide count, language, tone, verbosity and toggles. If files were attached it first calls PresentationGenerationApi.uploadDoc (POST /api/v1/ppt/files/upload). It then calls PresentationGenerationApi.createPresentation (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/presentation-generation.ts:82). Details: User journey.
  2. Create the row. create_presentation (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1682) validates the inputs and inserts a PresentationModel row with generation_mode="standard". Nothing has been generated yet. Details: Data model, Standard generation pipeline.
  3. Stream the outline. The outline page hook useOutlineStreaming opens GET /api/v1/ppt/outlines/stream/{id} (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/useOutlineStreaming.ts:108). stream_outlines (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/outlines.py:85) loads any documents, then iterates generate_ppt_outline (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_outlines.py:252), forwarding LLM chunks as server-sent events through safe_sse_stream (servers/fastapi/utils/sse.py:10). Details: Prompts and schemas, Streaming (SSE), Document ingestion.
  4. Review and prepare. The user edits outlines and picks a template. usePresentationGeneration calls presentationPrepare with {presentation_id, outlines, layout: <template id>} (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/usePresentationGeneration.ts:107-111). prepare_presentation (presentation.py:1841) loads the template and converts it to per-layout JSON schemas through get_template_schema (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:257, called from presentation.py:416), then asks the LLM to pick a layout index for each outline with generate_presentation_structure (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_structure.py:157) and stores the result as presentation.structure. Details: From template to schema to slide.
  5. Stream the slides. The editor opens with stream=true, and usePresentationStreaming calls GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/stream/{id} (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/usePresentationStreaming.ts:301). For each slide, stream_presentation calls get_slide_content_from_type_and_outline (presentation.py:2370, defined in servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_slide_content.py:229) to produce JSON that matches the chosen layout's schema, emits the slide immediately with placeholder assets, and starts process_slide_and_fetch_assets (presentation.py:2404, defined in servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:173) to resolve __image_prompt__ through the image provider and __icon_query__ through the icon index. Finished assets are pushed as further events. Details: Standard generation pipeline, Images, icons, web search.
  6. Edit. The Konva editor renders each slide's ui tree and saves edits back through the update endpoints. Details: Slide editor.
  7. Export. Clicking "Export as PPTX" runs fetch("/api/export-presentation", ...) (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/PresentationHeader.tsx:256). The Next.js route handler (servers/nextjs/app/api/export-presentation/route.ts:90) calls runBundledPresentationExport (servers/nextjs/lib/run-bundled-presentation-export.ts:138), which writes an export_task.json and spawns node runner.mjs <task>. @presenton/export-core loads /pdf-maker?id=... in Chromium, builds an editable PPTX, and writes it under app_data/exports. The route moves the file into app_data/exports/users/<user-id>/ and returns /api/export-presentation/file?name=..., which the browser downloads. Details: PPTX and PDF export.

The one-shot API (POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate) runs the same steps server-side inside generate_presentation_handler (presentation.py:2684): outlines, layout selection, slide content in batches of 10 with asyncio.gather (presentation.py:2984-3006), asset tasks, one commit that saves the presentation, slides and image assets together (presentation.py:3087-3091; the other commits in the handler only update the async task status row), then export_presentation (servers/fastapi/utils/export_utils.py:43) instead of the Next.js route.

Gotcha

The UI and the API export through different code paths that share the runtime. The browser path goes through the Next.js route and lib/run-bundled-presentation-export.ts; the API path goes through ExportTaskService.export_from_url in FastAPI (servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:422). A fix to one does not automatically apply to the other.

docs.title: Core vocabulary
docs.text:
These terms are used with exactly these meanings in the rest of the book.

Term Meaning Where it lives Presentation One deck: the prompt, settings, outlines, chosen layout payload, structure, theme and fonts PresentationModel (servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py) Outline Audience-facing Markdown for one slide, at most MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS words SlideOutlineModel.content (servers/fastapi/models/presentation_outline_model.py:8-21); stored in presentation.outlines Structure The list of layout indexes, one per slide PresentationStructureModel.slides: List[int] (servers/fastapi/models/presentation_structure_model.py:5-6); stored in presentation.structure Layout One slide design inside a template: an ID, a description and a list of components SlideLayout (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/layouts.py:98); at generation time a SlideLayoutModel with a json_schema (presentation.py:450-456) Slide content The JSON the LLM returns for one slide, conforming to the layout's schema, including fields such as __speaker_note__, __image_prompt__ and __icon_query__ SlideModel.content (servers/fastapi/models/sql/slide.py:26) Template v2 A complete design: layouts, merged components, theme, fonts and assets TemplateV2 table (servers/fastapi/models/sql/template_v2.py:16); built-ins in templates/<name>/template.json Component A positioned group of elements with an ID and description, the unit the certification passes reason about Component (templates/v2/models/layouts.py:54-58) Element A typed visual primitive: text, image, container, text list, table, vector, chart, infographic and others servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py Decorative flag decorative: bool on an element; false turns the element into an LLM-filled schema field, true keeps it fixed for example Text.decorative (elements.py:218) Smart slide A slide produced in Smart mode: sanitized HTML in html_content, with layout_group and layout set to "smart-html" presentation.py:2062-2066; prompts in servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_smart_presentation.py Export runtime The presentation-export/ directory: runner.mjs plus node_modules/@presenton/export-core, driven by headless Chromium installed by scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs; checked by ExportTaskService._ensure_runtime_ready (export_task_service.py:202-220) app_data The persistent data root named by APP_DATA_DIRECTORY (/app_data in Docker): database, userConfig.json, images, uploads, fonts, templates, exports, memory created by start.js:93-103; layout in Runtime topology

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• Presenton turns a prompt, documents or pre-written Markdown into an editable deck, using either Standard (template layouts plus outline review) or Smart (adaptive HTML) generation.
  • PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE (both, standard, smart) filters the UI and the MCP tools but does not restrict the REST API.
  • Sixteen built-in Template v2 designs with 383 layouts are imported at startup; custom designs come from PPTX files.
  • Text and image providers are pluggable through LLM and IMAGE_PROVIDER; defaults live in constants/llm.py, and misconfiguration surfaces only when a model is first called.
  • The same backend serves the Docker web app, the Electron app, the REST API and the MCP server, with per-user isolation enforced in middleware, SQL event hooks and file paths.
  • A Standard generation is create, outline stream, prepare, slide stream, edit, export, and each step has a named function you can open.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Continue with the Repository tour to see where each of these pieces lives on disk.

docs.title: Repository tour
docs.text:
Reads: start.js, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, nginx.conf, package.json, servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml, servers/nextjs/package.json, electron/package.json, .github/workflows/README.md · Builds on: What Presenton is · Time: ~30 min

This chapter walks the repository directory by directory and names the two to five files in each place that you will actually open. It also records verified size statistics for the snapshot, the full technology stack with exact versions, and a "where do I look for X?" index you can come back to whenever you need to find code. Treat it as a map; the later chapters are the guided walks.

docs.title: Step 1: Snapshot facts
docs.text:
Everything in this book refers to one commit. You can re-derive every number below with the commands in the collapsible block.

Fact Value Commit 571461f969beb1daa52cc68c5aaa9ba019530a35, dated 2026-11-01 Commits on that line 2,952 App version 0.9.12-beta (root package.json:3, electron/package.json:4) Export runtime pin v1.0.51 (root package.json:4) Python files in servers/fastapi, excluding tests/ 233 files, 58,185 lines Python test code in servers/fastapi/tests 114 test_*.py files, 31,899 lines in all .py files Alembic migrations 24 files in servers/fastapi/alembic/versions TypeScript in servers/nextjs (app, components, lib, store, utils, types) about 113,900 lines Built-in templates 16, with 383 layouts in total Commands that reproduce these numbers 
cd presenton-os
git rev-list --count 571461f
cd servers/fastapi
find . -name '*.py' -not -path './tests/*' -not -path './.venv/*' | wc -l
find . -name '*.py' -not -path './tests/*' -not -path './.venv/*' | xargs cat | wc -l
find tests -name 'test_*.py' | wc -l
ls alembic/versions | grep -c '\.py$'
cd ../..
for d in templates/*/; do
  python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('$d/template.json')); print('$d', len(d['layouts']))"
done

The FastAPI line count breaks down as api 10,204, services 17,559 (of which services/chat is 11,201), templates 14,283, utils 11,598 (of which utils/llm_calls is 2,255), alembic 1,801, models 1,222, constants 521, enums 84 and scripts 75, plus the top-level modules.

The largest single Python files are servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py (4,633 lines, PPTX template certification), servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py (4,131) and servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (3,393).

docs.title: Step 2: The root of the repository
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    Root["repository root"] --> StartJs["start.js, Docker process supervisor"]
    Root --> Docker["Dockerfile, Dockerfile.dev, docker-compose.yml"]
    Root --> Nginx["nginx.conf"]
    Root --> FastApi["servers/fastapi, Python backend"]
    Root --> NextJs["servers/nextjs, Next.js frontend"]
    Root --> Templates["templates, 16 built-in designs"]
    Root --> Electron["electron, desktop wrapper"]
    Root --> Scripts["scripts, sync and build helpers"]
    Root --> Docs["docs and .github/workflows"]
    StartJs --> FastApi
    StartJs --> NextJs
    StartJs --> Nginx
    Scripts -->|"installs"| ExportRt["presentation-export, gitignored runtime"]
    FastApi -->|"imports at startup"| Templates
    FastApi -->|"spawns runner.mjs"| ExportRt
    NextJs -->|"spawns runner.mjs"| ExportRt
    Electron -->|"spawns in dev and packaged builds"| FastApi
    Electron --> NextJs
File What it is start.js (738 lines) The container entry point (CMD ["node", "/app/start.js"], Dockerfile:153). Creates app_data directories, verifies the export runtime, writes userConfig.json from environment variables, starts nginx, then spawns FastAPI, the MCP server, Next.js and optionally Ollama. Runtime topology walks it line by line. Dockerfile (153 lines) Four stages: fastapi-builder (Python 3.11 venv via uv, spaCy model, FastEmbed cache warm-up), nextjs-builder (npm ci, next build), assets-builder (LiteParse dependencies and sync-presentation-export.cjs --force), and runtime (Debian trixie with pinned Chromium, nginx, Noto fonts, Tesseract, Node 22). See Docker build and deployment. Dockerfile.dev (93 lines) A single-stage development image that installs the same system packages, installs Python dependencies into the system interpreter, and runs node /app/start.js --dev (Dockerfile.dev:93). It expects the repository to be bind-mounted at /app. docker-compose.yml (534 lines) Four services: production, production-gpu, development, development-gpu, plus three named volumes for the development services. Each service forwards about 110 environment variables. See Running it locally. nginx.conf (213 lines) The only external listener (port 80). Routes / to Next.js, /api/v1/ and /api/v2/ to FastAPI, /mcp to the MCP server, and serves /app_data/... and /static/ from disk. Copied to /etc/nginx/nginx.conf by Dockerfile:150. layouts.json (247 KB) A Template v2 layout sample: {"layouts": {"layouts": [...]}} with 14 layouts (IDs such as business_proposal_cover_layout), each with id, description and components. Its image URLs point at http://127.0.0.1:8000/app_data/pptx-to-json/..., so it is the output of a PPTX conversion. No code at this snapshot references the file by name. package.json (26 lines) Root Node project: version 0.9.12-beta, presentationExportVersion v1.0.51, dependencies @llamaindex/liteparse and sharp, and the scripts sync:presentation-export, check:presentation-export, convert:template, convert:presentation-template and test. package-lock.json Lock file for the root project; also fingerprinted by scripts/sync-document-dependencies.cjs to decide whether the LiteParse runtime must be reinstalled. test-local.sh (83 lines) Runs the same three check groups as the test-all.yml workflow: repository tooling, the FastAPI pytest suite, and Next.js tests, lint, build and Cypress component tests. test_server.py (78 lines) Not a test. A stub of the remote version-check endpoint the Electron app polls (GET /versions), listening on port 8765 by default (test_server.py:59-63). NOTICE (1.27 MB) Third-party license notices, regenerated by scripts/rebuild_notice_all.py. README.md, VISION.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, LICENSE Product documentation, mission statement, contribution rules and Apache 2.0 license. .dockerignore, .gitignore Build context exclusions; note that presentation-export/, app_data and .env files are ignored by git. .do/deploy.template.yaml DigitalOcean App Platform spec that runs ghcr.io/presenton/presenton:latest on port 80. readme_assets/ Images and video used by the README.

Gotcha

CONTRIBUTING.md says contributions outside electron/ "may not be accepted at this time". That is a policy statement about upstream pull requests, not a technical boundary: the Electron app runs the shared servers/fastapi and servers/nextjs code, so most behavior you might want to change lives outside electron/.

docs.title: Step 3: servers/fastapi, the backend
docs.text: The backend is one Python package named presenton-backend (servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml:6) with requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.12". Setuptools packages api, enums, models, services, constants, utils and templates (pyproject.toml:48-58). The server is always started with the working directory set to servers/fastapi, because get_resource_path resolves bundled assets relative to os.getcwd() (servers/fastapi/utils/path_helpers.py:15-17).

docs.title: 3.1 Top-level modules
docs.text: File Role server.py 29-line launcher: parses --port (required), --reload ("true" or not) and --log-level, then runs uvicorn.run("api.main:app", host="127.0.0.1", ...) (server.py:21-29). mcp_server.py 480 lines. Builds a FastMCP server from openai_spec.json and serves it with the Streamable HTTP transport on 127.0.0.1:8001 (mcp_server.py:457-466). migrations.py 329 lines. Runs Alembic on startup when MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP is "true" or "True" (migrations.py:42-45), with special handling for databases created before Alembic was introduced. openai_spec.json A static OpenAPI document (despite the name, it has nothing to do with OpenAI) consumed by the MCP server. Regenerate it with scripts/generate_openapi_spec.py. server.spec PyInstaller spec used by npm run build:fastapi in electron/ to freeze the backend for desktop builds. alembic.ini Alembic configuration; scripts live in alembic/. uv.lock, pyproject.toml Dependency pins.

docs.title: 3.2 api/
docs.text:
The HTTP layer. api/main.py creates the app and mounts seven routers (api/main.py:68-74), mounts /app_data/<root> and /static file servers (api/main.py:77-86), and adds CORS, UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware and SessionAuthMiddleware (api/main.py:94-103). api/lifespan.py runs migrations, admin bootstrap and template import at startup.

Path Prefix Key files api/v1/ppt/ /api/v1/ppt endpoints/presentation.py (create, prepare, stream, generate, export), endpoints/outlines.py, endpoints/slide.py, endpoints/template.py, endpoints/chat.py, endpoints/files.py, endpoints/images.py, endpoints/icons.py, endpoints/fonts.py, plus provider helpers (openai.py, google.py, anthropic.py, ollama.py, openrouter.py, codex_auth.py) api/v1/auth/ /api/v1/auth router.py (status, verify, setup, login, logout), principal.py, users.py, assets.py, bootstrap.py, desktop.py, presenton_oauth.py api/v1/admin/ /api/v1/admin router.py (API keys, users, provider settings) api/v1/async_tasks/ /api/v1/async-tasks router.py (task status polling) api/v1/webhook/ /api/v1/webhook router.py (subscribe, unsubscribe) api/v1/mock/ /api/v1/mock router.py (sample webhook payloads) api/v2/ppt/ /api/v2/ppt endpoints/presentation.py (Smart /generate/smart and /generate/smart/async) api/middlewares.py (all) SessionAuthMiddleware, UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware

docs.title: 3.3 models/ and models/sql/
docs.text: models/ holds Pydantic request and response models: generate_presentation_request.py, presentation_outline_model.py, presentation_structure_model.py, presentation_layout.py, sse_response.py, user_config.py and others. models/sql/ holds 15 table modules: 13 SQLModel tables plus user.py and presenton_cloud_provider.py, which use a plain SQLAlchemy DeclarativeBase (models/sql/user.py:12-19) so they work with fastapi-users. They include presentation.py, slide.py, template_v2.py, user.py, api_key.py, async_task.py, provider_settings.py, image_asset.py, chat_history_message.py and webhook_subscription.py. See Data model.

docs.title: 3.4 services/
docs.text:
Stateful or I/O-heavy components.

  • database.py: engine, async_session_maker, owner-scoping event hooks (services/database.py:66-108), create_db_and_tables.
  • export_task_service.py: spawns the Node export runtime with a 300-second timeout (services/export_task_service.py:122).
  • image_generation_service.py: one method per image provider (services/image_generation_service.py:132).
  • icon_finder_service.py: FastEmbed vector search over Phosphor icons.
  • documents_loader.py and liteparse_service.py: document text extraction.
  • chat/: the assistant (service.py, tools.py, memory_layer.py, prompts.py).
  • Also: api_keys.py, async_tasks.py, webhook_service.py, provider_settings.py, mem0_presentation_memory_service.py, presenton_cloud_proxy.py, concurrent_service.py, temp_file_service.py.

docs.title: 3.5 utils/ and utils/llm_calls/
docs.text:
Pure helpers and configuration readers. The ones you will open most:

  • get_env.py: one getter per environment variable.
  • user_config.py: merges userConfig.json into the environment.
  • llm_config.py and llm_provider.py: build LLM client configurations and resolve model names.
  • process_slides.py: resolves __image_prompt__ and __icon_query__ into URLs.
  • sse.py: safe_sse_stream.
  • export_utils.py: export_presentation.
  • asset_directory_utils.py: per-user directories and path resolution.
  • web_search.py: grounding.

utils/llm_calls/ holds one module per LLM task: generate_presentation_outlines.py, generate_presentation_structure.py, generate_slide_content.py, generate_smart_presentation.py, edit_slide.py, edit_slide_html.py, select_slide_type_on_edit.py and generate_web_search_query.py. Prompts live inside these modules. See Prompts and schemas.

docs.title: 3.6 templates/ and templates/v2/
docs.text:
Gotcha

There are two directories named templates. The top-level templates/ holds the 16 design folders (data). servers/fastapi/templates/ is a Python package (code) that loads, previews and converts templates. The production Compose service bind-mounts the code package read-only from the host (docker-compose.yml:15), which replaces the image's copy of that Python code; it does not affect the design folders.

The Python package contains default_templates.py (imports the built-in designs at startup), pptx_font_utils.py (font catalog; the Docker build asserts it is non-empty, Dockerfile:22), fonts_and_slides_preview.py, presentation_layout.py, preview.py and assets/fonts.json. Its v2/ subpackage is the Template v2 engine:

  • schema.py: turns layouts into JSON schemas (get_template_schema, templates/v2/schema.py:257).
  • generation.py and certified_generation.py: the PPTX-to-template pipeline.
  • theme.py: theme roles.
  • content.py and tools.py: content helpers.
  • models/layouts.py and models/elements.py: the Pydantic models of layouts, components and elements.

See Template v2 format.

docs.title: 3.7 enums/, constants/
docs.text: enums/ has eight small enums: LLMProvider, ImageProvider, WebSearchProvider, Tone, Verbosity, AsyncTaskStatus, WebhookEvent and LLMCallType. constants/ has llm.py (default models), presentation.py (MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES = 50, outline word limit, default template order), documents.py (accepted upload types) and supported_ollama_models.py.

docs.title: 3.8 alembic/
docs.text: alembic/env.py, script.py.mako and 24 revision files under alembic/versions/, from 00b3c27a13bc_init.py to the head 026c0ba8b35c_add_async_task_payload_and_unified_api_.py (REVISION_HEAD, migrations.py:36-37). See Data model.

docs.title: 3.9 tests/
docs.text: 114 test_*.py files: 95 in tests/unit, 6 in tests/integration, 1 each in tests/regression and tests/edge_cases, the rest at the top level, plus conftest.py and shared mocks/. pyproject.toml:72-73 sets testpaths = ["tests"]. See CI, tests, security.

docs.title: 3.10 static/, assets/, scripts/
docs.text:
• static/ is served at /static/: icons/ (Phosphor icons in six weights, bold, duotone, fill, light, regular, thin, with 1,512 SVGs in bold alone, plus placeholder.svg), images/ (placeholder.jpg, replaceable_template_image.png) and vendor/ (Chart.js 4.5.1, chartjs-plugin-datalabels 2.2.0 and the Tailwind browser runtime 4.3.3, each with its license).
  • assets/ holds icons.json (9,072 icon entries with tags) and icons-vectorstore.json, the prebuilt embedding index loaded by IconFinderService.
  • scripts/ has generate_openapi_spec.py (rewrites openai_spec.json from app.openapi()) and warm_fastembed_cache.py (downloads FastEmbed weights during the Docker build).

docs.title: Step 4: servers/nextjs, the frontend
docs.text: A Next.js 16.4.1 app with output: "standalone" and distDir: ".next-build" (servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:8-11). Its request middleware is proxy.ts at the project root, which Next.js 16 runs for every request matched by config.matcher (proxy.ts:174-176).

docs.title: 4.1 app/ and its route groups
docs.text:
Route group or folder URLs What it holds app/page.tsx / Shows AuthGate (setup or sign in) or the home screen (app/page.tsx:7-26) app/(presentation-generator)/upload /upload Prompt, settings, document upload, mode selector app/(presentation-generator)/outline /outline Outline streaming, editing and template selection app/(presentation-generator)/presentation /presentation The editor and its streaming hooks app/(presentation-generator)/documents-preview /documents-preview Review extracted document content before generation app/(presentation-generator)/custom-template /custom-template PPTX to Template v2 wizard app/(presentation-generator)/template-preview /template-preview Preview a template's layouts app/(presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/... /dashboard, /templates, /community, /settings, /admin Dashboard shell pages app/(export)/pdf-maker /pdf-maker The page the export runtime renders app/api/... /api/export-presentation, /api/export-presentation/file, /api/export-presentation-data/[id], /api/user-config, /api/runtime-config, /api/has-required-key, /api/read-file, /api/upload-image, /api/update-svg, /api/telemetry-status, /api/github-stars Next.js route handlers (Node runtime)

The (presentation-generator) layout calls requireAppSession() before rendering any child (app/(presentation-generator)/layout.tsx:6-13), which redirects to / when there is no session.

docs.title: 4.2 The other folders
docs.text:
• components/: shared React components.
    • slide-editor/ (about 48,000 lines) is the Konva-based Template v2 editor, with its own README.md.
    • Auth/ holds AuthGate.tsx and LogoutButton.tsx.
    • OnBoarding/ holds the onboarding steps.
    • ui/ holds Radix-based primitives.
    • runtime/ holds the Tailwind browser runtime used for Smart slides.
    • Provider configuration forms such as LLMSelection.tsx and OpenAIConfig.tsx sit at the top level.
  • lib/: server-side helpers.
    • run-bundled-presentation-export.ts spawns the export runtime.
    • template-v2-json-to-html.ts (4,145 lines) renders layouts to HTML.
    • desktop-auth.ts holds the Electron guard.
    • fastapi-internal.ts resolves the FastAPI URL.
    • Also server-auth-role.ts and runtime-provider-config.ts.
  • store/: Redux Toolkit. store.ts combines four slices: presentationGeneration, pptGenUpload, userConfig and undoRedo (store/store.ts:7-14).
  • utils/: browser and server utilities.
    • api.ts provides getApiUrl and the same-origin rule.
    • serverAuth.ts provides getServerAuthStatus and requireAppSession.
    • auth.ts provides isAuthDisabled.
    • Also presentationGenerationMode.ts and providerConstants.ts.
  • types/: global.d.ts (the window.env and window.electron shapes) and llm_config.ts.
  • tests/: 27 node --test files (*.test.mjs) run by npm test ("test": "node --test").
  • cypress/: component-test support (support/), fixtures and security specs (security/). Seven *.cy.tsx component specs live next to the components they test.

See Next.js architecture.

docs.title: Step 5: templates/, the built-in designs
docs.text:
Each of the 16 folders contains template.json and static/ (fonts and images referenced by relative paths such as static/Montserrat Bold.ttf). The top-level keys of every template.json are id, name, description, thumbnail, merged_components, layouts, fonts and theme, and most also have icon_type (for example civic uses regular, standard uses bold). fonts maps a family name either to a bundled file (civic) or to a Google Fonts CSS URL (general, standard).

Template Layouts Template Layouts civic 29 modern 10 dynamic 32 momentum 28 editorial 24 mosaic 34 executive 32 nova 28 general 12 pulse 28 horizon 28 signal 24 landmark 27 standard 11 verdant 27 swift 9

constants/presentation.py:25-56 discovers these folders and orders them momentum, dynamic, executive, general, modern, standard, swift, then the rest alphabetically. templates/default_templates.py:58-59 resolves the folder as three levels above the Python package, so in Docker it is /app/templates (Dockerfile:131).

docs.title: Step 6: electron/, the desktop wrapper
docs.text:
• app/main.ts (547 lines) is the main process: finds two free ports, generates a per-launch desktop token, starts FastAPI and Next.js, and opens the window.
  • app/utils/servers.ts spawns the servers; in development it runs uv run python server.py --port <n> --reload true and npm run dev -- -H 127.0.0.1 -p <n> (electron/app/utils/servers.ts:137-139, servers.ts:207-211).
  • app/utils/desktop-auth.ts holds the desktop credential.
  • app/ipc/export_handlers.ts handles exports over IPC.
  • app/preloads/ holds the preload scripts.
  • resources/document-extraction/liteparse_runner.mjs is the LiteParse runner shared with Docker (Dockerfile:65).
  • scripts/ holds build helpers: sync-export-runtime.cjs, prepare-export-chromium.cjs, build-nextjs-resources.cjs, copy-templates.cjs and others.
  • build.js is the electron-builder driver.
  • version.json is the release message and download links.
  • package.json pins Electron 42.11.16 and electron-builder 26.15.0 and defines setup:env, dev, build:all and dist.

See Electron desktop app.

docs.title: Step 7: scripts/, shared Node helpers
docs.text: File Purpose sync-presentation-export.cjs Downloads presenton-export-core-opensource-<version>.tgz from the presenton/presenton-export GitHub releases and installs it into presentation-export/ (scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs:32-33, scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs:170-172). Flags: --force, --check-only, --allow-version-override. run-presentation-export.mjs Copied to presentation-export/runner.mjs. Reads a task JSON, calls runTask from @presenton/export-core, fixes permissions, writes <task>.response.json. export-permissions.cjs finalizeExportPermissions: gives export artifacts the nginx group and strips world access. sync-document-dependencies.cjs Installs and fingerprints the LiteParse runtime in document-extraction-liteparse/. user-config-env.cjs buildUserConfigFromEnv, used by start.js to write userConfig.json. presenton-terminal-banner.mjs, presenton-ascii.txt The startup banner. run-node-script.mjs fork wrapper used by start.js. convert-template.mjs, convert-presentation-template.mjs Convert template or presentation JSON into the packaged template format. rebuild_notice_all.py Regenerates NOTICE. *.test.mjs, glob-security-checks.cjs Tests run by root npm test.

docs.title: Step 8: docs/ and .github/workflows/
docs.text:
docs/ contains presentation-generation-modes.md, template-v2.md, amazon-bedrock.md, multi-docker-build.md (manual multi-architecture image release), presenton-resource-usage.md (a k6 load-test report of the five-call Standard workflow) and macos/dev/* (signing and notarization guides).

.github/workflows/ contains:

  • test-all.yml: three jobs, test-repository-tools, test-fastapi and test-nextjs, on push and pull request to main.
  • codeql.yml: CodeQL for Python, JavaScript/TypeScript and Actions.
  • export-runtime-regressions.yml: repository tools on a matrix of operating systems.
  • docker-release.yml: multi-architecture image on release.
  • electron-linux-ubuntu22.yml: test release build.
  • sync-releaes-to-r2.yml: uploads release assets to R2. The misspelling is in the file name.
  • docs-pages.yml: publishes this tutorial. It is not part of upstream Presenton.

.github/workflows/README.md documents how to run each group locally. See CI, tests, security.
