docs.text: Continue with Document ingestion to see how uploaded files become the Context: section of the outline prompt.

docs.title: Document ingestion
docs.text:
Reads: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/files.py, servers/fastapi/services/temp_file_service.py, servers/fastapi/services/documents_loader.py, servers/fastapi/services/liteparse_service.py, electron/resources/document-extraction/liteparse_runner.mjs, servers/fastapi/services/office_document_service.py, servers/fastapi/services/document_conversion_service.py, servers/fastapi/utils/ocr_language.py, servers/fastapi/services/score_based_chunker.py, scripts/sync-document-dependencies.cjs · Builds on: Streaming (SSE) · Time: ~40 min

This chapter follows an uploaded file from the browser's FormData to the Context: line of the outline prompt. You will see the three file endpoints and their limits, the per-owner temp directory that holds every upload, how DocumentsLoader dispatches each extension to a backend (pure-Python OOXML/ODF readers, Pillow image normalization, and the Node-based LiteParse runner with Tesseract OCR), how the extracted text is cleaned, and how it is concatenated into additional_context. It closes with the score-based chunker (and the fact that nothing calls it), and the supply-chain checks that pin the parser's Node dependencies.

docs.title: The big picture
docs.text:
Document ingestion in the web UI is a two-request dance that happens before the presentation row even exists. The upload page first sends the raw files, then asks the server to "decompose" them into plain .txt files, and only then calls /presentation/create with the paths of those .txt files. When the outline stream later runs, it reads the .txt files back and pastes their content into the prompt.

sequenceDiagram
    participant UI as UploadPage.tsx
    participant API as FastAPI /api/v1/ppt
    participant TFS as TempFileService
    participant DL as DocumentsLoader
    participant LP as liteparse_runner.mjs
    UI->>API: POST /files/upload (multipart files)
    API->>TFS: create_temp_dir(uuid4)
    API->>TFS: create_temp_file_path(name, dir) per file
    API-->>UI: ["/tmp/presenton/.../report.pdf", ...]
    UI->>API: POST /files/decompose {file_paths, language}
    API->>DL: DocumentsLoader(other_files, language).load_documents(temp_dir)
    DL->>LP: node runner --file ... --ocr-language ... (PDF, images)
    LP-->>DL: plain text on stdout
    DL-->>API: documents (list of str)
    API->>TFS: write <uuid>.txt per document
    API-->>UI: [{name, file_path}, ...]
    UI->>API: POST /presentation/create {file_paths: txt paths, ...}
    UI->>API: GET /outlines/stream/{id}
    API->>DL: DocumentsLoader(txt paths).load_documents(temp_dir)
    DL-->>API: text of each .txt
    API->>API: additional_context = "\n\n".join(documents)

The browser side lives in servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/upload/components/UploadPage.tsx:444-530 (handleDocumentProcessing) and the two API helpers uploadDoc and decomposeDocuments in servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/presentation-generation.ts:32-80.

docs.title: 1.1 The router and its three endpoints
docs.text:
FILES_ROUTER = APIRouter(prefix="/files", tags=["Files"]) (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/files.py:16) is mounted under API_V1_PPT_ROUTER = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1/ppt") (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/router.py:22-24). The full set of file routes is:

Method and path Handler Body Response POST /api/v1/ppt/files/upload upload_files (files.py:79-100) multipart, field files (repeatable) List[str] of absolute temp paths POST /api/v1/ppt/files/mcp-upload upload_files_for_mcp (files.py:103-130) JSON {"files": [{"filename", "content_base64"}]} {"file_paths": [...]} POST /api/v1/ppt/files/decompose decompose_files (files.py:133-173) JSON {"file_paths": [...], "language": "..."} List[DecomposedFileInfo] POST /api/v1/ppt/files/update update_files (files.py:176-184) multipart file_path + file {"message": "File updated successfully"}

docs.title: 1.2 What the browser sends
docs.text:
uploadDoc appends every File object under the same key files and posts it with getHeaderForFormData() (presentation-generation.ts:32-55):

servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/presentation-generation.ts (excerpt)
  static async uploadDoc(documents: File[]) {
    const formData = new FormData();

    documents.forEach((document) => {
      formData.append("files", document);
    });

    try {
      const response = await fetch(
        getApiUrl(`/api/v1/ppt/files/upload`),
        {
          method: "POST",
          headers: getHeaderForFormData(),
          body: formData,
          cache: "no-cache",
        }
      );

docs.title: 1.3 What the server does
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/files.py (excerpt)
@FILES_ROUTER.post("/upload", response_model=List[str])
async def upload_files(files: Optional[List[UploadFile]]):
    if not files:
        raise HTTPException(400, "Documents are required")

    temp_dir = TEMP_FILE_SERVICE.create_temp_dir(str(uuid.uuid4()))

    validate_files(files, True, True, 100, UPLOAD_ACCEPTED_FILE_TYPES)

    temp_files: List[str] = []
    if files:
        for each_file in files:
            temp_path = TEMP_FILE_SERVICE.create_temp_file_path(
                each_file.filename, temp_dir
            )
            with open(temp_path, "wb") as f:
                content = await each_file.read()
                f.write(content)

            temp_files.append(temp_path)

    return temp_files

In order:

  1. An empty list is rejected with 400 "Documents are required" (files.py:81-82).
  2. A fresh directory named by a UUID4 is created inside the owner's temp root (files.py:84, Step 2 explains the root).
  3. validate_files(files, nullable=True, multiple=True, max_size=100, accepted_types=UPLOAD_ACCEPTED_FILE_TYPES) (files.py:86) checks every file (servers/fastapi/utils/validators.py:23-48): if max_size * 1024 * 1024 < file.size it raises 400 "File '<name>' exceeded max upload size of 100 MB", otherwise if the type is not accepted it raises 400 "File '<name>' not accepted. Accepted types: [...]".
  4. Each file is written whole (await each_file.read()) to create_temp_file_path(each_file.filename, temp_dir) and the absolute path is appended to the response.

A typical response:

[
  "/tmp/presenton/3f0c9a3e-5f3c-4c1b-9c9a-6f1f2a0b7d11/quarterly-report.pdf",
  "/tmp/presenton/3f0c9a3e-5f3c-4c1b-9c9a-6f1f2a0b7d11/notes.txt"
]

When authentication is enabled and an owner is bound to the request, an extra <owner_id>/ segment appears after the base directory (Step 2).

docs.title: 1.4 Accepted types
docs.text:
UPLOAD_ACCEPTED_FILE_TYPES is the union of MIME types and extensions (servers/fastapi/constants/documents.py:65-80). The comment at documents.py:78-79 explains why both are kept: "some clients upload legacy office files with generic content-type values". _is_accepted_file_type (validators.py:8-20) accepts a file if its lower-cased content_type is in the MIME set, or else if its lower-cased suffix is in the extension set.

Family Extensions (constants/documents.py) MIME types PDF .pdf (line 1) application/pdf Text .txt (line 2) text/plain, text/markdown Word .doc .docx .docm .odt .rtf (line 4) application/msword, OOXML wordprocessing, macro-enabled, ODF text, application/rtf, text/rtf PowerPoint .ppt .pptx .pptm .odp (line 5) application/vnd.ms-powerpoint, OOXML presentation, macro-enabled, ODF presentation Spreadsheet .xls .xlsx .xlsm .ods .csv .tsv (line 6) Excel, OOXML sheet, macro-enabled, ODF sheet, text/csv, application/csv, text/tab-separated-values, text/tsv Image .jpg .jpeg .png .gif .bmp .tiff .tif .webp (lines 8-22) image/jpeg png gif bmp tiff webp

SVG_EXTENSIONS = [".svg"] is defined (documents.py:14) but is not part of IMAGE_EXTENSIONS nor of the accepted list, so SVG uploads are rejected.

Gotcha

The size limit is per file, not per request: validate_files loops over files and compares each file.size against 100 MB. There is no cap on the number of files in the multipart route. In front of FastAPI, the bundled nginx sets client_max_body_size 110M for location /api/v1/ (nginx.conf:45-46), so in the Docker image the whole multipart body is effectively capped at 110 MB.

Gotcha

create_temp_dir runs before validate_files (files.py:84-86). A rejected upload therefore leaves an empty UUID directory behind. It is harmless, but it means the temp root accumulates directories until the next restart (Step 2.4).

Gotcha

All files from one request share one directory and keep their sanitized basenames. Two files with the same name in one request (for example slides.pdf from two folders) map to the same path, the second overwrites the first, and the response lists the same path twice.

docs.title: 1.5 The MCP variant
docs.text:
MCP clients cannot send multipart bodies, so /files/mcp-upload accepts base64 (files.py:24-60). Limits are explicit:

Limit Value Source Combined decoded size MCP_FILES_UPLOAD_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 100 * 1024 * 1024 files.py:18 Combined base64 characters 4 * ((100 MiB + 2) // 3) + 4 * 32 files.py:19-21 Files per request 1 to 32 files.py:37-43 Filename length 1 to 255 files.py:25

_decode_mcp_file uses base64.b64decode(..., validate=True) and returns 400 "Invalid base64 content for '<name>'" on bad input, or 413 if one file alone exceeds 100 MiB (files.py:63-76). The handler accumulates a running total and raises 413 "Combined file upload exceeds 100 MiB" (files.py:111-120), then wraps each payload in a Starlette UploadFile(file=BytesIO(content), filename=..., size=len(content)) and calls the same upload_files function (files.py:122-130). That reuse means MCP uploads get the same validation and storage, with one difference: the UploadFile is built without headers, so its content_type is None and _is_accepted_file_type can only accept the file by its extension. A file named without a recognized suffix is rejected even if its bytes are a valid PDF. The MCP tool contract built around this endpoint is covered in REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP.

docs.title: Step 2: Where files live (TempFileService)
docs.text: Every path that ingestion touches goes through the singleton TEMP_FILE_SERVICE = TempFileService() (servers/fastapi/services/temp_file_service.py:191).

docs.title: 2.1 The base directory
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/services/temp_file_service.py (excerpt)
class TempFileService:

    def __init__(self):
        self.base_dir = get_temp_directory_env() or "/tmp/presenton"
        self.cleanup_base_dir()
        os.makedirs(self.base_dir, exist_ok=True)

get_temp_directory_env() returns os.getenv("TEMP_DIRECTORY") (servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:59-60). The Docker images set TEMP_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton (Dockerfile:83, Dockerfile.dev:11); Electron passes its own tempDir (electron/app/main.ts:372).

docs.title: 2.2 Per-owner subdirectories
docs.text: _owner_base_dir_realpath() (temp_file_service.py:21-33) reads get_current_owner_id() from a context variable (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/context.py:13-14). With no owner (auth disabled, or an internal call) the root is the base dir; otherwise it is <base>/<owner_id>, created on demand. Every other method resolves against that owner root, so one user cannot read or reference another user's uploads by path. How the owner gets bound to the request is in Auth and multi-user.

docs.title: 2.3 Path checks
docs.text:
Method What it guarantees Lines sanitize_upload_filename(name) Converts \ to /, keeps only os.path.basename, strips, rejects empty, . and .. with 400 "Invalid filename" temp_file_service.py:43-48 resolve_temp_path(path, must_exist) realpath(abspath(path)) must equal the owner root or start with root + os.sep; otherwise 400 "File path must stay within the temp directory"; 404 "File not found" if must_exist and missing temp_file_service.py:50-72 resolve_existing_temp_paths(paths) Applies resolve_temp_path(..., must_exist=True) to each path; empty input returns [] temp_file_service.py:74-79 create_dir_in_dir / create_temp_dir Directory name is sanitized (or a UUID4), realpath must stay inside the root temp_file_service.py:81-94 create_temp_file_path(name, dir) Sanitizes the name, checks both the directory and the final realpath temp_file_service.py:96-115

Because realpath resolves symlinks before the prefix check, a symlink inside the temp dir that points outside it is rejected. servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_temp_file_service_security.py covers the safe basename (line 17), paths outside the root (line 30), symlink escape (line 43), a symlinked parent of the managed dir (line 60), and the must-exist rule (line 80).

docs.title: 2.4 Lifetime
docs.text:
cleanup_base_dir() runs in the constructor (temp_file_service.py:15, 187-188), and the constructor runs when the module is first imported. Nothing else in the API calls cleanup_temp_dir (a repository-wide search finds only the definitions in temp_file_service.py:160-188). Uploaded files, decomposed .txt files and converted PNGs therefore stay on disk until the FastAPI process restarts, and are all deleted at that moment.

Gotcha

presentation.file_paths stores absolute temp paths in the database (servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py:50). If FastAPI restarts between /presentation/create and /outlines/stream/{id}, the startup cleanup deletes those files and the stream's DocumentsLoader constructor raises HTTPException(404, "File not found") from resolve_existing_temp_paths. Because the loader is built inside the stream generator (outlines.py:121-126), the browser does not get an HTTP 404: safe_sse_stream turns it into an SSE error frame with detail "File not found" (Streaming (SSE)). Uploads are not durable inputs; they are a short-lived working set.

docs.title: 2.5 /files/update
docs.text: update_files (files.py:176-184) validates one file with validate_files(file, False, False, 100, ...) and calls update_temp_file_from_upload(file_path, file) (temp_file_service.py:142-158), which overwrites an existing path inside the owner root. No component in servers/nextjs calls /files/update in this snapshot (a search for files/update under servers/nextjs returns nothing).

docs.title: Step 3: Decompose the uploads into text
3.1 The request
docs.text:
After the upload returns, handleDocumentProcessing immediately posts the paths plus the language selected in the UI (UploadPage.tsx:460-472, presentation-generation.ts:57-80):

{
  "file_paths": [
    "/tmp/presenton/3f0c9a3e-.../quarterly-report.pdf",
    "/tmp/presenton/3f0c9a3e-.../notes.txt"
  ],
  "language": "German (Deutsch)"
}

The upload page refuses to process documents while the language is Auto (UploadPage.tsx:384-388): "Please choose a language before processing uploaded documents." That is because the language drives the OCR model (Step 6).

docs.title: 3.2 The handler
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/files.py (excerpt)
    temp_dir = TEMP_FILE_SERVICE.create_temp_dir(str(uuid.uuid4()))
    resolved_file_paths = TEMP_FILE_SERVICE.resolve_existing_temp_paths(file_paths)

    txt_files = []
    other_files = []
    for file_path in resolved_file_paths:
        if file_path.endswith(".txt"):
            txt_files.append(file_path)
        else:
            other_files.append(file_path)

    documents_loader = DocumentsLoader(file_paths=other_files, presentation_language=language)
    await documents_loader.load_documents(temp_dir)
    parsed_documents = documents_loader.documents

    response = []
    for index, parsed_doc in enumerate(parsed_documents):
        file_path = TEMP_FILE_SERVICE.create_temp_file_path(
            f"{uuid.uuid4()}.txt", temp_dir
        )
        parsed_doc = parsed_doc.replace("<br>", "\n")
        with open(file_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as text_file:
            text_file.write(parsed_doc)

Step by step (files.py:133-173):

  1. A new UUID temp directory is created for the outputs (files.py:138).
  2. Every input path is resolved and must exist inside the owner root (files.py:139).
  3. Paths ending in lowercase .txt are passed through untouched; everything else goes to DocumentsLoader (files.py:141-151).
  4. Each extracted document has <br> replaced with newlines and is written as UTF-8 to <temp_dir>/<uuid4>.txt (files.py:153-160).
  5. The response pairs the original basename with the new .txt path, using models/decomposed_file_info.py:4-6 (name: str, file_path: str). Pass-through .txt files are appended at the end with their original path (files.py:167-171).
[
  {"name": "quarterly-report.pdf", "file_path": "/tmp/presenton/9b1e.../5d2c7f0e-....txt"},
  {"name": "notes.txt", "file_path": "/tmp/presenton/3f0c9a3e-.../notes.txt"}
]

Gotcha

The response is not in upload order: parsed documents come first, .txt files last. Code that zips the response with the original upload list by index will mismatch names. Use the name field.

Gotcha

The .txt split uses a case-sensitive endswith(".txt"). NOTES.TXT goes through DocumentsLoader, where the suffix is lower-cased and it is read as text anyway, then rewritten to a new UUID file. The result is the same text, just copied.

docs.title: 3.3 From decompose to create
docs.text: getDocumentPaths (UploadPage.tsx:131-144) flattens the responses and keeps every file_path string. Those .txt paths, not the original uploads, become file_paths in POST /presentation/create (UploadPage.tsx:486-503). create_presentation runs them through resolve_existing_temp_paths again and stores them on the row (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1737-1751). The rest of create is covered in Standard generation pipeline.

docs.title: Step 4: The DocumentsLoader dispatcher
docs.text:
DocumentsLoader (servers/fastapi/services/documents_loader.py:163-357) is the single entry point for text extraction. Its constructor does four things (documents_loader.py:166-182):

  • re-validates every path with TEMP_FILE_SERVICE.resolve_existing_temp_paths (so a caller can never smuggle in a path outside the owner root);
  • maps the presentation language to an OCR code with presentation_language_to_ocr_code (Step 6);
  • builds a LiteParseService(timeout_seconds=DECOMPOSE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) with DECOMPOSE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 600 (documents_loader.py:164);
  • builds a DocumentConversionService and an optional fallback DocumentServiceCls.

The fallback is imported in a try block from services.lightweight_document_service (documents_loader.py:31-35). That module does not exist in this snapshot, so DocumentServiceCls is None and the fallback branch in _parse_with_liteparse never runs.

docs.title: 4.1 Extension routing
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/services/documents_loader.py (excerpt)
            if extension in PDF_EXTENSIONS:
                document, imgs = await self.load_pdf(
                    file_path, load_text, load_images, temp_dir
                )
            elif extension in TEXT_EXTENSIONS:
                document = await self.load_text(file_path)
            elif extension in OFFICE_EXTENSIONS:
                document = await asyncio.to_thread(
                    self.load_office_document,
                    file_path,
                )
            elif extension in IMAGE_EXTENSIONS:
                document = await asyncio.to_thread(
                    self.load_image,
                    file_path,
                    temp_dir,
                )
            else:
                document = await asyncio.to_thread(self._parse_with_liteparse, file_path)

            document = clean_extracted_document_text(document)
            documents.append(document)
            images.append(imgs)

flowchart TD
    A["load_documents(temp_dir)"] --> B{"suffix.lower()"}
    B -->|".pdf"| C["load_pdf"]
    C --> C1["_is_scanned_pdf via pdfplumber"]
    C1 -->|"under 50 chars in first 5 pages"| C2["LiteParse dpi=300"]
    C1 -->|"has text"| C3["LiteParse dpi=LITEPARSE_DPI (120)"]
    B -->|".txt"| D["load_text: read UTF-8"]
    B -->|"Word, PowerPoint, Spreadsheet"| E["extract_office_document_text (zipfile + XML)"]
    E -->|".doc .ppt .xls .rtf"| E1["OfficeDocumentError then HTTP 400"]
    B -->|"jpg png gif bmp tiff webp"| F["convert_image_to_png (Pillow)"]
    F --> F1["LiteParse dpi=300"]
    B -->|"anything else"| G["LiteParse default dpi"]
    C2 --> H["clean_extracted_document_text"]
    C3 --> H
    D --> H
    E --> H
    F1 --> H
    G --> H
    H --> I["append to documents, then self._documents = documents"]

Files are processed sequentially in a for loop (documents_loader.py:203-241); blocking work is pushed to threads with asyncio.to_thread, so the event loop stays responsive but there is no parallelism across files. A missing file raises 404 "File <path> not found" (documents_loader.py:204-207).

Gotcha

text/markdown is an accepted MIME type, but .md is not in any extension list. A Markdown upload therefore passes validation (by MIME) and lands in the else branch, which sends it to LiteParse. Whether LiteParse handles .md is not verified here; if it does not, the user sees a 500. Rename to .txt to get the direct UTF-8 path.

docs.title: 4.2 Text files
docs.text: load_text opens the file with encoding="utf-8" and reads it in a thread (documents_loader.py:284-286). There is no errors= argument, so a .txt that is not valid UTF-8 (for example Latin-1 with accented characters) raises UnicodeDecodeError. Where that surfaces depends on the path. In the web UI flow, /files/decompose passes uploaded .txt files through without reading them, so the error appears later, inside the outline stream, as an SSE error frame with the generic "Failed to generate presentation outlines. Please try again." (Streaming (SSE)). In the one-shot API, which parses request.files inside the request, it is a plain 500. Note the asymmetry with .csv and .tsv, which the office reader opens with errors="replace".

docs.title: 5.1 Scanned PDF detection (pdfplumber)
docs.text:
pdfplumber is used for two things only: detecting scanned PDFs and rendering page images. _is_scanned_pdf (documents_loader.py:271-282) opens the PDF, sums len(page.extract_text().strip()) over the first sample_pages=5 pages, and returns True when the total is below threshold=50. Any exception returns False (treat as a normal PDF). load_pdf (documents_loader.py:246-269) then calls LiteParse with dpi=300 for scanned files and dpi=None (meaning "use the service default") otherwise.

get_page_images_from_pdf renders every page at resolution=150 to page_<n>.png (documents_loader.py:342-351), but only when load_images=True, and no production caller passes that flag. Tests in servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_documents_loader.py:129-165 pin the scanned-detection behavior, including the threshold edge case and the "corrupt PDF is not scanned" rule.

docs.title: 5.2 Images (Pillow)
docs.text:
load_image (documents_loader.py:295-310) first normalizes the image with DocumentConversionService.convert_image_to_png and then OCRs the PNG with LiteParse at dpi=300. If a temp_dir was given, the PNG goes there; otherwise into a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="image-convert-") that is deleted afterwards.

servers/fastapi/services/document_conversion_service.py (excerpt)
            with Image.open(file_path) as image:
                image.seek(0)
                converted = ImageOps.exif_transpose(image)

                if converted.mode in ("RGBA", "LA") or (
                    converted.mode == "P" and "transparency" in converted.info
                ):
                    rgba = converted.convert("RGBA")
                    background = Image.new("RGB", rgba.size, (255, 255, 255))
                    background.paste(rgba, mask=rgba.getchannel("A"))
                    converted = background
                elif converted.mode != "RGB":
                    converted = converted.convert("RGB")

                converted.save(output_path, format="PNG")

The conversion takes the first frame (seek(0), so only the first frame of a GIF or multi-page TIFF), applies EXIF orientation, flattens transparency onto white, and forces RGB (servers/fastapi/services/document_conversion_service.py:39-89). Output names avoid collisions: <stem>.png, or <stem>-converted.png if that would overwrite the input, or <stem>-1.png, <stem>-2.png and so on (document_conversion_service.py:18-37). Pillow OSError and UnidentifiedImageError become DocumentConversionError. The timeout_seconds argument is accepted and immediately discarded (del timeout_seconds, line 45).

Gotcha

load_image calls convert_image_to_png directly, outside _parse_with_liteparse (documents_loader.py:295-310). So although _parse_with_liteparse lists DocumentConversionError among the exceptions it maps to a friendly HTTPException(500, "Failed to parse document ..."), a corrupt or unreadable image never reaches that handler: the DocumentConversionError escapes load_documents and /files/decompose answers with FastAPI's generic 500 "Internal Server Error".

docs.title: 5.3 Office documents: no external converter
docs.text:
The scope question "which external tools convert office files?" has a short answer in this snapshot: none. extract_office_document_text (servers/fastapi/services/office_document_service.py:144-171) is pure Python on top of zipfile and xml.etree.ElementTree:

Extension Reader What it extracts Lines .csv .tsv open(..., errors="replace") The raw file office_document_service.py:146-148 .docx .docm _extract_docx word/document.xml, every <w:p>, its <w:t> nodes joined by spaces, paragraphs joined by \n 47-56 .pptx .pptm _extract_pptx ppt/slides/slideN.xml in natural numeric order, all <a:t> text per slide, slides joined by blank lines 59-69 .xlsx .xlsm _extract_xlsx xl/worksheets/sheetN.xml rows as tab-separated values, resolving shared strings and inline strings 83-131 .odt .odp .ods _extract_odf content.xml, every p and h element's text 134-141 .doc .ppt .xls .rtf none Raises OfficeDocumentError 150-154

_natural_key (office_document_service.py:20-24) splits names on digit runs so slide10.xml sorts after slide9.xml; servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_office_document_service.py:17 tests exactly that. Tag matching uses _local_name (strip the {namespace} prefix, line 27-28), so any element whose local name is t counts as text regardless of namespace.

DocumentsLoader.load_office_document turns OfficeDocumentError into HTTPException(400, detail=str(exc)) (documents_loader.py:288-293).

Gotcha

Legacy binary formats (.doc, .ppt, .xls) and .rtf pass the upload validation (constants/documents.py:4-6) and then fail at decompose with 400 and the message ".doc files require an external office conversion engine; save the document in a modern OOXML or OpenDocument format first" (office_document_service.py:150-154). The upload succeeds, only the second request fails. test_rejects_legacy_binary_office_formats (servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_office_document_service.py:48) asserts this.

Gotcha

Office extraction is text-only. Speaker notes (ppt/notesSlides/), charts, embedded images, headers and footers are not read, and spreadsheet formulas yield their cached <v> value, not the formula. Numbers are kept as raw strings, so dates in XLSX appear as serial numbers. Empty cells are skipped rather than emitted as empty fields (office_document_service.py:125-128), so columns shift left in sparse rows. In .docx, each <w:t> run is stripped and runs are joined with spaces (office_document_service.py:38-56), so a word that Word split across two formatting runs comes out with a space inside it.

docs.title: Step 6: The LiteParse runner and OCR
6.1 Language to Tesseract code
docs.text: presentation_language_to_ocr_code (servers/fastapi/utils/ocr_language.py:113-126) maps the exact UI label (for example "German (Deutsch)") to an ISO 639-3 Tesseract code ("deu") using an 89-entry table (ocr_language.py:15-106) whose keys must match the LanguageType values in the upload UI (comment at ocr_language.py:5-7). Lookup order: None or blank returns "eng"; exact key; case-insensitive key; unknown returns "eng". A final regex guard ^[a-zA-Z0-9_,+]+$ (ocr_language.py:110) ensures that nothing odd reaches the command line. Two notable entries: Chinese maps to chi_sim / chi_tra, and Tahitian deliberately maps to eng because there is "No dedicated Tahitian traineddata in default Tesseract bundles" (ocr_language.py:103-104). servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_small_surfaces_coverage.py:405-425 covers resolution and the bad-language fallback.

docs.title: 6.2 LiteParseService configuration
docs.text:
LiteParseService.__init__ (servers/fastapi/services/liteparse_service.py:67-80) reads its configuration from the environment:

Variable Default Clamp / meaning Source LITEPARSE_NODE_BINARY node Node executable; Electron sets it to its own process.execPath with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 (electron/app/main.ts:378-382) liteparse_service.py:70 LITEPARSE_DPI 120 (_DEFAULT_DPI) int clamped to 72..600 liteparse_service.py:21, 71 LITEPARSE_NUM_WORKERS max(os.cpu_count() - 2, 1) int clamped to 1..64; docker-compose sets ${LITEPARSE_NUM_WORKERS:-1} (docker-compose.yml:119) liteparse_service.py:22, 72-77 LITEPARSE_RUNNER_PATH first existing candidate from _resolve_runner_path path to liteparse_runner.mjs liteparse_service.py:78, 144-195 LITEPARSE_RUNNER_OUTPUT empty (plain) json selects the legacy one-JSON-line bridge liteparse_service.py:244-247 LITEPARSE_OCR_SERVER_URL unset passed as --ocr-server-url (HTTP OCR instead of local Tesseract) liteparse_service.py:291-293 LITEPARSE_TESSDATA_PATH unset passed as --tessdata-path liteparse_service.py:294-296 IMAGEMAGICK_BINARY, MAGICK_HOME unset their directories are prepended to the child PATH liteparse_service.py:82-120

_env_int (liteparse_service.py:48-64) logs a warning and falls back to the default for non-integers, and clamps out-of-range values; servers/fastapi/tests/test_liteparse_service.py:17-117 checks the defaults (--dpi 120, --python-bridge plain), env overrides, clamping, and the JSON bridge switch.

The runner is searched in this order (liteparse_service.py:148-191): /app/document-extraction-liteparse/liteparse_runner.mjs (the Docker runtime copy), <cwd>/../../resources/document-extraction/, a path relative to the service file, a PyInstaller layout <cwd>/../../app/resources/..., and finally <cwd>/../../electron/resources/document-extraction/. The npm project root, the directory whose node_modules/@llamaindex/liteparse exists, is found the same way (liteparse_service.py:122-142).

docs.title: 6.3 Readiness check on every parse
docs.text:
parse() begins with check_runtime_ready() (liteparse_service.py:197-242, 271-273), which:

  1. checks the runner file exists;
  2. runs node --version (10 s timeout);
  3. checks node_modules/@llamaindex/liteparse exists under the project root;
  4. runs node --input-type=module -e "import '@llamaindex/liteparse'" (20 s timeout), because the package "is ESM-only; require.resolve() fails" (comment at line 223).

Any failure raises LiteParseError(reason).

Gotcha

The readiness check is not cached: every PDF or image spawns two extra Node processes before the real parse. On a slow disk or under Electron, that is noticeable per file. If you profile ingestion, this is the first easy win.

docs.title: 6.4 The command line
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/services/liteparse_service.py (excerpt)
        command = [
            self.node_binary,
            self.runner_path,
            "--file",
            file_path,
            "--ocr-enabled",
            "true" if ocr_enabled else "false",
            "--ocr-language",
            ocr_language,
            "--dpi",
            str(effective_dpi),
            "--num-workers",
            str(self.num_workers),
        ]

DocumentsLoader._parse_with_liteparse always passes ocr_enabled=True and the mapped language (documents_loader.py:312-320). The command is a list (no shell), so file names with spaces or quotes are safe. Then --ocr-server-url, --tessdata-path and --python-bridge plain|json are appended (liteparse_service.py:291-299).

docs.title: 6.5 Inside liteparse_runner.mjs
docs.text:
The runner (electron/resources/document-extraction/liteparse_runner.mjs) is a small CLI around new LiteParse(config).parse(resolvedPath, true) from @llamaindex/liteparse (line 13, 125-126):

  • --file is required and must exist, otherwise exit code 2 (liteparse_runner.mjs:68-76).
  • --ocr-enabled accepts 1/true/yes/on and 0/false/no/off, default true (lines 21-27, 78).
  • --dpi defaults to 150 inside the runner and is clamped 72..600; --num-workers defaults to cpus - 2 clamped 1..64 (lines 79-85). Python always passes both, so the runner defaults only apply to manual runs.
  • The OCR language is LITEPARSE_OCR_LANGUAGE env first, then --ocr-language, then eng; commas become + (so deu,eng becomes deu+eng) (lines 36-45, 87-92).
  • --ocr-server-url falls back to LITEPARSE_OCR_SERVER_URL; --tessdata-path falls back to LITEPARSE_TESSDATA_PATH then TESSDATA_PREFIX (lines 97-108).
  • Plain bridge: writes the raw result.text to stdout and exits 0; on error writes the stack and message to stderr and exits 1 (lines 129-132, 150-156).
  • JSON bridge: one line {"ok": true, "filePath", "text", "pageCount", "ocr": {"engine": "tesseract" | "http", ...}}, or {"ok": false, "filePath", "error"} with exit 1 (lines 134-146, 160-167).

Gotcha

LITEPARSE_OCR_LANGUAGE in the environment overrides the language that Python computed from the UI (liteparse_runner.mjs:88-91). If you set it globally (for example to eng), choosing German in the UI has no OCR effect.

Gotcha

The production Dockerfile installs only tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng, and only when INSTALL_TESSERACT=true (the default, Dockerfile:77, 105). The language mapping can ask for deu, jpn and so on, but whether that traineddata is available depends on how LiteParse resolves Tesseract data (local data, LITEPARSE_TESSDATA_PATH, or an OCR server). That resolution happens inside @llamaindex/liteparse and is not verified in this chapter.

docs.title: 6.6 Running the process and reading output
docs.text:
In the default plain mode, _run_plain_bridge_to_text (liteparse_service.py:413-463) streams stdout into a NamedTemporaryFile(prefix="liteparse-stdout-") instead of a pipe, so large PDFs do not have to fit in a pipe buffer, and drains stderr in a daemon thread into a BoundedTextBuffer that keeps only the last 8192 characters (servers/fastapi/utils/runtime_limits.py:39-60). It waits up to timeout_seconds (600 from DocumentsLoader); on timeout it kills the child and raises LiteParseError("LiteParse timed out after 600 seconds"). The stdout file is read back with errors="replace" and always unlinked. A non-zero exit becomes LiteParseError carrying the return code and 600-character snippets of stderr and stdout (liteparse_service.py:345-351). Success returns {"ok": True, "text": stdout.lstrip("\ufeff"), "filePath": ..., "pageCount": 0}.

In JSON mode, subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, timeout=...) is used and _decode_runner_output takes the last stdout line that parses as a JSON object, tolerating stray log lines (liteparse_service.py:387-411).

Gotcha

In JSON mode the timeout surfaces as subprocess.TimeoutExpired, which is not one of the exceptions _parse_with_liteparse catches (LiteParseError, DocumentConversionError, OfficeDocumentError, documents_loader.py:321). It escapes as an unhandled 500 rather than the friendly "Failed to parse document" message. The default plain mode converts timeouts into LiteParseError and does not have this problem.

docs.title: 6.7 Failure mapping
docs.text: _parse_with_liteparse logs the failure, tries the (absent) fallback parser, and raises HTTPException(500, "Failed to parse document <basename>: <error>") (documents_loader.py:321-340). Because files are processed in one loop, one bad file fails the whole decompose request; there is no partial result.

docs.title: Step 7: Cleaning the extracted text
docs.text:
Every document, whatever its backend, goes through clean_extracted_document_text (documents_loader.py:146-160, called at line 239). It exists because older runner versions, or the JSON bridge, could leave the whole JSON line in the stored text. The function runs up to 4 passes of _clean_extracted_one_pass, which:

  1. Up to 3 times, calls _unwrap_liteparse_json_line_if_stored (documents_loader.py:40-59): if the text (left-stripped) parses as a JSON object with ok is True, a filePath key and a string text, return just text.
  2. If the text still starts with {, calls _try_extract_liteparse_text_value_from_malformed_json (documents_loader.py:116-129): it only proceeds if the first 10,000 characters contain both ok and filePath, finds the first "text": " with the regex "text"\s*:\s*" and decodes the JSON string by hand with _json_unescape_quoted_value (documents_loader.py:65-113), which handles \" \\ \/ \b \f \n \r \t \uXXXX and returns what it has if the closing quote is missing (truncated output).

The passes stop as soon as a pass changes nothing. Ordinary document text that does not start with { is returned unchanged. Tests: servers/fastapi/tests/test_documents_loader_unwrap.py:9-50 and servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_documents_loader.py:18-40, including nested payloads and truncated JSON.

Gotcha

A real document whose text starts with a JSON object containing "ok": true, "filePath" and "text" would be unwrapped too. This is unlikely, but if you ingest JSON exports of LiteParse results, expect them to be reduced to their text field.

docs.title: 8.1 Standard outline stream
docs.text:
When the outline stream starts (GET /api/v1/ppt/outlines/stream/{id}, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/outlines.py:84), it creates a temp dir (line 110) and, if the row has file_paths, loads them again:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/outlines.py (excerpt)
        additional_context = ""
        if presentation.file_paths:
            documents_loader = DocumentsLoader(
                file_paths=presentation.file_paths,
                presentation_language=presentation.language,
            )
            await documents_loader.load_documents(temp_dir)
            documents = documents_loader.documents
            if documents:
                additional_context = "\n\n".join(documents)

In the web UI flow these paths are the decomposed .txt files, so this second load is just load_text per file: the expensive parsing happened once, in decompose. The concatenation is a plain "\n\n".join(...) with no headers and no file names, so the LLM sees one undifferentiated block (outlines.py:120-129).

additional_context is then passed to get_outline_messages (for memory capture, outlines.py:142-168, stored as extracted_document_text) and to generate_ppt_outline (outlines.py:170-183). Inside, if external web search is active, search results are appended to the same string with another "\n\n" (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_outlines.py:350-353). The final user prompt ends with:

servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_outlines.py (excerpt)
        f"Today's Date: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}\n"
        f"Content: {content or ''}\n"
        "Instructions (apply as constraints; never quote as slide content): "
        f"{instructions or ''}\n"
        f"Context: {additional_context or 'None'}\n"

(generate_presentation_outlines.py:210-214). The system prompt tells the model to "Generate flow based on user content and use context just for reference" (generate_presentation_outlines.py:129), and the user prompt says conflicting language or slide-count requests inside Context are ignored (line 209). These rules are discussed in Prompts and schemas.

Gotcha

The Standard path never truncates additional_context. A 300-page PDF becomes one enormous Context: line, and the request can exceed the model's context window, failing at the provider. Smart mode, by contrast, caps its source context at 90,000 characters (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2023-2025). If you add a limit to Standard mode, do it in outlines.py right after the join so both memory capture and generation see the same text.

docs.title: 8.2 Other callers of DocumentsLoader
docs.text:
Caller How it loads Lines One-shot POST /presentation/generate (sync and async) DocumentsLoader(file_paths=request.files, presentation_language=request.language).load_documents() with no temp dir, skipped entirely when slides_markdown is given presentation.py:2732-2740 Smart mode stream Emits status "Reading source documents", joins non-empty documents with web search context, truncates to 90,000 chars presentation.py:2000-2025 v2 Smart API Passes request.files to create_presentation as file_paths servers/fastapi/api/v2/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:66-80 Chat attachments Loads attachments into a fresh temp dir for the chat context servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:599-604 Chat memory layer Loads presentation files one at a time servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:576-599

For API callers, the files in request.files are usually the raw uploads (from /files/upload or /files/mcp-upload), not decomposed .txt files, so the full parse happens inside the generation request. See REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP, Smart mode and Editing and chat assistant.

When Presenton Cloud proxying is active, /api/v1/ppt/files/upload and /api/v1/ppt/files/decompose are part of CLOUD_GENERATION_PATHS (servers/fastapi/services/presenton_cloud_proxy.py:42-49) and are forwarded rather than handled locally; that mechanism is out of scope here.

docs.title: Step 9: The documents-preview page
docs.text:
The App Router still contains a /documents-preview route (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/documents-preview/page.tsx, component documents-preview/components/DocumentPreviewPage.tsx). It reads config and files (the decompose responses) from Redux, fetches each .txt through window.electron.readFile in Electron or POST /api/read-file in the browser (DocumentPreviewPage.tsx:95-105), renders the selected document, and offers a create button that calls createPresentation with the .txt paths and navigates to /outline (DocumentPreviewPage.tsx:141-191). /api/read-file requires an authenticated session and uses readReadableLocalFile with the user's id and admin flag (servers/nextjs/app/api/read-file/route.ts:8-33).

In this snapshot the upload page does not navigate there: handleDocumentProcessing calls create directly and pushes /outline?id=... (or the Smart presentation URL) (UploadPage.tsx:309-316, 527-529). The only other reference is the header's path list (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/dashboard/components/Header.tsx:13, 26). The full journey through the UI is in User journey.

docs.title: Step 10: The score-based chunker
docs.text: servers/fastapi/services/score_based_chunker.py implements a heading-based splitter that returns DocumentChunk objects (servers/fastapi/models/document_chunk.py:6-13: heading, content, heading_index, score, plus to_slide_outline() which builds a SlideOutlineModel with content=f"{heading}\n{content}"). Its intended use is clearly "one chunk per slide outline". In this snapshot, however, no module outside the file imports ScoreBasedChunker; a search for it across servers/fastapi matches only its own file. It is dormant code, documented here because the scope asks for it and because it is the obvious hook if you want per-slide grounding.

docs.title: 10.1 The algorithm
docs.text:
1. extract_headings(text) (score_based_chunker.py:9-18): every line that, after strip(), starts with # is a heading. That includes #hashtag lines and lines like #1 priority.
  2. score_headings(headings) (score_based_chunker.py:20-47), with level = number of leading #:
    • levels 1 to 3: 10 - (level - 1) * 2, so 10, 8, 6;
    • level 4 and deeper: 4 - (level - 4) * 0.5, so 4, 3.5, 3, and so on;
    • the first heading gets +5;
    • every later heading gets a "distance bonus" min(5.0, (i - last_heading_index) * 0.5). Since last_heading_index is updated on every iteration, the distance is always 1, so the bonus is always exactly 0.5.
  3. get_chunks_from_headings(text, headings, scores, top_k) (score_based_chunker.py:49-153):
    • keep headings with score > 0 (only absurdly deep runs of # reach a score of 0 or less, for example a non-first heading with 13 or more #, and are dropped);
    • if at most top_k remain, select all of them in document order;
    • otherwise group indices by round(score) and walk groups from the highest score down. A group that fits is taken whole. If it does not fit and 1 slot remains, take the middle index; if 2 remain, take the first and last; otherwise take remaining evenly spaced indices with step = (len - 1) / (remaining - 1). Selected indices are sorted back into document order;
    • map each heading to the first line number where the stripped line equals it (duplicate headings map to successive occurrences);
    • each chunk's content runs from the line after its heading to the line of the next selected heading (or the end of the text), stripped.
  4. get_n_chunks(text, n) (score_based_chunker.py:155-163) runs the three steps in threads and raises ValueError("Only X chunks found, requested n") if fewer than n chunks result.

docs.title: 10.2 Worked example
docs.text:
Input headings, in order: # Intro, ## Background, ## Method, ### Details, #### Note, with top_k = 3.

i Heading Base First Distance Score round(score) 0 # Intro 10 +5 0 15.0 15 1 ## Background 8 0 +0.5 8.5 8 2 ## Method 8 0 +0.5 8.5 8 3 ### Details 6 0 +0.5 6.5 6 4 #### Note 4 0 +0.5 4.5 4

Five candidates exceed top_k, so grouping kicks in: group 15 gives [0] (2 slots left), group 8 gives [1, 2], which fits exactly. Selected: [0, 1, 2]. The third chunk, ## Method, runs to the end of the text and therefore swallows ### Details and #### Note as content.

Gotcha

Python's round() uses banker's rounding: round(8.5) == 8 and round(6.5) == 6, but round(7.5) == 8. Grouping is therefore not "nearest integer, halves up". Combined with the constant 0.5 distance bonus, every non-first heading at levels 1 to 3, and at even levels from 4 on (4.5, 3.5, ...), lands on a .5 score, while odd levels from 5 on land on whole numbers (level 5 scores 4.0, the same group as level 4's 4.5). This rounding rule therefore decides which levels share a group. Keep that in mind before wiring the chunker into production.

Gotcha

The chunker only understands Markdown headings. Text from office_document_service.py and from the LiteParse plain bridge usually contains no # lines at all, in which case get_n_chunks raises ValueError for any n > 0.

docs.title: Step 11: Supply-chain and security checks for the parser
docs.text: The parser runs untrusted files through a Node dependency tree, so the repository pins and tests it.

docs.title: 11.1 Pinned dependencies
docs.text: The root package.json depends on @llamaindex/liteparse ^1.5.2 and sharp ^0.35.5, with overrides forcing LiteParse's own sharp and zod ^4.6.6 (package.json:16-25).

docs.title: 11.2 scripts/sync-document-dependencies.cjs
docs.text:
syncDocumentDependencies() (scripts/sync-document-dependencies.cjs:24-57) guarantees that the installed parser matches the reviewed lockfile:

  1. Compute a SHA-256 fingerprint over package-lock.json bytes, the manifest's dependencies and overrides, and platform:arch:node ABI (lines 35-37).
  2. Mirror package.json, package-lock.json and liteparse_runner.mjs into <root>/document-extraction-liteparse (lines 38-42), the same directory the Docker image uses at /app/document-extraction-liteparse.
  3. For the root and the runtime directory, skip work only if the marker node_modules/.presenton-document-lock.sha256 equals the fingerprint, the critical packages (@llamaindex/liteparse, sharp, zod, axios, form-data, follow-redirects, line 6) have exactly the lockfile versions, and await import('@llamaindex/liteparse'); await import('sharp'); succeeds (lines 9-22, 44-48).
  4. Otherwise delete the marker, run npm ci --include=optional --omit=dev --prefer-offline --no-fund --no-audit, re-verify, and throw "Document dependencies do not match the reviewed lockfile" if verification still fails; only then write the marker (lines 49-54).

start.js runs it at container start only in development mode: ensurePresentationExportNodeDependencies (start.js:225-227) is called inside if (isDev) in main (start.js:723-726). Dockerfile.dev:53-55 also runs it at build. The production Dockerfile installs the runtime directly with npm --prefix /app/document-extraction-liteparse ci --omit=dev (Dockerfile:61-65). Tests in scripts/sync-document-dependencies.test.mjs cover replacing an old volume and reusing the locked result (line 29), repairing a downgraded package even with a current marker (line 44), and making sure a failed install cannot leave a trusted marker (line 54).

docs.title: 11.3 scripts/document-parser-security.test.mjs
docs.text: This test resolves follow-redirects exactly as LiteParse would reach it (LiteParse, then its axios, then follow-redirects, lines 7-10), which is the HTTP stack used for an OCR server. It starts a source server on 127.0.0.1 that answers 302 to a destination on localhost (a different origin), sends a request with array-form headers containing Authorization: Bearer test-canary and Cookie: canary=test, and asserts that the source saw both headers and the destination saw neither (lines 12-53). In other words, a malicious or misconfigured OCR server cannot redirect Presenton into leaking credentials to another host. Both scripts run in the root npm test (package.json:8). CI wiring is covered in CI, tests, security.

docs.title: 11.4 Server-side safety summary
docs.text:
Risk Mitigation Where Path traversal in filenames basename-only sanitization, ./.. rejected temp_file_service.py:43-48 Reading other users' files by path per-owner root plus realpath prefix check on every path, re-checked in DocumentsLoader temp_file_service.py:21-79, documents_loader.py:171 Symlink escape os.path.realpath before the prefix check temp_file_service.py:55-67 Shell injection via file names subprocess argument lists, no shell liteparse_service.py:277-299 OCR language injection regex guard on the OCR code ocr_language.py:110, 124-125 Runaway parser 600 s timeout and kill, bounded stderr buffer liteparse_service.py:438-446, runtime_limits.py:39-60 Malformed XML in office files parse errors become OfficeDocumentError (400); no hardening beyond the standard-library ElementTree parser (defusedxml is not used) office_document_service.py:31-35 Credential leak via OCR redirects follow-redirects version pinned and tested scripts/document-parser-security.test.mjs

Gotcha

There is no per-request limit on decompressed size or page count. A small zip-bomb style .docx, or a PDF with thousands of pages, is bounded only by the 600-second timeout (for LiteParse) or by memory (for the pure-Python office readers, which call archive.read(member) into memory). If you expose Presenton publicly, put limits in front of /files/decompose.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• The web UI uploads raw files to /files/upload, decomposes them into UTF-8 .txt files with /files/decompose, and stores only the .txt paths on the presentation row; the outline stream rereads them.
  • Every path lives under TEMP_DIRECTORY (default /tmp/presenton), optionally under a per-owner subdirectory, is validated with realpath prefix checks, and is wiped when FastAPI restarts.
  • DocumentsLoader routes by extension: UTF-8 read for .txt, pure-Python zip/XML readers for modern office formats (legacy .doc/.ppt/.xls/.rtf are rejected), Pillow normalization plus LiteParse OCR at 300 dpi for images, and LiteParse for PDFs with a pdfplumber scanned-PDF check that raises the DPI from 120 to 300.
  • LiteParse is a Node subprocess (liteparse_runner.mjs) configured by LITEPARSE_* variables, with a 600-second timeout, the OCR language mapped from the UI label, and a cleaning pass that strips leftover JSON wrappers.
  • The extracted texts are joined with blank lines into additional_context, untruncated in Standard mode (90,000 characters in Smart mode), and appear as the Context: line of the outline prompt.
  • ScoreBasedChunker exists but is not wired in; the parser's Node dependencies are pinned by a fingerprinted sync script and a redirect-credential test.

docs.title: Images, icons, web search
docs.text:
Reads: servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py, servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/images.py, servers/fastapi/services/icon_finder_service.py, servers/fastapi/utils/web_search.py · Builds on: Standard generation pipeline, Configuration and LLM providers · Time: ~45 min

Presenton decorates every generated slide with two kinds of media: raster images (AI generated or pulled from a stock library) and vector icons (picked from the bundled Phosphor set by semantic search). Separately, it can ground the outline step in live web results. This chapter follows each of those three subsystems from the call site to the bytes on disk: how a provider is chosen, how a template's image box becomes an API size or aspect ratio, where files land and how their URLs are formed, what happens when a provider fails, how icons are embedded and searched, and exactly how web results are fetched, cleaned and fenced off as untrusted text inside the prompt.

docs.title: Step 1: Where asset requests come from
docs.text:
Neither images nor icons are requested by the LLM directly. The slide-content LLM call (see Prompts and schemas) fills schema fields that carry a prompt string, and a post-processing pass in servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py walks the resulting JSON looking for those fields.

Constant Value Defined at IMAGE_PROMPT_KEYS ("__image_prompt__", "image_prompt", "prompt") servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:22 ICON_QUERY_KEYS ("__icon_query__", "icon_query", "query") servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:23 TEMPLATE_ASSET_MARKER_KEYS ("image_url", "icon_url", "image_prompt", "icon_query") servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:24

_asset_dicts_with_prompt (servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:161) collects every dict that contains one of the prompt keys with a non-blank string value. The URL that is written back depends on the slide flavor: a Template v2 slide (one that has a ui dict or uses the template marker keys) gets image_url / icon_url, while legacy content gets __image_url__ / __icon_url__ (_asset_url_key, servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:110). For template slides the legacy key is popped so the two never coexist (servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:125).

A typical asset dict before and after processing looks like this:

BeforeAfter (Template v2 slide) 
{
  "image": { "image_prompt": "Wind turbines on a ridge at sunrise" },
  "icon": { "icon_query": "lightning bolt energy" }
}

{
  "image": {
    "image_prompt": "Wind turbines on a ridge at sunrise",
    "image_url": "/app_data/images/users/6f1c.../3a9e....png"
  },
  "icon": {
    "icon_query": "lightning bolt energy",
    "icon_url": "/static/icons/bold/lightning-bold.svg"
  }
}

The values shown in "After" are illustrative; the shapes of the URLs are derived in Steps 6 and 10.

docs.title: 1.1 The first-generation pass
docs.text:
process_slide_and_fetch_assets (servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:173) is used by both the streaming UI pipeline and the REST /generate handler. For each image prompt it does one of two things:

  1. If the slide's outline contained explicit image URLs (only http(s) URLs ending in .jpg, .jpeg, .png or .webp, optionally followed by a query string, matched by IMAGE_URL_PATTERN at servers/fastapi/utils/outline_utils.py:13), the Nth image slot takes the Nth outline URL and no provider is called (servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:195). The streaming UI pipeline always extracts outline URLs (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2335); the REST /generate handler does so only when the request used slides_markdown (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3035).
  2. Otherwise it schedules image_generation_service.generate_image(ImagePrompt(...)), passing the target width and height that were measured from the template layout (Step 4).

Every icon query is scheduled as ICON_FINDER_SERVICE.search_icons(query, weight=...). All tasks, images and icons alike, are awaited with one asyncio.gather:

servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py (excerpt)
    results = (
        await asyncio.gather(*async_tasks, return_exceptions=allow_image_fallback)
        if async_tasks
        else []
    )

    return_assets = []
    for (task_type, asset_path), result in zip(async_task_meta, results):
        if task_type == "image":
            image_dict = get_dict_at_path(slide.content, asset_path)
            if isinstance(result, BaseException):
                if not allow_image_fallback:
                    raise result
                _set_asset_url(
                    image_dict,
                    "image",
                    normalize_slide_asset_url("/static/images/placeholder.jpg"),
                    template=template,
                )
                if image_warnings is not None and isinstance(result, Exception):
                    image_warnings.append(image_generation_warning(result))
                set_dict_at_path(slide.content, asset_path, image_dict)
                continue

Both pipelines call it with allow_image_fallback=True (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2413 for the stream, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3050 for /generate), so one failed image never fails a deck. The function returns the list of ImageAsset rows it produced; the caller commits them (Step 6).

In the streaming path the slide is first given placeholders (process_slide_add_placeholder_assets, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2395) so the editor can render immediately, then the real URLs arrive in a slide_assets SSE event that also carries the per-slide warnings list (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2436). The SSE mechanics are in Streaming (SSE).

flowchart TD
    A["Slide content JSON with image_prompt and icon_query fields"] --> B["process_slide_and_fetch_assets"]
    B --> C{"Outline supplied an image URL for this slot?"}
    C -->|yes| D["Use outline URL as is"]
    C -->|no| E["ImageGenerationService.generate_image"]
    B --> F["ICON_FINDER_SERVICE.search_icons"]
    E --> G{"Result type"}
    G -->|stock URL| H["Write URL into slide"]
    G -->|file path| I["ImageAsset row plus /app_data/images URL"]
    G -->|exception| J["placeholder.jpg plus warning dict"]
    F --> K{"Any hit?"}
    K -->|yes| L["/static/icons/WEIGHT/NAME.svg"]
    K -->|no| M["/static/icons/placeholder.svg"]

docs.title: 2.1 The enum and the environment
docs.text:
The provider is a string in IMAGE_PROVIDER. The allowed values are the members of ImageProvider (servers/fastapi/enums/image_provider.py:4):

Enum member Value PEXELS pexels PIXABAY pixabay GEMINI_FLASH gemini_flash NANOBANANA_PRO nanobanana_pro GPT_IMAGE_2 gpt-image-2 GPT_IMAGE_1_5 gpt-image-1.5 COMFYUI comfyui OPEN_WEBUI open_webui OPENAI_COMPATIBLE openai_compatible

get_selected_image_provider (servers/fastapi/utils/image_provider.py:49) reads the variable, maps the removed legacy value dall-e-3 to GPT_IMAGE_2, and otherwise calls ImageProvider(value). A legacy deployment also keeps its quality: when GPT_IMAGE_2_QUALITY is unset, get_gpt_image_2_quality_env returns high if IMAGE_PROVIDER=dall-e-3 and DALL_E_3_QUALITY=hd, and medium for any other dall-e-3 setup (servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:406).

Settings saved in the UI are written to the user config file and copied into os.environ at the start of every request by UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:23), so the os.getenv calls in this chapter always see the latest saved values. How that file is managed is covered in Configuration and LLM providers.

Gotcha

An unknown IMAGE_PROVIDER string makes ImageProvider(value) raise ValueError. Because ImageGenerationService.__init__ resolves the provider function immediately (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:139), constructing the service fails, and with it the whole generation request. The only escape is DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION=true, which short-circuits before the provider is looked up (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:159). An unset or empty IMAGE_PROVIDER is fine: it yields None and every image becomes the placeholder.

docs.title: 2.2 The service constructor
2.3 The provider matrix
docs.text:
IMAGE_PROVIDER Method Remote call Required settings Size control Result pexels get_image_from_pexels GET https://api.pexels.com/v1/search PEXELS_API_KEY none remote URL from photos[].src.large pixabay get_image_from_pixabay GET https://pixabay.com/api/ PIXABAY_API_KEY none remote URL from hits[].largeImageURL gemini_flash generate_image_gemini_flash google-genai generate_content, model gemini-3.1-flash-image GOOGLE_API_KEY closest of 10 aspect ratios local file, extension from MIME type nanobanana_pro generate_image_nanobanana_pro same, model gemini-3-pro-image GOOGLE_API_KEY closest of 10 aspect ratios local file gpt-image-2 generate_image_openai_gpt_image_2 OpenAI images.generate, model gpt-image-2 OPENAI_API_KEY; GPT_IMAGE_2_QUALITY optional closest of 3 sizes local .png from b64_json gpt-image-1.5 generate_image_openai_gpt_image_1_5 OpenAI images.generate, model gpt-image-1.5 OPENAI_API_KEY; GPT_IMAGE_1_5_QUALITY optional closest of 3 sizes local .png comfyui generate_image_comfyui POST /prompt, poll GET /history/ID, GET /view COMFYUI_URL, COMFYUI_WORKFLOW written into latent-image nodes local file, ComfyUI's extension open_webui generate_image_open_webui POST BASE/images/generations OPEN_WEBUI_IMAGE_URL; OPEN_WEBUI_IMAGE_API_KEY optional always 1024x1024 local .png openai_compatible generate_image_openai_compatible OpenAI SDK images.generate against a custom base URL OPENAI_COMPAT_IMAGE_BASE_URL, OPENAI_COMPAT_IMAGE_API_KEY, OPENAI_COMPAT_IMAGE_MODEL mapped only for gpt-image-2 / gpt-image-1.5 model names local .png

The "required settings" column is exactly the required_fields map that the test endpoint enforces (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/images.py:63). The model names are hard-coded at servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:492 and servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:503.

docs.title: Step 3: generate_image, the single front door
docs.text:
Every caller (the two generation pipelines, the slide editor in servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py:75, the chat assistant in servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:704, and the images endpoints) goes through one coroutine:

servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py (excerpt)
        is_stock_provider = self.is_stock_provider_selected()
        image_prompt = prompt.get_image_prompt(with_theme=not is_stock_provider)
        # ...
        try:
            if is_parallel_image_generation_enabled():
                image_path = await self._call_image_provider(
                    image_prompt, prompt.target_size
                )
            else:
                async with _get_image_generation_lock():
                    image_path = await self._call_image_provider(
                        image_prompt, prompt.target_size
                    )
            if image_path:
                if image_path.startswith("http"):
                    return image_path
                elif os.path.exists(image_path):
                    return ImageAsset(
                        path=image_path,
                        is_uploaded=False,
                        extras={
                            # ...
                        },
                    )
                elif image_path.startswith("/app_data/") or image_path.startswith(
                    "/static/"
                ):
                    return absolute_fastapi_asset_url(image_path)
            raise Exception(f"Image not found at {image_path}")

        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error generating image: {e}")
            normalized_error = normalize_image_generation_error(e)
            if normalized_error is e:
                raise
            raise normalized_error from e

Walking through it in order:

  1. Disabled or unconfigured. DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION is parsed by parse_bool_or_none (servers/fastapi/utils/parsers.py:1), which is true only for the literal string true in any case. A disabled service, or one with no provider function, returns the placeholder path /static/images/placeholder.jpg, made absolute when NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API is set (servers/fastapi/utils/asset_directory_utils.py:33).
  2. Prompt text. ImagePrompt.get_image_prompt(with_theme) returns f"{prompt}, {theme_prompt}" for AI providers and the bare prompt for stock providers (servers/fastapi/models/image_prompt.py:24). Stock search therefore always receives the raw query (asserted in servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_template_image_targets.py:145).
  3. Concurrency. ENABLE_PARALLEL_IMAGE_GENERATION defaults to true and accepts 1, true, yes, on (servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:320). When it is falsey, every provider call is wrapped in one asyncio.Lock per event loop, kept in a module-level WeakKeyDictionary (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:51 and servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:122). Because the lock is module level, it serializes image calls across every ImageGenerationService instance: presentation, editor and chat requests all queue behind each other.
  4. Dispatch. _call_image_provider (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:248) calls stock functions with only the query, and AI functions with (prompt, output_directory) plus target_size= when a size is known.
  5. Classifying the result. An http... string is a stock URL and is returned verbatim. An existing filesystem path becomes an unsaved ImageAsset. A /app_data/ or /static/ path becomes an asset URL. Anything else (including the empty string a stock search returns when it finds nothing) raises.
  6. Error normalization (Step 7).

Gotcha

DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION=1 or =yes does not disable images: only true does, because parse_bool_or_none compares value.lower() == "true". ENABLE_PARALLEL_IMAGE_GENERATION, by contrast, uses _is_truthy and accepts 1, yes and on (servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:11). The two flags look alike but parse differently.

Gotcha

No production call site sets ImagePrompt.theme_prompt: a repository-wide search finds it only in tests and in the extras dict above. For AI providers get_image_prompt(with_theme=True) therefore formats None into the string, and the provider receives "<prompt>, None". If you add theme-aware prompting, set theme_prompt at the ImagePrompt(...) construction sites in servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:212 and servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:350, or change get_image_prompt to skip a missing theme.

docs.title: Step 4: Turning a template box into a provider size
4.1 Measuring the slot
docs.text:
Template v2 slides are composed on a 1280 by 720 canvas (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/generation.py:99). image_target_sizes_from_template (servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:35) figures out how big each image slot is without modifying anything:

  1. Deep-copy the content and replace each image's URL with a unique marker such as https://presenton.invalid/image-slot/<nonce>/<index> (servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:53). The markers make repeated identical prompts distinguishable.
  2. Run the normal template hydrator on a copy of the layout.
  3. Walk the hydrated layout for elements with type == "image" whose data is one of the markers, and record their size.width / size.height when both are finite positive numbers.
  4. Return a map from JSON path key to (width, height). Any hydration exception returns {}: sizing is optional.

ImagePrompt enforces that target_width and target_height are both present or both absent, and both > 0 and finite (servers/fastapi/models/image_prompt.py:9).

docs.title: 4.2 Mapping a ratio to a supported option
5.1 OpenAI gpt-image-2 and gpt-image-1.5
docs.text:
Both wrappers call generate_image_openai(prompt, output_directory, model, quality, target_size) (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:259). Quality comes from GPT_IMAGE_2_QUALITY or GPT_IMAGE_1_5_QUALITY, falling back to medium; the test config restricts it to low, medium, high (servers/fastapi/models/image_provider_test.py:23).

  • Client: AsyncOpenAI() with no arguments in environment mode, so the OpenAI SDK reads OPENAI_API_KEY from the environment; AsyncOpenAI(api_key=config["OPENAI_API_KEY"]) in test mode.
  • Request: {"model": ..., "prompt": ..., "n": 1, "quality": ...} plus size=.
  • Retry: if the API raises BadRequestError whose text mentions size or dimension, and the chosen size was not already 1024x1024, it retries once with 1024x1024 (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:281).
  • Output: result.data[0].b64_json decoded into <output_directory>/<uuid4>.png.

docs.title: 5.2 Gemini Flash and NanoBanana Pro
docs.text:
_generate_image_google (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:416) builds types.GenerateContentConfig(response_modalities=["IMAGE"], image_config=ImageConfig(aspect_ratio=...)) and runs the synchronous client.models.generate_content in a worker thread via asyncio.to_thread. The client is genai.Client() (credentials resolved by the google-genai SDK itself) in environment mode, or genai.Client(api_key=config["GOOGLE_API_KEY"]) in test mode.

It reads image parts from response.parts, falling back to response.candidates[0].content.parts for older SDK shapes. For each part with inline_data, the file extension is the subtype of an image/* MIME type (else png), and the bytes are written with part.as_image().save(...) or, if that helper is missing, by base64-decoding inline_data.data. If no image part was found it raises HTTPException(500, "No image generated by google <model>").

docs.title: 5.3 Pexels and Pixabay
docs.text:
Stock providers are searches, not generators, and they share a signature: (prompt, api_key=None, limit=1). With limit <= 1 they return a single URL string (or ""), otherwise a list.

Detail Pexels (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:506) Pixabay (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:541) Endpoint GET https://api.pexels.com/v1/search GET https://pixabay.com/api/ Query params query, per_page = max(1, min(limit, 80)) key, q = prompt[:99], image_type=photo, per_page = max(3, min(limit, 200)) Auth raw key in Authorization (no Bearer), header omitted if no key key query parameter Timeout 20 s total 20 s total 401/403 HTTPException(401, "Invalid Pexels API key") HTTPException(401, "Invalid Pixabay API key: ...") Other errors 502 with response text 400 (or 401 if the text mentions "api key"), else 502 URL taken photo["src"]["large"] hit["largeImageURL"]

The returned URL points at the stock provider's CDN; nothing is downloaded and no ImageAsset row is created.

Gotcha

When a stock search has zero hits it returns "". generate_image then raises Exception("Image not found at "), which normalizes to the generic 500 message. Inside a deck this becomes a placeholder plus a warning, but GET /api/v1/ppt/images/generate surfaces it as an HTTP 500.

docs.title: 5.4 ComfyUI
docs.text:
generate_image_comfyui (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:593) treats COMFYUI_WORKFLOW as an API-format workflow JSON exported from ComfyUI and edits it in four passes before submission.

  1. Node index. _build_comfyui_node_index (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:880) walks the whole JSON and indexes every dict that has an inputs dict, keyed by its parent key or by its id field. Nested groups are therefore supported (servers/fastapi/tests/test_image_generation_comfyui.py:9).

  2. Prompt injection. _inject_prompt_into_workflow finds nodes whose _meta.title normalizes to input prompt and calls try_set on them:

    servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py (excerpt)
                # 1) preferred prompt-like keys
            for k in preferred_keys:
                if k in inputs and isinstance(inputs[k], str):
                    inputs[k] = prompt
                    return True

            # 2) fallback: exactly one unambiguous writable string field
            string_candidates = [
                k for k, v in inputs.items()
                if isinstance(v, str) and k not in ignore_keys
            ]
            if len(string_candidates) == 1:
                inputs[string_candidates[0]] = prompt
                return True

            # 3) follow links from ANY input key (node-type agnostic)
            for v in inputs.values():
                if is_link(v):
                    if try_set(v[0]):
                        return True

    The preferred keys are text, value, prompt, string, content, instruction, input, query. A link is a [node_id, output_index] pair, so a Reroute titled "Input Prompt" that links to a PrimitiveNode gets the primitive's value rewritten. 3. Size injection. _inject_target_size_into_workflow (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:676) writes the rounded target width and height into every node that is titled "image size" (case-insensitive) or whose class_type is EmptySD3LatentImage, contains EmptyLatentImage, or starts with Empty and contains LatentImage. It only overwrites literal positive integers; linked dimensions stay under workflow control. 4. Seed randomization. Any input key that normalizes to seed or ends in seed (seed, noise_seed, main_seed, variation_seed) with an integer or integer-string value gets secrets.randbelow(2**64), string-typed if it was a string (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:797). Without this, ComfyUI's API format would replay the exported seed and every regeneration would return the same picture.

Then the HTTP conversation:

Step Request Timeout Notes Submit POST {COMFYUI_URL}/prompt with {"prompt": workflow, "client_id": uuid4} 30 s needs prompt_id in the response Poll GET {COMFYUI_URL}/history/{prompt_id} every 4 s 30 s per call, 3000 s overall done when status.completed is true or outputs is non-empty; status.error raises Download GET {COMFYUI_URL}/view?filename=...&type=output[&subfolder=...] 60 s first image of the first output node that has images

Gotcha

The method's docstring says the prompt goes into a CLIPTextEncode node with "Positive" in its title, but the code requires a node titled exactly Input Prompt (after trimming and lowercasing) and raises ValueError("Could not find node with title 'Input Prompt'...") otherwise (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:784). Trust the code. Also note the overall polling budget is 3000 seconds, so a stuck ComfyUI queue holds the deck for up to 50 minutes.

docs.title: 5.5 Open WebUI
docs.text:
resolve_open_webui_api_base (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:107) appends /api/v1 to a bare origin such as http://127.0.0.1:8080, and leaves any URL that already has a path untouched. The request is POST {base}/images/generations with {"prompt": ..., "n": 1, "size": "1024x1024"}, a Bearer header when a key is configured, and a 300 s timeout.

The response may be a bare JSON array or {"data": [...]}. The first item's b64_json is decoded, or its url is downloaded (relative URLs such as /api/v1/files/.../content are prefixed with the origin, and the bearer key is sent on the download, with a 120 s timeout). A 404 or 405 response produces an error whose message hints that the URL should point at the API root.

docs.title: 5.6 OpenAI-compatible
docs.text:
generate_image_openai_compatible (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:1066) requires all three OPENAI_COMPAT_IMAGE_* settings, then uses AsyncOpenAI(base_url=..., api_key=...). It sends no quality. Size mapping applies only when the configured model name is literally gpt-image-2 or gpt-image-1.5, with the same "retry at 1024x1024 on a size error" rule.

If the response carries a url instead of b64_json, the image is downloaded with a 120 s timeout. The Authorization: Bearer <key> header is attached only for relative URLs or URLs with the same scheme and host as the configured base URL (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:1121), so the key is never leaked to a third-party CDN (servers/fastapi/tests/test_image_generation_openai_compatible.py:272).

docs.title: Step 6: Where files go, how URLs are formed, ImageAsset rows
6.1 The directory
docs.text:
Every pipeline constructs the service with ImageGenerationService(get_images_directory()). get_images_directory (servers/fastapi/utils/asset_directory_utils.py:227) resolves to:

  • $APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/images/users/<owner_id>/ when a user is authenticated (multi-user mode),
  • $APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/images/ when there is no owner (auth disabled, for example Electron),
  • with /tmp/presenton substituted when APP_DATA_DIRECTORY is unset.

File names are always uuid4() plus the extension, so two prompts never collide and nothing is overwritten.

docs.title: 6.2 The URL
docs.text: filesystem_image_path_to_app_data_url (servers/fastapi/utils/asset_directory_utils.py:63) converts a saved path back into a browser URL: it keeps http(s), data: and blob: values, returns /app_data/... and /static/... paths unchanged (made absolute when NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API is set), and maps anything inside $APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/images to /app_data/images/<relative path>. A path outside that root is returned untouched, and so is every path when APP_DATA_DIRECTORY is unset (the /tmp/presenton fallback directory has no URL mapping). So a file at /app_data/images/users/6f1c.../3a9e....png becomes the URL /app_data/images/users/6f1c.../3a9e....png, which FastAPI serves through an owner-checking StaticFiles mount (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:39). The ownership rules for /app_data are explained in Auth and multi-user.

docs.title: 6.3 The ImageAsset table
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/models/sql/image_asset.py (excerpt)
class ImageAsset(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: uuid.UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid.uuid4, primary_key=True)
    owner_id: Optional[uuid.UUID] = Field(
        default_factory=get_current_owner_id,
        exclude=True,
        sa_column=Column(
            ForeignKey("user.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), nullable=True, index=True
        ),
    )
    # ...
    is_uploaded: bool = Field(default=False)
    path: str
    extras: Optional[dict] = Field(sa_column=Column(JSON), default=None)
Column Meaning id UUID primary key owner_id FK to user.id, cascade delete; filled from the request's owner context created_at UTC timestamp, set by the column default is_uploaded False for generated images, True for user uploads path absolute filesystem path of the file extras for generated images: prompt, theme_prompt, target_width, target_height

The service only constructs the row. The caller adds and commits it: /generate commits all collected assets together with the presentation and slides (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3088), GET /images/generate commits immediately (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/images.py:280), and the chat assistant commits in servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:708. Stock results never produce rows.

docs.title: Step 7: Failures, placeholders, warnings
docs.text:
normalize_image_generation_error (servers/fastapi/utils/image_generation_error.py:58) maps any exception to an HTTPException:
