  4. buildSvgUpdateUrl produces /api/update-svg?url=<source>&color=<color>, explicitly clearing any stale fill and stroke while keeping other existing parameters such as strokeWidth and opacity.

The Next.js route GET /api/update-svg (servers/nextjs/app/api/update-svg/route.ts:168) then reads the icon from the local servers/fastapi/static/icons directory (never from the network: it resolves the URL's path, rejects any path whose real path falls outside the icons directory, opens the file with O_NOFOLLOW, and caps files at 5 MB) and returns the SVG with transformSvgMarkup applied, which sets color, and replaces fill and stroke values except none, url(...), inherit, transparent and similar preserved paints (servers/nextjs/lib/svg-color.ts:485-576).

Gotcha

SmartHtmlEditor (the edit-mode canvas) writes html_content into its container as is and never calls applySmartSlideIconColors; only the two SmartHtmlSlide renderers do. So a color attribute on an icon takes effect in thumbnails, present mode and other read-only views, but the main edit canvas shows the icon's original SVG colors.

docs.title: Step 11: Inline editing, selection and saving
Making text editable
docs.text:
SmartHtmlEditor (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/SmartHtmlEditor.tsx:92) writes the raw html_content into its container with container.innerHTML = html (no DOMPurify in this path), then marks text as editable in three passes (:272-316):

  1. Any element with text whose descendants are all inline tags (b, strong, span, a, code, br and others in INLINE_TEXT_TAGS) becomes contenteditable="true" as a unit.
  2. Any leaf element with text that is not already inside an editable element.
  3. Bare text nodes inside mixed-content elements are wrapped in a <span data-smart-text-wrapper="1"> and made editable.

script, style, svg, img, canvas, video and similar tags are never editable (EXCLUDED_TEXT_TAGS, :54). Each editable element tracks input, cut, paste and drop to set a dirty flag and saves on blur.

Clicking an <img> opens the image editor or the icon picker; it is treated as an icon if it has image-type="icon", an .svg source, or "icon" in its alt (:318-337). The prompt or query attribute pre-fills the search. Choosing a new asset rewrites src (and the attribute) and saves (:512-524). While the AI selector described below is on, its capture-phase click listener on the container calls preventDefault and stopPropagation for selectable targets (:388-394, :444), so a click on an image selects it for the assistant instead of reaching the image's own listener.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
saveHtml (:202-236) clones the container, unwraps the helper spans, strips data-editable-text, contenteditable, spellcheck and data-smart-editable-media, and dispatches updateSlideHtmlContent({slideIndex, slideId, html}) if the HTML changed. The Redux reducer finds the slide by ID, then by index, and replaces html_content (servers/nextjs/store/slices/presentationGeneration.ts:290). From there the generic autosave takes over: useAutoSave (default debounce 1,000 ms, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/useAutoSave.tsx:23; the presentation page passes debounceMs: 2000, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/PresentationPage.tsx:275) waits for quiet, diffs per-slide JSON fingerprints, and sends each changed slide to PATCH /api/v1/ppt/presentation/slide_update with body {"slide": {...}}. The handler (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2585) checks that both IDs are UUIDs, that the slide exists and that it belongs to the supplied presentation, then copies every field except id, presentation and index onto the stored row. Autosave is paused while streaming, so slides arriving over SSE are not echoed back. The slide editor and autosave are covered in chapter 22.

Gotcha

slide_update stores html_content exactly as received. It does not run normalize_smart_slide_html, so manual edits are never checked for overflow, and anything a client sends is stored and later re-executed by the chart injector in the editor. If you harden this path, call the normalizer in update_presentation_slide for rows whose layout is smart-html.

docs.title: Selecting an element for the AI
docs.text:
When the header's selector toggle is on (it defaults to on for smart decks after streaming and remembers the choice in localStorage["html-selector-mode"], servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/PresentationHeader.tsx:139-158), the editor adds capture-phase mouseover and click listeners (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/SmartHtmlEditor.tsx:345-478). normalizeSelectableElement climbs to the nearest [data-select-root], [data-card] or .card if present, and refuses the root <section> or any element covering at least 98% of the slide in both width and height. Hovering draws a light box and clicking draws the selected box with an "AI edit" label; both are rendered by SmartHtmlSelectionOverlay (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/SmartHtmlSelectionOverlay.tsx:10-51) into document.body as position: fixed divs, with rectangles re-measured on every animation frame so they stay attached while the assistant panel animates.

A click dispatches setChatHtmlSelection with slideId, slideIndex, slideNumber, the cleaned outerHTML of the element, its tag, the first 240 characters of its text, and a timestamp (:413-425). Clicking the same element again, or pressing Escape, clears the selection. PresentationPage opens the assistant panel automatically when a new selection arrives. What the assistant does with that selection is the subject of chapter 14.

docs.title: What smart mode does not use: LaTeX runs and native infographics
docs.text:
Two utilities sit next to the smart code but belong to the template (JSON) world, which is easy to miss when reading the tree.

servers/fastapi/utils/latex_text.py converts strings with <latex>...</latex> tags into text runs of the template v2 element model: parse_latex_tags("Area is <latex>\pi r^2</latex>") returns [{"text": "Area is "}, {"type": "latex", "latex": "\\pi r^2"}], returning None for nested or unbalanced tags and when there is no tag at all (:88-91); replace_text_runs rebuilds a run list while preserving the font of matching existing runs and can also turn **bold** into bold runs (:94-142); normalize_latex strips $$...$$ or \[...\] delimiters and caps the expression at 4,000 characters (:159-173). It is used by template content hydration in servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1156-1172 and by the chat tools.

servers/fastapi/utils/infographic_catalog.py defines 27 native infographic types (progress_bar, gauge, gantt, timeline, roadmap, funnel variants, pyramid, matrices, org_chart, decision_tree, mind_map and more, :4-32), each with a best_for description, required data shape, default size and example, plus normalize_infographic_data which validates the data contract (for example risk_matrix needs exactly four items and org_chart needs unique IDs with valid parent_ids, :512-639). These are rendered by the template v2 renderer (servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts, exercised by servers/nextjs/tests/infographic-rendering.test.mjs and vector-arrow-rendering.test.mjs) and by the editor's text component (latex-html-text-rendering.test.mjs).

Neither is referenced by generate_smart_presentation.py or stream_smart_presentation: a smart slide's equations or diagrams are whatever HTML, SVG or Chart.js the model writes. The chat tools that create infographics and LaTeX runs on template slides are covered in chapter 14, and the element model in chapter 16.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• Smart mode stores one validated HTML <section> per slide in slides.html_content; "auto" slide count means 8, and the maximum is 50.
  • The prompt is a fixed set of rules (1280x720 canvas, Tailwind on elements only, no document tags or handlers, Chart.js with chart-xxxxxx canvases, density and overflow rules), plus source context and up to 6 community reference slides as style-only context.
  • SmartSlideStreamParser emits a slide as soon as its SLIDE_END arrives; normalize_smart_slide_html and inspect_smart_slide_layout reject unsafe, scrolling, over-dense or overlapping slides, and each accepted slide is committed in its own session before the slide_html event is sent.
  • Failures retry up to 8 times in continuation mode, keeping the accepted prefix, and reconnects replay checkpoints instead of regenerating.
  • In the browser, slides render in a sandbox="allow-scripts" iframe (or DOMPurify plus an in-page stage on Linux desktop), Tailwind and Chart.js are vendored runtimes, and icons are recolored through /api/update-svg.
  • Inline edits go through Redux and autosave to PATCH /presentation/slide_update, which does not re-validate the HTML.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Continue with Editing and chat assistant to see how a selected element, a prompt or a tool-calling chat turn changes these slides on the server.

docs.title: Editing and chat assistant
docs.text:
Reads: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/edit_slide.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/select_slide_type_on_edit.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/edit_slide_html.py, servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/chat.py, servers/fastapi/services/chat/, servers/fastapi/services/mem0_oss_memory.py, servers/fastapi/services/mem0_presentation_memory_service.py, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx · Builds on: Smart mode, Prompts and schemas · Time: ~45 min

Presenton has two ways to change a slide with AI after it exists. The older one is a pair of single-shot endpoints, POST /slide/edit for JSON (template) slides and POST /slide/edit-html for HTML slides, which run one or two LLM calls and overwrite the row. The newer one is a tool-calling chat assistant that runs up to 40 rounds of tool calls against the live database, streams its progress over SSE, keeps conversation threads in SQL, and recalls background facts from a local Mem0 vector store. This chapter walks through both, request by request, then follows the chat assistant's tools down to the rows they mutate and the memory they write.

docs.title: Two editing surfaces
docs.text:
Surface Route Slide kinds LLM calls Used by the web UI in this snapshot Prompt edit POST /api/v1/ppt/slide/edit JSON content slides (template v2 or legacy layouts) Layout selection, then structured content edit No (API and Presenton Cloud proxy only) HTML prompt edit POST /api/v1/ppt/slide/edit-html Any slide with HTML One free-text call No (API only) Chat assistant POST /api/v1/ppt/chat/message[/stream] Standard and smart decks, with different tool sets Up to 40 tool rounds, plus an optional final synthesis call Yes (Chat.tsx)

A search of servers/nextjs finds no caller of /slide/edit or /slide/edit-html; the only in-repo references are servers/fastapi/services/presenton_cloud_proxy.py:52 and the tests. The endpoints are still part of the public API and the generated servers/fastapi/openai_spec.json. Both routers are mounted under /api/v1/ppt (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/router.py:22-40).

docs.title: Step 1: Edit a JSON slide with POST /slide/edit
1.1 Request and response
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/ppt/slide/edit
Content-Type: application/json

{"id": "6a1f0c7e-1b0a-4a1e-9a55-3d0d6a9e2c11", "prompt": "Make the headline punchier and add a solar icon"}

Both fields are required body parameters (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py:38-43). The response is the updated SlideModel (id, presentation, layout_group, layout, index, content, html_content, speaker_note, properties, ui) with a new id. Unknown slide or presentation IDs return 404 "Slide not found" / "Presentation not found" (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py:44-49).

The handler runs these sub-steps in order (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py:51-132):

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as slide.py edit_slide
    participant M as Mem0 presentation memory
    participant L as LLM
    participant A as Image and icon services
    participant D as Database
    C->>S: POST /slide/edit with id and prompt
    S->>D: load slide and presentation
    S->>M: retrieve_context(presentation_id, prompt)
    S->>L: select layout index (structured)
    S->>L: edit content against layout schema (structured)
    S->>A: fetch only new image prompts and icon queries
    S->>D: new slide id, content, layout, ui, speaker note, assets
    S->>M: store_slide_edit
    S-->>C: updated SlideModel

docs.title: 1.2 Retrieve memory
docs.text: MEM0_PRESENTATION_MEMORY_SERVICE.retrieve_context(presentation.id, prompt) returns up to 6,000 characters of related memories for this deck, or "" when Mem0 is unavailable (Step 8). The string is injected into both LLM prompts.

docs.title: 1.3 Decide whether the layout changes
docs.text:
_get_presentation_stream_layout(presentation) (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1435) builds a PresentationLayoutModel from the stored template payload (or the legacy layout). Then get_slide_layout_from_prompt (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/select_slide_type_on_edit.py:50) looks up the slide's current layout position with layout.get_slide_layout_index(slide.layout) (404 "Slide layout X not found" if it is not in the deck's layout, servers/fastapi/templates/presentation_layout.py:36-42) and asks the model for one integer. The system prompt contains layout.to_string() (for each layout: its index, name and description, no schemas, servers/fastapi/templates/presentation_layout.py:49-62), the memory block, and these notes:

servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/select_slide_type_on_edit.py (excerpt)
                # Notes
                - Do not select different slide layout than current unless absolutely necessary as per user prompt. 
                - If user prompt is not clear, select the layout that is most relevant to the slide data.
                - If user prompt is not clear, select the layout that is most relevant to the slide data.
                **Go through all notes and steps and make sure they are followed, including mentioned constraints**

The user message lists the prompt, the current slide data and the current layout index. The response schema is SlideLayoutIndex ({"index": int}, servers/fastapi/models/slide_layout_index.py:4), and the function returns layout.slides[index] (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/select_slide_type_on_edit.py:88-89).

Gotcha

The returned index is not range-checked. An out-of-range value raises IndexError, which handle_llm_client_exceptions turns into an HTTP 500, and a negative value silently selects a layout from the end of the list because Python indexing allows it. If you modify this call, clamp the index or add ge/lt constraints to the schema.

Gotcha

Calling /slide/edit on a smart slide fails. A smart presentation has layout = None, so presentation.get_layout() executes PresentationLayoutModel(**self.layout) (servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py:113-114) and raises a TypeError outside any handler, which surfaces as a 500. Smart slides must go through /slide/edit-html or the chat assistant.

docs.title: 1.4 Rewrite the content against the layout's schema
docs.text:
get_edited_slide_content (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/edit_slide.py:110) derives the response schema from the selected layout:

servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/edit_slide.py (excerpt)
    response_schema = remove_fields_from_schema(
        slide_layout.json_schema, ["__image_url__", "__icon_url__"]
    )
    response_schema = add_field_in_schema(
        response_schema,
        {
            "__speaker_note__": {
                "type": "string",
                "minLength": 100,
                "maxLength": 500,
                "description": "Speaker note for the slide",
            }
        },
        True,
    )
    response_schema = ensure_array_schemas_have_items(response_schema)

So the model never writes asset URLs, and it must write a required speaker note of 100 to 500 characters. The system prompt (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/edit_slide.py:30-68) adds the deck's instructions, tone and verbosity when present, and these rules: answer in the language given in the input, "Do not change Image prompts and Icon queries if not asked for in prompt", generate them only if asked, speaker notes as plain non-Markdown text, plus the retrieved memory with the instruction to use it "only if it is relevant". The user prompt (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/edit_slide.py:71-88) fixes the icon query and image prompt language to English, adds the current date and time, the slide content language (auto-detect for empty or auto values), the edit prompt, and the current slide.content. The call is generate_structured_with_schema_retries(..., validate_schema=True), the same structured-output helper described in chapter 9.

Gotcha

Both edit prompts interpolate Python dictionaries with f-strings ({slide_data}), so the model sees Python repr output (single quotes, True, None), not JSON. The edit path also keeps the generated __speaker_note__ key inside slide.content after copying it to slide.speaker_note (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py:113, :121).

docs.title: 1.5 Reuse or regenerate assets
docs.text:
process_old_and_new_slides_and_fetch_assets (servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:291) compares the old and new content and only pays for assets that actually changed. It finds every dictionary that carries a prompt or query under these keys (servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:22-24):

Asset Prompt keys (first non-empty wins) URL key written (legacy / template v2) Image __image_prompt__, image_prompt, prompt __image_url__ / image_url Icon __icon_query__, icon_query, query __icon_url__ / icon_url

The handler chooses the template v2 key style when the presentation has a template layout payload or the slide has a ui dict (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py:84-87). The reuse rule is exact-match:

servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py (excerpt)
    old_image_urls = {
        (prompt, (old_image_target_sizes or {}).get(_path_key(path))): image_url
        for path, asset, prompt in old_image_assets
        if (
            image_url := _get_asset_url(
                asset,
                "image",
                template=use_template_asset_fields,
            )
        )
    }
    # ...
    for path, new_image, image_prompt in new_image_assets:
        target_size = (new_image_target_sizes or {}).get(_path_key(path))
        image_key = (image_prompt, target_size)
        if image_key in old_image_urls:
            _set_asset_url(
                new_image,
                "image",
                old_image_urls[image_key],
                template=use_template_asset_fields,
            )
            continue

An image is reused only if the same prompt existed before and its target box size is the same. Target sizes come from image_target_sizes_from_template (servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:35-99), which tags each image slot with a unique https://presenton.invalid/image-slot/{nonce}/{i} URL, hydrates the layout, and reads back each tagged image element's size, so a prompt moved into a differently sized box is regenerated at the new size. Icons are reused by query string alone. Everything else is fetched concurrently with ImageGenerationService.generate_image(ImagePrompt(prompt, target_width, target_height)) and ICON_FINDER_SERVICE.search_icons(query, weight=icon_weight). With allow_image_fallback=True (the edit endpoint's setting), a failed image becomes /static/images/placeholder.jpg plus a warning that is only logged; an icon search with no result becomes /static/icons/placeholder.svg. Newly generated ImageAsset rows are returned and added to the session. Image generation itself is covered in chapter 12.

docs.title: 1.6 Persist
docs.text:
The handler then (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py:109-130):

  1. Assigns slide.id = uuid.uuid4() ("Always assign a new unique id to the slide"). The integration test asserts that afterwards exactly one slide row exists and it has the new ID (servers/fastapi/tests/integration/test_slide_edit_api.py:155-185).
  2. Sets content; when the layout changed and the deck uses a template payload, rebuilds ui from the new layout with _template_slide_ui; sets layout; re-hydrates ui from content (_hydrate_template_slide_ui); copies the speaker note.
  3. Adds the new assets and commits.
  4. Calls store_slide_edit(presentation_id, slide_index, edit_prompt, edited_slide_content).

Because every step before the commit only touches memory objects, a failing LLM call leaves the saved slide untouched (test_failed_ai_edit_leaves_saved_slide_unchanged, servers/fastapi/tests/integration/test_slide_edit_api.py:244). How template content becomes ui is the subject of chapter 17.

docs.title: Step 2: Edit HTML with POST /slide/edit-html
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/ppt/slide/edit-html
Content-Type: application/json

{"id": "6a1f0c7e-...", "prompt": "Turn the three bullets into cards", "html": null}

html is optional; when omitted the stored html_content is edited, and if neither exists the response is 400 "No HTML to edit" (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py:135-152). The handler retrieves memory, calls get_edited_slide_html(prompt, html, memory_context), assigns a new slide ID (the comment says this "is to ensure that the nextjs can track slide updates"), stores the result in html_content, commits, and records a store_slide_edit with the HTML as content (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py:154-180).

The LLM call (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/edit_slide_html.py:61-85) is a single non-streaming client.generate in a worker thread. The system prompt is a generic "expert HTML slide editor" brief: preserve structure, classes and IDs, keep styling unless asked, "Ensure modifications work across different screen sizes", preserve <style> and <script> tags. The user prompt contains the edit request, the memory block and the HTML in a fenced block. The reply is cut down to the span from the first < to the last >:

servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/edit_slide_html.py (excerpt)
def extract_html_from_response(response_text: str) -> Optional[str]:
    start_index = response_text.find("<")
    end_index = response_text.rfind(">")

    if start_index != -1 and end_index != -1 and end_index > start_index:
        return response_text[start_index : end_index + 1]

    return None

If no tag is found the original HTML is returned unchanged.

Gotcha

/slide/edit-html predates smart mode and does not apply any of its rules. The result is never passed through normalize_smart_slide_html, so it can contain scripts without new Chart(, event handlers, <style> tags, scrolling containers or a root that is not a 1280x720 <section>, and its prompt even mentions forms and responsive design. For smart slides, the chat assistant's saveSlide (Step 5) is the validated path.

docs.title: Step 3: The chat API surface
docs.text:
CHAT_ROUTER (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/chat.py:28) exposes five routes:

Method and path Input Output GET /api/v1/ppt/chat/conversations query presentation_id [{conversation_id, updated_at, last_message_preview}], newest first (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/chat.py:31) GET /api/v1/ppt/chat/history query presentation_id, conversation_id {presentation_id, conversation_id, messages: [{role, content, created_at}]} (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/chat.py:49) DELETE /api/v1/ppt/chat/conversation query presentation_id, conversation_id 204 (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/chat.py:91) POST /api/v1/ppt/chat/message ChatMessageRequest ChatMessageResponse (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/chat.py:105) POST /api/v1/ppt/chat/message/stream ChatMessageRequest text/event-stream (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/chat.py:124)

The Pydantic models (servers/fastapi/models/chat.py) all set extra="forbid":

Model Fields and limits ChatMessageRequest presentation_id: UUID; presentation_type: "standard" or "smart" (default standard); message: str 1 to 8,000 chars; conversation_id: UUID or null; attachments: list[ChatAttachment], at most 8 ChatAttachment type: "document"; name 1 to 255 chars; file_path 1 to 4,000 chars; mime_type up to 255 or null ChatMessageResponse conversation_id: UUID; response: str; tool_calls: list[str] (tool names in call order)

A smart-deck request from the editor looks like this (message abbreviated; Step 9 shows how the frontend builds it):

{
  "presentation_id": "9a1e6f1c-3a7b-4d0e-8f5d-2b2f1c7a9e10",
  "presentation_type": "smart",
  "message": "UI context: the user is editing a Smart HTML presentation. ...\nUI context: the currently selected slide is slide 3 (zero-based index 2).\nUser message: Make this chart a line chart",
  "conversation_id": "1d2c3b4a-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d",
  "attachments": []
}

The stream endpoint wraps PresentationChatService.stream_reply and maps its (event_type, value) pairs to SSE frames (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/chat.py:136-165):

Frame type Payload Emitted when status status: "Reading deck context", "Finalizing response" or "Saving chat" Start of turn, tool-limit path, before persisting chunk chunk: text delta Every content delta from the model trace trace: an object with kind model_note, tool_plan, tool_call or limit Reasoning summary, planned tools, each tool start and finish, tool-limit notice complete chat: {conversation_id, response, tool_calls} After the turn is saved error detail Only for an HTTPException raised while streaming

A pair of tool_call traces for a smart save:

event: response
data: {"type": "trace", "trace": {"kind": "tool_call", "round": 2, "tool": "saveSlide", "status": "start", "message": "Saving the slide", "slide_index": 2, "slide_number": 3}}

event: response
data: {"type": "trace", "trace": {"kind": "tool_call", "round": 2, "tool": "saveSlide", "status": "success", "message": "Smart slide at index 2 was replaced.", "slide_index": 2, "slide_number": 3}}

The slide_index fields come from _tool_focus_from_arguments and _tool_focus_from_result (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:632-754), which read index, resolved_index, componentId, elementPath and several spellings of target index lists, for a fixed set of slide-editing tools.

Gotcha

The stream endpoint only catches HTTPException. Validation errors raised inside the turn (wrong presentation_type, missing presentation, LLM errors converted by handle_llm_client_exceptions) arrive as error frames, but any other exception (for example a database error while persisting) ends the stream without a complete frame, and the browser reports "Chat stream ended before completion" (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/chat.ts:318).

docs.title: Step 4: One chat turn, step by step
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Chat.tsx
    participant R as chat.py stream route
    participant S as PresentationChatService
    participant T as ChatTools and memory layer
    participant L as LLM
    participant D as Database
    participant M as Mem0
    U->>R: POST /chat/message/stream
    R->>S: stream_reply(message, attachments)
    S-->>U: status Reading deck context
    S->>D: presentation, SQL history
    S->>M: deck memory and chat memory search
    loop up to 40 rounds
        S->>L: messages plus tool definitions (stream)
        L-->>U: chunk events
        L-->>S: completion with tool_calls
        S-->>U: trace tool_plan and tool_call start
        S->>T: execute_tool_call
        T->>D: read or mutate slides
        S-->>U: trace tool_call success or error
    end
    S->>D: append_turn adds two rows
    S->>M: store chat turn
    S->>D: commit
    S-->>U: complete with conversation_id, response, tool_calls

docs.title: 4.1 Construct the service
docs.text: PresentationChatService.__init__ (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:74-94) creates three collaborators: a ChatConversationStore (SQL history plus Mem0 chat memory), a PresentationContextStore (an alias of PresentationChatMemoryLayer from servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:103, servers/fastapi/services/chat/presentation_context_store.py:1-3) bound to the presentation and its type, and ChatTools(memory, mode=chat_mode). The chat_mode parameter defaults to "presentation" and no route passes anything else; ChatTools stores it but never reads it (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:91).

docs.title: 4.2 Prepare the context
docs.text:
stream_reply (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:114) first calls self._tools.set_turn_context(user_message) (which resets the per-turn list of generated assets), yields "Reading deck context", then _prepare_turn_context (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:275-351):

  1. Reject an empty message (400), a missing presentation (404), and a presentation_type that differs from the stored generation_mode (400 "Presentation type does not match the stored generation mode.").
  2. Build attachment context (4.3).
  3. Use the given conversation_id or create uuid4(); load the thread's history (Step 7) and convert rows to UserMessage/AssistantMessage, stripping any stored "UI context" prefix.
  4. Build a memory query from the user message without its UI context prefix, plus attachment names, and run two searches: self._memory.retrieve_context(query) (deck scope) and retrieve_semantic_context(...) (this conversation's scope).
  5. If attachments were parsed, store their text in deck memory as [document_extracted_text].
  6. Assemble [SystemMessage(build_system_prompt(...)), *history, UserMessage(model_user_message)].

build_system_prompt (servers/fastapi/services/chat/prompts.py:227) picks SMART_CHAT_AI_ASSISTANT_SYSTEM_PROMPT for smart decks and CHAT_AI_ASSISTANT_SYSTEM_PROMPT otherwise, then appends "Deck memory (background only; may be partial or stale):" and "Chat memory (earlier messages in this conversation):" blocks when non-empty. The smart prompt is the shorter of the two:

servers/fastapi/services/chat/prompts.py (excerpt)
# Required workflow
1. Use getSmartPresentationContext for deck-wide, visual-style, new-slide, or
   multi-slide requests.
2. Before editing an existing slide, call getSlideAtIndex with
   includeFullContent=true and treat the returned html as authoritative.
3. Call saveSlide with one complete replacement HTML fragment. Never pass a
   diff, Markdown, fenced code, JSON slide content, or plain text.
4. Treat the edit as complete only when saveSlide returns saved=true. Repair
   validation errors and retry when possible.

It goes on to restate the smart HTML rules from chapter 13 (root section classes, no scrolling or clipping, decoration-only positioning, complete Chart.js canvas plus script, no CDN scripts), replaceOldSlideAtIndex=true for edits and false for inserts, and a cap of 50 slides (servers/fastapi/services/chat/prompts.py:168-224). The standard prompt (servers/fastapi/services/chat/prompts.py:10-166) is a long protocol: 1-based slide numbers versus 0-based tool indexes, inspect with getSlideAtIndex before visible edits, prefer reusable template blocks over primitives (mandatory getAvailableBlocks before new tables and charts), vector and infographic rules, chart and table data-preservation rules, asset rules (generate first, reuse URLs exactly), outline tools limited to 50 slides and MAX_OUTLINE_CONTENT_WORDS words (default 100, MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS env, servers/fastapi/constants/presentation.py:5-23), and a one- or two-sentence final reply.

docs.title: 4.3 Attachments
docs.text: Documents attached in the chat composer have already been uploaded; the request carries their temp paths. _should_parse_attachments (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:516-531) decides whether to read them: always if the user text is empty or matches DOCUMENT_CONTENT_INTENT_PATTERN (words like read, extract, summarize, chart, table, create, generate, "based on", "use the attached document"); never if it only matches DIRECT_FILE_PLACEMENT_PATTERN (place, put, insert, attach, display, show, move, resize, position, replace, add); otherwise yes. When the files are not parsed, the model only gets a "UI context: the user attached document file(s), but this request appears to place or reference the file..." note followed by Document N: name lines. When parsing, DocumentsLoader loads every file and each document is trimmed to min(3000, remaining) characters out of a 6,000-character total (MAX_CHAT_ATTACHMENT_FILE_CHARS, MAX_CHAT_ATTACHMENT_CONTEXT_CHARS, servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:46-47). The resulting "UI context: the user attached parsed document(s)..." block is inserted just before the User message: line (_compose_user_message_for_model, servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:534-552). The persisted user message is the stripped text plus "Attached files: a.pdf, b.docx" (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:555-567).

docs.title: 4.4 The tool loop
docs.text:
The loop runs at most MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 40 rounds (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:45, :134). Each round streams the model with tools=build_chat_llm_tools(self._tools.get_tool_definitions()); build_chat_llm_tools returns the function tools unchanged, and its docstring notes that web search is intentionally not offered to chat (servers/fastapi/services/chat/llm_tools.py:4-9). Content deltas are yielded immediately as chunk events; reasoning deltas are collected and, after the round, summarized into one model_note trace (whitespace-collapsed, capped at 600 characters, servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:455-465).

servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py (excerpt)
            completion_tool_calls = list(
                getattr(completion_chunk, "tool_calls", []) or []
            )
            if completion_tool_calls:
                tool_names = [tool_call.name for tool_call in completion_tool_calls]
                called_tools.extend(tool_names)
                # ...
                messages = self._append_sanitized_assistant_tool_turn(
                    messages,
                    content=getattr(completion_chunk, "content", None),
                    tool_calls=completion_tool_calls,
                )

                last_tool_results = []
                for tool_call in completion_tool_calls:
                    # ...
                    tool_result = await self._tools.execute_tool_call(tool_call)
                    # ...
                    tool_response_content = json.dumps(tool_result, ensure_ascii=False)
                    messages.append(
                        ToolResponseMessage(
                            id=tool_call.id,
                            content=[TextContentPart(text=tool_response_content)],
                        )
                    )
                continue

Tool calls in one round run sequentially, in the order the model listed them. A round with no tool calls ends the loop: its streamed text (or the completion's text, or "I could not generate a response for that request.") is the final answer. If all 40 rounds call tools, the service emits a limit trace and the "Finalizing response" status, makes one more call without tools (_try_final_response_without_tools, servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:433-452), and if that fails falls back to the message of the last successful tool result or a generic "I completed several tool operations..." sentence (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:814-830).

The non-streaming POST /chat/message runs the same loop through _run_llm_with_tools (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:376-431) with blocking client.generate calls in a worker thread and no traces.

docs.title: 4.5 Execute a tool call
docs.text:
ChatTools.execute_tool_call (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:454-526) is the single dispatcher. It returns a JSON-serializable envelope that is fed back to the model verbatim:

servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py (excerpt)
        parsed_args: dict[str, Any] | None = None
        repair_notes: list[str] = []
        try:
            parsed_args = self._parse_args(tool_call.arguments)
            parsed_args, repair_notes = self._repair_tool_args(
                tool_call.name,
                parsed_args,
            )
            LOGGER.info("Executing chat tool %s", tool_call.name)
            try:
                result = await handler(parsed_args)
            except Exception as first_exc:
                retried = False
                for _attempt in range(MAX_TOOL_REPAIR_RETRIES):
                    retry_args, retry_notes = self._repair_tool_args(
                        tool_call.name,
                        parsed_args,
                        error=str(first_exc),
                    )

The pipeline is:

  1. Unknown name: {"ok": false, "error": "Unsupported tool: X", "recovery": {"retryable": false, ...}}.
  2. _parse_args (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:1039) accepts tolerant JSON: it tries dirtyjson then json on the raw string, on the contents of a Markdown fence, and on the outermost {...} or [...] substring, then converts any string "null" to None.
  3. _repair_tool_args (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:1190-1218) normalizes JSON-string fields (for example an object passed where content, element or component must be a JSON string), and for chart, table and image inserts fills in missing data from the user's latest message or from assets generated earlier in this turn. The chart repair parses label and number pairs such as "North 120, South 95" (at least 2 and at most 12 rows, servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:1515-1553); the table repair understands "headers A, B data: x, y; z, w" and CSV-like lines.
  4. Call the handler. On an exception, repair once more with the error text (MAX_TOOL_REPAIR_RETRIES = 1, servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:68) and retry only if the repair changed the arguments.
  5. Success: {"ok": true, "tool": name, "result": {...}}, plus "repair": {"applied": true, "notes": [...]} when repairs were made.
  6. Failure: {"ok": false, "tool": name, "error": str(exc), "repair": {...}, "recovery": {"retryable", "message", "guidance": [...], "expected"?, "received_keys"?}}, where _build_tool_recovery (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:1733-1845) maps error text to guidance and example payloads (a correct chart element, a table, an image with a generated URL, the reusable-block workflow).

Gotcha

ok: true only means the handler did not raise. Most mutating handlers report business failures as data, for example {"saved": false, "message": "Smart slide HTML failed validation.", "validation_errors": [...]}. The trace for such a call still has status: "success", and the frontend refreshes as if a mutation happened. The prompts tell the model to check saved=true; code that consumes traces should check the result too.

docs.title: 4.6 Persist the turn
docs.text: _persist_turn (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:353-374) calls ChatConversationStore.append_turn with the user message stripped of its UI context, the final answer and the list of tool names, commits the request session, and returns ChatTurnResult(conversation_id, response_text, tool_calls). The stream route turns that into the complete frame.

docs.title: Step 5: The tool sets
docs.text: ChatTools.get_tool_definitions (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:127) returns one of two lists, depending only on self._memory.presentation_type. All tools are declared with strict=False. Argument schemas live in servers/fastapi/services/chat/schemas.py; every model sets extra="forbid" and strict=True (servers/fastapi/services/chat/schemas.py:11-12), and the OpenAIStrictSchemaModel subclass fills omitted fields with None before validation (servers/fastapi/services/chat/schemas.py:15-28), which is why the prompt tells the model to "Include required nullable fields with null".

docs.title: Smart decks: 7 tools
docs.text:
Tool Arguments What it does getSmartPresentationContext includeSlideHtml (default false), maxHtmlCharsPerSlide 0 to 50,000 (0 means full) Returns title, language, tone, verbosity, instructions, fonts, community_design_ids, outlines, structure, slide count, and per slide its ID, index, title, HTML length and a 1,200-character text preview (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:985-1038) readSourceDocuments query, maxChars 1,000 to 30,000 Re-parses the deck's file_paths within a character budget (default 12,000); when no file can be read, falls back to a deck-memory search (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:554-683) searchSlide query 1 to 1,000 chars, limit 1 to 10 Scores slides by full-phrase match (8 points) plus matched tokens over text extracted from HTML (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:187-247) getSlideAtIndex index 0 to 1,000, includeFullContent Returns previews, and with includeFullContent=true the complete html (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:249-290); retries index-1 if nothing is found (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:597-614) generateAssets assets: 1 to 12 of {kind: "image" or "icon", prompt} Generates images (committing an ImageAsset row) or finds icons, returns URLs (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:763-786, servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:703-722) saveSlide html up to 500,000 chars, index, replaceOldSlideAtIndex, optional speakerNote, editPrompt save_html_slide (below) deleteSlide index Deletes and reindexes; deleting the last slide inserts an "Untitled slide" placeholder section (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:1161-1255)

save_html_slide (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:1040-1159) is where the chat assistant mutates a smart deck:

servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py (excerpt)
        try:
            normalized_html = normalize_smart_slide_html(html)
        except HTTPException as exc:
            return {
                "saved": False,
                "message": "Smart slide HTML failed validation.",
                "validation_errors": [str(exc.detail)],
            }

        target_index = max(0, index)
        title = self._smart_slide_title(normalized_html, target_index)
        if replace_old_slide_at_index:
            # ...
            slide.layout_group = "smart-html"
            slide.layout = "smart-html"
            slide.content = {"title": title}
            slide.html_content = normalized_html
            slide.ui = None

It refuses non-smart decks, runs exactly the generation-time validator from chapter 13 (so a chat edit with a scrolling container, an orphan chart canvas or overlapping positioned text is rejected with the validator's message, which the model then sees), derives the title from data-slide-title or the first heading, and either replaces the row in place (keeping its id) or inserts a new row at min(index, slide_count), shifting later slides and updating n_slides, with the 50-slide cap. The editPrompt argument is accepted by the schema but not used, and nothing is written to Mem0.

docs.title: Standard decks: 25 tools
docs.text:
Group Tools Backing method and notable behavior Outline addOutline, updateOutline, deleteOutline Edit presentation.outlines, recompute n_slides and title, then store_generated_outlines (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:4021-4041) Discovery getTemplateSummary, getAvailableLayouts, getContentSchemaFromLayoutId, getAvailableBlocks, getAvailableInfographics, searchSlide, getSlideAtIndex, readSourceDocuments Read-only. getAvailableBlocks searches reusable component blocks collected from presentation.layout and the referenced TemplateV2 row's merged components, components, layouts and raw layouts (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:2864-2911; default 20 results, max 50); getAvailableInfographics returns entries from INFOGRAPHIC_CATALOG Whole slide addNewSlide, addNewSlideLayout, saveSlide, updateSlide, deleteSlide save_slide validates content with Draft202012Validator against the layout schema (up to 10 errors); on replace it runs the asset reuse logic of Step 1.5 and assigns a new id, on insert it fetches all assets with process_slide_and_fetch_assets; both rebuild ui and store a [slide_edit] memory (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:777-983) Rendered UI addElement, addInfographic, updateElement, deleteElement, addComponent, createComponent, updateComponent, deleteComponent Mutate a deep copy of slide.ui and save it with _save_slide_ui, which strips component size and commits; the slide keeps its id; nothing is written to Mem0 (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:1320-1328) Assets generateAssets Same as in smart mode

Two of these use the utilities introduced at the end of chapter 13. addInfographic (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:855-910) validates data with normalize_infographic_data, defaults the position to (128, 170), the size to the catalog's default_size, the colors to a two-color meter palette or a six-color palette (white plus five blues), and the text color to 111111, optionally creating a blank slide first (target: "new_slide"). Text updates go through replace_text_runs, so a string such as "Area = <latex>\pi r^2</latex>" becomes a text run plus a LaTeX run that keeps the existing run's font (servers/fastapi/services/chat/slide_ui_helpers.py:2252). The rendered element model itself is documented in chapter 16.

addElement, addComponent and createComponent also enforce the "reuse template blocks first" rule in code: when the payload contains a chart or table element and no sourceBlockId is given, _require_reusable_block_first (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:1053-1108) looks for a reusable block of that type and, if one exists, raises an error naming its block_id so the model is pushed to getAvailableBlocks plus addComponent(sourceBlockId=...).

Gotcha

The tool list is filtered by deck type, but the handler table is not: _tool_handlers maps all 26 names for every deck (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:94-121). If a model invents a call to a standard tool on a smart deck (for example addNewSlide), execute_tool_call will run it and insert a template-style blank slide with ui and no html_content. If you rely on the separation, check presentation_type in execute_tool_call.

Gotcha

Whole-slide template saves (saveSlide, updateSlide with replace) give the row a new id, while UI-level tools and smart saveSlide keep it. Any client code that caches slide IDs across a chat turn must re-read the deck, which Chat.tsx does after mutating tools (Step 9).

docs.title: Step 6: How tools reach the database
docs.text: All chat tools share the request's AsyncSession through the memory layer, and each mutating method commits on its own (for example save_html_slide commits at servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:1102 or :1150). There is no turn-level transaction: if round 3 fails after round 2 saved a slide, the round 2 change stays. The final _persist_turn commit only covers the two history rows. Reads such as getSlideAtIndex query by (presentation, index) on every call, which is why the standard tool description calls it "Live SQL" and "authoritative" (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:251) and the smart prompt calls the returned HTML authoritative.

docs.title: SQL rows
docs.text:
Threads live in chat_history_messages (servers/fastapi/models/sql/chat_history_message.py:12):

Column Type Notes id UUID PK owner_id UUID FK user.id, nullable, indexed Defaults to the current owner; excluded from serialization presentation_id UUID FK presentations.id (cascade), nullable, indexed template_v2_id string FK template_v2.id (cascade), nullable, indexed Supported by sql_chat_history, but no route in this snapshot passes a template ID conversation_id UUID, indexed The thread position int, indexed, >= 1 Order within the thread role string user or assistant content Text Stripped user text or final assistant text created_at timezone-aware datetime Assistant row is user time plus 1 microsecond tool_calls JSON list of strings Set on the assistant row only

servers/fastapi/services/chat/sql_chat_history.py implements the operations. Every function requires exactly one of presentation_id or template_id (_resource_filter, :53-62). append_turn (:190-236) reads max(position) for the thread and inserts two rows at max+1 and max+2. list_conversations (:239-275) reads all rows for the deck newest first and keeps the first row per conversation, so last_message_preview is the latest message trimmed to 200 characters. delete_conversation and replace_messages filter deletes by owner_id as well. Owner scoping in general is covered in chapter 25.

docs.title: Legacy migration
docs.text:
Before SQL history existed, turns were only stored in Mem0. ChatConversationStore.load_history (servers/fastapi/services/chat/conversation_store.py:13-37) therefore reads SQL first and, when the thread is empty, loads the legacy Mem0 thread and writes it back with replace_messages. GET /chat/history does the same and commits when it migrated something (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/chat.py:60-74). append_turn writes to both stores (servers/fastapi/services/chat/conversation_store.py:39-61).

Gotcha

The SQL path loads the entire thread on every turn (load_messages has no limit), and only the final user and assistant texts are stored, not tool calls or tool results. Long threads grow the prompt without bound, and the model cannot see earlier tool outputs; it has to call discovery tools again. CHAT_MAX_STORED_TURNS (default 20) only limits the legacy Mem0 loader (servers/fastapi/services/chat/chat_memory_store.py:27-29, :343).

docs.title: One shared local client
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/services/mem0_oss_memory.py holds a single process-wide mem0.Memory instance used by both memory services. Its docstring describes the namespacing: deck-level memories use the Mem0 user_id {namespace}:{presentation_id}, chat threads use {namespace}:{presentation_id}:conversation:{conversation_id} (servers/fastapi/services/mem0_oss_memory.py:1-11). get_shared_mem0_client (:167-218) initializes it lazily and only once:

  1. Return None if MEM0_ENABLED is false (default true).
  2. If MEM0_REQUIRE_SPACY_MODEL is true (default), spacy.load(MEM0_SPACY_MODEL or "en_core_web_sm") must succeed, otherwise a warning is logged and Mem0 stays off.
  3. Build the configuration from the environment (_oss_config_from_env, :92-154), create the directories, point Mem0's telemetry directory at {mem0_dir}/telemetry/oss, and call Memory.from_config.
  4. Any exception is logged (with a specific hint when the fastembed model file is missing) and leaves the client None. _init_attempted is set before trying, so a failed initialization is not retried until the process restarts.
servers/fastapi/services/mem0_oss_memory.py (excerpt)
        "vector_store": {
            "provider": "qdrant",
            "config": {
                "collection_name": collection,
                "path": qdrant_path,
                "on_disk": True,
                "embedding_model_dims": dims,
            },
        },
        "embedder": {
            "provider": embedder,
            "config": {
                "model": model,
                "embedding_dims": dims,
            },
        },
        "history_db_path": history_db_path,
Environment variable Default Used for MEM0_ENABLED true Master switch (checked by the client and both services) APP_DATA_DIRECTORY /tmp/presenton Base for MEM0_DIR MEM0_DIR {APP_DATA_DIRECTORY}/mem0 (Compose sets /app_data/mem0) Root of all Mem0 files MEM0_QDRANT_PATH {MEM0_DIR}/qdrant Local on-disk Qdrant vector store MEM0_HISTORY_DB_PATH {MEM0_DIR}/history.db Mem0's SQLite history MEM0_COLLECTION_NAME presenton_memories Qdrant collection MEM0_EMBEDDER_PROVIDER fastembed Local embedding provider MEM0_EMBEDDER_MODEL BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 Embedding model MEM0_EMBEDDING_DIMS 384 Vector size, used by both store and embedder MEM0_LLM_MODEL OLLAMA_MODEL, else llama3.1:latest Mem0's LLM (provider openai, temperature 0.1, max tokens 2000) MEM0_LLM_API_KEY OPENAI_API_KEY, else ollama Mem0's LLM key MEM0_LLM_BASE_URL OLLAMA_URL, else http://host.docker.internal:11434 (suffixed with /v1) Mem0's LLM endpoint MEM0_SPACY_MODEL, MEM0_REQUIRE_SPACY_MODEL en_core_web_sm, true spaCy precondition MEM0_TOP_K 8 Results per search MEM0_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS 6000 Cap on the joined search result MEM0_PRESENTATION_NAMESPACE_PREFIX presentation Deck namespace MEM0_CHAT_NAMESPACE_PREFIX falls back to the presentation prefix Chat namespace CHAT_MAX_STORED_TURNS 20 Legacy chat history loader

The Compose file forwards the main variables to every profile (docker-compose.yml:108-117). Integer variables are clamped to at least 1. Every write in these services passes infer=False to client.add. The tests assert that the flag is passed (servers/fastapi/tests/test_mem0_presentation_memory_service.py:157, servers/fastapi/tests/test_chat_memory_store.py:110). In the Mem0 library that flag stores the message text as given instead of running LLM fact extraction, so the vector store holds Presenton's own tagged text; what Mem0 does with the flag is library behavior that no test in this repository exercises against a real Mem0 instance. A separate test checks that the LLM block defaults to a local Ollama-style endpoint when no OpenAI key is set (servers/fastapi/tests/test_mem0_presentation_memory_service.py:62).

docs.title: What is stored
docs.text:
Mem0PresentationMemoryService (servers/fastapi/services/mem0_presentation_memory_service.py:18) writes each memory as a single user message whose first line is a tag. Messages longer than 20,000 characters are cut and suffixed with [TRUNCATED] (:47-50).

Tag Written by Content [presentation_source_prompt], [presentation_generation_instructions], [outline_system_prompt], [outline_user_prompt], [document_extracted_text] store_generation_context, called from outline generation (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/outlines.py:153), the API generation path (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2764, :2846), and chat attachments (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:325, document text only) The generation inputs [generated_outlines] store_generated_outlines, from /prepare (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1923), outline endpoints, and chat outline tools Outline JSON [slide_edit] store_slide_edit, from /slide/edit, /slide/edit-html, and chat template save_slide (edit prompt [chat_tool_save_slide_replace] layout_id=... or [chat_tool_save_slide_new] ...) slide_index=, user_edit_prompt=, edited_slide_content= lines [chat_turn] ChatMemoryStore.store_chat_turn (servers/fastapi/services/chat/chat_memory_store.py:150) in the conversation scope turn_created_at=, user=, assistant= lines

Smart generation itself (stream_smart_presentation) writes nothing to Mem0, and neither does the chat assistant's smart saveSlide. For a smart deck, deck memory therefore only contains /slide/edit-html edits and documents attached in chat.

docs.title: Retrieval
docs.text: retrieve_context(presentation_id, query) (servers/fastapi/services/mem0_presentation_memory_service.py:186-242) calls client.search(query, filters={"user_id": scope}, top_k=MEM0_TOP_K), accepts either a {"results": [...]} dict or a list, takes each item's memory, text or data field, removes duplicates while keeping order, joins with blank lines and truncates to MEM0_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS. The chat store does the same in the conversation scope and also accepts memories or items keys (servers/fastapi/services/chat/chat_memory_store.py:103-116, :207-270). Both services retry add and search (and the chat store also get_all) with an alternative call signature on TypeError, to work across Mem0 versions. Note that _truncate appends \n\n[TRUNCATED] after the cut, so a capped context is slightly longer than MEM0_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS.

docs.title: Failure handling and concurrency
docs.text:
Memory is strictly best-effort. Each service method returns early when the client is None, catches BaseException, re-raises only exceptions that are neither Exception nor SystemExit (for example KeyboardInterrupt), turns a SystemExit from the Mem0 runtime into a per-process "disabled" flag on that service with a logged error, and logs everything else and continues with "" or [] (servers/fastapi/services/mem0_presentation_memory_service.py:92-102, :207-218). All blocking Mem0 calls run in asyncio.to_thread and are serialized by run_shared_mem0_operation, a process-wide RLock, because local Qdrant keeps one SQLite connection that fails on concurrent commits (servers/fastapi/services/mem0_oss_memory.py:32-42; covered by test_presentation_and_chat_operations_are_serialized, servers/fastapi/tests/test_mem0_presentation_memory_service.py:228). The scope-isolation test servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_mem0_session_scope_security.py checks that Mem0's session-scope encoding keeps a user_id like presentation:<uuid> intact and that crafted IDs cannot read another scope's history.

Gotcha

Because the lock is process-wide and searches run on every slide edit and chat turn, heavy concurrent use serializes on Mem0. The client is also created lazily on first use, so the first edit or chat turn after startup pays for initializing the embedder and the local Qdrant store. Setting MEM0_ENABLED=false removes memory entirely without any other behavior change, since every caller already tolerates an empty context.

docs.title: Step 9: The frontend at the boundary
Building the message
docs.text:
Chat.tsx sends through a small adapter (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/chat/chat-adapter.ts:4-23) to PresentationChatApi.streamMessage (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/chat.ts:398). Before sending, buildBackendMessage (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx:992-1126) prefixes the user's text with "UI context:" lines and ends with User message: .... For a smart deck with a selected element the lines are:

servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx (excerpt)
    if (presentationType === "smart" && variant === "presentation") {
      contextLines.push(
        "UI context: the user is editing a Smart HTML presentation. Read the authoritative target HTML with getSlideAtIndex, preserve its design and scripts, and save a complete validated HTML fragment with saveSlide.",
      );
    }
    if (presentationType === "smart" && selectionContext) {
      const selectedHtml =
        selectionContext.html.length > MAX_SELECTED_HTML_CONTEXT_CHARS
          ? `${selectionContext.html.slice(0, MAX_SELECTED_HTML_CONTEXT_CHARS)}\n<!-- selected HTML truncated -->`
          : selectionContext.html;
      contextLines.push(
        `UI context: the user selected one HTML element from slide ${selectionContext.slideNumber} (zero-based index ${selectionContext.slideIndex}). Edit this selected element within the authoritative full slide HTML; preserve unrelated elements.`,
      );

The selection is the chatHtmlSelection written by SmartHtmlEditor in chapter 13; its HTML is capped at 3,500 characters (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx:134) and wrapped in <selected_html> tags, preceded by Selected element tag: and Selected element text: lines. Other context lines cover the current slide, the outline variant, template v2 selections (component IDs and element paths), pasted images with optional extracted text, and links. The selection is cleared from Redux as soon as the message is sent (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx:1734). When a message starts with UI context:, the backend's _strip_ui_context_prefix (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:492-499) removes everything up to the first \nUser message: before storing or searching, so history and memory hold only what the user typed.

Gotcha

ChatMessageRequest.message is limited to 8,000 characters, and that limit applies to the full composed string, including the UI context lines and up to 3,500 characters of selected HTML. A long prompt plus a large selection fails with 422 before the assistant runs.

docs.title: Reading the stream
docs.text: streamChatMessage (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/chat.ts:104-319) uses fetch and a ReadableStream reader rather than EventSource (the request is a POST). It splits the buffer on blank lines, ignores frames whose event: is not response, and dispatches chunk to onChunk, status to onStatus, trace to onTrace (accepting both slide_index and slideIndex spellings), complete to the final response, and error by throwing (with a re-authentication prompt for ChatGPT session errors). If the stream ends without complete, it throws.

docs.title: Reacting to tools
docs.text:
Chat.tsx wires those handlers (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx:1767-1876): chunks are appended to the assistant bubble; statuses and formatted traces become an activity list; a start trace for a mutating tool snapshots the affected slide for an edit preview; a success trace for a mutating tool triggers refreshPresentationIncrementally, which calls the page's onPresentationChanged (a re-fetch) and, while one refresh is in flight, queues at most one more (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx:1383-1408); and after complete, refreshPresentationIfNeeded re-fetches once more if any returned tool name is mutating (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx:1410-1422). Mutating tools are the 15 names in MUTATING_TOOLS (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/chat/chat-activity.ts:28-44). The edit preview lets the user switch between the original and modified slides; switching writes the chosen slide objects back through PATCH /presentation/slide_update (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx:1307-1381).

The active conversation ID is kept in sessionStorage under presenton:chat:{scope}:{presentationType}:conversationId:{resourceId} (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/chat/chat-utils.ts:141-170), so a reload in the same tab reopens the thread through GET /chat/history.

Gotcha

MUTATING_TOOLS does not include addInfographic, so a turn whose only mutation is a new infographic does not refresh the editor; the change appears after the next reload or the next mutating turn. Separately, restoring the "original" version after a template saveSlide or updateSlide sends the pre-edit slide object, whose id no longer exists because save_slide assigned a new UUID (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:871), and slide_update answers 404 "Slide not found" (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2599-2601). Smart saveSlide keeps IDs, so restore works there.

Gotcha

The frontend appends presentation_type as a query parameter to the list, history and delete calls (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/chat.ts:330, :348, :369), but those routes do not declare it, so FastAPI ignores it. Threads are filtered by presentation only.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• /slide/edit makes two structured LLM calls (layout index, then content against the layout schema with a required 100 to 500 character speaker note), reuses assets whose prompt and target size are unchanged, and saves the slide under a new ID; /slide/edit-html makes one free-text call and stores the HTML without smart validation.
  • The chat assistant is a loop of at most 40 tool rounds; smart decks get 7 HTML tools whose saveSlide runs the same normalize_smart_slide_html validator as generation, standard decks get 25 tools over outlines, layouts, blocks, elements, components, infographics and assets.
  • Tool calls are parsed tolerantly, repaired from the user's message, retried once, and always answered with an ok envelope; business failures such as saved: false are data, not errors.
  • Each turn is stored as two SQL rows in chat_history_messages (plus a legacy Mem0 copy), and the stream speaks five frame types: status, chunk, trace, complete, error.
  • Mem0 runs locally (Qdrant on disk, fastembed bge-small-en-v1.5, 384 dimensions), stores tagged raw text with infer=False in deck and conversation scopes, and fails open to empty context.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Continue with REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP to see how the same generation paths, including smart mode, are exposed to programs and agents.

docs.title: REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP
docs.text:
Reads: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, servers/fastapi/api/v2/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/async_tasks/router.py, servers/fastapi/services/async_tasks.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/webhook/router.py, servers/fastapi/services/webhook_service.py, servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py, servers/fastapi/utils/mcp_public_urls.py · Builds on: Standard generation pipeline, Auth and multi-user · Time: ~50 min

Presenton is not only a web app: the same FastAPI process is a headless presentation API that other programs and AI agents can drive. This chapter walks through that product surface in execution order: how a program authenticates, the full GeneratePresentationRequest contract, what the synchronous /generate endpoint does and returns, how the async variant persists progress in an async_tasks row that you poll, what happens to those rows when the server restarts, how Smart generation is exposed under /api/v2, how webhooks are stored and delivered (and what they do not do), and how mcp_server.py turns a static OpenAPI document into a Model Context Protocol server with mode-gated tools and a key-for-session exchange.

docs.title: Step 1: The API surface at a glance
docs.text:
Three processes are involved in a Docker deployment: nginx on port 80, FastAPI on 8000, and the MCP server on 8001 (spawned by start.js:608). nginx forwards /api/v1/ and /api/v2/ to FastAPI with 30 minute timeouts, and /mcp to the MCP server (nginx.conf:45, nginx.conf:59, nginx.conf:94). The topology itself is covered in Runtime topology.

flowchart LR
    C["HTTP client (curl, SDK)"] --> N["nginx :80"]
    M["MCP client (VS Code, Open WebUI)"] --> N
    N -->|/api/v1 and /api/v2| F["FastAPI :8000"]
    N -->|/mcp| P["mcp_server.py :8001 (FastMCP)"]
    P -->|httpx with session cookie| F
    F --> DB[("async_tasks, webhook_subscriptions, presentations")]
    F -->|POST JSON| W["Webhook subscriber URLs"]
Method and path Purpose Defined at POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate Standard deck, blocking servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3169 POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate/async Standard deck, returns a task servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3240 GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/status/{id} Poll a task (legacy path) servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3282 POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/export Re-export an existing deck servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1642 POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/edit Patch slide content and export servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3301 POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/derive Copy a deck with patched content and export servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3352 POST /api/v2/ppt/presentation/generate/smart Smart deck, blocking servers/fastapi/api/v2/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:229 POST /api/v2/ppt/presentation/generate/smart/async Smart deck, returns a task servers/fastapi/api/v2/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:264 GET /api/v1/async-tasks List tasks with filters servers/fastapi/api/v1/async_tasks/router.py:20 GET /api/v1/async-tasks/status/{id} Poll any task servers/fastapi/api/v1/async_tasks/router.py:69 POST /api/v1/webhook/subscribe Register a webhook servers/fastapi/api/v1/webhook/router.py:23 DELETE /api/v1/webhook/unsubscribe Remove a webhook servers/fastapi/api/v1/webhook/router.py:40 GET /api/v1/mock/presentation-generation-completed Sample success payload servers/fastapi/api/v1/mock/router.py:12 GET /api/v1/mock/presentation-generation-failed Sample failure payload servers/fastapi/api/v1/mock/router.py:26 POST /api/v1/ppt/files/upload Multipart upload of source files servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/files.py:79 POST /api/v1/ppt/files/mcp-upload Base64 upload of source files servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/files.py:103

Every endpoint is also listed in the Endpoint index.

Gotcha

POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/export exists because a long blocking /generate call can be cut by a proxy or a client timeout after the deck was already saved; its docstring says so (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1649). With the presentation_id in hand you can export again (body {"export_as": "pdf"}) without regenerating. The catch is getting that id: a failed sync response does not contain it, while an async task carries it in data from the start.

docs.title: Step 2: Authenticate as a program
docs.text: With account login enabled, SessionAuthMiddleware requires authentication for every /api/ path except five public auth routes (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:30). It resolves a principal in resolve_request_principal (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/principal.py:22): a presenton_session JWT cookie first, otherwise an Authorization: Bearer <token> header verified as an API key.

docs.title: 2.1 Key format
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py (excerpt)
API_KEY_PREFIX = "sk-presenton-"
DEFAULT_EXPIRY_DAYS = 90
MAX_EXPIRY_DAYS = 365
API_KEY_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{16}$")
# ...
def build_api_key(api_key_id: str, secret: str) -> str:
    return f"{API_KEY_PREFIX}{api_key_id}.{secret}"

A key looks like sk-presenton-0123456789abcdef.<secret>: a 16-hex-character id (secrets.token_hex(8), also the api_keys.id primary key) and a secret from secrets.token_urlsafe(40). parse_api_key rejects anything without the prefix, a dot, a valid id, or a secret of at least 32 characters (servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:50). Only a password hash of the secret is used for verification; an encrypted copy of the whole token (Fernet, keyed by a SHA-256 of the auth secret) lets an admin reveal it again.

docs.title: 2.2 Verification
docs.text:
verify_api_key (servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:107) loads the row by id, rejects it if revoked or expired, checks the secret against secret_hash (upgrading the hash if the helper asks), requires the owning user to be active, and stamps last_used_at. The middleware then:

  1. Sets request.state.auth_principal with method="api_key".
  2. Mints an internal session JWT for that user (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:123). The export step needs it: the headless browser that renders the deck must load the editor page as that user, and build_export_cookie_header turns it into a presenton_session= cookie (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1486).
  3. Sets the owner context variables, so every row created during the request is stamped with the key owner's id and every ORM SELECT is filtered to it.

Keys are issued, listed, revealed and revoked under /api/v1/admin/api-keys from an admin browser session (servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:44). An API key can never call those admin routes, nor the handful of admin-only paths listed at servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:100. The full model, including hashing and tenancy, is in Auth and multi-user.

Note

When DISABLE_AUTH is enabled (Electron's single-user mode), the middleware returns before any of this and requests run without an owner (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:59). The README states that external REST and MCP access are not available in the Electron app.

docs.title: 3.1 Every field of GeneratePresentationRequest
docs.text:
Defined at servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py:8:

Field Type Default Behavior content str required The prompt. May be "" when slides_markdown or files carries the content. slides_markdown list[str] or null null One Markdown string per slide. Skips outline generation; n_slides becomes its length. instructions str or null null Extra guidance, passed to outline, structure and slide-content prompts. tone Tone "default" default, casual, professional, funny, educational, sales_pitch (servers/fastapi/enums/tone.py:4). verbosity Verbosity "standard" concise, standard, text-heavy (servers/fastapi/enums/verbosity.py:4). web_search bool false Grounds the outline step; see Images, icons, web search. n_slides int or null null 1 to 50. null lets the model choose. language str or null null Blank or null means auto-detect. template str "general" A bundled template name, a TemplateV2 id, or custom-<id>. include_table_of_contents bool false Needs n_slides >= 3 when n_slides is given. Ignored with slides_markdown. include_title_slide bool true Affects the outline prompt and TOC math. files list[str] or null null Paths returned by /api/v1/ppt/files/upload or /files/mcp-upload. export_as "pptx" or "pdf" "pptx" Output format of the exported file. trigger_webhook bool false Declared, documented in the OpenAPI schema, and never read (see Step 8).

Gotcha

The README's API table says language defaults to "English". The code default is None, which the outline prompt renders as auto-detect (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_outlines.py:170). Send "language": "English" explicitly if you need it.

docs.title: 3.2 Validation before any work
docs.text:
check_if_api_request_is_valid (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2620) allocates the presentation_id (a fresh uuid4) and rejects bad input with HTTP 400:

Condition detail content, slides_markdown and files all empty Either content or slides markdown or files is required to generate presentation n_slides <= 0 Number of slides must be greater than 0 n_slides > 50 or more than 50 slides_markdown items Number of slides cannot be greater than 50 include_table_of_contents with n_slides < 3 Number of slides cannot be less than 3 if table of contents is included template not in DB and not a bundled name Template not found. Please use a valid template.

The limit 50 is MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES (servers/fastapi/constants/presentation.py:4). Template lookup strips a custom- prefix, tries TemplateV2 by id, then resolve_default_template_id for bundled names such as general, modern or swift (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:212). If found in the DB, request.template is rewritten to the row id. Type errors (for example "export_as": "docx") are rejected earlier by Pydantic with HTTP 422.

docs.title: 3.3 slides_markdown and files
docs.text:
With slides_markdown, each string becomes a SlideOutlineModel(content=...) directly (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2838). Each item is still passed through the outline word limit (MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS, default 100) by the model's validator, and the LLM still chooses layouts and fills the template schema, so text can be rephrased. http(s) image URLs ending in .jpg, .jpeg, .png or .webp inside an item are used for that slide's image slots instead of generating images.

files are resolved by DocumentsLoader, which only accepts paths inside the server's temp upload area (servers/fastapi/services/documents_loader.py:171). Upload first:

curl -s -X POST http://localhost:5001/api/v1/ppt/files/upload \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PRESENTON_KEY" \
  -F "files=@quarterly-report.pdf"
# ["/tmp/presenton/<owner>/<uuid>/quarterly-report.pdf"]

The returned array (path shape shown schematically) goes into files unchanged. Document parsing is covered in Document ingestion.

docs.title: 4.1 Execution order
docs.text:
generate_presentation_sync (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3170) validates, then awaits generate_presentation_handler (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2684) with async_status=None. The handler is the same code the async path runs. Its stages, which Standard generation pipeline explains in depth:

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant API as generate_presentation_sync
    participant H as generate_presentation_handler
    participant L as LLM
    participant A as Image and icon providers
    participant X as Export runtime
    participant W as WebhookService
    C->>API: POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate
    API->>API: check_if_api_request_is_valid
    API->>H: request, presentation_id, async_status None
    H->>L: outline (skipped for slides_markdown)
    H->>H: resolve template layout
    H->>L: structure (skipped for ordered layouts)
    loop batches of 10 slides
        H->>L: slide content, concurrently
        H->>A: asset tasks start in background
    end
    H->>A: gather all asset tasks
    H->>H: commit presentation, slides, image assets
    H->>X: export_presentation as pptx or pdf
    H-->>W: fire and forget, presentation.generation.completed
    H-->>API: PresentationPathAndEditPath
    API-->>C: 200 JSON with path and edit_path
  1. Outline. Unless slides_markdown is set: load files into additional_context, compute the outline count (adjusted for a TOC), store generation context in Mem0, stream generate_ppt_outline into a string, parse it with dirtyjson, and normalize it. Fewer outlines than requested is a 400 (Failed to generate presentation outlines with requested number of slides. Please try again.); extra outlines are silently truncated (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2830).
  2. Layout. _resolve_generation_layout loads the TemplateV2 row and returns the layout payload, a PresentationLayoutModel, fonts and theme. A bundled template whose row was never imported yields 503 Bundled template '<name>' is not available. Restart the service to import bundled templates. (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:279).
  3. Structure. Ordered layouts map one to one; otherwise an LLM picks a layout index per outline. Out-of-range indices are replaced with random valid ones.
  4. Table of contents layouts are inserted when requested.
  5. Slides are generated in batches of 10 with asyncio.gather, and each slide's asset task starts immediately so images overlap the next batch's LLM calls (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2985).
  6. Persist. After all asset tasks finish, the presentation, slides and generated ImageAsset rows are committed in one transaction (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3088).
  7. Export via export_presentation(presentation_id, title, export_as, cookie_header=...) (servers/fastapi/utils/export_utils.py:43), described in PPTX and PDF export.
  8. Respond and fire the completion webhook.

docs.title: 4.2 The response model
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/models/presentation_and_path.py
from pydantic import BaseModel
import uuid


class PresentationAndPath(BaseModel):
    presentation_id: uuid.UUID
    path: str


class PresentationPathAndEditPath(PresentationAndPath):
    edit_path: str

path is the exported file's location on the server. ExportTaskService._move_export_to_owner places it in $APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/exports/users/<owner_id>/ when there is an owner (servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:773). The Docker image sets APP_DATA_DIRECTORY=/app_data (Dockerfile:82), so the filesystem path doubles as the URL path that nginx serves from /app_data/exports/ behind an auth subrequest (nginx.conf:167). edit_path is always /presentation?id=<presentation_id>, a Next.js route.
