                )

Four things happen at once: the hash changes, auth_version increments (killing the admin's JWTs even before the secret rotation), every API key in the database is deleted (not only the admin's), and the signing secret is regenerated (killing every other user's JWT). The admin's id is preserved, so owned rows keep pointing at the same account.

Gotcha: RESET_AUTH and AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV are not one-shot

Both flags are evaluated on every startup. If you leave RESET_AUTH=true in your compose file, every container restart rotates the secret, deletes all API keys and logs out every user. The README tells operators to remove the flag after a successful startup. The two flags are behaviorally identical in code; they differ only in intent.

Gotcha: plain AUTH_USERNAME/AUTH_PASSWORD only matter on an empty database

Without one of the two flags, the env credentials are used only when no user exists at all (bootstrap.py:91 onward). Changing AUTH_PASSWORD on a running deployment does nothing until you also set AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV=true for one start.

docs.title: 3.3 Migrating a pre-multi-user install
docs.text:
Older Presenton releases had a single account stored only in userConfig.json as AUTH_USERNAME plus an AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH of the form pbkdf2_sha256$<iterations>$<salt>$<digest>. Bootstrap picks those up through get_legacy_admin_credentials (config.py:84) and inserts them as the primary admin without rehashing. Two cooperating pieces make that work:

  • LegacyAwarePasswordHelper.verify_and_update (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/users.py:31) recognises the pbkdf2_sha256$ prefix, verifies with verify_legacy_password_hash (config.py:50, hmac.compare_digest on a PBKDF2-SHA256 digest), and returns a modern replacement hash. Login then stores the replacement (router.py:176), so the legacy hash disappears after the first successful sign-in.
  • LoginCredentialsRequest allows passwords of 6 characters (schemas.py:45) because the legacy system did; new passwords still need 8.

Finally _backfill_legacy_ownership (bootstrap.py:128) claims all orphaned data for the admin:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/bootstrap.py (excerpt)
    for model in owned_models:
        await session.execute(
            update(model)
            .where(model.owner_id.is_(None))
            .values(owner_id=admin.id)
        )
    # Built-in templates intentionally remain shared; only custom templates
    # migrate into the bootstrap admin's private workspace.
    await session.execute(
        update(TemplateV2)
        .where(TemplateV2.owner_id.is_(None), TemplateV2.is_default.is_(False))
        .values(owner_id=admin.id)
    )

The owned models are presentations, slides, async tasks, async presentation generation tasks, chat history, image assets and webhook subscriptions. This runs on every startup when an admin exists, so any row created with a NULL owner (for example while DISABLE_AUTH was on) is adopted by the admin on the next boot.

Gotcha: toggling DISABLE_AUTH off hands desktop data to the admin

Rows written while auth was disabled have owner_id = NULL. The next startup with an admin present runs the backfill, and they all become the primary admin's private data. Normal users never see them.

docs.title: Step 4: Login, the cookie, and the JWT
4.1 POST /api/v1/auth/login
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/auth/login
Content-Type: application/json

{"username": "ADMIN", "password": "secret123"}

login (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:155) executes:

  1. If there are no users: 428 {"detail": "Login setup is required"}.
  2. Look up the user with func.lower(User.username) == username.casefold().
  3. If missing or inactive: hash the submitted password anyway (PASSWORD_HELPER.hash(body.password), a timing equalizer so "unknown user" and "wrong password" take similar time) and return 401 {"detail": "Unauthorized"}.
  4. PASSWORD_HELPER.verify_and_update(password, user.hashed_password); on failure 401. On success with a replacement hash (legacy or outdated algorithm), store it and commit.
  5. get_jwt_strategy().write_token(user) produces the token.
  6. Build the JSON body and attach the cookie with _set_login_cookie.

The response:

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: presenton_session=eyJhbGciOi...; HttpOnly; Max-Age=2592000; Path=/; SameSite=lax
Content-Type: application/json

{"configured": true, "authenticated": true,
 "id": "3f6c...", "username": "admin", "role": "admin",
 "created_at": "2026-11-02T10:00:00+00:00"}

The token is never in the body; the integration test asserts "access_token" not in payload and that the set-cookie header contains HttpOnly (servers/fastapi/tests/integration/test_auth_endpoints.py:134).

servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py (excerpt)
def _secure_request(request: Request) -> bool:
    return (
        request.headers.get("x-forwarded-proto", "").lower() == "https"
        or request.url.scheme == "https"
    )


def _set_login_cookie(response: JSONResponse, token: str, request: Request) -> None:
    response.set_cookie(
        SESSION_COOKIE_NAME,
        token,
        max_age=SESSION_TTL_SECONDS,
        httponly=True,
        secure=_secure_request(request),
        samesite="lax",
        path="/",
    )
Cookie attribute Value Source Name presenton_session config.py:11 Max-Age 2,592,000 s (30 days) config.py:12 HttpOnly always router.py:51 Secure only when X-Forwarded-Proto: https or the request scheme is https router.py:39 SameSite lax router.py:53 Path / router.py:54

Gotcha: there is no login rate limit

test_repeated_failed_logins_are_not_rate_limited posts ten wrong passwords and expects ten 401s (servers/fastapi/tests/integration/test_auth_endpoints.py:244). Brute-force protection, if you need it, belongs in your reverse proxy.

Gotcha: lower() versus casefold()

Login compares SQL lower(username) with Python str.casefold(). For ASCII names they agree. For some non-ASCII names they can differ (for example casefold() maps "ß" to "ss", and SQLite's built-in lower() only folds ASCII), which could make such a user unable to sign in. The username pattern ^\S+$ does allow non-ASCII characters.

docs.title: 4.2 Inside the JWT
docs.text:
VersionedJWTStrategy (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/users.py:136) subclasses FastAPI Users' JWTStrategy and overrides both directions:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/users.py (excerpt)
    async def write_token(self, user: User) -> str:
        return generate_jwt(
            {
                "sub": str(user.id),
                "av": user.auth_version,
                "aud": self.token_audience,
            },
            self.encode_key,
            self.lifetime_seconds,
            algorithm=self.algorithm,
        )

The payload has three Presenton-visible claims plus the exp that generate_jwt adds from lifetime_seconds:

{"sub": "3f6c0d4e-...", "av": 1, "aud": ["fastapi-users:auth"], "exp": 1764673200}

The algorithm and audience are not set in Presenton code; they are the FastAPI Users JWTStrategy defaults (HMAC with the AUTH_SECRET_KEY secret, audience fastapi-users:auth in the library). read_token (users.py:137) rejects a token when decoding fails, when sub is missing, when av is not an int, when the user no longer exists, when is_active is false, or when user.auth_version != av. That last check is the revocation mechanism: the admin password reset endpoint increments the target user's auth_version (servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:231), so that user's existing cookies stop working immediately without a session table.

docs.title: 4.3 Why FastAPI Users is configured but its routers are not mounted
docs.text: users.py:187 builds a CookieTransport, an AuthenticationBackend named cookie-jwt and a FastAPIUsers instance, but no FASTAPI_USERS.get_auth_router(...) is ever included. The comment at users.py:185 explains: the explicit /login route handles the dynamic Secure flag, and the backend object only "centralizes the package's account/auth abstractions". What Presenton actually uses from the library is BaseUserManager, BaseUserDatabase, PasswordHelper, JWTStrategy, and the decode_jwt/generate_jwt helpers. UserManager disables self-service flows (the token secrets at users.py:110 are placeholders) and enforces 8 to 128 character passwords in validate_password (users.py:116). The password hashing itself is the FastAPI Users PasswordHelper, which wraps pwdlib (locked at 0.3.0 alongside argon2-cffi and bcrypt in servers/fastapi/uv.lock).

docs.title: 4.4 Status, verify and logout
docs.text:
Endpoint Auth required by middleware Handler Response GET /api/v1/auth/status No router.py:58 {"configured", "authenticated", "username", "user_id", "role"} from the cookie only GET /api/v1/auth/verify No (it authenticates itself) router.py:81 {"authenticated": true, id, username, role, created_at, "method": "jwt" or "api_key"} or 401/403 POST /api/v1/auth/setup No router.py:110 see Step 3.1 POST /api/v1/auth/login No router.py:155 see Step 4.1 POST /api/v1/auth/logout No router.py:191 {"success": true} plus a cookie deletion with the same attributes

status reads only the cookie (read_user_from_cookie, users.py:202); an API key never makes status report authenticated: true. verify uses the full principal resolution (cookie, then bearer key) and is the endpoint nginx calls for static files (Step 8).

Logout is stateless: it deletes the cookie in the browser. The JWT itself stays valid until expiry or until auth_version/the secret changes. LogoutButton calls it and always navigates to / even if the call fails (servers/nextjs/components/Auth/LogoutButton.tsx:36, :59).

sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser
  participant NG as nginx
  participant F as FastAPI
  participant DB as Database
  participant NX as Next.js
  B->>NG: POST /api/v1/auth/login (JSON username, password)
  NG->>F: proxy_pass 127.0.0.1:8000
  F->>F: SessionAuthMiddleware sees public auth path, call_next
  F->>DB: SELECT count(*) FROM user
  F->>DB: SELECT user WHERE lower(username) = casefold(input)
  F->>F: PASSWORD_HELPER.verify_and_update
  F->>DB: UPDATE hashed_password (only if a replacement hash exists)
  F->>F: write_token(sub, av, aud) signed with AUTH_SECRET_KEY
  F-->>B: 200 JSON user + Set-Cookie presenton_session (HttpOnly, Lax, 30 days)
  B->>NG: GET /dashboard (Cookie presenton_session)
  NG->>NX: proxy_pass 127.0.0.1:3000
  NX->>F: GET /api/v1/auth/status (forwarded Cookie)
  F->>DB: SELECT user by sub, compare auth_version
  F-->>NX: authenticated true, role admin
  NX-->>B: rendered dashboard

docs.title: Step 5: Resolving a principal on every request
5.1 Middleware order
docs.text: servers/fastapi/api/main.py:94 to :103 registers middleware in this order: CORSMiddleware, UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware, SessionAuthMiddleware, and then the @app.middleware("http") icon fallback at main.py:106. Starlette wraps each newly added middleware around the previous ones, so at runtime a request passes through the icon fallback, then SessionAuthMiddleware, then UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware, then CORS, then the router. Authentication therefore runs before CORS and before provider settings are reloaded into os.environ.

docs.title: 5.2 Which paths need auth
5.3 The dispatch sequence
docs.text:
SessionAuthMiddleware.dispatch (middlewares.py:55) runs these steps:

  1. Desktop transport guard. desktop_request_denied(request) runs first, for every path, including public ones (Step 9).
  2. Auth disabled. If DISABLE_AUTH is truthy, the request passes through after a possible Presenton Cloud proxy hop, with no principal and no owner context.
  3. Skip OPTIONS, non-protected paths, and the five public auth paths.
  4. Setup gate. If the user table is empty: 428 {"detail": "Login setup is required", "setup_required": true}.
  5. Resolve (principal, user) = await resolve_request_principal(request, session). None means 401 {"detail": "Unauthorized"}.
  6. Admin-only gate (below).
  7. Publish request.state.auth_principal, current_user, auth_username, and for API keys a freshly minted internal_session_token JWT.
  8. Set owner contextvars to principal.user_id and principal.is_admin.
  9. For cookie sessions, give maybe_proxy_presenton_cloud_request a chance to answer (provider proxying is covered in Configuration and LLM providers).
  10. For /app_data/ paths, run is_app_data_path_authorized; failure is 404 {"detail": "Asset not found"} (not 403, to avoid confirming existence).
  11. call_next, and in finally reset both contextvars.

docs.title: 5.4 resolve_request_principal: cookie first, then API key
5.5 Admin-only paths
5.6 Route-level dependencies
docs.text:
Some routes add their own checks on top of the middleware:

  • get_current_user (users.py:211) and get_current_admin (users.py:219) read only the cookie. The admin router's user and key endpoints depend on get_current_admin, so they need a cookie even before the middleware rule.
  • require_settings_admin (servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:131) allows the provider-settings endpoints when DISABLE_AUTH is on (Electron) and otherwise requires a cookie admin.
  • require_presenton_manager (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/presenton_oauth.py:65) does the same for the Presenton Cloud device flow.

docs.title: Step 6: API keys end to end
6.1 Format
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py (excerpt)
API_KEY_PREFIX = "sk-presenton-"
DEFAULT_EXPIRY_DAYS = 90
MAX_EXPIRY_DAYS = 365
API_KEY_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{16}$")
# ...
def build_api_key(api_key_id: str, secret: str) -> str:
    return f"{API_KEY_PREFIX}{api_key_id}.{secret}"

A key looks like sk-presenton-1f2e3d4c5b6a7980.Wq3... (prefix, 16 hex ID, dot, a secrets.token_urlsafe(40) secret of roughly 54 characters). parse_api_key (api_keys.py:50) rejects anything without the prefix, without the dot, with an ID that is not exactly 16 lowercase hex characters, or with a secret shorter than 32 characters. The ID half is a lookup key; only the secret half is hashed.

docs.title: 6.2 Creation: POST /api/v1/admin/api-keys
docs.text:
The admin panel (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/admin/AdminPanel.tsx:310) sends:

{"user_id": "8b1d...-...", "label": "Automation", "expiry_days": 90}

AdminCreateApiKeyRequest (schemas.py:56) enforces label 1 to 120 characters (default "API client") and expiry_days 1 to 365 (default 90); the UI offers 30, 90, 180 and 365. create_api_key (admin/router.py:60) checks that the target user exists and is active (404 "Active user not found" otherwise) and calls issue_api_key (api_keys.py:79):

servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py (excerpt)
    secret = secrets.token_urlsafe(40)
    api_key_id = secrets.token_hex(8)
    token = build_api_key(api_key_id, secret)
    api_key = ApiKey(
        id=api_key_id,
        user_id=user_id,
        created_by_id=created_by_id,
        label=label.strip() or "API client",
        secret_hash=PASSWORD_HELPER.hash(secret),
        token_encrypted=encrypt_api_key(token),
        expires_at=get_current_utc_datetime() + timedelta(days=expiry_days),
    )

The 201 response is ApiKeyCreated (schemas.py:75), the public fields plus the plaintext token:

{"id": "1f2e3d4c5b6a7980", "user_id": "8b1d...", "created_by_id": "3f6c...",
 "label": "Automation", "created_at": "...", "expires_at": "...",
 "last_used_at": null, "revoked_at": null,
 "token": "sk-presenton-1f2e3d4c5b6a7980.Wq3..."}

The admin panel copies the token to the clipboard and keeps it in component state.

docs.title: 6.3 List, reveal, revoke
docs.text:
Endpoint Handler Behavior GET /api/v1/admin/api-keys admin/router.py:44 All keys for all users, newest first, as ApiKeyPublic (no token, no hash) GET /api/v1/admin/api-keys/{id}/token admin/router.py:85 Decrypts token_encrypted; 404 unknown, 410 revoked, 409 undecryptable; sets Cache-Control: no-store POST /api/v1/admin/api-keys/{id}/revoke admin/router.py:111 Sets revoked_at once (idempotent) and returns the key

There is no hard delete endpoint for keys. Revocation is permanent: verify_api_key rejects any key with revoked_at set.

Gotcha: keys are reversible, not only hashed

Because the admin can re-display a key, the full token is stored encrypted with a key derived from AUTH_SECRET_KEY. Anyone who can read both the database and userConfig.json can recover every active API key. Protect app_data accordingly.

docs.title: 6.4 Verification on each request
docs.text:
verify_api_key (api_keys.py:107) runs: parse, session.get(ApiKey, id), reject revoked, reject if expires_at <= now (naive datetimes are treated as UTC by _utc_aware), PASSWORD_HELPER.verify_and_update(secret, secret_hash), load the user and reject inactive or missing, then set last_used_at = now, store any upgraded hash, and commit. Every API-key request therefore performs a password-hash verification and a write.

Back in the middleware, an API-key principal causes one extra step:

servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py (excerpt)
            if principal.method == "api_key" and user is not None:
                request.state.internal_session_token = (
                    await get_jwt_strategy().write_token(user)
                )

That JWT is what downstream code hands to the export browser so headless Chromium can load the user's slides with a normal cookie (Step 7).

sequenceDiagram
  participant C as API client
  participant NG as nginx
  participant MW as SessionAuthMiddleware
  participant K as verify_api_key
  participant DB as Database
  participant H as Route handler
  C->>NG: GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/all with Authorization Bearer sk-presenton-ID.SECRET
  NG->>MW: proxy_pass 127.0.0.1:8000
  MW->>MW: desktop_request_denied returns None (not Electron)
  MW->>DB: SELECT count(*) FROM user
  MW->>MW: no presenton_session cookie, use bearer branch
  MW->>K: verify_api_key(session, token)
  K->>K: parse_api_key gives 16-hex id and secret
  K->>DB: SELECT api_keys WHERE id
  K->>K: check revoked_at, expires_at, verify secret hash
  K->>DB: SELECT user, UPDATE last_used_at, COMMIT
  K-->>MW: VerifiedApiKey(api_key_id, user)
  MW->>MW: not an admin-only path, mint internal_session_token
  MW->>MW: set owner_id and is_admin contextvars
  MW->>H: call_next
  H->>DB: SELECT presentations (do_orm_execute adds owner_id filter)
  H-->>C: 200 only this user's presentations
  MW->>MW: finally reset contextvars

docs.title: 6.5 The same keys on MCP
docs.text: The MCP server (port 8001, behind nginx /mcp) validates the same keys with PresentonTokenVerifier (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:285): it ignores anything that does not start with sk-presenton-, calls verify_api_key, and stores a one-hour JWT (MCP_INTERNAL_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS = 60 * 60, mcp_server.py:39) in the access-token claims. When the MCP server calls back into FastAPI, attach_request_auth_header (mcp_server.py:365) sends that JWT as a presenton_session cookie rather than forwarding the raw key. The MCP tool surface itself is covered in REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP.

docs.title: Step 7: Internal auth for trusted server-side callers
docs.text:
Several server-side components must call Presenton as the user: the export runtime opens /pdf-maker in headless Chromium, background tasks finish work after the HTTP request has returned, and the MCP server proxies tool calls. None of them has the user's password. They all use the same trick: mint a short or normal-lifetime JWT for the current owner and present it as a cookie.

authenticated_internal_request_headers (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/internal.py:10) packages that:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/internal.py (excerpt)
async def authenticated_internal_request_headers() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Issue a database-backed JWT for the current trusted internal request."""
    if is_disable_auth_enabled():
        cookie = desktop_cookie_header()
        return {"Cookie": cookie} if cookie else {}

    owner_id = get_current_owner_id()
    if owner_id is None:
        return {}

    async with async_session_maker() as session:
        user = await session.get(User, owner_id)
        if user is None or not user.is_active:
            return {}
        token = await get_jwt_strategy().write_token(user)
    return {"Cookie": f"{SESSION_COOKIE_NAME}={token}"}

In this snapshot that helper is exercised by servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_internal_auth_headers.py but no production module imports it. The production paths build the same header inline:

  • build_export_cookie_header (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1473) prefers, in order: the desktop cookie (Electron, appended to any incoming cookie), the request's own Cookie header, request.state.internal_session_token (API-key callers), and finally the bare session cookie.
  • Background tasks receive that header plus the owner ID as arguments and re-enter the owner context themselves (Step 10.3).

The export path that consumes the header is described in PPTX and PDF export.

docs.title: Step 8: nginx auth_request and per-user asset paths
8.1 Why nginx needs a subrequest
docs.text:
In Docker, nginx serves /app_data/* directly from disk with alias for speed, so the FastAPI middleware never sees those requests. The auth_request module fills the gap:

nginx.conf (excerpt)
    location = /_auth_check {
      internal;
      proxy_pass http://localhost:8000/api/v1/auth/verify;
      proxy_pass_request_body off;
      proxy_set_header Content-Length "";
      proxy_set_header X-Original-URI $request_uri;
      proxy_set_header Host $host;
      proxy_set_header Cookie $http_cookie;
      proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;
    }
    # ...
    location /app_data/images/ {
      auth_request /_auth_check;
      alias /app_data/images/;
      disable_symlinks on;
      expires 1y;
      add_header Cache-Control "private, max-age=31536000";
    }
Location auth_request Notes /app_data/images/, /exports/, /uploads/, /pptx-to-html/, /pptx-to-json/ yes private, owner-checked /app_data/fonts/, /app_data/templates/ no shared, public /mcp, /mcp/ no FastMCP validates the bearer key itself (nginx.conf:79)

/api/v1/auth/verify resolves the principal from the forwarded Cookie or Authorization, then checks the X-Original-URI header with is_app_data_path_authorized (router.py:96). nginx treats 2xx as allow and 401/403 as deny. All private locations also set disable_symlinks on, so even an authorized path cannot follow a planted symlink.

docs.title: 8.2 The ownership rules
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py defines the namespaces:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py (excerpt)
PRIVATE_APP_DATA_ROOTS = {
    "images",
    "exports",
    "uploads",
    "pptx-to-html",
    "pptx-to-json",
}
SHARED_APP_DATA_ROOTS = {"fonts", "templates"}
# ...
def _namespace_authorized(parts: tuple[str, ...], *, user_id: uuid.UUID, is_admin: bool) -> bool:

    root = parts[0]
    if root in SHARED_APP_DATA_ROOTS:
        return True
    if root not in PRIVATE_APP_DATA_ROOTS or len(parts) < 2:
        return False

    relative_parts = parts[1:]
    if relative_parts[0] == "users":
        return (
            len(relative_parts) >= 3
            and relative_parts[1] == str(user_id)
        )

    # Pre-multi-user assets remain in the legacy root and belong only to the
    # migrated primary administrator.
    return is_admin

Concretely:

URL Caller Result /app_data/fonts/Inter.ttf anyone allowed /app_data/images/users/<own-uuid>/a.png that user allowed /app_data/images/users/<other-uuid>/a.png any user, including admin denied /app_data/images/users/<own-uuid> (no file segment) owner denied (needs at least 3 parts after the root) /app_data/images/legacy.png admin allowed (legacy pre-multi-user layout) /app_data/images/legacy.png normal user denied /app_data/fastapi.db or /app_data/userConfig.json anyone denied (root not in either set)

New files land in the per-user layout because _owned_directory (servers/fastapi/utils/asset_directory_utils.py:23) appends users/<owner_id> whenever an owner is in context.

docs.title: 8.3 Traversal and alias defenses
docs.text:
normalized_app_data_parts (assets.py:47) is deliberately paranoid:

  1. Take only the URL path (urlsplit).
  2. URL-decode repeatedly, up to 8 times, until stable; if it is still changing after 8 rounds, fail closed. This defeats %252e%252e style double-encoding regardless of how many layers a proxy decodes.
  3. Reject NUL bytes, backslashes, and anything not starting with /app_data/.
  4. Split and reject empty, . or .. segments.

is_app_data_path_authorized (assets.py:78) then authorizes twice: once on the visible namespace, and once on the canonical target after os.path.realpath, relative to the realpath of the asset root (so a symlinked volume root is allowed, but a symlink inside it that points into another user's folder is not). When FastAPI itself serves the file (Electron, or direct access to port 8000), _OwnerScopedStaticFiles.lookup_path (assets.py:25) repeats the check on the exact filesystem path StaticFiles resolved, and returns "not found" on failure.

docs.title: Step 9: DISABLE_AUTH and the desktop transport guard
9.1 What DISABLE_AUTH turns off
docs.text:
is_disable_auth_enabled() (servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:79) is true for 1, true, yes or on. When it is true:

  • The middleware skips principal resolution entirely (middlewares.py:59).
  • /api/v1/auth/status returns a fixed admin: {"configured": true, "authenticated": true, "username": "electron", "user_id": null, "role": "admin"} (router.py:63); /verify returns "method": "local".
  • Settings and Presenton Cloud management dependencies allow the call.
  • No owner contextvar is set, so the ORM filter is inactive and every row is visible (Step 10).
  • Next.js mirrors the same switch through isAuthDisabled() (servers/nextjs/utils/auth.ts:18), which reads window.env.DISABLE_AUTH in the renderer (exposed by the Electron preload) or process.env.DISABLE_AUTH on the server.

Electron starts both servers with DISABLE_AUTH=true unless ELECTRON_DISABLE_AUTH or DISABLE_AUTH is explicitly set to a false value (electron/app/main.ts:150). The full desktop process model is in Electron desktop app.

Gotcha: never set DISABLE_AUTH=true on a shared server

With auth disabled, any network caller is the admin and sees every user's presentations (the owner filter is off). The desktop guard below only engages when PRESENTON_ELECTRON=true; on Docker nothing replaces the login.

docs.title: 9.2 The desktop guard
docs.text:
Disabling accounts on a loopback server is still dangerous: any local process, or any web page performing DNS rebinding against 127.0.0.1, could call the API. Electron therefore authenticates itself to its own servers with a per-launch capability token. The FastAPI half is desktop_request_denied (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/desktop.py:25):

servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/desktop.py (excerpt)
def desktop_request_denied(request: Request) -> JSONResponse | None:
    if os.getenv("PRESENTON_ELECTRON") != "true":
        return None

    token = desktop_token()
    origins = set(filter(None, os.getenv("PRESENTON_DESKTOP_ORIGINS", "").split(",")))
    hosts = {urlsplit(origin).netloc for origin in origins}
    if len(token) < 32 or not hosts:
        return JSONResponse({"detail": "Desktop session unavailable"}, status_code=503)
    # Check the actual Host, not forwarded headers: DNS rebinding must not turn
    # an attacker's hostname into an authorized local application origin.
    origin = request.headers.get("origin")
    if request.headers.get("host") not in hosts or (
        origin is not None and origin not in origins
    ):
        return JSONResponse({"detail": "Forbidden desktop origin"}, status_code=403)
    # ...
    supplied = request.headers.get(DESKTOP_TOKEN_HEADER) or request.cookies.get(
        DESKTOP_COOKIE_NAME, ""
    )
    if not hmac.compare_digest(supplied.encode(), token.encode()):
        return JSONResponse({"detail": "Unauthorized"}, status_code=401)
    return None
Check Failure PRESENTON_DESKTOP_TOKEN shorter than 32 characters, or no PRESENTON_DESKTOP_ORIGINS 503 Desktop session unavailable (fail closed) Host header not one of the two loopback host:port values 403 Forbidden desktop origin Origin present but not exactly one of the two origins 403 CORS preflight from an exact origin passes so CORSMiddleware can answer Token in x-presenton-desktop-token header or presenton_desktop_session cookie does not match 401 Unauthorized (constant-time compare)

The Next.js half, desktopRequestDenied (servers/nextjs/lib/desktop-auth.ts:14), implements the same Host, Origin and token rules with timingSafeEqual (it has no CORS preflight exemption, because Next.js routes do not need one) and runs first in proxy() (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:98) for every request except _next/static and favicon.ico (the matcher at proxy.ts:175), so pages, the image optimizer and /pdf-maker are covered too. servers/nextjs/tests/desktop-security.test.mjs:59 asserts that ten different URLs, including /dashboard and /_next/image?url=private, return 401 without the token.

The token is generated, attached and kept off the renderer by the Electron main process; Step 6 of Electron desktop app traces that flow.

docs.title: 10.1 The two contextvars
docs.text: servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/context.py is 34 lines: two ContextVars (presenton_current_owner_id, default None, and presenton_current_owner_is_admin, default False) with get, set and reset helpers. The middleware sets them around call_next and resets them in finally (middlewares.py:127 to :152). Starlette runs the downstream app in a task that copies the current context, so route handlers and everything they call observe the values.

docs.title: 10.2 Automatic stamping and filtering in services/database.py
docs.text:
Isolation is enforced by two global SQLAlchemy ORM event listeners, not by hand-written WHERE clauses:

servers/fastapi/services/database.py (excerpt)
_STRICT_OWNER_MODELS = (
    PresentationModel,
    SlideModel,
    ChatHistoryMessageModel,
    ImageAsset,
    AsyncTaskModel,
    AsyncPresentationGenerationTaskModel,
    WebhookSubscription,
)


@event.listens_for(Session, "do_orm_execute")
def _scope_owned_selects(execute_state) -> None:
    """Apply tenant criteria to every ORM SELECT performed during a request."""
    owner_id = get_current_owner_id()
    if (
        owner_id is None
        or not execute_state.is_select
        or execute_state.execution_options.get("skip_owner_scope")
    ):
        return

    statement = execute_state.statement
    for model in _STRICT_OWNER_MODELS:
        statement = statement.options(
            with_loader_criteria(
                model,
                lambda row: row.owner_id == owner_id,
                include_aliases=True,
            )
        )
    # ...
  • Reads. _scope_owned_selects (database.py:67) adds with_loader_criteria(model, owner_id == current) for the seven strict models on every ORM SELECT, including joins and aliases. TemplateV2 gets a looser rule (database.py:87): the caller's own templates or owner_id IS NULL AND is_default, so built-in templates stay shared.
  • Writes. _stamp_new_owned_rows (database.py:100) runs on before_flush and overwrites owner_id on every new instance of those eight models with the current owner. In addition, each model's owner_id field has default_factory=get_current_owner_id (for example servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py:25), and exclude=True keeps owner_id out of API responses.
  • Escape hatch. Any statement executed with execution_options(skip_owner_scope=True) bypasses the read filter. In this snapshot, no production code passes that option (only database.py:74 mentions it).

docs.title: 10.3 Verifying with real endpoints
docs.text:
The dashboard list endpoint GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/all (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1499) builds select(PresentationModel, SlideModel).join(...) with no owner clause at all. It still returns only the caller's presentations because the event adds the criteria to both entities. The unit test test_owned_queries_are_isolated_and_only_default_templates_are_shared (servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_owner_isolation.py:14) proves exactly this: with owner A in context, select(PresentationModel) returns only A's row, and select(TemplateV2) returns only the shared default template, not an unowned custom one nor B's private one.

Bulk deletes are different. Smart regeneration deletes slides like this:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt)
    await sql_session.execute(
        delete(SlideModel).where(
            SlideModel.presentation == id,
            SlideModel.owner_id == get_current_owner_id(),
        )
    )

The explicit owner_id predicate (presentation.py:1633, and again at :2490, :3330, and in servers/fastapi/services/chat/sql_chat_history.py:137, :184) is required because the read filter checks execute_state.is_select and does nothing for DELETE or UPDATE statements.

Background tasks lose the request context, so they receive the owner explicitly and re-enter it. The async generation endpoint schedules _run_generate_presentation_task(..., get_current_owner_id()) (presentation.py:3270) and the task starts with:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt)
    owner_token = set_current_owner_id(owner_id)
    admin_token = set_current_owner_is_admin(False)

(presentation.py:3205). Template creation does the same: the endpoint passes get_current_owner_id() to the task (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:1616) and _run_create_template_task re-enters it with set_current_owner_id (template.py:1486).

Filesystem isolation follows the same owner ID: _owned_directory (servers/fastapi/utils/asset_directory_utils.py:23) for images, exports and uploads, and TempFileService._owner_base_dir_realpath (servers/fastapi/services/temp_file_service.py:21) for TEMP_DIRECTORY/<owner_id>.

Gotcha: admins are tenants too

Nothing in _scope_owned_selects consults is_admin. The administrator sees only presentations they own, exactly like a normal user. is_admin only widens access to legacy /app_data/<root>/<file> assets that predate the per-user layout.

Gotcha: new bulk statements must carry their own owner predicate

If you add an update(...) or delete(...) against an owned model, add Model.owner_id == get_current_owner_id() yourself. The ORM event will not protect you, and a missing predicate deletes other tenants' rows.

Gotcha: owner_id IS NULL in auth-disabled mode

With DISABLE_AUTH, get_current_owner_id() is None, the read filter is off, and Model.owner_id == None compiles to IS NULL in the delete predicates above. Desktop deletes therefore only touch unowned rows, which is all of them in a pure desktop database.

docs.title: Step 11: The admin panel endpoints
docs.text:
All routes live under /api/v1/admin (servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:41) and are double-guarded: by the middleware's admin-browser rule and by the route dependency.

Method and path Dependency Request Response and rules GET /users get_current_admin none PublicUser[] ordered by created_at desc, username asc POST /users get_current_admin {"username", "password"} (same rules as setup) 201 PublicUser; 409 "Username already exists" (case-insensitive); always is_superuser=False PUT /users/{id}/password get_current_admin {"password"} (8 to 128) Rehash and auth_version += 1; 403 for self or any superuser ("managed through deployment settings") DELETE /users/{id} get_current_admin none 204; 403 for self or superuser; cascades rows by FK and removes per-user directories GET/POST /api-keys, GET /api-keys/{id}/token, POST /api-keys/{id}/revoke get_current_admin see Step 6 see Step 6 GET /provider-settings require_settings_admin none Saved provider settings plus PRESENTON_CONNECTED and PRESENTON_EMAIL PUT /provider-settings require_settings_admin JSON object Saved settings; then update_env_with_user_config()

User deletion cleans up storage carefully:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py (excerpt)
    roots = (
        os.path.join(get_app_data_directory_env(), "images", "users"),
        os.path.join(get_app_data_directory_env(), "exports", "users"),
        os.path.join(get_app_data_directory_env(), "uploads", "users"),
        os.path.join(get_app_data_directory_env(), "pptx-to-html", "users"),
        os.path.join(get_app_data_directory_env(), "pptx-to-json", "users"),
        get_temp_directory_env() or "/tmp/presenton",
    )
    for root in roots:
        owned_dir = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(root, str(user_id)))
        root_dir = os.path.realpath(root)
        if owned_dir.startswith(f"{root_dir}{os.sep}") and os.path.isdir(owned_dir):
            shutil.rmtree(owned_dir)

Database rows go through ON DELETE CASCADE on every owner_id foreign key (for example servers/fastapi/models/sql/slide.py:17) and on api_keys.user_id/created_by_id. On SQLite those cascades only fire because services/database.py enables PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON on every new connection (servers/fastapi/services/database.py:45).

Gotcha: the primary admin password cannot be changed in the UI

The reset endpoint refuses superusers. The only way to change the admin's password is AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV=true with a new AUTH_PASSWORD for one startup (Step 3.2).

The Next.js page is a server component that calls requireAdminSession() before rendering AdminPanel (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/admin/page.tsx:8). The panel calls the endpoints above with credentials: "include". The UI side of settings and onboarding is in Settings, onboarding, auth UI.

docs.title: Step 12: Presenton OAuth (the cloud provider, not a login)
docs.text:
PRESENTON_OAUTH_ROUTER (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/presenton_oauth.py:29) is mounted under /api/v1/auth/presenton. Despite the folder, it does not sign anyone into Presenton. It links the installation to Presenton Cloud as a text-generation provider using the OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant (DEVICE_GRANT_TYPE = "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code"). The issuer and client ID are constants: https://api.presenton.ai and ptc_presenton_open_source (servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:7).

Endpoint Guard Upstream call GET /status any authenticated principal none; returns enabled, issuer, linked, can_manage, and the linked email only to managers POST /device/start admin cookie or DISABLE_AUTH POST {issuer}/oauth/device_authorization with client_id, device_name (max 120) POST /device/poll admin cookie or DISABLE_AUTH POST {issuer}/oauth/token, then GET {issuer}/oauth/userinfo, then store credentials POST /logout admin cookie or DISABLE_AUTH revoke and clear; if LLM == "presenton", set LLM to None

Details worth knowing:

  • Every upstream call goes through _provider_request (presenton_oauth.py:77) with a 15-second timeout and follow_redirects=False.
  • device/start validates that all six RFC fields are present, then overwrites verification_uri_complete with the plain verification_uri so the user code never appears in a URL, browser history or logs (presenton_oauth.py:204). Responses carry Cache-Control: no-store.
  • device/poll maps authorization_pending and slow_down to 202 {"status": "pending", "error": ...}, validates the profile with PresentonUserInfo, defaults expires_in to 30 days when absent, and in a finally block revokes the fresh access token if storing it failed (presenton_oauth.py:310).

How the stored credential is used for generation is covered in Configuration and LLM providers.

docs.title: Step 13: The Next.js side
docs.text:
Next.js has three auth helpers, all of which ask FastAPI rather than decoding tokens:

Helper File Used by Behavior proxy() servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:97 every request (middleware) Desktop guard; rewrites /api/v1, /api/v2, /app_data, /static to FastAPI when not behind nginx; gates Next's own /api/* routes requireAppSession() / requireAdminSession() servers/nextjs/utils/serverAuth.ts:94, :110 server layouts and pages Redirect to / or /?reason=unauthorized; non-admins on admin pages go to /dashboard authStatusForRequest() / requireAdminApi() servers/nextjs/lib/server-auth-role.ts:20, :56 route handlers such as app/api/user-config/route.ts 401/403 JSON responses

docs.title: 13.1 proxy() decision order
docs.text:
1. desktopRequestDenied (Electron only).
  2. Non-API, non-asset pages (except /pdf-maker) pass through; layouts protect them.
  3. /app_data/* and /static/* are rewritten to FastAPI at request time (needed in Electron, where there is no nginx and ports are random).
  4. /pdf-maker?exportSession=<jwt> converts the query parameter into an HttpOnly presenton_session cookie and redirects to the same URL without it (proxy.ts:114). This is how the export browser receives a session.
  5. With DISABLE_AUTH, continue.
  6. OPTIONS and exempt paths continue: /api/v1/auth/*, /api/telemetry-status, /api/update-svg, /api/export-presentation-data/* (proxy.ts:87).
  7. Authorization: Bearer sk-presenton-...: FastAPI paths are rewritten (FastAPI validates the key); Next.js's own API routes answer 403 {"detail": "API keys are only accepted by the Presenton API"} (proxy.ts:147).
  8. Otherwise call GET /api/v1/auth/status with the cookie and return 428 (not configured) or 401 (not authenticated), both with Cache-Control: no-store.

Gotcha: in Docker, nginx bypasses proxy.ts for FastAPI paths

nginx sends /api/v1/ and /api/v2/ straight to port 8000 (nginx.conf:45, :59), so those requests never reach Next.js. In Docker, proxy.ts only gates Next.js's own routes under /api/* (for example /api/user-config, /api/export-presentation). The rewrite branches exist for Electron.

Gotcha: an unreachable FastAPI looks like \"logged out\"

getAuthStatus in proxy.ts:65 and getServerAuthStatus in serverAuth.ts:37 both map network errors and non-2xx responses to authenticated: false. requireAppSession then redirects to / because available is false (serverAuth.ts:99). A crashed backend therefore shows the login screen, not an error page.

docs.title: 13.2 Role-aware route handlers
docs.text:
app/api/user-config/route.ts shows the pattern for routes that serve both roles: GET returns the real provider settings to admins (forwarded from /api/v1/admin/provider-settings) and a redacted copy to regular users, where every non-empty value whose key ends in API_KEY|ACCESS_KEY_ID|SECRET_ACCESS_KEY|SESSION_TOKEN|ACCESS_TOKEN|REFRESH_TOKEN|PASSWORD becomes "__configured__" and AUTH_* keys are dropped (servers/nextjs/lib/runtime-provider-config.ts:12). POST requires requireAdminApi and a Content-Type of exactly application/json (else 415), which blocks the classic text/plain cross-site form post.

utils/authErrors.ts normalizes FastAPI detail payloads for toasts, and utils/chatgptAuth.ts is unrelated to Presenton accounts: it detects ChatGPT/Codex provider re-authentication (x-presenton-auth-action: codex-reauth or a CHATGPT_AUTH_REQUIRED: marker) and dispatches a browser event.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• Accounts live in a username-only user table; one primary admin is enforced by the unique admin_slot, and the role is just is_superuser.
  • Login writes a 30-day HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax presenton_session JWT whose av claim is checked against user.auth_version, giving per-user revocation without a session store; the signing secret lives in userConfig.json.
  • SessionAuthMiddleware resolves the cookie first and Bearer sk-presenton-... second, rejects API keys on admin paths, mints internal JWTs for API-key callers, and sets owner contextvars.
  • Two ORM event listeners stamp and filter owner_id on every SELECT and insert, but bulk DELETE/UPDATE must carry explicit owner predicates.
  • nginx gates private /app_data files through /api/v1/auth/verify with X-Original-URI, using repeated decoding, realpath checks and disable_symlinks.
  • DISABLE_AUTH removes accounts and tenant isolation; Electron compensates with a per-launch desktop token checked on both servers.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Continue with Docker build and deployment to see how this auth system is packaged into the production image and configured through AUTH_* variables and reverse proxies.

docs.title: Docker build and deployment
docs.text:
Reads: Dockerfile, Dockerfile.dev, docker-compose.yml, .dockerignore, nginx.conf, start.js, scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs, .do/deploy.template.yaml, .github/workflows/docker-release.yml, docs/multi-docker-build.md, docs/presenton-resource-usage.md, servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py · Builds on: Runtime topology, Running it locally · Time: ~40 min

This chapter is about producing and shipping the Presenton container: what each of the four Dockerfile stages builds and why, what the final image contains and what makes it large, how the development image differs, how docker-compose.yml forwards configuration, how the multi-architecture image reaches ghcr.io, and what you must configure for a real deployment (public URL, reverse proxy, external database, air-gapped mode, sizing). The processes that run inside the container (nginx, FastAPI, MCP, Next.js, optional Ollama) and how start.js supervises them are covered in Runtime topology; this chapter only touches start.js where it matters for deployment.

docs.title: Step 0: The build context and .dockerignore
docs.text:
docker build . sends the repository root as the build context, filtered by .dockerignore:

Pattern Why it is excluded .git, node_modules, **/node_modules, **/.next, **/.next-build, **/.venv Host build outputs and dependencies are rebuilt inside the image for Linux **/.pytest_cache, **/__pycache__, **/*.pyc, **/debug Python caches **/fastembed_cache, **/chroma, .cache Model and vector caches are regenerated by the warm-up step app_data, container.db User data must never be baked into an image presentation-export Re-downloaded at the pinned version by the assets stage servers/fastapi/tests, servers/nextjs/cypress, servers/nextjs/cypress.config.ts, **/*.cy.ts, **/*.cy.tsx Tests are not shipped electron/* with negations Only electron/resources/document-extraction/liteparse_runner.mjs survives

The Electron block is a three-level negation (.dockerignore:30 to :35): exclude electron/*, re-include electron/resources, exclude its children, re-include document-extraction, exclude its children, re-include the one runner file. Docker and the desktop app therefore share the exact same LiteParse runner.

Gotcha: tests are not in the image

Because servers/fastapi/tests is ignored, you cannot run pytest inside the production image. CI runs tests on the source tree instead (see CI, tests, security).

docs.title: Step 1: The stage graph
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph FB["fastapi-builder (python:3.11-slim-trixie)"]
    A1["uv export --frozen"] --> A2["uv pip install into /opt/venv"]
    A2 --> A3["install project package and font catalog check"]
    A3 --> A4["spaCy en_core_web_sm wheel"]
    A4 --> A5["warm FastEmbed caches (online)"]
    A5 --> A6["re-warm with --network=none"]
  end
  subgraph NB["nextjs-builder (node:22-bookworm-slim)"]
    B1["npm ci"] --> B2["next build (standalone)"]
  end
  subgraph AB["assets-builder (node:22-bookworm-slim)"]
    C1["npm ci LiteParse runtime"] --> C2["sync-presentation-export --force"]
  end
  subgraph RT["runtime (python:3.11-slim-trixie)"]
    D1["apt: pinned Chromium, nginx, ImageMagick, Noto fonts, Tesseract, Node 22"]
    D2["delete non-Noto fonts"]
    D3["COPY venv, caches, Next standalone, export runtime, start.js, nginx.conf"]
    D1 --> D2 --> D3
  end
  FB --> RT
  NB --> RT
  AB --> RT

The file starts with # syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7 (Dockerfile:1). That front end is required for the RUN --mount=type=cache and RUN --network=none instructions used below.

docs.title: 2.1 A pip-less virtual environment managed by uv
docs.text:
Dockerfile (excerpt)
FROM python:3.11-slim-trixie AS fastapi-builder

WORKDIR /app/servers/fastapi

ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 \
    UV_LINK_MODE=copy

RUN python -m venv --without-pip /opt/venv \
    && pip install --no-cache-dir uv

COPY servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml servers/fastapi/uv.lock ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv export --frozen --no-dev --no-emit-project -o /tmp/requirements.txt \
    && uv pip install --python /opt/venv/bin/python -r /tmp/requirements.txt
  • The venv is created without pip; uv is installed into the base interpreter and pointed at the venv with --python /opt/venv/bin/python. Only /opt/venv is copied to the runtime stage, so neither pip nor uv exists at runtime.
  • UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 compiles .pyc files at install time, so the first import in the container does not pay that cost. UV_LINK_MODE=copy avoids hard links into the cache mount, which would dangle once the cache is unmounted.
  • uv export --frozen --no-dev --no-emit-project turns uv.lock into a fully pinned requirements file without the dev group (pytest, pytest-cov) and without the project itself. --frozen means the lock is used as-is; a lock that disagrees with pyproject.toml is not silently re-resolved.
  • Copying only pyproject.toml and uv.lock first means dependency layers are reused when only application code changes.

docs.title: 2.2 Installing the application and checking packaged data
docs.text:
Dockerfile (excerpt)
COPY servers/fastapi /app/servers/fastapi
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv pip install --python /opt/venv/bin/python --no-deps . \
    && cd /tmp \
    && /opt/venv/bin/python -c "from templates.pptx_font_utils import get_static_font_catalog; assert get_static_font_catalog(), 'Packaged font catalog is empty'"

uv pip install --no-deps . installs the presenton-backend package defined by servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml, whose setuptools configuration includes the api*, models*, services*, utils*, templates* (and other) packages and ships templates/assets/fonts.json as package data (pyproject.toml:48 to :61). The assertion runs from /tmp, so templates is imported from the installed package, not from the source checkout; the build fails if the font catalog JSON did not make it into the wheel.

docs.title: 2.3 The spaCy model
docs.text:
Dockerfile (excerpt)
# mem0/spaCy BM25 lemmatization loads en_core_web_sm at runtime; spaCy tries pip to
# download it otherwise. Runtime image has no pip in PATH (--without-pip venv).
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv pip install --python /opt/venv/bin/python \
    "https://github.com/explosion/spacy-models/releases/download/en_core_web_sm-3.8.0/en_core_web_sm-3.8.0-py3-none-any.whl"

The model is not in uv.lock; it is fetched by URL at a fixed version (3.8.0). The comment states the reason: without it, spaCy would try to pip install the model at runtime, which cannot work in a pip-less venv.

docs.title: 2.4 Baking FastEmbed weights, then proving they work offline
docs.text:
Dockerfile (excerpt)
ENV HF_HOME=/root/.cache/huggingface \
    FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH=/root/.cache/presenton/fastembed \
    PRESENTON_FASTEMBED_ICON_CACHE_DIR=/root/.cache/presenton/fastembed-icons
# Warm FastEmbed caches into the image (not a BuildKit cache mount, or HF weights would be missing).
RUN /opt/venv/bin/python scripts/warm_fastembed_cache.py
RUN --network=none HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /opt/venv/bin/python scripts/warm_fastembed_cache.py

servers/fastapi/scripts/warm_fastembed_cache.py initializes three models: the icon-search embedding index through ICON_FINDER_SERVICE.ensure_initialized() (the docstring names AllMiniLML6V2), the Mem0 dense embedder (MEM0_EMBEDDER_MODEL, default BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, warm_fastembed_cache.py:28) and the Qdrant/bm25 sparse model (warm_fastembed_cache.py:49). The first RUN downloads them into normal image layers. The second RUN repeats the warm-up with networking disabled and HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1: if any weight is missing, initialization tries the network, fails, and the build stops. This is the image's offline guarantee for embeddings.

Gotcha: changing the embedder model at runtime defeats the bake

Only the default BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (or whatever MEM0_EMBEDDER_MODEL was at build time) is cached. Setting a different MEM0_EMBEDDER_MODEL in compose makes the container download weights on first use, which fails in air-gapped deployments. The Dockerfile declares no ARG or ENV for MEM0_EMBEDDER_MODEL in the fastapi-builder stage, so to bake a different model you must add one before the warm-up RUN lines and rebuild.

docs.title: Step 3: Stage nextjs-builder
docs.text:
Dockerfile (excerpt)
FROM node:22-bookworm-slim AS nextjs-builder

WORKDIR /app/servers/nextjs

ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1

COPY servers/nextjs/package.json servers/nextjs/package-lock.json ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.npm \
    npm ci

COPY servers/nextjs /app/servers/nextjs
RUN npm run build \
    && rm -rf .next-build/cache

servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:10 sets distDir: ".next-build" and output: "standalone", so the build emits a self-contained server.js plus only the traced node_modules under .next-build/standalone. The build cache is deleted in the same layer so it never reaches the final image. npm ci honors the overrides in servers/nextjs/package.json (pinned brace-expansion, minimatch, glob, systeminformation floors), which are covered in CI, tests, security.

Gotcha: no NEXT_PUBLIC_* at build time

The Docker build passes no NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API or NEXT_PUBLIC_URL. Browser code therefore uses same-origin paths like /api/v1/..., which nginx routes. If you add build-time NEXT_PUBLIC_* values, remember Next.js inlines them into the client bundle, so the image becomes tied to one hostname.

docs.title: Step 4: Stage assets-builder
docs.text:
This stage produces two Node runtimes that FastAPI shells out to: the LiteParse document parser and the closed-source export engine.

Dockerfile (excerpt)
COPY package.json package-lock.json /app/

RUN mkdir -p /app/document-extraction-liteparse \
    && cp /app/package.json /app/package-lock.json /app/document-extraction-liteparse/ \
    && npm --prefix /app/document-extraction-liteparse ci --omit=dev

COPY electron/resources/document-extraction/liteparse_runner.mjs /app/document-extraction-liteparse/liteparse_runner.mjs
COPY scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs /app/scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs
COPY scripts/run-presentation-export.mjs /app/scripts/run-presentation-export.mjs
COPY scripts/export-permissions.cjs /app/scripts/export-permissions.cjs
RUN rm -rf /app/presentation-export \
    && node /app/scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs --force

docs.title: 4.1 LiteParse runtime
docs.text: The root package.json declares exactly two dependencies, @llamaindex/liteparse ^1.5.2 and sharp ^0.35.5, with overrides that force LiteParse's own sharp and zod to safe versions (package.json:16 to :25). npm ci --omit=dev installs them from the lock file into /app/document-extraction-liteparse, next to the shared runner script. How FastAPI calls this runner is covered in Document ingestion.

docs.title: 4.2 The pinned export engine
docs.text:
scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs --force installs @presenton/export-core at the version pinned in the root package.json ("presentationExportVersion": "v1.0.51", package.json:4). Its main() (scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs:359) does the following:

  1. Read the pin (readPinnedVersion, :155). EXPORT_RUNTIME_VERSION is honored only with --allow-version-override, so the Docker build always uses the pin.
  2. Download presenton-export-core-opensource-1.0.51.tgz from https://github.com/presenton/presenton-export/releases/download/v1.0.51/ (or copy EXPORT_CORE_ARCHIVE if set), following at most 5 redirects.
  3. installRuntime (:295) empties /app/presentation-export (it clears contents instead of deleting the directory because the development compose service mounts a named volume there), copies runner.mjs and export-permissions.cjs, writes a package.json that depends on the tarball and overrides sharp to 0.35.5 and katex to 0.18.10, then runs npm install --omit=dev --ignore-scripts --no-package-lock --no-fund --no-audit.
  4. Write presenton-export-version.json and re-validate with validateExistingRuntime (:253): the installed version and package name must match, sharp must be at least 0.35.5 with the exact native @img/sharp-<platform> package its manifest expects, and katex must be at least 0.18.2.

getRuntimePlatformArch (:40) distinguishes glibc from musl Linux, so the check expects @img/sharp-linux-x64 or @img/sharp-linux-arm64 on these Debian-based images.

Gotcha: --ignore-scripts is deliberate

Lifecycle scripts never run for the export engine or its dependencies. If a future dependency needs a postinstall step, the install will not run it and validateExportRuntime (or the export itself) is where you will see the failure.

docs.title: 5.1 Arguments and environment
docs.text:
Dockerfile (excerpt)
ARG INSTALL_TESSERACT=true
ARG CHROMIUM_VERSION=149.0.7827.196-1~deb13u1
ARG CHROMIUM_SNAPSHOT=20260625T180000Z
Variable (Dockerfile:82 to :92) Value Consumer APP_DATA_DIRECTORY /app_data Everything persistent: SQLite DB, userConfig.json, assets TEMP_DIRECTORY /tmp/presenton Per-owner scratch space EXPORT_PACKAGE_ROOT /app/presentation-export Export runner location PRESENTON_APP_ROOT /app Next.js route handlers locating FastAPI static files HF_HOME, FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH, PRESENTON_FASTEMBED_ICON_CACHE_DIR under /root/.cache Must match the paths used at bake time PATH /opt/venv/bin:$PATH python resolves to the venv NODE_ENV production Next.js and Node scripts START_OLLAMA false start.js PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH /usr/bin/chromium Export engine uses system Chromium

docs.title: 5.2 Pinned Chromium from a Debian snapshot
docs.text:
Dockerfile (excerpt)
RUN set -eux; \
    printf 'Acquire::Check-Valid-Until "false";\n' > /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99snapshot; \
    printf 'deb [check-valid-until=no] http://snapshot.debian.org/archive/debian-security/%s trixie-security main\n' "$CHROMIUM_SNAPSHOT" > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/chromium-snapshot.list; \
    # ...
    if [ "$INSTALL_TESSERACT" = "true" ]; then packages="$packages tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng"; fi; \
    apt-get update; \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends --allow-downgrades \
    $packages \
    chromium="${CHROMIUM_VERSION}" \
    chromium-common="${CHROMIUM_VERSION}" \
    chromium-driver="${CHROMIUM_VERSION}"; \
    apt-mark hold chromium chromium-common chromium-driver; \
    curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_22.x | bash -; \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nodejs; \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

The export engine's rendering is sensitive to the browser build, so the image does not take "whatever Chromium trixie-security has today". It adds a snapshot.debian.org source frozen at 20260625T180000Z, disables Valid-Until checks (snapshot metadata is old by design), installs exactly 149.0.7827.196-1~deb13u1 (with --allow-downgrades in case the live mirror is newer), and holds the packages. The same build ID (149.0.7827.196) is pinned for the desktop app in electron/package.json:6, so Docker and Electron export with the same browser revision.

The rest of the package list provides nginx, fontconfig, imagemagick, zstd, curl, the Chromium shared libraries (libgtk-3-0t64, libnss3, libgbm1 and others), and fonts. Node.js 22 comes from the NodeSource setup script, not from Debian.

docs.title: 5.3 A Noto-only font set
docs.text:
Dockerfile (excerpt)
# Remove any non-Noto fonts that may have been installed as dependencies.
RUN find /usr/share/fonts -type f ! -iname 'Noto*' -delete \
    && find /usr/share/fonts -type d -empty -delete \
    && fc-cache -fsv

Every system font whose filename does not start with Noto is deleted and the fontconfig cache rebuilt. This makes font fallback during export deterministic: when a slide requests a font the image does not have, Chromium falls back to a Noto family rather than whichever font a dependency happened to pull in. Template fonts are loaded separately (see Themes and fonts).

Gotcha: deleting files in a later layer does not shrink the image

fonts-liberation is installed by the apt layer and then removed by this one. The bytes remain in the earlier layer, so the deletion changes behavior (no Liberation fallback) but not image size. The same applies to anything you "clean up" in a separate RUN.

docs.title: 5.4 Directories and the assembly copies
docs.text:
Dockerfile (excerpt)
RUN mkdir -p /app_data/exports /app_data/images /app_data/uploads /app_data/fonts /app_data/templates /app_data/pptx-to-html /app_data/pptx-to-json \
    && chmod -R a+rX /app_data

COPY --from=fastapi-builder /opt/venv /opt/venv
COPY --from=fastapi-builder /app/servers/fastapi /app/servers/fastapi
COPY --from=fastapi-builder /root/.cache/huggingface /root/.cache/huggingface
# ...
COPY --from=assets-builder /app/presentation-export /app/presentation-export
# ...
RUN test -f /app/presentation-export/runner.mjs \
    && test -f /app/presentation-export/node_modules/@presenton/export-core/dist/index.js

COPY --from=nextjs-builder /app/servers/nextjs/.next-build/standalone/ /app/servers/nextjs/
COPY --from=nextjs-builder /app/servers/nextjs/public /app/servers/nextjs/public
COPY --from=nextjs-builder /app/servers/nextjs/.next-build/static /app/servers/nextjs/.next-build/static
Destination Source stage Purpose /opt/venv fastapi-builder Python dependencies, project package, spaCy model /app/servers/fastapi fastapi-builder Source tree (FastAPI runs from here, so static/, assets/, alembic/ are found relative to the working directory) /root/.cache/huggingface, /root/.cache/presenton/fastembed* fastapi-builder Baked model weights /app/templates build context Bundled template packs /app/document-extraction-liteparse assets-builder LiteParse runtime and runner /app/presentation-export assets-builder Export engine (guarded by two test -f checks) /app/scripts/* assets-builder and context Export sync and permission helpers, banner, user-config-env.cjs, run-node-script.mjs /app/servers/nextjs/ nextjs-builder Standalone server, public/, and hashed static chunks /app/start.js, LICENSE, NOTICE context Supervisor and license files /etc/nginx/nginx.conf context Reverse proxy

The image ends with EXPOSE 80 and CMD ["node", "/app/start.js"] (Dockerfile:152). There is no USER instruction, so the container runs as root unless the orchestrator overrides it. start.js spawns the Next.js standalone server only when servers/nextjs/server.js exists and the process is not in --dev mode (start.js:35, :539).

docs.title: Step 6: What makes the image large
docs.text:
The repository contains no measured image size, so this is a qualitative inventory of what the Dockerfile puts into layers:

Contributor Where Notes Chromium 149 plus GTK, NSS, X11 and audio libraries Dockerfile:97 to :111 Required by the export engine and template previews Noto font families, including fonts-noto-cjk and fonts-noto-cjk-extra and color emoji Dockerfile:98 to :99 CJK coverage is the largest font component Python ML stack: fastembed (ONNX Runtime), mem0ai[nlp] (spaCy), pandas, pdfplumber, provider SDKs /opt/venv Driven by servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml:12 to :39 Baked embedding weights /root/.cache Three models (Step 2.4) Node.js 22 runtime NodeSource Needed by Next.js, LiteParse and export Export engine with sharp/libvips native binaries and KaTeX /app/presentation-export Pinned v1.0.51 LiteParse with its own sharp /app/document-extraction-liteparse Separate install from the export engine Tesseract OCR with English data optional Skip with --build-arg INSTALL_TESSERACT=false ImageMagick, nginx apt Document conversion and reverse proxy

The only size knob the Dockerfile exposes is INSTALL_TESSERACT. Building without it removes OCR for scanned documents; nothing in the Dockerfile substitutes another OCR engine.

docs.title: Step 7: Dockerfile.dev
docs.text:
The development image is a single stage built for bind-mounted source:

Aspect Dockerfile Dockerfile.dev Stages 4 1 Python packages /opt/venv (no pip, no uv at runtime) System site-packages via UV_SYSTEM_PYTHON=1 and uv pip install --system, uv installed with the astral.sh script Tesseract optional (INSTALL_TESSERACT) always installed LiteParse install npm ci --omit=dev scripts/sync-document-dependencies.cjs (fingerprinted, see below) Next.js prebuilt standalone not built; start.js --dev runs npm ci then next dev --webpack Command node /app/start.js node /app/start.js --dev

The comment at Dockerfile.dev:68 explains the system-site-packages choice: the compose bind mount .:/app would hide a .venv inside servers/fastapi, so dependencies must live outside /app.

scripts/sync-document-dependencies.cjs is the development counterpart to the production npm ci. It computes a SHA-256 fingerprint of package-lock.json, the dependencies and overrides blocks, and process.platform:arch:modules (sync-document-dependencies.cjs:35), and reinstalls only when the stored marker differs, a critical package version (@llamaindex/liteparse, sharp, zod, axios, form-data, follow-redirects) does not match the lock, or import('@llamaindex/liteparse') and import('sharp') fail. A failed reinstall throws "Document dependencies do not match the reviewed lockfile" and never writes the marker.

In --dev mode start.js also: runs npm ci in servers/nextjs on every start (start.js:171), re-syncs the document dependencies (:226), forces a fresh export runtime sync if the check fails (:463), copies the bind-mounted nginx.conf over /etc/nginx/nginx.conf (:468), starts FastAPI with --reload true, waits for log lines instead of HTTP probes (:633), and restarts FastAPI or Next.js if either exits with code 0 (:582).

docs.title: 8.1 Four services, not profiles
docs.text:
The compose file defines four services (no Compose profiles: key is used): production (docker-compose.yml:2), production-gpu (:130), development (:264) and development-gpu (:395). You pick one by name: docker compose up production.

Service Dockerfile Volumes GPU production Dockerfile ./app_data:/app_data, ./servers/fastapi/templates:/app/servers/fastapi/templates:ro no production-gpu Dockerfile ./app_data:/app_data 1 NVIDIA device development Dockerfile.dev .:/app, three named volumes, ./app_data:/app_data no development-gpu Dockerfile.dev same as development 1 NVIDIA device

All four publish ${PRESENTON_HTTP_HOST_PORT:-5001}:80 and 1455:1455. Port 1455 is commented as "Required for Codex OAuth callback (OpenAI redirects browser directly to localhost:1455)" (docker-compose.yml:11).

docs.title: 8.2 Bind mounts versus named volumes in development
docs.text:
docker-compose.yml (excerpt)
    volumes:
      - .:/app
      - presenton_root_node_modules:/app/node_modules
      - presenton_document_extraction_liteparse:/app/document-extraction-liteparse
      - presenton_presentation_export:/app/presentation-export
      - ./app_data:/app_data

The whole repository is mounted at /app so source edits reload live. Three named volumes are mounted on top of paths inside that bind mount; they shadow whatever the host has there. This keeps Linux-built native modules (sharp, the export engine) inside Docker-managed storage, isolated from a macOS or Windows host's node_modules. This is also why installRuntime clears the contents of /app/presentation-export rather than deleting the directory: deleting a mount point fails with EBUSY (scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs:296). The root test package-metadata.test.mjs asserts that presenton_presentation_export:/app/presentation-export appears exactly twice in the compose file and is declared under top-level volumes: (scripts/package-metadata.test.mjs:56).

The production service's read-only templates mount replaces the image's servers/fastapi/templates package with the host copy. FastAPI is started as python server.py from /app/servers/fastapi (start.js:521), so that directory is first on sys.path and the mounted package is the one imported.

docs.title: 8.3 GPU services
docs.text:
docker-compose.yml (excerpt)
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              count: 1
              capabilities: [gpu]

The image contains no CUDA libraries. The GPU reservation matters for an Ollama server started inside the container with START_OLLAMA=true, which start.js installs at startup from https://ollama.com/install.sh if the binary is missing (start.js:433) and then runs as ollama serve (:662). The NVIDIA Container Toolkit must be installed on the host.

docs.title: 8.4 Environment forwarding
docs.text:
Every service forwards roughly 110 variables using the pattern - NAME=${NAME:-default}. Most defaults are empty, which forwards an empty string. Two mechanisms make empty values harmless:

  • start.js seeds userConfig.json from the environment through scripts/user-config-env.cjs. envValue treats both undefined and "" as "not set" (scripts/user-config-env.cjs:130), so an empty compose variable never erases a value saved in the UI.
  • setupUserConfigFromEnv (start.js:490) writes the file only if it is empty or at least one recognised key is non-empty; otherwise it leaves a UI-managed configuration alone.

Non-empty compose defaults worth knowing:

Variable Compose default Effect MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP true (hard-coded, not ${...:-true}, so a shell variable cannot override it) Run Alembic at startup (otherwise create_all on a fixed table list) PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE both Standard and Smart generation PRESENTON_COMMUNITY_ENABLED true Community gallery on START_OLLAMA false No in-container Ollama ENABLE_PARALLEL_IMAGE_GENERATION true MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS 100 MEM0_LLM_MODEL ${OLLAMA_MODEL:-llama3.1:latest} Mem0 points at Ollama by default MEM0_LLM_BASE_URL ${OLLAMA_URL:-http://host.docker.internal:11434} MEM0_EMBEDDER_MODEL, MEM0_EMBEDDING_DIMS BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, 384 Matches the baked weights LITEPARSE_DPI, LITEPARSE_NUM_WORKERS 120, 1 Document parsing cost PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH /usr/bin/chromium

Authentication variables (AUTH_USERNAME, AUTH_PASSWORD, AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV, RESET_AUTH) are forwarded by all four services; their semantics are in Auth and multi-user. DISABLE_AUTH is not forwarded by compose, which keeps accounts on for Docker unless you add it yourself.

Gotcha: two different host-port variable names

The port mapping uses PRESENTON_HTTP_HOST_PORT, but the environment block forwards PRESENTON_HOST_HTTP_PORT (note the word order), defaulting to 5001 (and to 5000 in production-gpu). Inside the container that value only feeds the startup banner (scripts/presenton-terminal-banner.mjs:97). If you only set PRESENTON_HTTP_HOST_PORT=8080, the app works on 8080 but the banner still prints 5001.

Gotcha: platform defaults to linux/amd64

Every service sets platform: ${PRESENTON_DOCKER_PLATFORM:-linux/amd64}. On Apple Silicon or ARM servers, compose builds and runs an emulated amd64 image unless you export PRESENTON_DOCKER_PLATFORM=linux/arm64.

docs.title: 9.1 The CI workflow
docs.text:
.github/workflows/docker-release.yml runs on release: published and on workflow_dispatch:

.github/workflows/docker-release.yml (excerpt)
      - name: Build and push multi-architecture image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@c3c9e263c25d99ce0380d002d59b67737d91b0dc # v7
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.docker-tags.outputs.tags }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
  1. Check out the release tag (or the dispatched ref).
  2. Set up QEMU and Buildx (both actions pinned by commit SHA), log in to ghcr.io with secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN (the job has packages: write).
  3. Tag: ghcr.io/presenton/presenton:<release tag> for releases, ghcr.io/presenton/presenton:dev (MOVING_TAG) for manual runs.
  4. Build both platforms in one Buildx invocation with the GitHub Actions cache backend.
  5. docker buildx imagetools inspect the pushed tag and grep for both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.

The concurrency group keys on the tag with cancel-in-progress: false, so two releases never cancel each other.

Gotcha: CI never moves latest

The workflow pushes only the release tag or dev. The latest tag used by docker run ghcr.io/presenton/presenton:latest and by the DigitalOcean template is promoted by hand, following docs/multi-docker-build.md step 4.

docs.title: 9.2 The documented manual flow
docs.text:
docs/multi-docker-build.md describes the alternative used when building natively on two machines: build on macOS (arm64) and Linux (amd64), tag the local image presenton-3-production:latest as ghcr.io/presenton/presenton:<version>-arm64 and -amd64, push both, then stitch them with docker buildx imagetools create -t ghcr.io/presenton/presenton:<version> <amd64> <arm64>, promote with a second imagetools create -t ...:latest ...:<version>, and verify that both manifests list linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. Native builds avoid QEMU emulation, which matters for a build that compiles Python bytecode, installs Chromium and warms ONNX models.

Because Buildx runs the assets-builder stage once per platform, each architecture gets its own @img/sharp-linux-<arch> native package, and validateSharpRuntime checks the right one.

docs.title: 10.1 DigitalOcean App Platform
docs.text:
.do/deploy.template.yaml (excerpt)
  services:
    - name: presenton
      image:
        registry_type: GHCR
        registry: ghcr.io
        repository: presenton/presenton
        tag: latest
      http_port: 80
      instance_count: 1
      instance_size_slug: apps-s-1vcpu-2gb
      envs:
        - key: MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP
          value: "true"
          scope: RUN_TIME
          type: GENERAL

The template deploys the prebuilt latest image to one apps-s-1vcpu-2gb instance on port 80, sets MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP=true and START_OLLAMA=false, and alerts on DEPLOYMENT_FAILED and DOMAIN_FAILED. It declares no volume and no DATABASE_URL, so the SQLite database, userConfig.json (with the JWT signing secret) and all generated assets live on the container filesystem under /app_data. If the platform does not persist that filesystem across deploys, every redeploy resets accounts and data; add a managed database through DATABASE_URL and check your provider's storage options before relying on it.

docs.title: 10.2 Railway
docs.text: The repository contains no Railway configuration file. The README links to a hosted Railway template (https://railway.com/deploy/presenton-ai-presentations); its contents are not part of this source tree and are not verified here.

docs.title: 10.3 Kubernetes and OpenShift
docs.text:
No Helm chart or manifest ships in the repository. What the code does provide is tolerance for volumes owned by an arbitrary UID:

start.js (excerpt)
// Volumes mounted by the host (e.g. a Kubernetes/OpenShift PVC owned by an
// arbitrary non-root UID) may already have sufficient permissions without
// letting this process chmod them. Treat chmod as best-effort so a restricted
// environment doesn't crash the whole process on startup.
const chmodBestEffort = (path, mode) => {
  try {
    chmodSync(path, mode);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error && (error.code === "EPERM" || error.code === "EACCES")) {
      return;
    }
    throw error;
  }
};

At startup start.js creates the seven asset directories with mode 0755 (start.js:93), applies chmodBestEffort to them and to userConfig.json/.bak (0600, :104), and normalizes permissions under exports, pptx-to-html and pptx-to-json with legacy: true (start.js:89). In legacy mode an existing directory keeps its owner and group bits and only loses world access (stat.mode & 0o7770) instead of being forced to 0750; a non-root process also switches to legacy mode on its own for any directory it does not own (scripts/export-permissions.cjs:24). When running as root, exported files are re-grouped to www-data (or nginx) and set to 0640 so the nginx worker (user www-data;, nginx.conf:1) can read them without making them world-readable (exportReaderGid, scripts/export-permissions.cjs:4).

Gotcha: one replica only

start.js runs FastAPI, the MCP server, Next.js and nginx inside one container, async generation tasks are in-process BackgroundTasks that are marked failed after a restart (servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py:60), and assets are on local disk. Nothing in the repository coordinates multiple replicas; run one instance per data volume.

docs.title: Step 11: Public URL and reverse proxies
11.1 Header handling in nginx
11.2 PRESENTON_PUBLIC_URL
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py (excerpt)
def get_presenton_public_url() -> str | None:
    value = (os.getenv("PRESENTON_PUBLIC_URL") or "").strip().rstrip("/")
    if value.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
        return value
    return None

The value must start with http:// or https:// or it is ignored. When set it is used for:

  • MCP links: absolute_mcp_url prefers it over X-Forwarded-Proto/X-Forwarded-Host for path, edit_path and preview_url fields (servers/fastapi/utils/mcp_public_urls.py:22).
  • The MCP DNS-rebinding allowlist: its origin is appended to the loopback origins (get_mcp_allowed_origins, servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:128). Without it, browser-based MCP clients on your public hostname are rejected.
  • Template endpoints answering MCP requests (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:109).
  • The trusted-origin check for custom provider discovery (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/ollama.py:29).

docs.title: 11.3 Outer proxy checklist
docs.text: From the code above, an outer proxy (Traefik, Caddy, a cloud load balancer) in front of the container should: terminate TLS and send X-Forwarded-Proto: https (otherwise the presenton_session cookie is issued without Secure), send X-Forwarded-Host or preserve Host with its port, allow request bodies of at least 110 MB on /api/v1/ (145 MB on /mcp), and use idle timeouts long enough for streaming generation (nginx itself allows 30 minutes).

docs.title: Step 12: External databases with DATABASE_URL
docs.text:
get_database_url_and_connect_args (servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:57) decides the runtime URL:

Input Runtime URL Alembic URL (to_sync_sqlalchemy_url, :103) unset sqlite+aiosqlite:///$APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/fastapi.db (default /tmp/presenton/fastapi.db) sqlite:///... sqlite://... sqlite+aiosqlite://..., parent directory created sqlite:///... postgresql://... postgresql+asyncpg://... postgresql+psycopg://... mysql://... mysql+aiomysql://... mysql+pymysql://... anything else unchanged unchanged

All three drivers are in pyproject.toml (aiosqlite, asyncpg, aiomysql, psycopg[binary]). For server databases, services/database.py:38 adds pool settings from get_pool_kwargs (db_utils.py:34): DB_POOL_SIZE (5), DB_MAX_OVERFLOW (10), DB_POOL_TIMEOUT (30 s), DB_POOL_RECYCLE (1800 s), DB_POOL_PRE_PING (true).

servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py (excerpt)
        if split_result.query:
            query_params = parse_qsl(split_result.query, keep_blank_values=True)
            driver_scheme = split_result.scheme
            for k, v in query_params:
                key_lower = k.lower()
                if key_lower == "sslmode" and "postgresql+asyncpg" in driver_scheme:
                    if v.lower() != "disable" and "sqlite" not in database_url:
                        connect_args["ssl"] = ssl.create_default_context()

            database_url = urlunsplit(
                (
                    split_result.scheme,
                    split_result.netloc,
                    split_result.path,
                    "",
                    split_result.fragment,
                )
            )

Gotcha: every query parameter is dropped
