  MAN --> D
  MAN --> L
Workflow Triggers Jobs Secrets and permissions codeql.yml push to main and fix/security-and-vulnerabilities, PR to main, manual analyze matrix over actions, javascript-typescript, python security-events: write, actions: read; no secrets test-all.yml push to main, PR to main, manual test-repository-tools, test-fastapi, test-nextjs contents: read; no secrets export-runtime-regressions.yml push to main and the security branch, PR to main, only when scripts/**, package.json, package-lock.json or the workflow change; manual test matrix over ubuntu-latest, windows-latest contents: read; no secrets docker-release.yml release: published, manual build-and-push packages: write; GITHUB_TOKEN for GHCR electron-linux-ubuntu22.yml push to electron-linux-ubuntu22, manual build-and-release RELEASE_REPO_TOKEN sync-releaes-to-r2.yml release: published upload in environment sync_r2 GITHUB_TOKEN, R2_ACCESS_KEY, R2_SECRET_KEY, R2_ACCOUNT_ID

Every workflow declares a top-level permissions: block that starts from contents: read, so the default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only unless a job widens it.

Not part of upstream

The mirror that hosts this tutorial also contains .github/workflows/docs-pages.yml, which builds the MkDocs site under tutorial/. It is not part of the Presenton source and is not discussed further.

docs.title: Step 2: codeql.yml
docs.text:
Static analysis for three languages (.github/workflows/codeql.yml:17 to :55):

.github/workflows/codeql.yml (excerpt)
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        language: [actions, javascript-typescript, python]
    steps:
      - name: Checkout source
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Initialize CodeQL
        uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4
        with:
          languages: ${{ matrix.language }}
          build-mode: none
          queries: security-extended
  • build-mode: none means CodeQL extracts source without compiling. Nothing is built or published.
  • queries: security-extended runs the broader security query pack, not only the default.
  • persist-credentials: false keeps the checkout token out of .git/config.
  • Results are uploaded to code scanning and also kept as a codeql-<language> SARIF artifact for 14 days (:49 to :55).
  • concurrency: codeql-<workflow>-<ref> with cancel-in-progress: true (:13 to :15) cancels superseded runs on the same branch.

The actions language scans the workflow files themselves. Separately, third-party actions in other workflows are pinned by commit SHA (for example astral-sh/setup-uv@d0cc045d... in test-all.yml:63 and every docker/* action in docker-release.yml:32 to :62).

docs.title: Step 3: test-all.yml
docs.text: Three independent jobs on ubuntu-latest (.github/workflows/test-all.yml:13 to :111).

docs.title: 3.1 test-repository-tools
docs.text:
Node 20, npm ci at the repository root, then:

  1. npm test: runs test:template-converter and seven other node --test files under scripts/ (package.json:8).
  2. npm run sync:presentation-export: downloads the pinned @presenton/export-core (presentationExportVersion: v1.0.51, package.json:4) into presentation-export/.
  3. npm run check:presentation-export: sync-presentation-export.cjs --check-only validates it without downloading.

This proves the template converters still work and that the export runtime version pinned for Docker can actually be installed.

docs.title: 3.2 test-fastapi
docs.text:
.github/workflows/test-all.yml (excerpt)
    env:
      APP_DATA_DIRECTORY: /tmp/presenton-app-data
      TEMP_DIRECTORY: /tmp/presenton-temp
      DATABASE_URL: sqlite+aiosqlite:////tmp/presenton-test.db
      DISABLE_ANONYMOUS_TRACKING: "true"
      DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION: "true"

Python 3.11 (matching requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.12", servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml:11), uv sync --locked --dev (fails if uv.lock is out of date), create the two directories, then uv run --locked python -m pytest --verbose --tb=short (:68 to :75). The workflow configures no LLM key or other secret, so the suite has to pass without network access to a model.

docs.title: 3.3 test-nextjs
docs.text:
Node 20, npm ci in servers/nextjs, then in order: npm test (which is node --test, servers/nextjs/package.json script test), npm run lint (eslint .), npm run build with NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API=http://localhost:8000 and NEXT_PUBLIC_URL=http://localhost:3000, and npx cypress run --component --browser electron (:95 to :111). A production build failing (type errors, bad imports) fails CI even if no test covers the file.

Gotcha: Node versions differ between workflows

test-all.yml uses Node 20, while export-runtime-regressions.yml, the Linux Electron build, and the Docker image use Node 22. A syntax or API only available in Node 22 can pass the export regression job and fail test-all, or the reverse.

docs.title: 3.4 Running the same checks locally
docs.text: test-local.sh reproduces the workflow (test-local.sh:32 to :61). It requires uv, npm and node on PATH, runs the three groups through run_check, counts failures instead of stopping at the first, and exits non-zero if any failed. The FastAPI group uses /tmp/presenton-tests/{app-data,temp} and sqlite+aiosqlite:////tmp/presenton-tests/test.db. .github/workflows/README.md documents running each group on its own with the same commands.

docs.title: Step 4: export-runtime-regressions.yml
docs.text: A narrow, cross-platform job (.github/workflows/export-runtime-regressions.yml:1 to :39): when anything under scripts/ or the root package*.json changes, run npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund and npm test on both ubuntu-latest and windows-latest with Node 22 and a 15-minute timeout. The Windows leg exists because scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs and scripts/run-node-script.mjs spawn processes and build paths, and the tests check for shell-argument and path handling bugs (Step 7). --ignore-scripts means no package install script runs during CI.

docs.title: Step 5: The release workflows
docs.text:
These are covered in their own chapters; the summary here is what they verify.

  • docker-release.yml builds linux/amd64,linux/arm64 with QEMU and Buildx, tags ghcr.io/presenton/presenton:<release tag> (or :dev on manual dispatch), uses the GitHub Actions cache, and then verifies with docker buildx imagetools inspect that both platforms are present in the manifest (.github/workflows/docker-release.yml:44 to :77). It does not run tests against the image. See Docker build and deployment.
  • electron-linux-ubuntu22.yml builds the Linux .deb and .AppImage on Ubuntu 22.04 and asserts both exist before uploading. sync-releaes-to-r2.yml mirrors published release assets to the presenton-desktop/<version> R2 prefix with rclone. See Electron desktop app.

Gotcha: one release event, two workflows

Publishing a GitHub release triggers both docker-release.yml and sync-releaes-to-r2.yml. The R2 job expects desktop installers named Presenton-<version>.<ext> on that release; a Docker-only release will make it fail.

docs.title: 6.1 Layout
docs.text:
[tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths = ["tests"] (servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml:72 to :73). Dev dependencies are only pytest>=9.0.3 and pytest-cov>=7.1.0 (:66 to :70); there is no pytest-asyncio, so async code is driven with asyncio.run(...) inside synchronous tests, through FastAPI's TestClient, or with @pytest.mark.anyio and an anyio_backend fixture, which uses the pytest plugin that ships with the transitive anyio dependency (for example servers/fastapi/tests/test_image_generation_comfyui.py:157).

Directory Files Test functions (approx.) Purpose tests/unit/ 95 ~790 One module or one security property per file: auth middleware, API keys, owner isolation, provider discovery, export permissions, safe logging, regex bounds, migrations tests/integration/ 6 ~70 Full routers mounted on a throwaway FastAPI() with a temporary SQLite engine: auth endpoints, image provider test, images, generation flow, Presenton OAuth login, slide edit tests/regression/ 1 + snapshots/outline_generation.json 1 Golden-output check of outline generation with a scripted LLM stream tests/edge_cases/ 1 3 Empty input rejected by validation, very large input, invalid LLM payload mapped to a structured HTTP error tests/ (top level) 11 ~114 Chat, documents loader, image generation backends (ComfyUI, Open WebUI, OpenAI-compatible), LiteParse, mem0, PPTX fonts, generation API tests/mocks/ llm.py, normalizers.py FakeLLMClient, content_event(chunk), normalize_payload (sorts dict keys, collapses whitespace)

docs.title: 6.2 Shared fixtures (tests/conftest.py)
docs.text:
Fixture Returns fake_async_session A FakeAsyncSession that records add, add_all, delete, counts commit, returns preset objects from get, and returns empty results from execute and scalars (servers/fastapi/tests/conftest.py:8 to :56) snapshots_dir tests/regression/snapshots (:59 to :61) load_snapshot A loader that parses a JSON snapshot by name (:64 to :70)

Most security tests build their own fixtures instead. The pattern in tests/unit/test_desktop_security.py:28 to :73 is representative: monkeypatch.setenv the runtime variables, create a temp-file SQLite engine with create_async_engine("sqlite+aiosqlite:///..."), create only the needed tables, seed rows, override get_async_session, mount the real routers and middleware on a new FastAPI(), and yield a TestClient. tests/integration/test_auth_endpoints.py adds an autouse fixture that wraps every test in patch.dict("os.environ"), because settings endpoints write provider values into os.environ.

docs.title: 6.3 The regression snapshot
docs.text: tests/regression/test_outline_generation_snapshots.py patches get_model, get_client, get_llm_config, get_generate_kwargs and stream_generate_events in utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_outlines.py, feeds four content_event chunks that together form {"slides":[{"content":"## Intro - Point A - Point B"},{"content":"## Details 1. Item one 2. Item two"}]}, collects the streamed output, validates it as PresentationOutlineModel, normalizes it, and compares it with the snapshot. It pins the streaming contract described in Standard generation pipeline without any network.

docs.title: 6.4 Running a subset
docs.text:
cd servers/fastapi
uv sync --locked --dev
APP_DATA_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton-tests/app-data TEMP_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton-tests/temp \
DATABASE_URL=sqlite+aiosqlite:////tmp/presenton-tests/test.db \
uv run --locked python -m pytest tests/unit/test_owner_isolation.py -q

Coverage is configured but not run in CI: [tool.coverage.run] uses statement coverage (branch = false) and omits tests/*, virtualenvs, alembic/versions/* and scripts/* (servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml:77 to :92). Add --cov to the pytest command to use it.

Gotcha: tests read the real environment

Many modules read os.environ at call time (utils/get_env.py). A variable such as DISABLE_AUTH=true or PRESENTON_ELECTRON=true exported in your shell changes middleware behavior and can make auth tests fail or, worse, pass for the wrong reason. Run tests from a clean shell, as CI does.

docs.title: 7.1 servers/nextjs/tests (node --test)
docs.text:
npm test runs every *.test.mjs under servers/nextjs/tests/ with Node's built-in runner. Tests that need TypeScript sources bundle them on the fly with esbuild into a temp .cjs file and require it (for example tests/desktop-security.test.mjs:16 to :45, tests/font-descriptor-security.test.mjs:13 to :17). The files cover rendering (flow-layout-text-sizing, latex-html-text-rendering, infographic-rendering, vector-arrow-rendering, template-v2-*), client behavior (presentation-autosave, clipboard, wheel-slide-navigation, provider-setup-navigation), backend reachability (backend-connectivity, runtime-provider-config), and five security files:

File What it pins desktop-security.test.mjs The desktop transport guard on every path, Host/Origin checks, CSRF on /api/user-config (415 for text/plain), redaction of provider keys for non-admin users, document reader path restrictions, Electron cookie and header injection. Detailed in Electron desktop app svg-route-security.test.mjs /api/update-svg: paint-value escaping, CDATA handling, bounded scanning of unterminated sections, outside-root and symlink rejection, time-of-check races, size bound (Step 9.3) font-descriptor-security.test.mjs Font-family parsing cannot backtrack exponentially on \! runs; runs the probe in a child with a 2000 ms timeout (:21 to :30) dependency-security.test.mjs Behavior of patched dependencies: Windows service query output from systeminformation, inherited attribute objects, math rendering trust flags, ESLint brace expansion, Markdown attribute tokenizer bounds, postcss-selector-parser with many classes, the Cypress query parser font-cors.test.mjs next.config.mjs grants Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * only to /vendor/fonts/:path*

docs.title: 7.2 Cypress component tests
docs.text:
servers/nextjs/cypress.config.ts enables component testing with the Next.js framework and webpack bundler and sets allowCypressEnv: false. The specs live in cypress/security/ and run in Cypress's Electron browser in CI:

Spec Test dependencies.cy.ts DOMPurify with USE_PROFILES: { html, svg, svgFilters } keeps a heading, its data-slide-title, an SVG circle and an <img src>, and removes <script>, onload, onerror and javascript: links editors.cy.tsx Serialized editor DOM does not copy inherited event handlers; inline text edits, undo, formatting and LaTeX atoms still work math.cy.ts Equations stay measurable and exportable as SVG images

These run in a real browser DOM, which Node tests cannot provide.

docs.title: 7.3 Root scripts/ tests
docs.text:
npm test at the root (package.json:8) runs:

File Pins convert-template.test.mjs, convert-presentation-template.test.mjs Template conversion output shape and failure before writing on missing assets or unmapped layouts package-metadata.test.mjs Application versions stay aligned; Docker and Electron use the same pinned export runtime; sync preserves a mounted runtime root desktop-export.test.mjs Startup Node helpers keep literal paths and arguments; export credentials are scoped to the two desktop origins sync-presentation-export.test.mjs Cache paths never reach shell arguments; glibc vs musl detection; Sharp native package validation; rejection of known-vulnerable versions and nested engine copies user-config-env.test.mjs Env-to-config normalization, DALL-E to GPT Image 2 migration export-permissions.test.mjs Export files get group-only read access; symlinks are not followed; startup keeps config and recovery files owner-only document-parser-security.test.mjs LiteParse's OCR HTTP stack (axios with follow-redirects) strips credentials when a redirect crosses origins sync-document-dependencies.test.mjs The document parser volume is replaced or repaired when stale, and a failed install never leaves a trusted cache marker

docs.title: 7.4 Electron
docs.text: cd electron && npm run test:security compiles app/ and runs scripts/security-dependencies.test.cjs and scripts/private-storage.test.cjs. This suite is not in any workflow.

docs.title: Step 8: What the suites cover, mapped to features
docs.text:
Feature Representative tests Auth, sessions, roles tests/integration/test_auth_endpoints.py, tests/unit/test_session_auth_middleware.py, test_auth_bootstrap.py, test_auth_schemas.py API keys and MCP auth tests/unit/test_api_keys.py, test_mcp_server_auth.py, test_nginx_mcp_config.py Multi-user isolation tests/unit/test_owner_isolation.py, test_asset_ownership_security.py, test_mem0_session_scope_security.py Generation pipeline tests/unit/test_generate_presentation_outlines.py, test_generate_presentation_structure.py, test_generate_slide_content.py, tests/integration/test_presentation_generation_flow.py, the regression snapshot Providers test_available_models.py, test_model_availability*.py, test_ollama*.py, test_openrouter_providers.py, test_openai_discovery_security.py, test_presenton_cloud*.py Export test_export_cookie_header.py, test_export_permissions.py, scripts/export-permissions.test.mjs Desktop test_desktop_security.py, servers/nextjs/tests/desktop-security.test.mjs Dependency advisories test_python_advisory_regressions.py (Authlib JWS), test_dependency_dos_regressions.py (JOSE and ASN.1 bounds), test_certifi_security.py, test_dns_advisory_regression.py, servers/nextjs/tests/dependency-security.test.mjs

There is no end-to-end test that drives a browser against a running Docker image, and no test that calls a real LLM.

docs.title: Step 9: Security hardening catalogue
docs.text: Each entry below names the protection, where it lives, and what breaks if you remove it.

docs.title: 9.1 Path traversal and file access
docs.text:
Protection Location Detail Containment by canonical path servers/fastapi/utils/asset_directory_utils.py:169 to :180 _existing_file_within(candidate, root) resolves both with os.path.realpath, requires the candidate to start with root + os.sep (so images-other cannot satisfy images), and requires a regular file Per-asset-root containment for /app_data servers/fastapi/utils/asset_directory_utils.py:128 to :137 The root is app_data/<first segment>, so a symlink inside images/ cannot read private config elsewhere in app data Owner-scoped resolution servers/fastapi/utils/asset_directory_utils.py:183 to :198, :201 to :219 _app_data_url_allowed applies the same rules as nginx's auth_request (is_app_data_path_authorized); absolute paths are only accepted under app data, the owner's temp subfolder, or static/ Owner directories servers/fastapi/utils/asset_directory_utils.py:23 to :30 images/, exports/, uploads/ become <root>/users/<owner_id> when a principal is set Upload type and size servers/fastapi/utils/validators.py:8 to :48 validate_files rejects files larger than max_size MB; a file is accepted when either its client-declared Content-Type or its filename extension is in accepted_types (_is_accepted_file_type), so this is a declared-type filter, not a content check Generated file names servers/fastapi/utils/file_utils.py:13 to :31 get_file_name_with_random_uuid appends ----<uuid4> and applies os.path.basename only to string paths (an UploadFile.filename is used as given); get_original_file_name reverses it. In this snapshot only get_original_file_name has a production caller (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:459) nginx /static/ trailing slash nginx.conf:144 to :157 The comment explains that a bare location /static would let /static../server.py resolve through alias to any file under /app nginx disable_symlinks on nginx.conf:159 to :211 Every /app_data/* location refuses to serve symlinks; all except fonts and templates also require auth_request /_auth_check SVG route containment servers/nextjs/app/api/update-svg/route.ts:89 to :166 Only /static/icons/*.svg; rejects NUL bytes; checks containment before and after realpath; opens with O_NOFOLLOW; stats the open handle (not the path) to defeat swap races; caps at 5 MB (:16) both by stat and while streaming Electron read-file IPC electron/app/utils/readable-file-access.ts:45 to :70 Only .txt files under app-data subfolders or temp, re-checked after realpath

Gotcha: path_helpers.py and file_utils.py are not traversal guards

get_resource_path and get_writable_path (servers/fastapi/utils/path_helpers.py:15 to :29) simply join a relative path onto the working directory or APP_DATA_DIRECTORY with os.path.abspath; they do not check containment. file_utils.py only manipulates names. Pass user input through resolve_app_path_to_filesystem or _existing_file_within, never through these helpers.

docs.title: 9.2 SSRF and outbound requests
docs.text:
Protection Location Detail Model discovery URL validation servers/fastapi/utils/available_models.py:120 to :151 Rejects control characters and backslashes, non-http(s) schemes, missing host, any query or fragment, \ % ? # in the decoded path, and . or .. path segments, then applies a strict full-match regex No redirects in discovery servers/fastapi/utils/available_models.py:187 to :192, :209 aiohttp allow_redirects=False with a 3xx mapped to an error ("configure the final API URL"); the OpenAI SDK gets DefaultAsyncHttpxClient(follow_redirects=False) Ollama URL validation servers/fastapi/utils/ollama.py:46 to :70 The same checks (a missing scheme defaults to http://), canonicalized through yarl's URL No redirects to Ollama servers/fastapi/utils/ollama.py:117 to :125, :186 to :190 A 3xx on /api/tags becomes 502; a 3xx on /api/pull is reported as an SSE error event Request intent for provider overrides servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/ollama.py:16 to :40, :51 to :57 On GET /api/v1/ppt/ollama/models/available with auth enabled, an ollama_url override is honored only if Origin/Referer match the app's own origin, the configured public URLs, or the desktop origins, or Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin; "must originate from the app, not merely carry an admin cookie" (:54) OpenRouter, Presenton Cloud, OAuth servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/openrouter.py:108, servers/fastapi/services/presenton_cloud.py:164, :209, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/presenton_oauth.py:84 All disable redirects Community catalog servers/fastapi/services/community_presentations.py:205 to :233 Path must match (?:/[1-9][0-9]*)?; redirects are an error community_redirect_not_allowed; disabled community opens no connection Credential stripping on redirects in dependencies scripts/document-parser-security.test.mjs:12, electron/scripts/security-dependencies.test.cjs:7 Tests that follow-redirects and electron-builder's HttpExecutor drop Authorization across origins

Tests: servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_openai_discovery_security.py (invalid roots never reach either transport, redirects rejected without follow-up), test_ollama_request_security.py (cross-site navigation never reaches the network helper), test_ollama_transport_security.py, test_community_request_security.py.

Gotcha: the URL checks do not block private addresses

None of these validators reject localhost, 127.0.0.1 or RFC 1918 addresses; local Ollama and LiteLLM are first-class use cases. The defenses are that the discovery endpoints are admin-only in SessionAuthMiddleware and that the Ollama discovery override must come from the app's own origin (the only caller of _require_provider_request_intent). If you expose provider discovery to non-admin users, you will need an address-range check as well.

docs.title: 9.3 SVG and HTML sanitization
docs.text:
The SVG recoloring endpoint /api/update-svg is public by design (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:87 to :95 lists it as auth-exempt, because Konva and <img> load it directly). Its defenses:

  1. Only local icons: anything not under /static/icons/ returns 400 {"error":"Only /static/icons SVG sources are supported"} (servers/nextjs/app/api/update-svg/route.ts:196 to :202). There is no remote fetch, so no SSRF.
  2. Every style parameter goes through a validator in servers/nextjs/lib/svg-color.ts: normalizeSvgColor (:289 to :316) returns null for anything containing a double or single quote, <, >, a backtick, {, }, ;, CR or LF (UNSAFE_SVG_VALUE_CHARS, :19) and otherwise accepts only hex colors (a bare hex value gets a # prefix), a list of CSS color functions, or a bare keyword; normalizeSvgNumberish (:318 to :329) accepts only a number with an optional CSS unit; line caps and joins are matched against fixed sets.
  3. The file must contain <svg; transformSvgMarkup then escapes values at insertion (covered by svg-route-security.test.mjs:57 to :78).
  4. The response is image/svg+xml; charset=utf-8 with Cache-Control: no-store (route.ts:223 to :229).

Slide HTML rendered by the app is passed through DOMPurify with explicit forbidden tags (for example SANITIZE_CONFIG in app/(presentation-generator)/components/SmartHtmlSlide.tsx:25 onward), and the Cypress spec in Step 7.2 checks that profile.

docs.title: 9.4 Font descriptor validation
docs.text: fontFamilyFromFontDescriptor (servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/text/local-fonts.ts:615 to :618) extracts the family with an anchored pattern ^[^"]*"((?:\\.|[^"\\])*)"\s*$. The comment notes that generated descriptors contain one quoted family and anchoring the opening quote prevents the engine from retrying at every position. tests/font-descriptor-security.test.mjs:21 to :40 feeds 1000 repetitions of an escaped character with no closing quote, in a child process with a 2 s timeout, and requires it to finish. On the Python side tests/unit/test_regex_security.py does the same for font-name normalization, chart parsing and table parsing.

docs.title: 9.5 Dependency pinning and overrides
docs.text:
Mechanism Location Pins uv lockfile servers/fastapi/uv.lock, enforced by uv sync --locked in CI and uv export --frozen in Docker (Dockerfile:15) Every Python dependency uv constraints servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml:43 to :46 joserfc>=1.7.6, pyasn1>=0.6.5 as transitive floors Exact pins servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml:35 llmai==0.3.15 npm overrides (Next.js) servers/nextjs/package.json:86 onward systeminformation>=5.33.16, brace-expansion@^1.0.0 -> 1.1.21, brace-expansion@^2.0.0 -> 2.1.7, postcss-selector-parser 6.1.5 under @tailwindcss/typography, minimatch@>=9 <11.0.1 -> ^11.0.3, glob@>=9 <14.0.2 -> ^14.0.3 npm overrides (Electron) electron/package.json:101 to :111 sharp ^0.35.5 and zod ^4.6.6 under LiteParse, minimatch ^3.1.5 under serve-handler, plus the same minimatch and glob ranges npm overrides (root) package.json:20 to :25 sharp and zod under LiteParse Exact tool versions electron/package.json:94 to :95 electron 42.11.16, electron-builder 26.15.0 Pinned Chromium snapshot Dockerfile:95 to :96 Chromium from a dated snapshot.debian.org archive Action SHAs test-all.yml:63, docker-release.yml:32 to :62 Third-party actions by commit Glob regression checks scripts/glob-security-checks.cjs:8 to :65 Modern minimatch respects braceExpandMax (64) under a 128 MB heap; aborted glob walks stop reading directories; the legacy matcher still works. Registered from electron/scripts/security-dependencies.test.cjs:46 to :50

The overrides are paired with behavior tests (dependency-security.test.mjs, the advisory regression tests in servers/fastapi/tests/unit/) so that removing an override, or a dependency upgrade that reintroduces a bug, is caught by CI rather than by an advisory feed.

docs.title: 9.6 Log safety (escaping, not redaction)
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/utils/safe_logging.py protects log integrity:

servers/fastapi/utils/safe_logging.py (excerpt)
_CONTROL_ESCAPES = {
    code: f"\\x{code:02x}"
    for code in (*range(32), *range(127, 160))
}
_CONTROL_ESCAPES.update({9: "\\t", 0x2028: "\\u2028", 0x2029: "\\u2029"})


def _escape_controls(rendered: str) -> str:
    return rendered.replace("\r", "\\r").replace("\n", "\\n").replace("\x1b", "\\x1b").translate(_CONTROL_ESCAPES)

safe_log(logger, level, message, *args) (:29 to :44) formats the message exactly like logging would, then escapes CR, LF, ESC, C0/C1 controls and Unicode line separators, so an attacker-controlled value (an export URL, a provider error) cannot forge extra log lines or send terminal escape codes. Exceptions are re-rendered with the traceback text escaped too (:16 to :26), and a formatting error logs a fixed message instead of raising (:36 to :38). tests/unit/test_log_callsite_security.py:10 to :22 checks a real call site with a URL containing \nFORGED\r\x1b[2J.

Secret redaction is handled elsewhere and narrowly: _redact_url_credentials replaces user:pass@ in the SearXNG URL with ***:***@ before logging (servers/fastapi/utils/web_search.py:219 to :226), image provider test calls accept the placeholder __configured__ instead of a real key so the UI never echoes stored keys (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/images.py:53 to :61), and non-admin users receive redacted settings from /api/user-config (Step 7.1).

Gotcha: safe_log does not remove secrets

Do not assume that routing a value through safe_log hides it. It only escapes control characters. Never log API keys, Authorization headers or cookies.

docs.title: 9.7 File permissions
docs.text: Item Location Mode userConfig.json and .bak (FastAPI) servers/fastapi/utils/user_config_store.py:25 to :32, :180 to :192 Temp file created with O_CREAT and O_EXCL and 0o600, fsync, os.replace, then chmod 0o600; existing files (and the .bak) are re-chmodded on every read_user_config_file call (:202 to :205) userConfig.json (Docker start-up) start.js:73 (chmodBestEffort), :105, :133, :145, :164 0o600; chmodBestEffort tolerates read-only or foreign-owned volumes (Kubernetes, OpenShift) userConfig.json (Electron) electron/app/utils/user-config-store.ts:105 to :209 Lock, temp and backup files 0o600; parent directory 0o700 via ensurePrivateDirectory Export artifacts servers/fastapi/utils/export_permissions.py:5 to :6, :47; called from servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:271, :814, :842 Directories 0o750, files 0o640, group set to www-data or nginx when running as root, so nginx can serve exports without making them world-readable; symlinks are skipped and artifacts outside managed roots raise Export permissions (Node) scripts/export-permissions.cjs:4 to :60 Same contract for the Node export runner Electron export task file electron/app/ipc/export_handlers.ts:97 wx, 0o600

docs.title: 9.8 MIME handling
docs.text: init_sandbox_safe_mimetypes() (servers/fastapi/utils/mime_types.py:23 to :40), called at import time in servers/fastapi/api/main.py:29, initializes Python's mimetypes with files=[] so it never reads OS MIME databases (sandboxed macOS builds are denied /etc/apache2/mime.types), then registers explicit types for .avif, .docx, .gif, .jpeg, .jpg, .otf, .pdf, .png, .pptx, .svg, .ttf, .webp, .woff, .woff2, .xlsx. Static responses therefore have deterministic Content-Type headers on every platform. tests/unit/test_mime_types.py:6 checks that no system file is read.

docs.title: 9.9 Auth on /docs and /openapi.json
docs.text: SessionAuthMiddleware._PROTECTED_NON_API_PATHS = {"/docs", "/openapi.json", "/redoc"} (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:42) and _requires_auth returns true for them (:44 to :53). The interactive API documentation, which reveals every route and schema, therefore requires a session or API key in account mode. In desktop mode the transport guard still requires the desktop token (tests/unit/test_desktop_security.py:76 to :79). Details of principal resolution are in Auth and multi-user.

docs.title: 9.10 CodeQL
docs.text:
Step 2. The security-extended suite over Python, TypeScript/JavaScript and the workflows themselves runs on every push and PR to main.

flowchart TB
  subgraph Request["Inbound request"]
    A["Desktop transport guard"] --> B["Session or API key principal"]
    B --> C["owner_id contextvar scoping"]
  end
  subgraph Files["File access"]
    D["realpath containment"] --> E["owner-scoped app_data roots"]
    E --> F["nginx auth_request and disable_symlinks"]
  end
  subgraph Outbound["Outbound calls"]
    G["URL validation"] --> H["no redirects"]
    H --> I["origin intent check for overrides"]
  end
  subgraph Supply["Supply chain"]
    J["locks, overrides, constraints"] --> K["behavior regression tests"]
    K --> L["CodeQL security-extended"]
  end

docs.title: Step 10: Contributor checklist
docs.text:
CONTRIBUTING.md sets the ground rules:

  • Scope: contributions are focused on the Electron application (desktop app, FastAPI backend, Next.js frontend, local runtime integrations), and "Contributions outside electron/ may not be accepted at this time" (CONTRIBUTING.md:16 to :25, :129).
  • Workflow: fork, branch (examples feature/add-template-support, fix/export-pptx-error, docs/update-readme), open a PR (:44 to :59).
  • A signed Contributor License Agreement is required; PRs without a CLA for more than 30 days may be closed (:119 to :125).
  • PRs must run locally in both development and build environments, be small and focused, explain what and why, and include screenshots for UI changes (:127 to :134).
  • AI-assisted PRs are welcome but must say so, state the testing done, and confirm the code was reviewed (:138 to :146).

Combined with the CI above, a practical pre-PR checklist is:

  1. ./test-local.sh passes (repository tools, FastAPI, Next.js tests, lint, build, Cypress).
  2. If you touched electron/: npm run typecheck, npm run lint:main, npm run test:security, and npm run dev starts.
  3. If you touched scripts/ or root package*.json: npm test also on Windows, or rely on export-runtime-regressions.yml.
  4. New routes: decide public or protected in SessionAuthMiddleware, and confirm the desktop guard behavior.
  5. New file reads: go through _existing_file_within or resolve_app_path_to_filesystem.
  6. New outbound HTTP: validate the URL and disable redirects, matching Step 9.2.
  7. New dependencies: lockfile updated; if PyInstaller cannot trace it, update servers/fastapi/server.spec.
  8. Logs: use safe_log for request-derived values and never log secrets.

The repository is Apache License 2.0 (LICENSE), with third-party notices aggregated in NOTICE (regenerated by scripts/rebuild_notice_all.py). VISION.md states the guiding goal behind many of these measures: generation that runs locally, inside private networks, and in air-gapped environments.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• Six upstream workflows exist: CodeQL (three languages, security-extended), test-all (repository tools, FastAPI pytest, Next.js tests plus lint, build and Cypress), cross-platform export regressions, and three release workflows for GHCR, Linux desktop builds and R2.
  • The FastAPI suite has about 980 test functions across unit, integration, regression, edge_cases and the top-level files, runs with plain pytest (plus asyncio.run or the anyio marker), and uses temp SQLite engines with real routers instead of a shared app fixture.
  • Next.js tests run on node --test with esbuild bundling, Cypress covers sanitization in a real DOM, and root scripts/ tests guard the export runtime, permissions and document parser.
  • Path access is guarded by canonical containment and owner-scoped roots (not by path_helpers.py), outbound calls validate URLs and refuse redirects, and the SVG route accepts only local icons with validated paint values.
  • safe_logging.py prevents log forging but does not redact secrets; config files are 0o600, exports 0o640 with a proxy group, and MIME types are deterministic.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Part VII starts the Superset design: continue with Part VII landing.

docs.title: Part VII: Data-Bound Documents for Apache Superset
docs.text:
Reads: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py, superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py, superset/tasks/scheduler.py, superset/utils/pdf.py · Builds on: Part I landing · Time: ~8 min

Part VII is the design half of the book. It takes what Parts I to VI showed about Presenton (prompt plus template in, finished deck out) and specifies how to build the same workflow inside Apache Superset, with one hard difference: every number in every output comes from a live Superset query, and nothing is ever a screenshot. This page states the problem, gives the answer in one paragraph, shows the whole architecture on one diagram, maps the Presenton mechanisms we reuse to the chapters that explain them, and lists every Part VII chapter in reading order.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
Presenton generates a deck from a prompt and a template. Its language model writes the chart numbers itself: the chart content schema asks the model for categories and series[].values (presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:1490-1534) and the hydrator copies them into the slide (presenton: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1367-1432). That is acceptable for a pitch deck written from a paragraph of notes. It is not acceptable for a quarterly business review built from a governed BI tool, where the numbers must match the dashboard to the cent and must differ correctly between two users with different row-level security.

Superset, on the other hand, has the governed numbers but no way to produce a native document from them. Its Alerts and Reports feature delivers dashboards as PNG screenshots or as a PDF made of those screenshots (apache/superset: superset/utils/pdf.py:30-41), because chart rendering lives only in the browser. A slide built that way is a picture: it cannot be edited, searched, refreshed or checked.

The request behind Part VII asks for both at once: a common framework that brings Presenton's automated flow to Superset for decks, documents, text and pages, triggered on demand or by events, with dynamic data and no screenshots.

docs.title: The answer in one paragraph
docs.text: Superset Data-Bound Documents (Data-Bound Documents in prose, dbd and databound in identifiers) is one output-agnostic generation framework, shipped as a preinstalled Python wheel (superset-databound-docs) plus a thin Superset extension (databound-docgen-<version>.supx, extension id databound.docgen). A user, a schedule, an alert or an agent submits a prompt, a template and a Superset data context (a filtered dashboard, charts, datasets or a SQL Lab query). A Global Task Framework task runs inside Superset as that user, builds a token-budgeted Data Digest, lets the language model plan sections and choose among validated data bindings, resolves every binding through ChartDataCommand with the user's permissions and RLS, computes facts deterministically, has the model write prose that cites those facts only through tokens such as {{f:f_rev}}, verifies that prose, and renders the resulting Document Spec into native PPTX charts with embedded workbooks, DOCX, vector PDF, Markdown, email and Slack text, or a live HTML page. The language model never writes a number, and every artifact can be refreshed in place when the data changes.

docs.text:

Three properties of this picture matter more than any box in it:

  • Superset is the data plane. All data access runs in-process under override_user, through the same ChartDataCommand the dashboard uses (apache/superset: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py:36), so raise_for_access and RLS apply without any credential handling.
  • The agent proposes, the engine disposes. The language model outputs structure, ids chosen from enums and prose with tokens. Deterministic code produces every value, label and series.
  • One spec, many renderers. The same DocumentSpec becomes a deck, a document, a page or a text brief, and it can be re-resolved later to refresh any of them.

docs.text:

Availability tags used throughout Part VII

[M] means present only on master at cabd8d4ecc6101f04184bd93b5fa77152d139c4d (2026-11-02); it is expected in 7.0, but that mapping is unverified. [M*] means present in 6.1.0 but changed on master. Every master-only dependency in the design has a stated 6.1 fallback.

docs.title: Reading order
docs.text:
Read the chapters in order the first time. Each one builds on the vocabulary of the previous one.

  1. Vision and requirements: the request, the interpretation adopted, personas, twelve use cases with prompts, functional and non-functional requirements, and the exact meaning of "dynamic data" and "no screenshots".
  2. Superset landscape (6.1): every Superset API and extension point the design builds on, with a 6.1.0 versus master availability table and the reasons Alerts and Reports cannot be reused for rendering.
  3. Target architecture: components, processes, deployment topology, configuration and the decisions that shaped them.
  4. Data-bound slide model: the Document Spec, bindings, facts, the token grammar, template data slots and provenance.
  5. Generation flow: the ten steps from Context Capture to export, with prompts, schemas, the Narrative Verifier and the event protocol.
  6. Native rendering, no screenshots: the PPTX, DOCX, HTML, PDF and Text Renderers, the viz_type mapping and the no-screenshot guarantee.
  7. Building the Superset extension: the .supx bundle, REST API, GTF tasks, MCP tools, frontend contributions and the Superset Adapter.
  8. Building the generation service: the databound_docs wheel, storage tables, the LLM provider layer, caching and Celery routing.
  9. Security, RLS, auth: identity propagation, permissions, RLS-safe narratives, sharing, prompt injection and webhook hardening.
  10. Scheduling and live refresh: live pages, refresh in place, narrative policies, triggers and provenance stamps.
  11. Roadmap: MVP, v1 and v2 scope, testing, prototype gates, risks and the upstream SIP outline.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• Presenton lets the language model write chart numbers, and Superset's reports deliver pictures; Data-Bound Documents closes both gaps at once.
  • The framework is a preinstalled wheel plus a thin databound.docgen extension, with no new service or database server.
  • All data runs in-process through ChartDataCommand as the requesting or run-as user, so permissions and RLS apply automatically.
  • The language model chooses validated bindings and writes tokenized prose; deterministic code produces every value.
  • Part VII reuses Presenton's stage shape, schema builder, retries, SSE envelope and template model, and replaces its export runtime.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Start with Vision and requirements to see exactly what the framework must do and what it deliberately does not do.

docs.title: Vision and requirements
docs.text:
Reads: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py, superset/charts/data/api.py, superset/reports/notifications/webhook.py, superset/utils/pdf.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py · Builds on: Part VII landing · Time: ~30 min

This chapter turns a one-paragraph request into a specification you can build and test. You will read the request, the interpretation this design adopts and why, the people who use the system, twelve concrete use cases with the exact prompts and triggers they involve, the functional and non-functional requirements with numeric targets, and precise definitions of "dynamic data" and "no screenshots" that later chapters implement. It ends with the explicit non-goals, which matter as much as the goals because they keep the design small enough to ship on Superset 6.1.

docs.title: Step 1: The request
docs.text:
The request that drives Part VII, in substance:

I want to create a common framework and integrate it with Apache Superset, the way Presenton provides an automated workflow. You can generate a PPT out of it just by giving some prompts and, let's say, choosing some templates. Similarly, I want the same flow to be present for Apache Superset's documents, text, or pages for different event features, so that the user can automatically generate these things on the fly. It should also support dynamic data, and the prepared PPT should use dynamic data. It shouldn't use screenshots. Think from that perspective, and design a step-by-step technical-level explanation with respect to how it should be implemented for the Apache Superset project.

Six phrases in it carry the requirements:

Phrase What it demands Where it is met "a common framework" One engine and one data model shared by every output type, not four separate generators Data-bound slide model "the way Presenton provides an automated workflow" Prompt plus template in, finished artifact out, with Presenton's staged pipeline Generation flow "documents, text, or pages" Decks are only one of four output families Native rendering, no screenshots "for different event features ... on the fly" Interactive generation in seconds, plus generation started by events Scheduling and live refresh "dynamic data ... the prepared PPT should use dynamic data" Numbers come from live queries and can be refreshed in an already prepared file Scheduling and live refresh "It shouldn't use screenshots" No pixel capture of Superset UI anywhere, including the PDF path Native rendering, no screenshots

docs.title: Step 2: The interpretation adopted
docs.text:
The design reads the request as follows, and every later chapter is bound by this reading.

Build one common, output-agnostic generation framework, Superset Data-Bound Documents. It turns three inputs into an artifact:

  1. a prompt in natural language ("Q3 review for EMEA leadership, focus on growth drivers");
  2. a chosen template from the Template Registry (a deck layout set, a document master, a page template or a text brief template);
  3. a Superset data context: a dashboard with its live native-filter state, saved charts, datasets with their saved metrics, a semantic view [M], or a SQL Lab query.

It produces four kinds of output:

  • (a) PowerPoint decks (PPTX) with native, editable charts, tables, KPI groups and speaker notes.
  • (b) Documents: DOCX, PDF (printed from vector HTML) and Markdown.
  • (c) Text: narratives, executive summaries, emails, Slack posts and alert briefs.
  • (d) Web pages: interactive HTML reports that re-query as each viewer opens them, and in v2, generated Superset dashboards.

Generation starts in one of two ways:

  • On demand: a button or chat message in Superset, a REST call, or an MCP tool call from an agent.
  • By events: cron schedules (cron), Superset Alerts firing a webhook when a data condition holds (alert_webhook), data freshness changes (freshness), chart or dashboard definition changes (definition_change) and signed external webhooks from tools such as dbt or Airflow (external_webhook).

The data rules are strict and non-negotiable:

  • Every chart, table, KPI and number comes from a live Superset query run with the requesting user's permissions and row-level security (RLS). For scheduled and event runs, the explicitly recorded run-as user is used instead.
  • Data elements are rendered natively: editable PPTX and DOCX charts with an embedded workbook, real tables, real text, vector SVG on the web. No Superset UI page is ever captured as pixels.
  • Every artifact is re-runnable. A refresh re-executes the queries and replaces data in place. The language model is involved in a refresh only when the narrative policy requires it.

"The Presenton flow" means Presenton's stage shape (outline, layout structure, schema-constrained content, hydration, export; see Standard generation pipeline) with one essential change. Presenton asks the model for chart categories and series[].values (presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:1490-1534). Here, the language model never produces a number. It chooses bindings from validated menus and writes prose with fact tokens. Numbers enter an artifact only through the Binding Resolver and the Fact Engine.

flowchart LR
    subgraph Inputs["Inputs"]
        P["Prompt"]
        T["Template (deck, document, page, text)"]
        C["Data context: dashboard and filters, charts, datasets, SQL Lab query"]
    end
    subgraph Triggers["Triggers"]
        OD["On demand: Studio, chat, REST, MCP"]
        EV["Events: cron, alert_webhook, freshness, definition_change, external_webhook"]
    end
    F["Data-Bound Documents: one Document Spec, governed bindings, facts, tokenized prose"]
    subgraph Outputs["Outputs"]
        D["Deck (PPTX)"]
        DOC["Document (DOCX, PDF, Markdown)"]
        TX["Text (summary, email, Slack, alert brief)"]
        PG["Page (live HTML, v2 Superset dashboard)"]
    end
    P --> F
    T --> F
    C --> F
    OD --> F
    EV --> F
    F --> D
    F --> DOC
    F --> TX
    F --> PG

Why one framework and not four generators

Decks, documents, pages and briefs differ only in the last step. The hard parts (capturing context, choosing data, running queries as the right user, computing facts, writing and checking prose, refreshing) are identical. A single DocumentSpec with kind set to deck, document, page or text lets one pipeline serve all four, and lets one document be exported to several formats from the same resolved data.

docs.title: Step 3: Personas
docs.text:
Persona Superset role (typical) What they do with Data-Bound Documents Permissions on DataBoundDocs Analyst (author) Alpha or Gamma with dataset access Generates decks and reports from dashboards, refines them in chat, exports, shares can_read, can_generate, can_write, can_refresh Executive (consumer) Gamma, often read-only Receives emails and decks, opens live pages, asks for a quick brief can_read, sometimes can_generate for text briefs Regional manager (RLS viewer) Gamma with RLS restricting rows to a region Opens a shared live page and sees only their region's numbers and prose consistent with them can_read BI engineer (template admin) Alpha or Admin Imports branded PPTX and DOCX masters with named slots, publishes templates to roles, sets data exposure policies can_manage_templates, can_admin for policies Platform operator Superset Admin Installs the wheel and .supx, configures DATABOUND_DOCS, Celery routing, storage and the LLM endpoint, runs superset dbd doctor can_admin Scheduler owner Alpha Creates cron, alert and freshness triggers with an explicit run-as user, chooses delivery targets can_schedule Agent developer API or MCP client Drives generation from an external agent through dbd_* MCP tools or REST Same permissions as the user the agent resolves to On-call engineer Gamma Receives an alert brief in Slack within a minute of an alert firing, follows links to the live dashboard can_read

The persona that shapes the design most is the regional manager. Because a shared live page re-resolves every binding as the viewer, two managers looking at the same page must see different numbers, and neither may see prose that was written from the other's data. That single requirement is why prose carries tokens instead of literal values or category names (see Security, RLS, auth).

docs.title: Step 4: Use cases with example prompts
docs.text:
Each use case names its trigger, the document kind, the built-in template it starts from, the data context and the outputs. Template ids are the built-ins listed in the blueprint's Template Registry (tpl_exec_review, tpl_dashboard_walkthrough, tpl_analytical_report, tpl_interactive_report, tpl_kpi_brief, tpl_weekly_email, alert_brief).

# Use case Persona Trigger kind Template Data context Outputs UC1 Quarterly business review deck Analyst on demand (chat [M], Studio page [6.1]) deck tpl_exec_review Sales dashboard, Region = EMEA, Period = last quarter PPTX, PDF UC2 Dashboard walkthrough deck Analyst on demand deck tpl_dashboard_walkthrough (ordered, one section per tab) any dashboard with tabs PPTX UC3 Incident brief when an alert fires On-call engineer alert_webhook text alert_brief the alert's chart and dashboard Slack post, email UC4 Weekly KPI email Executive cron (Monday 07:00 local) text tpl_weekly_email KPI dashboard, Period = last week HTML email with KPI cards, optional PPTX attachment UC5 Monthly analytical report Analyst cron or on demand document tpl_analytical_report Finance dashboard plus a dataset DOCX, PDF, Markdown UC6 Interactive regional report Regional managers on demand, then opened live page tpl_interactive_report Sales dashboard, no region filter (RLS supplies it) live HTML page, shared live UC7 Brief from a SQL Lab result Analyst on demand (sqllab.results menu) text tpl_kpi_brief the last SQL Lab query, or a dataset saved from it Markdown, Slack UC8 Board deck from an external agent Agent developer MCP dbd_generate_document deck tpl_exec_review Finance dashboard chosen by the agent PPTX UC9 Refresh when the nightly load lands Scheduler owner freshness (sentinel MAX(updated_at)) deck existing UC1 document the UC1 document's bindings refreshed PPTX in place, email UC10 Data quality report after a dbt run BI engineer external_webhook (HMAC-signed) document tpl_analytical_report data quality dataset PDF, store and notify UC11 Conversational refinement Analyst chat message on an existing document deck the document's template the document's context new document version UC12 Air-gapped scheduled brief Platform operator cron text tpl_kpi_brief with the template planner (no LLM) KPI dataset email

docs.title: UC1: QBR deck from the Sales dashboard for EMEA, last quarter
docs.text:
The analyst opens the Sales Overview dashboard, sets Region to EMEA and Period to last quarter, and types in the chat panel (master) or the Studio page (6.1):

QBR deck from the Sales dashboard for EMEA, last quarter. Board template. Lead with revenue versus prior year, then product mix, then top countries.

Context Capture reads the dashboard's native_filters_key from the URL, converts it into a durable permalink, and submits a request like this:

CreateDocumentRequest for UC1
{
  "prompt": "QBR deck from the Sales dashboard for EMEA, last quarter. Board template. Lead with revenue versus prior year, then product mix, then top countries.",
  "title": "Q3 2026 Sales Review: {{p:region}}",
  "kind": "deck",
  "template": {"id": "tpl_exec_review", "version": null},
  "formats": ["pptx", "pdf"],
  "context": {
    "dashboard": {"id_or_slug": "sales-overview", "native_filters_key": "kq8sP0", "permalink_key": null},
    "chart_ids": [], "dataset_ids": [7], "sqllab": null
  },
  "parameters": {"region": ["EMEA"]},
  "options": {"language": "en", "tone": "executive", "max_sections": 8, "exposure": "aggregates",
              "planner_strategy": null, "mode": "live", "sync": false}
}

The response is 202 with document_id, job_id and task_uuid. Sections stream into the preview as section.ready events. The resulting PPTX has a KPI group whose revenue value is the same number the dashboard's Big Number chart shows for the same user and filters, a stacked column chart whose "Edit Data" opens the monthly rows by product line, and a native table of the top countries. The narrative reads, for example, Revenue moved {{f:f_rev_yoy}} year over year across the region, with the token rendered as a separate text run.

docs.title: UC3: Incident brief when an alert fires
docs.text:
An Alert in Superset evaluates "orders in the last hour below threshold" every five minutes. Its Webhook recipient targets https://<superset>/extensions/databound/docgen/v1/hooks/<token>. When the alert triggers, the Trigger Service validates the token, ignores the payload's text fields, and runs the alert_brief template as the trigger's run-as user. Within seconds a Slack post appears:

What fired: Hourly orders below threshold (threshold from the alert's validator_config_json, last value from the report execution log). What changed: orders fell {{f:f_orders_chg.abs}} versus the previous hour, led by {{f:f_worst_region.label}}. Where to look: links to the live dashboard and chart.

No screenshot is taken by Superset either: the alert is chart-scoped with report_format = TEXT on 6.1, or NONE on master, so the reports pipeline never starts a browser (see Superset landscape (6.1)).

docs.title: UC4: Weekly KPI email
docs.text:
The executive asks once, in the Studio: "Every Monday at 7 in Paris, email me a one-screen KPI summary of last week from the Executive KPIs dashboard." The analyst saves the document and creates a trigger:

TriggerSpec for UC4
{
  "document_id": "doc_01JC8Z6Q4M5K",
  "type": "cron",
  "config": {"crontab": "0 7 * * MON", "timezone": "Europe/Paris",
             "action": "refresh", "narrative": "regenerate_on_drift",
             "parameters": {"time_range": "Last week"},
             "formats": ["email"],
             "deliver": [{"type": "email", "to": ["cfo@example.com"]}, {"type": "store"}],
             "skip_if_unchanged": true},
  "run_as_id": 42,
  "active": true
}

Every Monday the beat task databound_docs.trigger_tick schedules run_trigger. The refresh re-resolves every binding as user 42, rolls Last week forward, keeps the prose and updates its tokens unless a drift rule fires (a sign flip, a change in the top three, or a cited value moving more than 10%), and sends the email. If nothing changed, refresh.unchanged is recorded and no new version is created.

docs.title: UC6: Interactive regional report
docs.text: The analyst generates a page from the Sales dashboard with no region filter and shares it in live mode with the Regional Managers role. When the manager for EMEA opens GET /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/pages/<document_id>, the page calls render-model?live=1, and the server re-resolves every binding as that manager. RLS restricts the rows to EMEA, tokens resolve to EMEA values, and claim lint re-checks each narrative against the manager's facts. If the narrative no longer holds for that viewer's data, it is replaced by deterministic sentences with a "Summary written for different data" notice and a "Regenerate for me" button.

docs.title: UC7: Brief from a SQL Lab result
docs.text:
In SQL Lab, after a query succeeds, the analyst clicks "Generate brief from results" in the results toolbar (sqllab.results). The panel captures the query's remoteId from sqlLab.onDidQuerySuccess. The backend reloads the Query row, checks that it belongs to the user, and accepts it as a sql binding only when the operator enabled DATABOUND_DOCS["ALLOW_SQL_BINDINGS"] (default False) and raise_for_access(sql=..., force_dataset_match=True) passes. Otherwise the panel offers "save as dataset first", after which the brief is built from a governed dataset binding. The prompt might be:

Two-paragraph brief of this result for the ops channel: what stands out, what to check next.

docs.title: UC8: Board deck from an external agent
docs.text: An external agent connected to superset mcp run calls the MCP prompt dbd_deck_from_dashboard(dashboard, template, audience) to get the ordered steps, then extensions.databound.docgen.dbd_list_templates, then extensions.databound.docgen.dbd_generate_document with a CreateDocumentRequest, and polls dbd_get_job. On master the call runs as the user the agent's JWT or API key resolves to. On 6.1, MCP calls run as MCP_DEV_USERNAME unless middleware sets g.user, so DBD's mutate and data tools refuse to run for the dev user unless DATABOUND_DOCS["MCP_ALLOW_DEV_USER"] (a Data-Bound Documents setting, not a Superset one) is set for development.

docs.title: UC11: Conversational refinement
docs.text:
On an existing deck the analyst types:

Make slide 2 a line chart and add a slide on deal size by country.

The Planner runs in edit mode and returns JSON Patch operations restricted to /sections, /facts, /title, plus binding additions that go through the Binding Registry. The server validates the patch against the current version, re-runs only the affected bindings and narratives, and writes a new version. If the planner cannot decide (two datasets both have a deal_size column), it emits job.needs_input with options and ends the task; the answer schedules continue_generation.

docs.title: UC12: Air-gapped scheduled brief
docs.text:
A regulated deployment has no LLM endpoint. The operator sets the template planner strategy, and tpl_kpi_brief declares fixed bindings and deterministic sentences such as {binding_title}: {{f:x}} ({{f:delta}} versus the prior period). The same Binding Resolver, Fact Engine, renderers and triggers run. Only the prose is less fluent.

Gotcha: prompts are not data access

A prompt such as "include salaries by employee" cannot widen what a user sees. The Planner can choose only from candidates and datasets the user can already access, and every binding is re-checked by ChartDataCommand.validate(), which calls raise_for_access before running anything (apache/superset: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py:107-108). A request for data outside the user's access becomes an entry in the outline's gaps, not a query.

docs.title: Step 5: Functional requirements
docs.text: Requirements are grouped by the stage they constrain. "Must" items are MVP scope unless the Phase column says otherwise; phases are defined in Roadmap.

docs.title: Step 6: Non-functional requirements
Step 7: What "dynamic data" means, precisely
docs.text: "Dynamic" is ambiguous. In this design it has a precise meaning: every data-bearing element is a re-executable reference to a governed Superset query, not a copy of numbers. The reference is a DataBinding; the numbers are a BindingResult produced by running it at a specific time as a specific identity.

docs.title: 7.1 Bindings, not copies
docs.text:
A binding records what to run, not what came back:

  • its source (chart, dataset, semantic [M] or sql);
  • its filters: dashboard native filters to apply, explicit filters, time_range, time_grain, $param.* references;
  • its shape (scalar, series, xy, xyz, table, pivot) and format;
  • its mode (live or snapshot) and, for chart sources, follow (live reloads the chart's current saved query context on every run; pinned uses a stored snapshot of it and flags definition_changed when the live chart drifts).

Rows exist in an artifact only as rendered output: chart caches and embedded workbooks in PPTX, table cells, token runs, embedded JSON in a static page. They are stored in dbd_binding_result.rows only for snapshot mode or when an audit policy requires it.

docs.title: 7.2 The four data modes
docs.text:
Mode What happens when the artifact is used Whose data LLM involved Live page Every open re-resolves live bindings as the viewer; tokens re-resolve; narratives follow the viewer rule the viewer only on "Regenerate for me" Refresh in place Re-resolve, then replace_data, table rewrite and guarded token rewrite inside the existing PPTX or DOCX; a new version the run-as user (or the requester) only if the narrative policy fires Regenerate Full pipeline with the same prompt, template and context; structure may change the requester yes Snapshot Frozen rows, never re-queried; exported and shared as generated stored no 
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Generated: generate_document
    Generated --> Exported: export (pptx, docx, pdf, html, md, text)
    Exported --> Refreshing: user, trigger or page open
    Refreshing --> Unchanged: all data_hash equal and skip_if_unchanged
    Refreshing --> NewVersion: data changed
    NewVersion --> Exported: render in place
    Unchanged --> Exported
    Generated --> Snapshot: mode snapshot
    Snapshot --> [*]

docs.title: 7.3 Refresh semantics
docs.text:
A refresh is defined by five rules:

  1. Same query, new time. Parameters roll forward: a binding with time_range: "$param.time_range" and a parameter value of Last quarter resolves to the quarter that is "last" at refresh time. Absolute ranges (2026-07-01 : 2026-10-01) stay absolute.
  2. Same filters. Dashboard filters come from the stored permalink (filter_mode: "captured"), or from the dashboard's current defaults when the document opts into filter_mode: "defaults".
  3. Same identity rules. Refreshes run as the requesting user, or as the trigger's run_as_fk, which is re-validated (active, still has can_refresh, still has access to every bound datasource) before every run. There is no fallback to another user.
  4. In place, never re-laid-out. A refresh rewrites chart caches, embedded workbooks, table cells and token runs, and nothing else. An XML diff between two refreshes of a PPTX touches only those parts. A token run edited by a human since generation is skipped and reported as token_edited_skipped.
  5. Prose follows policy. With the default regenerate_on_drift, a narrative is rewritten only when a drift rule fires for one of its facts (sign_flip, rank_change_top3, abs_change_pct>10); otherwise only its tokens update. user_edited narratives are never rewritten.

Gotcha: filter state keys expire, permalinks do not

The native_filters_key in a dashboard URL points to filter state held in FILTER_STATE_CACHE_CONFIG, a cache with a TTL. The default is a SupersetMetastoreCache with a 90-day timeout that is refreshed on every read (apache/superset: superset/config.py:1551-1555), but operators often move it to Redis with a shorter timeout, and any cache entry can be evicted. A document that stored only that key could silently lose its filters. Context Capture therefore converts it into a dashboard permalink at capture time. Permalinks are key-value rows written without an expiry (apache/superset: superset/commands/dashboard/permalink/create.py:110-115), and the permalink key is what refreshes use months later.

docs.title: 7.4 What "dynamic" does not mean
docs.text:
• It does not mean real-time streaming. Data changes are detected by schedules, alert conditions, freshness sentinels and definition-change listeners. Superset has no change data capture or dataset-refresh event to subscribe to.
  • It does not mean a PPTX that queries Superset by itself when opened in PowerPoint. Office files are refreshed by Data-Bound Documents (on a trigger, in the Studio, or by uploading a previously exported copy to POST /documents/<id>/refresh-upload); the live, open-time behavior belongs to page documents.
  • It does not mean the LLM re-reads the data on every refresh. Most refreshes involve no LLM call at all.

docs.title: 8.1 The rule
docs.text:
No pixel of a Superset UI page is ever captured, and no bound element is ever stored as a raster image. Superset's own report pipeline does exactly what this forbids: PNG reports are browser captures and PDF reports are a stack of those captures (apache/superset: superset/utils/pdf.py:30-41). Superset landscape (6.1) explains why that pipeline exists and why the design cannot reuse it for rendering.

Allowed Forbidden A native PPTX or DOCX chart built from resolved rows, with an embedded workbook A PNG or JPEG of a Superset chart or dashboard, from any source A native table with formatted text cells build_pdf_from_screenshots or any PDF made of images of charts Vector SVG computed from rows in Python (Vega-Lite through vl-convert-python), or later ECharts server-side SVG Loading a Superset page in a headless browser, for any purpose, including "to make the frontend save a query context" Chromium printing DBD's own static HTML to PDF with network access disabled (text stays text, SVG stays vector) Importing superset.utils.webdriver, superset.utils.screenshots, superset.utils.screenshot_utils or superset.utils.pdf A PNG rasterized from DBD's own SVG, only for email clients that block SVG MCP get_chart_preview with format: "png" Static template assets (logos, backgrounds) as image elements An image element whose source is a capture

docs.title: 8.2 Editable native charts
docs.text: "Native" has a testable meaning in PPTX: the chart is a c:chartSpace part with cached category and value points and an embedded .xlsx workbook, so PowerPoint's "Edit Data" opens the real rows. python-pptx produces exactly this: ChartPart.new writes the chart XML and then chart_workbook.update_from_xlsx_blob(chart_data.xlsx_blob), and Chart.replace_data later rewrites both the cached values and the workbook while keeping formatting. Values are stored as numbers with an Excel number format derived from Superset's d3 format, so a reader can restyle, re-sort or copy them.

docs.title: 8.3 Enforcement
docs.text:
The requirement is enforced by machines, not by convention:

  • an import-linter contract in superset-databound-docs forbids the screenshot and PDF-from-screenshot modules listed above;
  • a renderer contract test unzips every generated PPTX and DOCX and fails if any shape named dbd:*, or any dbd:binding content control, targets an image part (the only exception is a native: "svg" element whose SVG was generated from rows);
  • unsupported viz types fall back to vector SVG from rows, a native table, or a link to the live chart.

Gotcha: Alerts used as triggers must not take screenshots either

A dashboard-scoped Report or Alert always produces PNG or PDF attachments, so pointing one at the DBD webhook would still start a browser on every run. Use a chart-scoped alert with report_format = TEXT on 6.1, or NONE on master, and keep the dashboard id in the DBD trigger record.

docs.title: Step 9: Explicit non-goals
docs.text:
Non-goal Why What happens instead Putting an LLM, or any Presenton code, into apache/superset core Superset should not depend on an LLM; importing Presenton code into an ASF repository would be a code donation Data-Bound Documents lives in its own Apache-2.0 repository as a wheel plus extension; only small generic hooks are proposed upstream (Roadmap) Letting the LLM author SQL or adhoc expressions Large attack surface and no governance The LLM chooses chart candidates and proposes dataset queries over saved metrics and columns only; sql bindings are opt-in and come from saved queries, the user's own SQL Lab queries or template admins Pixel-identical reproduction of Superset's ECharts look in Office files Office charts are a different engine Office charts approximate colors, formats and types; the live page uses ECharts for parity Rendering WebGL maps (deck.gl, Mapbox) natively No faithful vector rendering exists An aggregated native table, a narrative and an "Open live map" link Replacing Superset dashboards or Alerts and Reports They remain the authoring and alerting tools DBD reads dashboards and uses alerts as triggers; Superset dashboard output arrives only in v2 A new authentication path, service account or credential broker Any of these is an exfiltration risk All data access is in-process under override_user; schedules use an explicit run-as user Real-time streaming dashboards in documents No upstream change event exists Event triggers and live pages Generation for embedded (guest) users in MVP Guest identity on 6.1 is unverified, and extensions do not load in embedded dashboards Guest live pages are v2 and master only Using @presenton/export-core License unknown, distributed outside npm, browser DOM measurement python-pptx, a DrawingML writer and vector HTML printing (PPTX and PDF export shows what is replaced) Free-form "smart mode" HTML generated by the LLM Cannot guarantee data provenance Template-driven pages whose data elements are bindings Multi-tenancy beyond Superset's Tenancy follows the Superset deployment Owner-scoped documents, explicit shares, template visibility scopes

Gotcha: 6.1 has no button on dashboards

On stock 6.1 an extension can contribute UI only in SQL Lab; the global chat slot that appears on dashboards and Explore exists only on master. UC1 on 6.1 therefore starts from the standalone Studio page (GET /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/studio?dashboard=12&native_filters_key=..., reachable from a dashboard Markdown link or a bookmark) or from the SQL Lab panel's dashboard picker. This is a limitation of the host, documented in Superset landscape (6.1), not a missing feature.
