databound_docs/render/svg_vegalite.py (sketch)
import vl_convert as vlc

def chart_svg(el, res, fmt, colors: list[str], width=640, height=320) -> str:
    long_rows = [{"x": fmt.iso_x(r[res.shape_x]), "series": fmt.label(c), "value": r[c]}
                 for r in res.rows for c in res.series_columns if r[c] is not None]
    mark = {"column": "bar", "bar": "bar", "line": "line", "area": "area",
            "pie": "arc", "doughnut": "arc", "scatter": "point"}.get(el.native, "bar")
    enc = {"color": {"field": "series", "type": "nominal",
                     "scale": {"range": colors}, "legend": {"orient": "bottom", "title": None}}}
    if mark == "arc":
        enc |= {"theta": {"field": "value", "type": "quantitative", "stack": True}}
    else:
        enc |= {"x": {"field": "x", "type": "temporal" if res.x_kind == "temporal" else "ordinal",
                      "title": None},
                "y": {"field": "value", "type": "quantitative", "title": None,
                      "stack": None if el.grouping == "clustered" else ("normalize" if el.grouping == "percent" else "zero"),
                      "axis": {"format": fmt.d3("*"), "formatType": "number"}}}
        if el.native == "bar":
            enc["x"], enc["y"] = enc["y"], enc["x"]
    spec = {"$schema": "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json",
            "width": width, "height": height, "data": {"values": long_rows},
            "mark": {"type": mark, "innerRadius": 60} if el.native == "doughnut" else mark,
            "encoding": enc, "config": {"font": "Inter", "view": {"stroke": None}}}
    return vlc.vegalite_to_svg(vl_spec=spec)

Optional hydration with ECharts from the embedded JSON gives interactive static pages. Vega-Lite does not reproduce the ECharts look users know; a v2 Node sidecar dbd-echarts-ssr would call ECharts renderToSVGString() (available since ECharts 5.3; Superset 6.1 uses ^5.6.0 and master ^6.1.0, apache/superset: superset-frontend/package.json:167) and, after a spike, Superset's own transformProps. Running transformProps in Node without DOM shims is unverified.

docs.title: 11.3 Superset dashboard output (v2)
docs.text: A page document can be published as a Superset dashboard: chart-source bindings reuse the existing charts; dataset-source bindings become new charts created through the same commands as the MCP generate_chart and generate_dashboard tools, after explicit confirmation and as the user; narratives become MARKDOWN components with resolved values and an "as of" stamp, because Markdown components cannot hold live tokens.

docs.title: Step 12: PDF as vector
docs.text:
The PDF Printer prints the HTML Renderer's own static HTML, never a Superset page. Decks get one 16:9 page per section (@page { size: 13.333in 7.5in; margin: 0 }); documents get A4 or Letter with running headers.

databound_docs/render/pdf.py (playwright engine, sketch)
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

def print_pdf(html_path: Path, *, deck: bool) -> bytes:
    url = html_path.resolve().as_uri()
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch()
        context = browser.new_context(offline=True, java_script_enabled=False)
        page = context.new_page()
        page.route("**/*", lambda route: route.continue_()
                   if route.request.url.startswith("file:") else route.abort())
        page.goto(url, wait_until="load")
        pdf = page.pdf(print_background=True, prefer_css_page_size=True,
                       **({} if deck else {"format": "A4", "display_header_footer": True}))
        browser.close()
        return pdf
Engine (PDF_ENGINE) How Notes playwright Chromium page.pdf() on a local file, network disabled, JavaScript off (SVG is already rendered) text stays text, SVG stays vector paths; on master Playwright with Chromium is the only report and thumbnail backend (installed through the playwright extra, apache/superset: pyproject.toml:268), on 6.1 (Selenium with Firefox by default) the operator installs it printer_sidecar the same in a separate container keeps Chromium out of the worker image weasyprint browser-free (BSD) SVG fidelity unverified (gate G7) LibreOffice (optional) headless conversion of the PPTX or DOCX for "PDF identical to the PPTX"; MPL-2.0 (ASF Category B), never bundled

Gotcha: a browser is not the problem, a captured UI is

Chromium printing DBD's own local HTML file is not a screenshot: no Superset page, no auth cookies, no readiness wait, and the output keeps selectable text and vector paths. The import-linter rule in Step 16 still forbids superset.utils.webdriver, superset.utils.screenshots and superset.utils.pdf, so nobody can "simplify" this path into build_pdf_from_screenshots.

docs.title: Step 13: Text, Markdown, email and Slack
docs.text:
• Markdown: headings per section, narratives with tokens resolved, GitHub tables (top N rows), KPI lines such as **Revenue:** $2.91M (+8.4% vs prior year). Each chart becomes a deterministic sentence from facts plus a link to the live page, for example "Bar chart: monthly revenue by product line, Jul to Sep 2026, peak Sep 2026". Charts are never images in Markdown.
  • Plain text: the same without markup, for MCP results and chat replies.
  • Email: HTML from the static renderer with each inline SVG converted to PNG derived from that SVG (many clients block SVG), KPI cards, the verified narrative, a provenance footer and optional PPTX or PDF attachments. It is sent through send_email_smtp(to, subject, html_content, config, ..., images=...) (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:939, internal; the adapter passes keywords because the signature has changed between versions) with Superset's SMTP settings.
  • Slack: mrkdwn blocks with KPI lines and narrative, tables as preformatted text of at most 10 rows, optional file upload with a bot token from DATABOUND_DOCS.
  • Alert brief (kind: text, template alert_brief): "What fired" (alert name, threshold from validator_config_json, last value from the report execution log read in-process as the run-as user), "What changed" (facts from the alert's chart binding), "Where to look" (links).
databound_docs/render/text.py (Markdown, sketch)
def render_markdown(inp: RenderInput) -> str:
    out = [f"# {resolve_text(inp.spec.title, inp)}", ""]
    for s in inp.spec.sections:
        if s.title:
            out += [f"## {resolve_text(s.title, inp)}", ""]
        for el in s.elements:
            if el.type in ("narrative", "text") and el.text:
                out += [resolve_text(el.text, inp), ""]
            elif el.type == "kpi":
                v = inp.facts[el.value_fact].display
                c = f" ({inp.facts[el.comparison_fact].display} {el.comparison_label or ''})".rstrip() \
                    if el.comparison_fact else ""
                out += [f"**{resolve_text(el.label, inp)}:** {v}{c}", ""]
            elif el.type == "table":
                out += [markdown_table(el, inp.results[el.binding_id], inp), ""]
            elif el.type == "chart":
                out += [chart_sentence(el, inp) + f" [Open live]({live_url(inp, el)})", ""]
    out.append(provenance_footer(inp))        # data as of, filters, truncation, run-as user
    return "\n".join(out)

docs.title: Step 14: The viz_type mapping
docs.text:
Tier 1 ships in the MVP. Tier 2 ships in v1 as native emulations or vector SVG. Tier 3 is an honest fallback, never a picture of the chart. Viz keys come from superset-frontend/packages/superset-ui-core/src/chart/types/VizType.ts; 6.1.0 has the same enum minus butterfly and point_cluster_map.

viz_type Shape PPTX DOCX HTML live Fallback Tier big_number_total, pop_kpi scalar KPI group KPI paragraph KPI card none needed 1 big_number scalar plus series KPI plus LINE sparkline KPI plus chart part KPI plus sparkline KPI only 1 echarts_timeseries_line, echarts_timeseries, echarts_timeseries_smooth, compare, time_pivot series (temporal) LINE or LINE_MARKERS, smooth for smooth chart part ECharts line table 1 echarts_timeseries_bar series COLUMN or BAR, clustered, stacked or stacked_100 chart part bar table 1 echarts_area series AREA, AREA_STACKED, AREA_STACKED_100 chart part area table 1 echarts_timeseries_step series XY_SCATTER_LINES_NO_MARKERS with duplicated points chart part step line LINE 1 echarts_timeseries_scatter xy XY_SCATTER (date serial x) chart part scatter table 1 pie series (one) PIE or DOUGHNUT, per-point colors, percentage labels chart part pie table with share 1 bubble_v2 xyz BUBBLE chart part scatter with symbol size table 1 radar series RADAR, RADAR_MARKERS, RADAR_FILLED chart part radar table 1 histogram_v2 series (bins from server histogram post-processing) COLUMN_CLUSTERED, gap_width = 0 chart part bar bin table 1 table, ag-grid-table table native table Word table sortable HTML table truncated table 1 pivot_table_v2 pivot (result_type=post_processed) table with merged headers table with merges table with spans flattened table 1 mixed_timeseries two queries DrawingML combo (gate G1) combo chart part multi-axis two native charts 2 funnel series BAR_STACKED with a transparent offset series chart part funnel ordered table 2 waterfall series COLUMN_STACKED with a transparent base series chart part stacked bar running-total table 2 gauge_chart, bullet scalar KPI with min, max and target; bullet as a BAR_CLUSTERED overlay paragraph or chart part gauge, bullet KPI text 2 heatmap_v2 pivot heat table (cell fills) shaded table heatmap plain table 2 box_plot table (quartiles from server boxplot post-processing) quartile table table boxplot quartile table 2 butterfly [M], gantt_chart series mirrored or offset stacked bars chart part bar table 2 treemap_v2, sunburst_v2, sankey_v2, graph_chart, tree_chart, rose, candlestick table SVG from rows (vector, native: "svg") plus data table SVG ECharts equivalent hierarchical, edge or OHLC table 2 word_cloud table ranked table table word cloud ranked table 3 world_map, country_map table by region ranked region table plus link (v2: SVG choropleth from bundled GeoJSON) table ECharts map region table 3 deck_*, mapbox, point_cluster_map [M], cartodiagram aggregated table aggregated table plus narrative plus "Open live map" link same link never rasterized 3 handlebars table text from server-side rendering (Python Handlebars unverified) paragraphs HTML raw rows table 3

Backend post-processing already shapes many of these: timeseries arrive pivoted wide, histogram_v2 arrives binned, box_plot arrives as quartiles, and table and pivot results can be requested as post_processed. The renderer maps rows to series and does no analytics of its own. The Data Digest shows each candidate's tier, and the planner prefers tier 1 for hero slots.

Gotcha: chartex types do not exist in python-pptx

Office 2016 "chartex" charts (waterfall, treemap, sunburst, funnel, box and whisker, histogram, pareto) are not even in XL_CHART_TYPE, and 3-D, surface and stock types raise NotImplementedError in python-pptx's XML writer factory. Every such type above is either an emulation over a creatable type or row-derived SVG, which is why the mapping is tiered rather than one-to-one.

docs.title: Step 15: Theme and color mapping
docs.text:
Superset source Target Rule Dashboard json_metadata.label_colors per-series and per-point colors highest precedence Dashboard json_metadata.map_label_colors, shared_label_colors same next, so "Classic Cars" keeps its dashboard color Chart form_data.color_scheme, dashboard color_scheme palette by scheme name hex lists copied from Superset's built-in categorical and sequential schemes at wheel build time; EXTRA_CATEGORICAL_COLOR_SCHEMES and EXTRA_SEQUENTIAL_COLOR_SCHEMES merged at runtime (apache/superset: superset/config.py:1228, 1385); no REST API returns palettes Dashboard theme.json_data, else THEME_DEFAULT (apache/superset: superset/config.py:1264-1313): colorPrimary, colorSuccess, colorError, fontFamily, brandLogoUrl PPTX and DOCX accent1 to accent6 (palette first six), positive and negative colors, latin font if available, logo slot; HTML CSS variables only when the template's theme.lock is false Chart linear_color_scheme heat tables sequential scale databound_docs/render/colors.py (sketch)
def series_colors(el, res, theme: ThemeSpec) -> list[str]:
    labels = res.point_labels if el.native in ("pie", "doughnut") else [str(s) for s in res.series_labels]
    explicit = {**theme.label_colors, **el.colors}             # element overrides dashboard
    palette = theme.palette or palette_for(theme.color_scheme or "supersetColors")
    used, out, i = set(explicit.values()), [], 0
    for label in labels:
        if label in explicit:
            out.append(explicit[label])
            continue
        while palette[i % len(palette)] in used and i < 2 * len(palette):
            i += 1                                             # skip colors already pinned to labels
        out.append(palette[i % len(palette)])
        i += 1
    return out


def apply_theme_accents(prs, theme: ThemeSpec) -> None:
    if theme.lock:
        return                                                 # template brand wins
    from lxml import etree
    from pptx.opc.constants import RELATIONSHIP_TYPE as RT
    from pptx.oxml.ns import qn
    master = prs.slide_masters[0]
    theme_part = master.part.part_related_by(RT.THEME)         # ppt/theme/theme1.xml
    root = etree.fromstring(theme_part.blob)
    scheme = root.find(".//" + qn("a:clrScheme"))
    for n, color in enumerate(theme.palette[:6], start=1):
        srgb = scheme.find(qn(f"a:accent{n}")).find(qn("a:srgbClr"))
        if srgb is not None:
            srgb.set("val", color.lstrip("#").upper())
    theme_part._blob = etree.tostring(root, xml_declaration=True, encoding="UTF-8", standalone=True)
    # theme parts are plain blob parts in python-pptx, so the XML is edited and written back

Colors are assigned by label, not by position, so a refresh that adds a series keeps every existing color, and the same label has the same color in the dashboard, the deck, the document and the live page.

docs.title: Step 16: The no-screenshot guarantee, enforced
docs.text:
The requirement is turned into checks that fail CI:

superset-databound-docs/pyproject.toml (import-linter contract)
[tool.importlinter]
root_packages = ["databound_docs", "databound"]

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Data-Bound Documents never imports Superset screenshot or webdriver code"
type = "forbidden"
source_modules = ["databound_docs", "databound.docgen"]
forbidden_modules = [
    "superset.utils.webdriver",
    "superset.utils.screenshots",
    "superset.utils.screenshot_utils",
    "superset.utils.pdf",
]
allow_indirect_imports = false
tests/render/test_no_raster.py
import re
import zipfile
from io import BytesIO
from lxml import etree

NS = {"p": "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/presentationml/2006/main",
      "a": "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/main"}

def test_no_bound_shape_is_a_picture(rendered_pptx: bytes, manifest: dict):
    svg_ok = {n for n, s in manifest["shapes"].items() if s.get("native") == "svg"}
    with zipfile.ZipFile(BytesIO(rendered_pptx)) as z:
        for name in z.namelist():
            if not re.match(r"ppt/slides/slide\d+\.xml$", name):
                continue
            root = etree.fromstring(z.read(name))
            for pic in root.iterfind(".//p:pic", NS):
                shape_name = pic.find("./p:nvPicPr/p:cNvPr", NS).get("name")
                if shape_name.startswith("dbd:"):
                    assert shape_name in svg_ok, f"{name}: bound shape {shape_name} is a raster picture"
                    assert pic.find(".//a:blip", NS) is not None
                    # the svg element must carry an svgBlip extension generated from rows
                    assert b"svgBlip" in etree.tostring(pic)

The same test runs on DOCX for every dbd:binding content control. The only images that may exist are template assets (image elements, never captures) and PNG conversions of DBD's own SVG for email clients.

docs.title: Step 17: Golden-file testing of renderers
docs.text:
Renderer output is XML in a zip, so it can be compared exactly once the volatile parts are normalized. Golden files are checked in per renderer version; a change to them is a reviewed change.

tests/render/golden.py
import zipfile
from io import BytesIO
from lxml import etree
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from pptx import Presentation

VOLATILE_ATTRS = {"id", "{http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships}id"}
VOLATILE_PARTS = {"docProps/core.xml", "docProps/app.xml"}

def canonical_xml(blob: bytes) -> bytes:
    root = etree.fromstring(blob)
    for el in root.iter():
        for attr in list(el.attrib):
            if attr in VOLATILE_ATTRS:
                del el.attrib[attr]
    return etree.tostring(root, method="c14n")

def canonical_package(blob: bytes) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    out = {}
    with zipfile.ZipFile(BytesIO(blob)) as z:
        for name in sorted(z.namelist()):
            if name in VOLATILE_PARTS or name.endswith(".xlsx"):
                continue                                   # workbooks are compared by cell values
            data = z.read(name)
            out[name] = canonical_xml(data) if name.endswith((".xml", ".rels")) else data
    return out

def workbook_cells(pptx_blob: bytes) -> dict[str, list[list]]:
    prs = Presentation(BytesIO(pptx_blob))
    cells = {}
    for slide in prs.slides:
        for shape in slide.shapes:
            if shape.has_chart and shape.name.startswith("dbd:chart:"):
                xlsx = shape.chart.part.chart_workbook.xlsx_part.blob
                ws = load_workbook(BytesIO(xlsx), read_only=True).active
                cells[shape.name] = [list(r) for r in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True)]
    return cells

def test_exec_review_deck(golden, render_fixture):
    blob = render_fixture("tpl_exec_review", "example_deck_v1.json", "results_v1.json")
    assert canonical_package(blob) == golden.package("exec_review_v1")
    assert workbook_cells(blob) == golden.json("exec_review_v1.cells")

def test_refresh_changes_only_data(render_fixture, refresh_fixture):
    before = render_fixture("tpl_exec_review", "example_deck_v1.json", "results_v1.json")
    after = refresh_fixture(before, "results_v2.json")
    diff = {k for k, v in canonical_package(after).items() if canonical_package(before).get(k) != v}
    allowed = {n for n in diff if n.startswith(("ppt/charts/", "ppt/slides/", "customXml/"))}
    assert diff == allowed                                  # no theme, layout or master changes

The renderer test layer, in full:

Test What it proves Golden PPTX and DOCX canonicalized XML (sorted attributes, ids and timestamps stripped) equals the checked-in package, chart XML included Workbook read-back every embedded workbook, opened with openpyxl, holds exactly the shaped rows with raw numbers (not formatted strings) replace_data round trip refresh with new fixture rows changes only chart caches, workbooks, table cells and token runs (XML diff), and re-applied colors match labels Guarded token rewrite a run edited after rendering is reported as token_edited_skipped and left unchanged No raster no dbd:* shape or dbd:binding control targets an image part, except row-derived SVG Office compatibility LibreOffice headless conversion in CI checks page counts and text extraction (no pixel diffs); PowerPoint 365, Keynote and LibreOffice open the files with working Edit Data before each release (gates G1 to G6) PDF text is selectable and charts are vector (pdffonts output and path counts), with no image XObjects for chart areas Format mapping table-driven tests for d3_to_excel and the vendored format_number_with_config against values produced by the frontend formatter

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• Superset's PNG and PDF reports are browser captures because chart rendering lives in TypeScript, so Data-Bound Documents reuses only Superset's data path and renders every output from BindingResult rows.
  • The PPTX Renderer builds native python-pptx charts whose embedded XlsxWriter workbook holds raw numbers with Excel formats, plus native tables, KPI groups and one run per token, all named dbd:* and described in alt text.
  • Combo charts come from the DrawingML Chart Writer and other non-native types from stacked-bar emulations or row-derived SVG, with the honest tiered viz_type mapping and its prototype gates.
  • A manifest part, shape names and fallbacks let refresh call Chart.replace_data, rewrite tables, and rewrite token runs only when their text is unchanged.
  • DOCX shares the DrawingML chart builder (gate G5), live pages re-resolve as the viewer and draw with ECharts, static HTML embeds Vega-Lite SVG, and PDF is printed offline from that vector HTML.
  • An import-linter contract, a no-raster test and golden-file tests with workbook read-back make "no screenshots, native and refreshable" a property CI checks on every change.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Continue with Building the Superset extension, which packages these renderers, the generation flow and the REST API into the databound.docgen extension and its wheel.

docs.title: Building the Superset extension
docs.text:
Reads: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py, superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py, superset/tasks/decorators.py, superset/core/mcp/core_mcp_injection.py, superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/views/index.ts · Builds on: Target architecture · Time: ~45 min

This chapter builds the DBD Extension (databound.docgen), the thin Superset wiring of Superset Data-Bound Documents, from an empty folder to a deployable .supx bundle. You will scaffold it with the real superset-extensions CLI, write the extension.json, the backend entrypoint, the @api REST class, the @task Global Task Framework (GTF) tasks and the @tool MCP tools, then the frontend contributions (SQL Lab panel, commands, menus, the master-only chat slot and the standalone Studio page). The chapter ends with the local development loop, bundling, deployment and testing. Every API that exists only on Superset master is flagged with the fallback that keeps the extension working on 6.1.0.

The generation runtime itself (the databound_docs library that the extension calls) is the subject of the next chapter, Building the generation service. Here we only build what must live inside a .supx.

Interpretation this chapter implements

Data-Bound Documents is one common, output-agnostic generation framework. It turns a prompt, a chosen template and a Superset data context (a dashboard with its live filter state, saved charts, datasets with their saved metrics, or a SQL Lab query) into (a) PowerPoint decks, (b) documents (DOCX, PDF, Markdown), (c) text (narratives, summaries, emails, alert briefs) and (d) web pages (interactive HTML reports, and in v2 generated Superset dashboards). It runs on demand (button, chat, REST, MCP) or on events (cron schedules, alerts, data freshness, definition changes, webhooks). Every chart, table, KPI and number comes from a live Superset query executed with the requesting user's permissions and RLS, is rendered natively (editable PPTX charts with an embedded workbook, real tables, real text), is never a screenshot, and can be re-run to refresh with new data. The extension built here is the part of that framework that plugs into Superset's processes and UI. See Vision and requirements for the full requirement list.

docs.title: Versions and availability tags
docs.text:
The chapter targets two Superset lines at once, exactly as the blueprint does:

Published tooling used in this chapter (registry metadata, all released 2026-05-11):

Master's superset-core still declares 0.1.0 but already carries APIs that UPDATING.md describes as "available from 0.2.0" (apache/superset: UPDATING.md:331-333). Treat anything you do not find in the 0.1.0 packages as master only.

docs.title: Step 1: Decide what goes into the .supx
docs.text:
A .supx is a zip with manifest.json, frontend/dist/<files> and backend/src/<files>. Any other entry is rejected with "Unexpected file in bundle" (apache/superset: superset/extensions/utils.py:43-48, regexes FRONTEND_REGEX and BACKEND_REGEX; the check is in get_loaded_extension, apache/superset: superset/extensions/utils.py:189-239). Every backend/src entry is handed to the in-memory importer as Python source for a module whose name is the path with the file extension stripped (InMemoryFinder._get_module_name, apache/superset: superset/extensions/utils.py:122-131). The CLI copies only files matched by [tool.apache_superset_extensions.build] include and installs nothing (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py:225-275). So the split is fixed by the platform, and the blueprint's principle "thin .supx, fat wheel" follows from it:

Lives in the .supx (databound/docgen/...) Lives in the wheel superset-databound-docs (databound_docs) entrypoint.py, api.py, tasks.py, tools.py, triggers.py Document Spec models, Planner, Binding Registry, Binding Resolver core, Fact Engine superset_adapter.py (the Superset Adapter, the only module that imports Superset internals) Narrative Writer and Verifier, Renderers, DrawingML Chart Writer Frontend: SQL Lab panel, chat panel, Studio page bundle, live page bundle Template Registry and importers, LLM providers, storage backends, Alembic env celery_routing.py, the superset dbd CLI

The wheel is preinstalled with python-pptx==1.0.2, python-docx==1.2.0, httpx, vl-convert-python, jsonschema and optionally playwright in every Superset image that loads the extension: web, Celery worker and MCP.

Gotcha: the bundle cannot carry dependencies or binary assets

[project] dependencies in the backend pyproject.toml and a requirements.txt next to it are never installed by anything. A .supx also cannot usefully carry a .pptx master in backend/src: the bundle regex accepts any file there, but the importer treats it as the source of a module named after the path, and there is no resource reader to get the bytes back. Built-in template masters therefore ship inside the wheel as package data, and admin-uploaded masters go to object storage through the Template Registry.

docs.title: Step 2: Scaffold with superset-extensions init
docs.text:
Install the CLI in a separate virtual environment (it does not need Superset) and scaffold non-interactively. The option names are the ones defined on init (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py:792-823):

Scaffold the DBD Extension
python -m venv .venv-ext && . .venv-ext/bin/activate
pip install "apache-superset-extensions-cli==0.1.0"

mkdir -p superset-databound-docs && cd superset-databound-docs
superset-extensions init \
  --publisher databound \
  --name docgen \
  --display-name "Data-Bound Documents" \
  --version 1.0.0 \
  --license Apache-2.0 \
  --frontend --backend
mv docgen extension

init creates docgen/ with extension.json, .gitignore, frontend/{package.json, webpack.config.js, tsconfig.json, src/index.tsx} and backend/{pyproject.toml, src/databound/docgen/entrypoint.py}. Renaming the folder to extension/ matches the repository layout of the blueprint; the CLI only cares about the current working directory when you run build, bundle or dev. It also sets the npm package name to @databound/docgen and the backend project name to databound-docgen (generate_extension_names, apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/utils.py:334-390).

Gotcha: the published 0.1.0 CLI and master's CLI scaffold different webpack configs

Line references in this chapter are to the CLI source on master. The init options, the bundle -o option and the default bundle name are the same in the 6.1.0 tag, but the frontend template is not: the 6.1.0 template maps @apache-superset/core to window.superset with externalsType: "window" and shares only react, react-dom and antd, while master's template shares @apache-superset/core as a singleton instead. pip install apache-superset-extensions-cli==0.1.0 was released with 6.1, so expect the 6.1 form; Step 10.2 replaces the generated file with one that builds both.

The names the CLI derives from publisher and name:

Identifier Value How it is derived Extension id databound.docgen f"{publisher}.{name}" (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/extensions/types.py:38-84) Backend entrypoint databound.docgen.entrypoint f"{publisher_snake}.{name_snake}.entrypoint" (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py:149-184) Module Federation name databound_docgen f"{camel(publisher)}_{camel(name)}" (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/utils.py:318-331) REST base /extensions/databound/docgen/v1 /extensions/{publisher}/{name} plus /{resource_name} (apache/superset: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py:189-207) GTF task types extensions.databound.docgen.<task> prefix added in extension context (apache/superset: superset/tasks/decorators.py:147-160) MCP tool names extensions.databound.docgen.<tool> prefix added in extension context (apache/superset: superset/core/mcp/core_mcp_injection.py:123-142) Frontend asset URL /api/v1/extensions/databound/docgen/<file> webpack publicPath in the template

docs.title: Step 3: Write extension.json
docs.text:
extension/extension.json
{
  "publisher": "databound",
  "name": "docgen",
  "displayName": "Data-Bound Documents",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "license": "Apache-2.0",
  "description": "Prompt and template driven decks, documents, pages and briefs bound to live Superset data",
  "dependencies": [],
  "permissions": []
}

Validation rules come from BaseExtension: publisher and name match ^[a-z]([a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*)?$, displayName matches ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9\s\-_\.]*$ (so the hyphen in "Data-Bound" is fine), and version matches ^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$. superset-extensions validate checks these, the npm version (at least 10.8.2), the presence of an include list in backend/pyproject.toml, and the conventional entry files backend/src/databound/docgen/entrypoint.py and frontend/src/index.tsx (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py:314-441). Master's CLI additionally fails when the version or license in frontend/package.json or backend/pyproject.toml differs from extension.json; the 6.1.0 CLI does not compare them. Keep all three at 1.0.0 and Apache-2.0 so both pass.

Gotcha: permissions, dependencies and description do nothing at runtime

No host code enforces permissions or dependencies on master (dependencies is only echoed by GET /api/v1/extensions/). Authorization comes from FAB permissions on the API class and on the MCP tools (Step 6 and Step 8). build_manifest also does not copy description or license into dist/manifest.json, so GET /api/v1/extensions/ reports an empty description for this extension. Keep "permissions": [] so nobody mistakes it for an enforcement point.

docs.title: Step 4: Lay out the project tree
docs.text:
After the scaffold and the files written in this chapter, extension/ looks like this:

extension/ (DBD Extension project)
extension/
├── extension.json
├── frontend/
│   ├── package.json
│   ├── tsconfig.json
│   ├── webpack.config.js          # Module Federation remote (two variants, Step 10)
│   ├── webpack.page.config.js     # standalone Studio and live page bundles
│   └── src/
