Gotcha: extension code is fully trusted

A .supx backend runs unsandboxed in the web, worker and MCP processes (R1 1.7), with the same database and secrets access as Superset itself. Every control in this chapter assumes the DBD code is the code you reviewed. Treat installing or upgrading the extension like upgrading Superset: pinned artifacts, review, and on master the version policy and denylist.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• Data-Bound Documents has no data authorization of its own: it makes g.user correct for every entry point and lets ChartDataCommand.validate() and Superset's RLS injection decide, adding raise_for_access(..., force_dataset_match=True) only where Superset does not check (raw SQL through Database.execute).
  • override_user(user, force=False) silently skips when g.user is already set, so the adapter asserts the switch; scheduled and webhook runs use an explicit run-as user that is re-validated before every run, with no fallback.
  • RLS-correct numbers are guaranteed by execution; RLS-safe prose is guaranteed by tokens, the entity scan, the RLS fingerprint and the viewer rule on live pages; every DBD cache is keyed at least as strictly as Superset's RLS-aware cache key.
  • The LLM sees only the Data Digest and per-section FACTS, bounded by exposure levels, PII defaults and optional label masking; data and metadata are treated as hostile input and outputs are encoded per format, including spreadsheet-formula escaping in embedded workbooks.
  • Audit, secrets, tenancy and air-gapped operation reuse Superset's own mechanisms (event_logger, Talisman CSP, rate limiting, one instance per tenant) and the template strategy removes the LLM entirely when required.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: With identity and access settled, Scheduling and live refresh follows the same document through its life: refresh on open, refresh in place, triggers, caching and delivery.

docs.title: Scheduling and live refresh
docs.text:
Reads: superset/tasks/scheduler.py, superset/tasks/cron_util.py, superset/config.py, superset/reports/notifications/webhook.py, superset/models/slice.py, superset/common/query_context_processor.py, superset/charts/data/api.py, superset/utils/core.py · Builds on: Data-bound slide model, Native rendering, no screenshots, Security, RLS, auth · Time: ~50 min

A generated document in Data-Bound Documents is not a file, it is a DocumentSpec whose every value is a re-runnable query. This chapter follows that document through the rest of its life: what happens when someone opens a live page, how a PowerPoint or Word file is refreshed in place without being rebuilt, the exact difference between refreshing and regenerating, how schedules and Superset Alerts start runs without an interactive user, how data changes and chart edits are detected, which caches sit in the path and how their keys are built, what provenance is stamped on every artifact, and how results are delivered by email, Slack, webhook or storage. Sequence diagrams show each path end to end.

This is the "dynamic data" half of the requirement adopted for Part VII (see Vision and requirements): the prepared PPT, document, text or page must use live Superset data, never screenshots, and must be re-runnable to refresh with new data.

Availability tags

[6.1] means present in the 6.1.0 tag (May 2026) and on master. [M] means master only (expected in 7.0, mapping UNVERIFIED). Superset citations refer to master at cabd8d4 unless marked otherwise.

docs.title: Step 1: Four lifecycles for one document
docs.text:
Every document version can be consumed in four ways: as a live page, by refresh (which has two render modes, in place and re-render), by regeneration, or as a snapshot. They differ in whose data appears, whether the LLM runs, and whether a new version is created.

Mode Trigger Queries run as LLM New version Output Live page a viewer opens GET /pages/<document_id> the viewer never on open (only "Regenerate for me") no HTML rendered client-side from render-model Refresh in place user, schedule or event, mode: "in_place" the requester or run-as user only when the narrative policy fires yes, reason: "refresh" the existing PPTX or DOCX with data replaced Re-render user, schedule or event, mode: "rerender" same only when the narrative policy fires yes fresh files from the template Regenerate user (POST /documents/<id>/regenerate) or a generate trigger the requester or run-as user yes, full or per section yes, reason: "generate" new structure, possibly different sections Snapshot mode: "snapshot" bindings, snapshot shares stored rows never no the stored rows, never re-queried 
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> v1: generate
    v1 --> v1: live page open (no new version)
    v1 --> v2: refresh, data changed
    v1 --> v1: refresh, data unchanged (refresh.unchanged)
    v2 --> v3: chat edit or manual edit
    v3 --> v4: regenerate section
    v4 --> v5: scheduled refresh
    v5 --> [*]

Versions are immutable rows in dbd_document_version with a reason column, and the stored spec records provenance.parent_version and provenance.reason (DocumentProvenance). Binding results are appended to dbd_binding_result and never overwritten, so the question "what data was in the file emailed on Monday" always has an answer.

docs.title: Step 2: Regenerate versus refresh, precisely
docs.text:
The two words are easy to blur. The design defines them by what they are allowed to change.

Part of the spec Refresh Regenerate (whole document) Regenerate (sections) sections, layouts, slot assignments kept rebuilt by the Planner rebuilt for the listed sections bindings kept (same ids, same sources) re-proposed through the Binding Registry re-proposed for the listed sections Binding results and facts values recomputed recomputed recomputed Token runs in text re-resolved rewritten rewritten in the listed sections Narratives (status: "verified") per narrative policy (Step 3.3) rewritten rewritten in the listed sections Narratives (status: "user_edited") text kept, tokens re-resolved, claim lint may flag kept unless the user explicitly includes them same Pinned values (TextElement.pinned_note) kept, still marked "edited, not live" kept kept Template version kept kept unless the request names a new one kept User formatting in the PPTX (in-place mode) kept lost (new file) not applicable

Refresh is cheap and deterministic: zero LLM calls in the common case. Regenerate is an LLM job with the same prompt, template and context, which is what you want when the story itself should change (a new quarter with a different driver).

docs.title: 2.1 The refresh request
2.2 Parameter roll-forward
docs.text:
Parameters decide whether "refresh next quarter" means anything. A Parameter of type time_range stores both value and default:

DocumentSpec.parameters (excerpt)
"time_range": {"type": "time_range", "value": "2026-07-01 : 2026-10-01",
               "default": "Last quarter", "label": "Period",
               "native_filter_id": "NATIVE_FILTER-time"}

At generation time the captured dashboard filter produced the absolute value. On refresh the run uses, in order: an explicit parameters override in the request or trigger; otherwise the parameter's default when the document was created with a relative intent (the trigger config says "parameters": {"time_range": "Last week"} for a weekly brief); otherwise the stored value. Superset's own time grammar resolves the relative string at query time, and the resolved from_dttm and to_dttm come back in the chart-data result and are stored in Provenance. The period_label fact turns them into text, so a title like Revenue for {{f:f_period}} updates itself.

Gotcha: an absolute range never moves

A document captured from a dashboard filtered to 2026-07-01 : 2026-10-01 will refresh that same quarter forever unless something rolls it forward. That is correct for an audit deck and wrong for a weekly brief. The trigger form makes the choice explicit by showing the effective time_range for the next run.

docs.title: Step 3: The refresh algorithm
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["Refresh requested (user, trigger, page open)"] --> B["Apply parameter roll-forward"]
    B --> C["Resolve live bindings as the run identity"]
    C --> D{"All data_hash values unchanged"}
    D -->|"yes and skip_if_unchanged"| E["refresh.unchanged, no new version"]
    D -->|"no"| F["Recompute facts"]
    F --> G{"Narrative policy and drift rules"}
    G -->|"retoken"| H["Update token runs"]
    G -->|"drift"| I["Narrative Writer and Verifier for affected narratives only"]
    H --> J["New version, reason refresh"]
    I --> J
    J --> K["Render in place: replace_data, tables, guarded token runs"]
    K --> L["Deliver per trigger and update provenance stamps"]

docs.title: 3.1 The task body
docs.text:
backend/src/databound/docgen/tasks.py (refresh_document)
@task(name="refresh_document", scope=TaskScope.PRIVATE, timeout=600)
def refresh_document(document_id: str, user_id: int, narrative: str = "regenerate_on_drift",
                     mode: str = "in_place", force: bool = False) -> None:
    ctx = get_context()
    cancel = CancelToken()
    ctx.on_abort(cancel.set)
    with sa.as_user(user_id=user_id):
        job = repo.jobs.start_refresh(document_id, user_id)
        spec = repo.documents.current_spec(document_id)
        params = rollforward(spec, job.parameters)
        prev = repo.results.latest_by_binding(document_id, spec.version)

        results = {}
        live = [b for b in spec.bindings if b.mode == "live"]
        for i, b in enumerate(live):
            cancel.check()
            results[b.id] = Resolver(sa).resolve(b, spec.context, params, force=force)
            ctx.update_task(progress=(i + 1, len(live)),
                            payload={"stage": "resolve", "document_id": document_id})
            repo.events.append(job.id, "binding.resolved", results[b.id].summary())

        if spec.refresh_policy.skip_if_unchanged and all(
                prev.get(k) and prev[k].provenance.data_hash == r.provenance.data_hash
                for k, r in results.items()):
            repo.events.append(job.id, "refresh.unchanged",
                               {"document_id": document_id, "version": spec.version})
            return

        new_facts = FactEngine().compute(spec.facts, results)
        plan = NarrativePolicy(narrative, spec.refresh_policy.drift_rules).plan(
            spec, old_facts=spec.facts, new_facts=new_facts)
        new_spec = apply_refresh(spec, new_facts, plan, writer=Writer(cancel=cancel),
                                 verifier=Verifier())
        version = repo.documents.save_version(new_spec, reason="refresh",
                                              parent=spec.version, results=results)
        render_in_place(document_id, version, mode=mode, formats=job.formats)
        repo.events.append(job.id, "document.ready",
                           {"document_id": document_id, "version": version})

Two hashes drive this loop, and they answer different questions:

Hash Over Answers query_hash the canonical query context JSON, without force "is this the same question?" A change means the chart definition or a filter changed data_hash the canonical shaped rows (sorted keys, normalized numbers, ISO datetimes) "is this the same answer?" A change means the data changed

skip_if_unchanged compares data_hash only. A changed query_hash with an identical data_hash (for example a chart's color changed) still skips the data refresh but records the new query_hash in provenance.

docs.title: 3.2 Change detection: the drift rules
docs.text:
Facts are compared one by one between the previous version and the new results. Each rule is a pure function over (old_fact, new_fact):

databound_docs/facts/drift.py
from databound_docs.spec.models import Fact


def sign_flip(old: Fact, new: Fact) -> bool:
    return old.sign is not None and new.sign is not None and old.sign != new.sign


def rank_change_top3(old: Fact, new: Fact) -> bool:
    if old.op in ("argmax", "argmin", "label_at"):
        return old.label != new.label
    if old.op == "rank_of":
        return (old.value != new.value) and min(old.value or 99, new.value or 99) <= 3
    if old.op == "top_k":
        return [x["label"] for x in old.value[:3]] != [x["label"] for x in new.value[:3]]
    return False


def abs_change_pct_gt(threshold: float):
    def rule(old: Fact, new: Fact) -> bool:
        if not isinstance(old.value, (int, float)) or not isinstance(new.value, (int, float)):
            return False
        if old.value == 0:
            return new.value != 0
        return abs(new.value - old.value) / abs(old.value) * 100 > threshold
    return rule


RULES = {"sign_flip": sign_flip, "rank_change_top3": rank_change_top3,
         "abs_change_pct>10": abs_change_pct_gt(10.0)}

A narrative drifts when any rule fires for any fact in its fact_ids. A worked example:

Drift evaluation for narrative e7 (refresh of version 1)
{
  "element_id": "e7",
  "fact_ids": ["f_best_month"],
  "old": {"f_best_month": {"label": "Sep 2026", "value": 1041233.5}},
  "new": {"f_best_month": {"label": "Aug 2026", "value": 1102877.0}},
  "rules_fired": ["rank_change_top3"],
  "decision": "regenerate"
}

The old text was {{f:f_best_month.label}} was the strongest month of the quarter. Retokening alone would render "Aug 2026 was the strongest month", which is still true, so why regenerate? Because the rule cannot know whether the surrounding sentence depended on the old label (for example "...as the back-to-school push landed"). Regeneration costs one short LLM call for one narrative; the verifier then checks the new text against the new facts.

docs.title: 3.3 Narrative policies
docs.text:
Policy On refresh LLM calls keep text kept, tokens re-resolved; if claim lint fails against the new facts, the narrative is marked flagged ("stale narrative") none retoken tokens re-resolved only none regenerate_on_drift (default) narratives whose facts trip a drift rule are rewritten by the Narrative Writer and checked by the Narrative Verifier; the rest are retokened one per drifted narrative regenerate every non-edited narrative rewritten one per section

Claim lint (direction words against signs, superlatives next to rank facts, numeric comparatives) runs on every narrative under every policy, including user_edited ones, because tokens in a sentence a human wrote can still flip under new data. A user_edited narrative is never rewritten automatically; when lint fails it is flagged and the owner sees "your text may no longer match the data".

Gotcha: a flagged narrative still ships under keep

keep means "do not call the LLM". If lint flags a narrative during a scheduled delivery, the artifact still contains it, with a visible "stale narrative" footnote. Deliveries that must never contain flagged text set narrative: "regenerate_on_drift" (the default) or configure the trigger to hold delivery when any narrative is flagged ("hold_on_flagged": true in the trigger config).

docs.title: Step 4: Refresh on open for live pages
docs.text:
A page document with refresh_policy.on_open: true re-queries every time anyone opens it.

sequenceDiagram
    participant V as Viewer browser
    participant W as Superset web (DBD REST API)
    participant AD as Superset Adapter
    participant C as DATA_CACHE (Redis)
    participant DB as Analytics database
    V->>W: GET /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/pages/doc_id
    W-->>V: HTML shell with nonce, loads dbd-page.hash.js
    V->>W: GET /documents/doc_id/render-model?live=1&parameters=...
    loop each live binding
        W->>AD: build query context, apply dashboard filters and parameters
        AD->>C: ChartDataCommand looks up cache_key (includes RLS)
        alt cache hit
            C-->>AD: rows, is_cached true
        else cache miss
            AD->>DB: SQL with the viewer RLS predicates
            DB-->>AD: rows
            AD->>C: store under cache_key with TTL
        end
        AD-->>W: shaped rows plus provenance
    end
    W->>W: Fact Engine, token resolution, viewer narrative rule
    W-->>V: sections with rows, facts, provenance
    V->>V: ECharts draws charts, tables and KPIs

Details that matter in production:

  • No HTTP round trip. render-model calls ChartDataCommand in-process under the viewer's request. That avoids the 6.1 GLOBAL_ASYNC_QUERIES behavior where the chart-data HTTP endpoint answers 202 and then 401 without the async cookie (R2 1.7). The in-process command runs synchronously on both versions, so the async path never applies.
  • The data cache does the heavy lifting. Repeat opens by the same RLS context are cache hits in DATA_CACHE_CONFIG. Out of the box that is NullCache (apache/superset: superset/config.py:1532), so nothing is cached and every open re-runs every query. superset dbd doctor warns about this.
  • TTL per binding. DataBinding.cache_ttl is passed as the query context's custom_cache_timeout (a ChartDataQueryContextSchema field, apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1681), which is step 1 of the timeout chain and wins over chart, dataset and database timeouts (apache/superset: superset/common/query_context_processor.py:816-840). Leave it null to follow the dashboard's own caching.
  • Parameters re-resolve without the LLM. Period and region controls on the page send parameters= to render-model; facts and token text update, narratives follow the viewer rule from Security, RLS, auth.
  • Large pages. A page with many bindings and slow sources can set on_open: false. It then shows the last refreshed version with its "Data as of" stamp and a "Refresh now" button, and a cron or freshness trigger keeps it current.
  • "Refresh now" sends force=1, which bypasses the cache for that request only. It needs can_refresh.

Gotcha: live pages put query load on the web tier

Every open runs inside a gunicorn worker. A page shared with 500 people at 9:00 is 500 concurrent render-model calls; with a warm Redis data cache they are cheap, with NullCache they are 500 times every query. Configure DATA_CACHE_CONFIG, set sensible cache_ttl values, and prefer on_open: false plus a schedule for heavy pages.

docs.title: Step 5: Refresh in place for PPTX and DOCX
docs.text: In-place refresh keeps the file a person has already formatted. It is the PPTX Renderer's second mode (see Native rendering, no screenshots).

docs.title: 5.1 PPTX, step by step
docs.text:
1. Open the base file. The last artifact for the base version, or a file the user uploaded through POST /documents/<id>/refresh-upload (their own edited copy).
  2. Find the document. Read /customXml/dbd-manifest.json (relationship type urn:databound-docs:manifest). If PowerPoint dropped it on save (gate G3), fall back to the docProps/custom.xml property DbdDocumentId, the dbd:* shape names, and the JSON blob in the notes of the hidden last slide.
  3. Re-resolve bindings (Step 3).
  4. Charts. For every graphic frame named dbd:chart:<element_id>:<binding_id>, build new chart data from the shaped rows and call chart.replace_data(new_chart_data). python-pptx's implementation rewrites the cached series and category values through SeriesXmlRewriterFactory, then replaces the embedded workbook (self._workbook.update_from_xlsx_blob(chart_data.xlsx_blob)), leaving formatting alone (R3 2.1). When the series set changes, colors are re-applied by label from the theme's label_colors.
  5. Tables. For every dbd:table:<element_id>:<binding_id>, rewrite cell text. Rows are added up to max_rows by copying the last row's XML (so the user's row formatting carries over); extra rows are removed and a "+N more rows" footer updated.
  6. Token runs, guarded. For every run in the manifest, rewrite it only if its current text still equals the recorded rendered_text.
  7. Narratives per policy: drifted narratives get new runs built from the new token text, which replaces the paragraph's runs only when every run in that paragraph is unedited.
  8. Stamps. Update the footer stamp, alt text (descr) and the manifest.
databound_docs/render/pptx/refresh.py (guarded token rewrite)
def rewrite_token_runs(prs, manifest, displays) -> list[dict]:
    """displays maps a token string such as '{{f:f_rev}}' to its new display text."""
    report = []
    slides = {s.slide_id: s for s in prs.slides}
    for entry in manifest["token_runs"]:
        slide = slides.get(entry["slide_id"])
        shape = next((sh for sh in slide.shapes if sh.name == entry["shape_name"]), None) \
            if slide else None
        if shape is None or not shape.has_text_frame:
            report.append({**entry, "status": "binding.orphaned"})
            continue
        try:
            run = shape.text_frame.paragraphs[entry["paragraph_index"]].runs[entry["run_index"]]
        except IndexError:
            report.append({**entry, "status": "token_edited_skipped"})
            continue
        if run.text != entry["rendered_text"]:
            report.append({**entry, "status": "token_edited_skipped"})   # a human edited it
            continue
        run.text = displays[entry["token"]]
        entry["rendered_text"] = run.text
        report.append({**entry, "status": "ok"})
    return report

The guard is the reason a user can type over a number in PowerPoint and not lose it on the next refresh. The refresh report lists every skipped run, and the Studio shows them as "edited in the file, not refreshed".

Gotcha: deleted and renamed shapes

If a user deletes a bound chart or renames its shape in the Selection Pane, refresh cannot find it. It records binding.orphaned for that binding in the refresh report (a report status, like token_edited_skipped, not a job event) and leaves the slide alone. It never re-adds the chart at its old position, because the user may have removed it on purpose. Re-render mode (mode: "rerender") restores the template layout.

Gotcha: combo charts are re-emitted, not replaced

replace_data on a multi-plot chart is UNVERIFIED (gate G2). The DrawingML Chart Writer therefore re-emits the whole c:chartSpace for combo charts and copies the old part's formatting elements (c:spPr, c:txPr, axis settings) onto the new one. Until gate G1 passes, mixed_timeseries renders as two stacked native charts, and each of those refreshes with plain replace_data.

docs.title: 5.3 DOCX
docs.text: Bound content in DOCX sits in content controls (w:sdt with w:tag="dbd:binding:<id>" or dbd:fact:<id>). Refresh finds each control by tag and rewrites its content: table cells, chart parts (option A, behind gate G5) through the same DrawingML builder, and token runs under the same "unchanged text only" guard. Whether Word preserves content controls wrapped around drawings on save is UNVERIFIED (gate G6); the fallback anchors are bookmarks named after the same tags. Until G5 passes, DOCX charts are vector SVG pictures computed from rows, and refresh replaces the picture part with a newly computed SVG and its PNG fallback.

docs.title: Step 6: Scheduled generation
docs.text: GTF runs work now; it has no cron, no run_at and no retry policy (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/tasks/types.py:143-150). Schedules therefore come from a Celery beat entry the operator adds once, which fires a plain Celery task every minute. That task finds due triggers and schedules GTF tasks for them.

docs.title: 6.1 Configuration
6.2 Finding due triggers
docs.text:
cron_schedule_window(triggered_at, cron, timezone) (apache/superset: superset/tasks/cron_util.py:74) yields the cron times inside a window of ALERT_REPORTS_CRON_WINDOW_SIZE seconds centered on the trigger time (59 by default, apache/superset: superset/config.py:2810), converted to naive UTC. An invalid timezone falls back to UTC with a warning.

databound_docs/triggers/tick.py
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from flask import current_app


def due_cron_triggers(request_expires: str | None):
    from databound_docs.db import repo
    try:
        from superset.tasks.cron_util import cron_schedule_window     # [6.1]
    except ImportError:
        from databound_docs.compat.cron_window import cron_schedule_window   # vendored copy

    if request_expires:
        triggered_at = (datetime.fromisoformat(request_expires)
                        - current_app.config["CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULER_EXPIRES"])
    else:
        triggered_at = datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc)
    for trig in repo.triggers.active(type="cron"):
        cfg = trig.config
        for scheduled_for in cron_schedule_window(triggered_at, cfg["crontab"],
                                                  cfg.get("timezone", "UTC")):
            yield trig, scheduled_for
backend/src/databound/docgen/tasks.py (beat tick)
@celery_app.task(name="databound_docs.trigger_tick", bind=True, ignore_result=True)
def trigger_tick(self) -> None:
    from databound_docs.triggers.tick import due_cron_triggers
    for trig, scheduled_for in due_cron_triggers(self.request.expires):
        run_trigger.schedule(
            trigger_id=trig.id, scheduled_for=scheduled_for.isoformat(), event=None,
            options=TaskOptions(task_key=f"{trig.id}:{scheduled_for.isoformat()}",
                                task_name=f"DBD trigger {trig.id}"))

The task_key "<trigger_id>:<scheduled_for>" is what makes duplicate ticks harmless: two beat processes, a retried tick, or two adjacent windows that both contain the same cron time all submit the same key, and GTF joins the existing task instead of creating a second one.

Gotcha: GTF dedup only covers active tasks

GTF deduplicates against tasks that are still pending or running. If a run finished in 20 seconds and a late duplicate tick arrives a minute later, the key is free again. run_trigger therefore also checks dbd_job for a completed job with the same (trigger_id, scheduled_for) and returns immediately when one exists.

docs.title: 6.3 One scheduled run, end to end
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Celery beat
    participant K as trigger_tick (databound_docs queue)
    participant T as GTF TaskManager
    participant W as run_trigger (SYSTEM scope)
    participant AD as Superset Adapter
    participant L as LLM
    participant O as Object storage
    participant D as Delivery (SMTP or Slack)
    B->>K: databound_docs.trigger_tick every minute
    K->>K: cron_schedule_window over active cron triggers
    K->>T: run_trigger.schedule with task_key trigger and scheduled_for
    T->>W: tasks.execute routed by task_type
    W->>W: preflight run_as (active, can_refresh, datasource access)
    W->>AD: as_user(run_as), resolve bindings with rolled-forward parameters
    alt data unchanged and skip_if_unchanged
        W->>W: refresh.unchanged, no delivery
    else data changed
        W->>W: facts, drift rules
        opt narrative drifted
            W->>L: Narrative Writer for drifted narratives only
        end
        W->>O: refresh PPTX in place, print PDF from static HTML
        W->>D: email with attachments and provenance footer
    end
    W->>W: update last_run_on, last_status, last_data_hashes

run_trigger runs with TaskScope.SYSTEM because it is started by the platform, not by a user's click, and it switches to the run-as user only after preflight (see Security, RLS, auth). The body calls the refresh pipeline inline rather than scheduling a second task, so one GTF row represents one trigger run in the Task List.

docs.title: 6.4 The trigger record
docs.text:
TriggerSpec (cron, weekly brief)
{
  "document_id": "doc_01JC8Z6Q4M5K",
  "type": "cron",
  "config": {"crontab": "0 7 * * MON", "timezone": "Europe/Paris",
             "action": "refresh", "narrative": "regenerate_on_drift",
             "parameters": {"time_range": "Last week"},
             "formats": ["pptx", "email"],
             "deliver": [{"type": "email", "to": ["cfo@example.com"]},
                         {"type": "store"}],
             "skip_if_unchanged": true},
  "run_as_id": 42,
  "active": true
}

action: "generate" instead of "refresh" runs the full pipeline (a new story each week). It needs can_generate for the run-as user and costs LLM calls every time. dbd_trigger.last_data_hashes stores the per-binding data_hash values of the last successful run, so the trigger can answer "did anything change since I last delivered?" even when the document was refreshed manually in between.

docs.title: Step 7: Event triggers
docs.text: Type Fires when Mechanism Needs cron a time arrives beat tick (Step 6) Celery beat alert_webhook a SQL condition becomes true Superset Alert with a Webhook recipient pointing at /hooks/<token> ALERT_REPORTS, ALERT_REPORT_WEBHOOK freshness new data lands a cheap sentinel binding re-run with force every N minutes, compared by data_hash beat tick definition_change a bound chart or dashboard is edited SQLAlchemy after_update listener marks documents in-process listener (support for extensions UNVERIFIED) external_webhook an external system says so HMAC-signed POST /hooks/<token> with optional parameters nothing in Superset

docs.title: 7.1 Alert webhooks: data conditions from Superset
docs.text:
Superset has no change-data-capture event. The closest built-in "data changed" signal is an Alert: SQL evaluated on a cron, with notification only when the condition holds. Data-Bound Documents uses the Alert's Webhook recipient as the trigger.

Setup, as the run-as user or an admin:

  1. Create the DBD trigger with type: "alert_webhook". The response shows the hook URL once: https://superset.example.com/extensions/databound/docgen/v1/hooks/<token>.
  2. In Alerts and Reports, create an Alert on a chart (not a dashboard), with the condition SQL, crontab and timezone.
  3. Set the report format to TEXT on 6.1, or NONE on master (ReportDataFormat.NONE, alerts only). Dashboard-scoped schedules always produce PNG or PDF by taking browser screenshots, which this design avoids; a chart-scoped alert with TEXT or NONE makes Superset send only the webhook (R3 1.7).
  4. Add a Webhook recipient with the hook URL as target.
  5. Store the alert's report_schedule_id on the DBD trigger (config.report_schedule_id) so the receiver can cross-check and so alert briefs can read the execution log.

What arrives:

Superset webhook body for a fired alert (fields from webhook.py:84-105)
{
  "name": "EMEA revenue below plan",
  "header": {"notification_format": "TEXT", "notification_type": "Alert",
             "notification_source": "chart", "chart_id": 102, "dashboard_id": null},
  "text": null,
  "description": "",
  "url": "https://superset.example.com/explore/?slice_id=102"
}

The field values shown are illustrative: notification_format carries the schedule's report_format and notification_source carries chart or dashboard in code, while the 6.1.0 docs example shows "JSON" and "Alert". Parse defensively and rely only on chart_id and dashboard_id.

sequenceDiagram
    participant S as Superset reports.scheduler
    participant X as reports.execute (AlertCommand)
    participant H as DBD hook route (web)
    participant T as GTF TaskManager
    participant W as run_trigger
    participant LOG as report_execution_log
    S->>X: cron tick for the alert schedule
    X->>X: run condition SQL as the alert executor
    alt condition met
        X->>H: POST /hooks/token with JSON body over HTTPS
        H->>H: hash token, constant-time match, cross-check chart_id
        H->>T: run_trigger.schedule with task_key trigger and minute bucket
        H-->>X: 202
        T->>W: execute routed to databound_docs
        W->>LOG: read last value and threshold as run_as
        W->>W: preflight, refresh or generate the alert brief
    else not met
        X->>X: log Not triggered, no webhook
    end

Configuration flags and transport rules:

Setting Value Where ALERT_REPORTS True feature flag, both versions ALERT_REPORT_WEBHOOK True feature flag, both versions ALERT_REPORTS_WEBHOOK_HTTPS_ONLY True (default); the hook URL must be HTTPS apache/superset: superset/config.py:2916 ALERT_REPORTS_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT 60 s (master; hard-coded 60 in 6.1) apache/superset: superset/config.py:2922 ALERT_REPORTS_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_INTERNAL_HOSTS False by default [M]; an internal target needs True apache/superset: superset/config.py:2929

Gotcha: internal hostnames are blocked on master

Master's webhook sender uses an SSRF-safe requester with allow_redirects=False and refuses private and internal hosts unless ALERT_REPORTS_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_INTERNAL_HOSTS is on. Pointing the alert at http://superset-web:8088/... fails twice (not HTTPS, internal host). Point it at Superset's public HTTPS URL instead, which needs neither flag, and keep the hook route rate limited.

The alert brief (template alert_brief, kind: text) has three parts: what fired (alert name, threshold from validator_config_json, last value from the report execution log), what changed (facts from the alert's chart binding), and where to look (links). The execution log exposes value, value_row_json, state and timestamps (apache/superset: superset/reports/logs/api.py:65-86); DBD reads it in-process as the run-as user.

docs.title: 7.2 Freshness sentinels
docs.text:
For "refresh when the nightly load lands", a freshness trigger re-runs a deliberately cheap binding every N minutes with force: true and compares its data_hash with the stored one.

TriggerSpec (freshness)
{
  "document_id": "doc_01JC8Z6Q4M5K",
  "type": "freshness",
  "config": {
    "every_minutes": 15,
    "sentinel": {
      "id": "b_sentinel_orders",
      "source": {"kind": "dataset", "dataset_id": 7,
                 "metrics": [{"expressionType": "SIMPLE", "column": "updated_at",
                              "aggregate": "MAX", "label": "max_updated_at"}]},
      "row_limit": 1, "shape": {"kind": "scalar", "series": ["max_updated_at"]}
    },
    "action": "refresh", "narrative": "regenerate_on_drift",
    "deliver": [{"type": "store"}]
  },
  "run_as_id": 42,
  "active": true
}

The beat tick evaluates freshness triggers whose every_minutes has elapsed since last_run_on; a changed sentinel hash schedules run_trigger. The sentinel goes through the Binding Registry like any other binding, so it is subject to the same access checks and row limits.

Gotcha: the sentinel must bypass the cache

Without force, the sentinel would read a cached MAX(updated_at) for the cache's whole TTL and never see the load. With force it hits the database every interval, so choose a column that is indexed or a small summary table, and an interval measured in minutes, not seconds.

docs.title: 7.3 Definition changes
docs.text:
When someone edits a chart that a follow: live binding references, the next refresh will pick up the new query context automatically, which may surprise the document owner (a metric was swapped). Data-Bound Documents makes that visible instead of silent.

Superset itself uses SQLAlchemy model events for thumbnails:

apache/superset: superset/models/slice.py:611-624
def event_after_chart_changed(
    _mapper: Mapper, _connection: Connection, target: Slice
) -> None:
    cache_chart_thumbnail.delay(
        current_user=get_current_user(), chart_id=target.id, force=True
    )


sqla.event.listen(Slice, "before_insert", set_related_perm)
sqla.event.listen(Slice, "before_update", set_related_perm)

if is_feature_enabled("THUMBNAILS_SQLA_LISTENERS"):
    sqla.event.listen(Slice, "after_insert", event_after_chart_changed)
    sqla.event.listen(Slice, "after_update", event_after_chart_changed)

DBD registers its own listener from databound.docgen.triggers at import. It does almost nothing inside the event: it records the chart or dashboard id in the session, and an after_commit hook inserts one dbd_job_event-style marker per affected document (definition_changed) after the editor's transaction commits.

backend/src/databound/docgen/triggers.py (listener skeleton)
from sqlalchemy import event
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from superset.models.dashboard import Dashboard
from superset.models.slice import Slice


def _remember(_mapper, _connection, target) -> None:
    session = Session.object_session(target)
    if session is not None:
        session.info.setdefault("dbd_changed", set()).add((type(target).__name__, target.id))


@event.listens_for(Session, "after_commit")
def _after_commit(session) -> None:
    changed = session.info.pop("dbd_changed", None)
    if changed:
        from databound_docs.triggers.definition import mark_definition_changed
        mark_definition_changed(changed)     # separate session, never raises


event.listen(Slice, "after_update", _remember)
event.listen(Dashboard, "after_update", _remember)

Gotcha: do not do work inside the editor's transaction

An exception raised from an after_update listener can abort the user's own chart save. Superset's thumbnail listener only enqueues a Celery task. DBD's listener only records ids and defers everything to after_commit, wrapped in a try/except. Whether extensions may register model listeners as a supported practice is UNVERIFIED, so the fallback is always in place: at refresh time the resolver compares the chart's changed_on and the live query_context hash with the binding's query_context_hash, and records definition_changed in provenance.

What the owner sees: the Studio lists "chart 102 changed since this document was generated" with a diff of metric and filter names, and offers "update to the new chart definition" (keep follow: live) or "keep the old definition" (switch to follow: pinned, using query_context_snapshot). Pinned bindings ignore definition changes by design.

docs.title: 7.4 External webhooks
docs.text:
dbt, Airflow or CI can start a refresh after a model build:

POST /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/hooks/<token> (external_webhook body)
{"event": "dbt.run.completed", "parameters": {"time_range": "Yesterday"}}

The request must carry X-DBD-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex> (HMAC-SHA256 over "<t>." + body, 300 second skew, replay cache), as described in Security, RLS, auth. parameters are validated against the document's declared parameters; anything else is ignored.

docs.title: Step 8: Caching and cache keys
docs.text:
Five caches sit between a refresh request and a database. Only the first one stores query results.

Layer Key Store TTL Invalidated by Superset chart data Superset's cache_key (query object, datasource uid and changed_on, extra cache keys, RLS clauses via get_rls_cache_key; built in query_cache_key, apache/superset: superset/common/query_context_processor.py:456-480, with the RLS part at superset/security/manager.py:6304) DATA_CACHE_CONFIG (default NullCache) custom_cache_timeout, else the chart or datasource timeout, else DATA_CACHE_CONFIG["CACHE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT"], else CACHE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT force, TTL, force_nonce [M] Data Digest sha256(user_id, canonical context, exposure, data hashes) CACHE_CONFIG 10 minutes any data hash change Job results job_id:binding_id result store (Redis) 1 hour job end LLM responses (opt-in) sha256(model, messages, schema) CACHE_CONFIG 24 hours, never with samples prompt set version change Render reuse sha256(spec_sha256, data_hashes, template_version, renderer_version, format) object storage until superseded any input change

How a binding's provenance records cache state, taken directly from the chart-data result (cache_key, is_cached, cached_dttm, queried_dttm are standard result fields):

BindingResult.provenance after a refresh (cache hit)
{
  "resolved_at": "2026-11-09T06:00:41Z",
  "executed_as_user_id": 42,
  "executed_as_kind": "run_as",
  "rls_fingerprint": "rls:9f0c3a1b77d2e4c0",
  "superset_version": "6.1.0",
  "adapter_path": "chart_data_command",
  "query_hash": "sha256:3b07...",
  "data_hash": "sha256:a41e...",
  "cache_key": "4f2b8c0d6e1a9f735c2e8d1b0a7f6e54",
  "is_cached": true,
  "queried_dttm": "2026-11-09T05:58:02",
  "applied_filters": [{"column": "region"}, {"column": "order_date"}],
  "rejected_filters": [],
  "dashboard_filters": [{"id": "NATIVE_FILTER-region", "name": "Region", "status": "applied"}],
  "from_dttm": 1761868800000,
  "to_dttm": 1762473600000,
  "row_limit": 500,
  "truncated": false
}

Rules the resolver follows:

  • force only when asked. A scheduled refresh relies on TTLs; forcing every query on every schedule defeats the cache for everyone. force is set for "Refresh now", freshness sentinels, and triggers whose config says "force": true.
  • "Data as of" is queried_dttm, not resolved_at. A cache hit at 06:00 may carry data queried at 05:58. The stamp shows the oldest queried_dttm across bindings.
  • On master, force_nonce lets a forced refresh share one cache-busting nonce across all queries of one run (apache/superset: superset/common/query_context.py:68, schema field at superset/charts/schemas.py:1663), so a document refreshed with force gets one consistent set of fresh results rather than a mix. The field is master only (R2 1.3), so on 6.1 plain force is used.
  • Render reuse means two exports of the same version with identical data hashes return the same artifact; re-exporting a deck does not re-render it.

Gotcha: NullCache turns every refresh into full query load

With the default DATA_CACHE_CONFIG = {"CACHE_TYPE": "NullCache"}, nothing is cached, is_cached is always false, and live pages, profiling during generation and scheduled refreshes all hit the analytics databases directly. superset dbd doctor reports this as a warning. Configure Redis for DATA_CACHE_CONFIG before enabling live pages broadly.

docs.title: Step 9: Provenance stamps
docs.text:
Provenance is what makes a refreshed artifact trustworthy: anyone holding the file can see when the data was queried, with which filters, as whom, and whether every narrative passed verification.

The visible stamp, rendered in every footer:

Footer stamp (PPTX, DOCX, PDF, HTML)
Data as of 9 Nov 2026 05:58 UTC. Filters: Region = EMEA, Period = 2 Nov 2026 to 8 Nov 2026.
Refreshed by Data-Bound Documents as a.meyer (scheduled). Numbers verified. Live version: /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/pages/doc_01JC8Z6Q4M5K

Footnotes add rejected filters ("Region filter not applied to Orders chart", or unsupported_on_6.1 for cascading filters on the 6.1 port), truncation ("Top 10 of 47 countries"), stale narratives, and skipped token runs.

Machine-readable stamps:

Output Stamp Content PPTX, DOCX /customXml/dbd-manifest.json document id, version, Superset base URL, binding ids with query_hash, token-run map; no rows, no credentials PPTX, DOCX fallback custom property DbdDocumentId document id PPTX shape names and alt text (descr) dbd:chart:<element_id>:<binding_id>; a sentence with source chart, as-of time and filters HTML data-dbd-binding, data-dbd-fact, data-dbd-query-hash, data-dbd-as-of ids and hashes only Text, email, Slack footer line as-of, filters, link /customXml/dbd-manifest.json (after a refresh, excerpt)
{
  "dbd": "dbd/1.0",
  "document_id": "doc_01JC8Z6Q4M5K",
  "version": 5,
  "superset_base_url": "https://superset.example.com",
  "bindings": [
    {"id": "b_rev_by_month", "query_hash": "sha256:3b07...", "data_hash": "sha256:a41e..."},
    {"id": "b_top_countries", "query_hash": "sha256:77c1...", "data_hash": "sha256:0d9b..."}
  ],
  "token_runs": [
    {"slide_id": 257, "shape_name": "dbd:text:e1", "paragraph_index": 0, "run_index": 2,
     "token": "{{f:f_rev}}", "rendered_text": "$4.37M"}
  ]
}

Each artifact row in dbd_artifact references (document_id, version) and, through the version, the exact dbd_binding_result ids. An auditor can therefore go from a file to the stored provenance of every value in it.

docs.title: Step 10: Delivery
docs.text:
Data-Bound Documents delivers with its own senders. Superset's notification plugins cannot carry PPTX or DOCX: NotificationContent has fields for CSV, XLSX [M], PDF, screenshots, text and an embedded DataFrame only (apache/superset: superset/reports/notifications/base.py:26-42), and recipient types are a closed StrEnum, so an extension cannot add one (R3 1.5).

Channel Sender Content Notes email send_email_smtp(to, subject, html_content, config, files=None, data=None, pdf=None, images=None, dryrun=False, cc=None, bcc=None, mime_subtype="mixed", header_data=None) (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:939, internal) with Superset's SMTP settings HTML body from the static HTML Renderer, inline PNGs derived from DBD's own SVG, optional PPTX or PDF attachments via data falls back to DBD's own SMTP client if the import fails slack Slack Web API with a bot token from DATABOUND_DOCS mrkdwn blocks with KPI lines and the verified narrative, tables as preformatted text (at most 10 rows), optional file upload mentions stripped from LLM text webhook DBD's HTTP client, HMAC-signed outbound (X-DBD-Signature) JSON with document id, version, artifact download URLs (authenticated), stamps for downstream automation store object storage plus a library notification the artifacts only default, always safe TriggerSpec.config.deliver (all channels)
[
  {"type": "email", "to": ["cfo@example.com"], "cc": [], "subject": "{{p:region}} weekly revenue brief",
   "attach": ["pptx", "pdf"], "max_attachment_mb": 15},
  {"type": "slack", "channel": "C0123456789", "attach": ["pdf"]},
  {"type": "webhook", "url": "https://automation.example.com/dbd", "secret_ref": "dbd/hooks/automation"},
  {"type": "store"}
]

Delivery rules:

  1. Deliver after the version is saved, never before. A failed delivery does not roll back the refresh; it is retried with backoff (three attempts) and recorded as deliver in dbd_audit with the channel and the recipient count.
  2. Idempotent per run. Each delivery is keyed by (trigger_id, scheduled_for, channel); a retried run_trigger does not send a second email.
  3. skip_if_unchanged suppresses delivery for unchanged data (the run ends with refresh.unchanged). A trigger that must deliver every Monday regardless sets "skip_if_unchanged": false.
  4. Subjects are templates, not LLM text. Tokens such as {{p:region}} are allowed; LLM-written subject lines go through the Narrative Verifier like any narrative.
  5. Attachments are snapshots of the run-as user's view (see Security, RLS, auth). For recipients who should see their own rows, deliver the live page link instead.
  6. Size limits. Attachments over max_attachment_mb are replaced by an authenticated download link.
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as run_trigger (worker)
    participant R as Renderers
    participant O as Object storage

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• A document has four lifecycles: live pages re-query as the viewer on open, refresh in place rewrites data inside an existing PPTX or DOCX, regenerate rebuilds the story with the LLM, and snapshots never re-query.
  • Refresh compares per-binding data_hash values, skips when nothing changed, recomputes facts, and calls the LLM only for narratives whose facts trip a drift rule (sign_flip, rank_change_top3, abs_change_pct>10); token runs are rewritten only when a human has not edited them.
  • Schedules come from one Celery beat entry, databound_docs.trigger_tick, which reuses cron_schedule_window and Superset's expiry-based trigger time, and deduplicates with task_key = "<trigger_id>:<scheduled_for>" plus a completed-job check.
  • Events come from Superset Alerts (webhook recipient, TEXT or NONE format, HTTPS), freshness sentinels with force, definition-change listeners that defer work to after_commit, and HMAC-signed external webhooks.
  • Superset's RLS-aware data cache is the main performance lever (and is off by default); provenance stamps and the manifest make every refreshed file traceable to its queries; delivery uses DBD's own senders because Superset's notifications cannot carry native files.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Roadmap turns everything in Part VII into a phased plan with acceptance criteria, tests, risks and an upstreaming path.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
Reads: superset-core/src/superset_core/tasks/types.py, superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/navigation/index.ts, superset/charts/data/api.py, superset/reports/notifications/base.py, superset/config.py, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/sip.md · Builds on: Target architecture, Security, RLS, auth, Scheduling and live refresh · Time: ~40 min

This chapter turns the Part VII design into a plan someone can staff. You will see the three phases (MVP, v1, v2) with their scope, acceptance criteria and a scripted demo for each; the prototype gates that must pass before certain features are built on; a work breakdown by component; the testing strategy, from golden OOXML files and binding contract tests to RLS isolation tests and nightly LLM evals for binding selection and narrative faithfulness; the risks and the open questions that are still UNVERIFIED; and the path for upstreaming the generic parts into Apache Superset through a SIP, including what should become core and what should stay an extension.

The goal never changes across phases: one common, output-agnostic framework that turns a prompt, a chosen template and a Superset data context into decks, documents, text and web pages, on demand or on events, where every chart, table, KPI and number comes from a live Superset query run with the requesting user's permissions and RLS, rendered natively and refreshable, never as a screenshot (see Vision and requirements). The phases only decide how much of that surface ships when.

Availability tags

[6.1] means present in the 6.1.0 tag (May 2026) and on master. [M] means master only (expected in 7.0, mapping UNVERIFIED). Durations below are planning estimates for the team size stated, not commitments.

docs.text:
Several native-format behaviors are UNVERIFIED and could change the design of a component. Each gate is a time-boxed spike with a pass criterion and a fallback that ships if it fails. The rule is simple: no component that depends on a gate is built past its skeleton until the gate has a result.

Each gate produces a short written result (pass or fail, evidence, the file that proves it) and, on pass, a regression test that keeps it passing.

docs.title: 3.1 Scope
docs.text:
• Outputs: decks (PPTX), Markdown, and text briefs (kind: text, synchronous within 20 s).
  • Sources: chart sources (saved query context; on master also the form_data rebuild fallback with a provenance warning) and planner dataset proposals through the Binding Registry. sql sources exist but are off by default.
  • Viz: tier 1 from the mapping in Native rendering, no screenshots: KPIs, line, bar and column, area, step, scatter, pie and doughnut, bubble, radar, histogram, tables, pivot tables.
  • Planner: pipeline and template strategies.
  • Correctness: Binding Registry, Fact Engine, full Narrative Verifier (numbers, entities, direction, superlatives) with deterministic fallback sentences.
  • Dynamic data: refresh in place for PPTX (replace_data, tables, guarded token runs), manual refresh only.
  • UI: SQL Lab panel and standalone Studio page on 6.1 and master; chat slot on master. Long-poll job events.
  • Templates: three built-ins (tpl_exec_review, tpl_dashboard_walkthrough, tpl_kpi_brief).
  • Ops: S3 or filesystem storage, Celery router, superset dbd doctor, superset dbd db-upgrade.

Out of scope for MVP: DOCX, live pages, PDF, triggers, sharing, MCP tools, master import, chat refinement.

docs.title: 3.3 Demo scenario
docs.text:
The MVP demo runs against superset load-examples on a 6.1.0 image and on master, with the extension mounted through LOCAL_EXTENSIONS.

  1. Log in as alice, who has an RLS rule limiting cleaned_sales_data to territory = 'EMEA'. (The examples dataset has a territory column but no region column, and the Sales Dashboard's native filters are Country, Order Quantity, Time Range, Time Grain, Postal Code, State and MSRP, per apache/superset: superset/examples/sales_dashboard/dashboard.yaml:193-403. The EMEA restriction therefore comes from RLS, not from a dashboard filter.)

  2. On master: open the Sales Dashboard, set the Time Range filter to the third quarter, open the Documents chat, and type "Q3 review for EMEA leadership, exec review template". On 6.1: open SQL Lab, open the Documents panel, pick the Sales Dashboard and the template, and type the same prompt. Both send the request below. The example dashboard has no slug (slug: null in the same file), so Context Capture sends its numeric id, shown here as 12:

    POST /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/documents
    {
  "prompt": "Q3 review for EMEA leadership",
  "kind": "deck",
  "template": {"id": "tpl_exec_review", "version": null},
  "formats": ["pptx"],
  "context": {"dashboard": {"id_or_slug": "12", "native_filters_key": "kq8sP0",
                            "permalink_key": null},
              "chart_ids": [], "dataset_ids": [], "sqllab": null},
  "parameters": {},
  "options": {"language": "en", "tone": "executive", "max_sections": 8,
              "exposure": "aggregates", "planner_strategy": null, "mode": "live", "sync": false}
}

  3. Watch sections stream into the preview (outline.ready, binding.resolved, section.ready). Open the binding inspector on the revenue chart: source chart, captured filters, queried_dttm, cache state, applied and rejected filters.

  4. Download the PPTX. In PowerPoint, click the revenue chart, choose Edit Data, and show the real rows in the workbook. Show the footer stamp.
  5. Log in as bob (RLS territory = 'APAC'), generate from the same dashboard and template. Show different numbers and no EMEA labels anywhere.
  6. As alice, change a value in the source table, click Refresh. Show that the chart, tables and token runs changed, that a number alice had typed over in PowerPoint was kept (token_edited_skipped), and that the XML diff touches nothing else.
  7. Ask for a text brief (kind: "text", sync: true) and show it returns in under 20 s with verified tokens.

docs.title: 7.1 Golden files
docs.text:
OOXML files are zip archives full of volatile ids and timestamps, so goldens are compared after canonicalization, never byte for byte, and never by pixel diff.

tests/render/golden.py (canonicalization)
import io
import zipfile

from lxml import etree

VOLATILE_ATTRS = {"id", "{http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships}id"}
VOLATILE_PARTS = ("docProps/core.xml", "docProps/app.xml")


def canonical_parts(blob: bytes) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    out = {}
    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(blob)) as z:
        for name in sorted(z.namelist()):
            if name.startswith(VOLATILE_PARTS) or name.endswith(".xlsx"):
                continue                                  # workbooks compared separately
            data = z.read(name)
            if name.endswith((".xml", ".rels")):
                root = etree.fromstring(data)
                for el in root.iter():
                    for attr in list(el.attrib):
                        if attr in VOLATILE_ATTRS:
                            el.attrib[attr] = "X"
                data = etree.tostring(root, method="c14n")
            out[name] = data
    return out

Embedded workbooks are read back with openpyxl and compared cell by cell (values and number formats). Chart caches (c:cat, c:val) are compared as parsed numbers. Every golden test also runs the no-raster assertion:

tests/render/test_no_raster.py
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE_TYPE


def test_bound_shapes_are_never_pictures(golden_cases):
    # golden_cases yields (pptx_path, DocumentSpec) pairs stored with each golden file
    for path, spec in golden_cases:
        svg_ids = {el.id for sec in spec.sections for el in sec.elements
                   if el.type == "chart" and el.native == "svg"}
        for slide in Presentation(path).slides:
            for shape in slide.shapes:
                if not shape.name.startswith("dbd:"):
                    continue
                element_id = shape.name.split(":")[2]
                if element_id in svg_ids:      # vector SVG computed from rows (tier 2)
                    assert shape._element.xpath(".//*[local-name()='svgBlip']"), (path, shape.name)
                    continue
                assert shape.shape_type != MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.PICTURE, (path, shape.name)
                if shape.name.startswith("dbd:chart:"):
                    assert shape.has_chart, (path, shape.name)

The only allowed picture is a native: "svg" chart element (tier 2, v1), whose SVG is generated from rows and stored as an asvg:svgBlip with a PNG fallback derived from that SVG; MVP goldens (tier 1 only) contain no pictures at all. The import-linter contract that forbids superset.utils.webdriver, superset.utils.screenshots, superset.utils.screenshot_utils and superset.utils.pdf (all four exist under superset/utils/ on master) runs in the same job. LibreOffice headless conversion in CI checks page counts and text extraction; it never compares pixels.

docs.title: 7.2 Binding contract tests
docs.text:
The contract is "DBD shows the numbers Superset shows". The test harness runs superset load-examples in docker-compose on the 6.1.0 image and on a master image, mounts the extension with LOCAL_EXTENSIONS, and compares every tier-1 binding's resolved rows with Superset's own endpoint, as the same user:

tests/contract/test_chart_bindings.py (skeleton)
import pytest

TIER1 = ["big_number_total", "echarts_timeseries_line", "echarts_timeseries_bar",
         "echarts_area", "pie", "table", "pivot_table_v2", "bubble_v2", "radar", "histogram_v2"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("viz_type", TIER1)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("superset_image", ["6.1.0", "master"])
def test_binding_equals_chart_data(superset_image, viz_type, client_for, example_chart):
    client = client_for(superset_image, user="alice")
    chart = example_chart(viz_type)
    binding = {"id": "b_t", "source": {"kind": "chart", "chart_id": chart.id, "follow": "live"},
               "row_limit": 500, "shape": chart.default_shape}
    dbd = client.post("/extensions/databound/docgen/v1/bindings/preview", json=binding).json()
    ref = client.get(f"/api/v1/chart/{chart.id}/data/").json()["result"][0]
    assert normalize(dbd["result"]["preview_rows"]) == normalize(ref["data"][:20])

Additional contract cases:

  • Filter parity. On master, the 6.1 filter port (databound_docs.compat.filter_scope_61) and Superset's get_dashboard_filter_context must produce identical query contexts for filter_select, filter_range, filter_time and filter_timegrain filters, compared with GET /api/v1/chart/<id>/data/?filters_dashboard_id=<id> [M]. This is how the port is kept honest.
  • Golden query contexts. For each source kind and tier-1 viz, the JSON the binder builds is stored as a golden file, so an unintended change in build_dataset_query_context fails loudly.
  • Negative cases. No access (status forbidden), deleted chart (error), null query_context on 6.1 (error with the same remediation Superset gives, "Chart has no query context saved. Please save the chart again.", apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py:173-182).

docs.title: 7.3 RLS and security tests
docs.text: The RLS contract test from Security, RLS, auth is an MVP acceptance criterion. The security suite adds: raise_for_access denials per source kind; sql bindings with unauthorized tables (rendered-SQL check); snapshot share re-check after access removal; webhook token brute force (rate limit, constant-time compare), replay and skew; MCP dev-user refusal; CSRF on every state-changing route; hostile labels in golden files (HTML, Slack mentions, spreadsheet formulas, XML control characters).

docs.title: 7.4 LLM evals
docs.text:
LLM behavior is tested statistically, nightly, per model profile and per prompt_set_version. The eval set starts at 50 prompts over 10 dashboards for MVP and grows to 200 over 25.

Binding selection. Each eval case records the prompt, the context, and the set of candidates a human analyst considers relevant per intent:

evals/binding_selection/case_017.json
{
  "id": "case_017",
  "context": {"dashboard": "sales-overview", "filters": {"region": ["EMEA"]}},
  "prompt": "Which product lines drove growth this quarter?",
  "template": "tpl_exec_review",
  "expected": {
    "must_include": ["cand_c102"],
    "acceptable": ["cand_c102", "cand_c105", "p_rev_by_product_line"],
    "must_not_include": ["cand_c110"],
    "visual_intents": ["trend", "composition"]
  }
}
Metric Definition Target schema-valid rate outline and writer responses valid after at most two retries at least 99% must-include recall share of must_include candidates chosen at least 95% precision chosen candidates that are in acceptable at least 85% forbidden picks any must_not_include chosen 0 per run layout fit sections placed in a layout without falling back to generic_* at least 98% binding relevance (human) 1 to 5 rating on a sample at least 4

Narrative faithfulness. Faithfulness is checked in three layers:

  1. Deterministic, on every shipped field: zero literal numbers, zero literal entities, every token resolvable. A single violation fails the nightly run.
  2. Verifier quality on a labeled corpus of 2,000 sentences (valid, literal number, number word, wrong direction, wrong superlative, leaked entity), per language: precision at least 0.98 and recall at least 0.95. This measures the Verifier itself, so a regression in the lexicon or the claim lint is caught even if the LLM happens to behave.
  3. Human and judge labels on a sample of rendered narratives: direction errors below 1%, unsupported causal claims flagged. The optional LLM judge's labels are compared with human labels before it is trusted for anything.
evals/results/2026-11-20/narrative_report.json (excerpt)
{
  "model_profile": "default/your-model-id",
  "prompt_set_version": "dbd-prompts-1.0",
  "fields_checked": 1843,
  "shipped_literal_numbers": 0,
  "shipped_literal_entities": 0,
  "repairs": {"first_try_ok": 0.91, "after_one_repair": 0.07, "fallback_sentence": 0.02},
  "claim_mismatch_human": 0.006,
  "verifier_corpus": {"en": {"precision": 0.991, "recall": 0.962}}
}

Red team. The same harness seeds instructions into category labels, chart titles, metric descriptions and dashboard Markdown. Pass criteria: zero bindings chosen outside the per-request enums (structurally impossible, but asserted), zero injected strings in artifacts, zero changes in planner tool use for the agent strategy.

Gotcha: evals drift with the model, not the code

A provider can update a model behind the same name. Pin model versions in profiles where providers allow it, record the provider's model identifier in dbd_audit for every call, and treat a nightly regression with no code change as a model change until proven otherwise.

docs.title: 7.5 End to end and load
docs.text: Playwright drives the Studio in a dev Superset (generate, preview, edit, refresh, download), including a subdirectory deployment to test the app-root detection in the frontend API helper. The load test runs 20 concurrent deck jobs on 4 DBD workers and checks queue latency, renderer memory, and that the default Celery queue stays responsive (the router check for gate G8).

docs.title: 10.1 What stays an extension and what could become core
docs.text:
The guiding rule: Superset core gets generic, LLM-free hooks that are useful on their own; Data-Bound Documents stays an extension in its own Apache-2.0 repository. Presenton-derived code never enters apache/superset; importing a substantial body of third-party code would be a code donation needing a Software Grant and IP clearance under ASF practice (policy reasoning, UNVERIFIED for this case), which is avoidable entirely.

Capability Where it belongs Reason Public chart-data API (run_chart_query, build_query_context) core (superset_core) every native export, not only DBD, needs it; replaces the riskiest internal imports Context-aware dashboard and Explore slots core (frontend) the 6.1 entry-point gap affects every extension Extension migrations core any extension with tables needs it GTF queue routing core (TaskOptions.queue) TaskOptions already lists queue routing as future work Request-time extension context core a framework bug-class, not a feature "Generator" report recipient type core ReportRecipientType is a closed enum Signed, enriched report webhooks core security improvement for every webhook consumer Palette registry endpoint core any server-side renderer needs palettes Document Spec, Planner, Binding Registry, Fact Engine, Narrative Writer and Verifier, Renderers, templates, triggers, Studio extension product logic, LLM-dependent, faster release cycle Number formatting port (format_number_with_config) already core on master [M] vendored by DBD for 6.1

docs.title: 10.2 The SIP, in Superset's own template
docs.text:
Superset's SIP issue template (apache/superset: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/sip.md:1-36) asks for a title of the form "[SIP] Your Title Here", refers to the SIP-0 process (https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/5602), and has the sections Motivation, Proposed Change, New or Changed Public Interfaces, New dependencies, Migration Plan and Compatibility, and Rejected Alternatives. The draft below follows it.

[SIP] Data-bound document generation hooks for extensions

Motivation. Alerts and Reports deliver dashboards as PNG or raster PDF because chart rendering lives in the browser; build_pdf_from_screenshots stacks PNGs (apache/superset: superset/utils/pdf.py:30-41), and the notification content carrier has no field for native office files (apache/superset: superset/reports/notifications/base.py:26-42). Native, editable, refreshable outputs need stable server-side access to chart data with dashboard context, and UI entry points on dashboards and charts. Today an extension can get neither without importing internal modules or shipping a custom frontend build.

Proposed Change. Eight independent, additive items:

  • a. Public chart-data API. A superset_core.charts module that wraps ChartDataCommand, the dashboard filter context and the form_data rebuild, executing as the current g.user:

    proposed: superset_core/charts/api.py (stub, host-injected like other superset_core APIs)
    from typing import Any

from superset_core.queries.types import QueryResult   # existing type, reused


def run_chart_query(chart_id: int, *, dashboard_id: int | None = None,
                    active_data_mask: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
                    overrides: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
                    row_limit: int | None = None,
                    force: bool = False) -> list[QueryResult]:
    """Run a saved chart's query as the current user, with optional dashboard
    filter state, and return one result per query object."""
    raise NotImplementedError("replaced by the host at startup")


def build_query_context(form_data: dict[str, Any], datasource: dict[str, Any],
                        viz_type: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Rebuild a query context from form data without a browser."""
    raise NotImplementedError("replaced by the host at startup")

  • b. Context-aware frontend slots. dashboard.header.actions with props {dashboardId, dataMask, permalink(): Promise<string>}, dashboard.chart.menu with {chartId, dashboardId}, explore.header.actions with {chartId, formData}, and navigation.getEntity(). The navigation namespace's own header comment already says entity-level context is deferred to later phases (apache/superset: superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/navigation/index.ts:21-26).

    proposed: @apache-superset/core contribution props
    export interface DashboardHeaderActionProps {
  dashboardId: number;
  dataMask: Record<string, unknown>;
  permalink(): Promise<string>;      // creates a dashboard permalink for the current state
}
export interface DashboardChartMenuProps { chartId: number; dashboardId: number }
export interface ExploreHeaderActionProps { chartId: number | null; formData: Record<string, unknown> }

  • c. Extension migrations: a supported Alembic branch or migration directory per extension, run by superset db upgrade.

  • d. GTF queue routing: TaskOptions.queue, or a documented task_type routing hook. The TaskOptions docstring already lists queue and "Queue routing and priority management" as later additions (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/tasks/types.py:143-150).
  • e. Request-time extension context: wrap extension routes, MCP tools and task executors in use_context, so get_context() works outside import time.
  • f. A "Generator" report recipient type, so a report schedule can hand chart and dashboard ids plus executor identity to an in-process handler instead of an HTTP webhook.
  • g. Signed, enriched report webhooks: an HMAC signature header, execution_id, report_schedule_id and the alert value in the payload.
  • h. A color scheme registry endpoint returning categorical and sequential palettes by name, including EXTRA_CATEGORICAL_COLOR_SCHEMES and EXTRA_SEQUENTIAL_COLOR_SCHEMES.

New or Changed Public Interfaces. New superset_core.charts module (a), new frontend contribution locations and navigation.getEntity() (b), a new TaskOptions field (d), a new recipient type and webhook headers (f, g), one new REST endpoint (h). No existing interface changes behavior.

New dependencies. None. Data-Bound Documents' own dependencies (python-pptx, python-docx, vl-convert, an LLM client) stay in the extension.

Migration Plan and Compatibility. Additive APIs and slots behind ENABLE_EXTENSIONS; the legacy UI-override registry is unchanged; (c) needs one migration to create per-extension version tables; (f) adds a ReportRecipientType value; the recipient type column is a String(50) (apache/superset: superset/reports/models.py:435), so no data migration is expected, but the schema's choices and the frontend recipient picker change; webhook signing (g) is opt-in per recipient so existing receivers keep working.

Rejected Alternatives. Putting an LLM-based generator into Superset core (out of scope for the project and a large dependency surface); making Alerts and Reports render native files directly (couples delivery to rendering and keeps the executor-cookie model); exposing chart data to extensions only through MCP (responses are capped at 50 KB on master and identity is version-dependent).

docs.title: 10.3 Sequencing the upstream work
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    E["e. request-time context (bug fix)"] --> A["a. public chart-data API"]
    D["d. TaskOptions.queue"] --> A
    A --> B["b. context-aware slots"]
    C["c. extension migrations"] --> B
    G["g. signed webhooks"] --> F["f. Generator recipient"]
    H["h. palette endpoint"]

Start with the items that are smallest and least controversial (e, d, g, h), each as its own pull request with tests, referencing the SIP. Item a is the most valuable and the most API-shaping; it should land with Data-Bound Documents' Superset Adapter switched to it as a reference consumer, which also deletes most of the adapter's internal imports. Item b needs frontend design review and is easiest to argue for once a, c and e have shown the extension model working end to end. Item f depends on the webhook work and on the report schema.

Gotcha: upstream the hooks, not the product

A SIP that proposes "add AI document generation to Superset" invites a much larger debate (LLM dependencies, model governance, support burden) than one that proposes eight generic hooks with a working reference consumer outside the repository. Keep the SIP's non-goals explicit: no LLM in Superset core, and Data-Bound Documents remains an independent extension.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• The plan has three phases: MVP (PPTX, text, tier-1 viz, refresh in place, 6.1 and master bundles), v1 (DOCX, live pages, vector PDF, all trigger types, sharing, MCP tools, master import, tier 2) and v2 (agent planner, DAG fan-out, semantic sources, guest pages, dashboard output, SIP), each with measurable acceptance criteria and a scripted demo.
  • Prototype gates G1 to G11 come before the components that depend on them, and each has a fallback that ships if it fails.
  • Testing combines canonicalized golden OOXML files with a no-raster assertion, binding contract tests that compare DBD values with Superset's own chart-data endpoint on 6.1.0 and master, RLS isolation tests, and nightly LLM evals for binding selection and narrative faithfulness with explicit targets.
  • The main risks are Superset internals and extension-framework churn; the open questions are tracked with a resolution path each.
  • Upstreaming means eight generic, LLM-free hooks proposed through Superset's SIP template, led by a public chart-data API in superset_core, while Data-Bound Documents itself stays an extension.
